> feat: add minor currency support (#372)
> 
> * fix: differentiate minor currencies (GBp) from major (GBP)
> 
> Yahoo Finance denominates some securities in a currency's minor unit
> (e.g. GBp/pence) rather than its major unit (GBP/pounds). Ticker
> previously uppercased the currency code, collapsing GBp into GBP and
> treating pence-denominated prices as pounds, inflating Value, Cost, and
> Change figures by 100x.
> 
> Preserve the case of the Yahoo currency code so GBp survives, and
> synthesize a minor-currency conversion rate by scaling the major rate by
> 10^-n (n = minor unit). The Yahoo pair API force-uppercases symbols, so
> the pence rate is derived from the major rate rather than fetched.
> 
> Also validate that the configured display currency is a blank or 3-char
> uppercase ISO 4217 major code.
> 
> Fixes #282
> 
> * build: upgrade to go 1.26.4 to resolve stdlib vulnerabilities
> 
> govulncheck flagged four Go standard library vulnerabilities affecting
> the codebase (GO-2026-5039, GO-2026-5037, GO-2026-4971, GO-2026-4918),
> fixed in go 1.26.3/1.26.4. Bump the go directive and pinned CI Go
> versions to 1.26.4.
- 233855b66c0ca38fd7014d9bb5f8b0e25a7b19b4 — https://github.com/achannarasappa/ticker/commit/233855b66c0ca38fd7014d9bb5f8b0e25a7b19b4
> build: upgrade to go 1.26.2 and add govulncheck as go tool

- a8e240ed949f682122f3248252307d544bbc4fda — https://github.com/altair-graphql/altair/commit/a8e240ed949f682122f3248252307d544bbc4fda
> feat!: Introduced zod validation for AltairGraphQL init options and settings (#2968)
> 
> BREAKING CHANGE: This introduces runtime validation to the options and
> settings. Invalid options or settings will no longer work.
> 
> ### Fixes #
> <!-- Mention the issues this PR addresses -->
> 
> ### Checks
> 
> - [ ] Ran `yarn test-build`
> - [ ] Updated relevant documentations
> - [ ] Updated matching config options in altair-static
> 
> ### Changes proposed in this pull request:
> <!-- Describe the changes being introduced in this PR -->
> 
> ## Summary by Sourcery
> 
> Introduce Zod-based schemas across core Altair configuration, theming,
> authorization and settings, and validate AltairGraphQL init options
> using these schemas.
> 
> New Features:
> - Define Zod schemas for Altair window/config options, settings, request
> handlers, OAuth2 responses, environments, HTTP verbs, and themes, and
> use them as the single source of truth for types.
> - Validate AltairGraphQL.init options in altair-static and render a
> safe, correctly indented JS options literal, including nested objects
> and arrays.
> 
> Bug Fixes:
> - Ensure typed handling of partial theme and settings objects by using
> Zod input/output types and schema.partial() rather than loose partial
> interfaces.
> - Fix tests and Jest configuration in altair-static so that Zod-based
> core packages are transformed correctly and renderAltair tests stub
> getAltairHtml using Vitest spies.
> 
> Enhancements:
> - Refactor AltairConfig to store parsed options instead of a custom
> initialData structure and wire all consumers in the app to use the new
> options shape.
> - Centralize language definitions and defaults, and update language
> selection UI and config to use the shared language schema and enums.
> - Simplify theme defaults by extracting foundation colors, replacing the
> ITheme interface with a Zod-based schema, and updating default theme
> variants to depend on shared color constants.
> - Replace ad‑hoc and Ajv-based settings validation with Zod-based
> validation on both core and app sides, including generating JSON schema
> for settings UI and editor integrations.
> - Refine utility helpers and mappers (e.g., header and key/value
> mapping) to work with more generic value types while keeping
> string-based behavior where needed.
>

> Refactor breadcrumb styles to use semantic class selectors (#2992)
> 
> Breadcrumb styling used generic element selectors (`li`, `a`, `span`)
> which reduced specificity and increased collision risk with other
> components.
> 
> ## Changes
> 
> **HTML** - Added semantic classes to breadcrumb elements:
> - `.breadcrumb-item` on all list items
> - `.breadcrumb-link` on navigation links  
> - `.breadcrumb-text` on text spans
> - `.breadcrumb-current` on active item
> 
> **CSS** - Replaced element selectors with class selectors:
> 
> ```scss
> // Before
> .doc-viewer-breadcrumbs {
>   li { padding: 5px 8px; }
>   a { color: var(--secondary-color); }
>   span { overflow: hidden; }
> }
> 
> // After  
> .doc-viewer-breadcrumbs {
>   .breadcrumb-item { padding: 5px 8px; }
>   .breadcrumb-link { color: var(--secondary-color); }
>   .breadcrumb-text { overflow: hidden; }
> }
> ```
> 
> ## Screenshot
> 
> ![Class-based breadcrumb
> styling](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8470001a-0d69-452e-8a82-e8a10fbc0057)
> 
> Visual appearance and behavior unchanged. Existing unit tests unaffected
> as they target TypeScript methods, not CSS classes.

> ## Security Fixes
> 
> ### Least Privileged GitHub Actions Token Permissions
> 
> The GITHUB_TOKEN is an automatically generated secret to make
> authenticated calls to the GitHub API. GitHub recommends setting minimum
> token permissions for the GITHUB_TOKEN.
> 
> - [GitHub Security
> Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication#using-the-github_token-in-a-workflow)
> - [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security
> Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#token-permissions)
> ### Pinned Dependencies
> 
> GitHub Action tags and Docker tags are mutable. This poses a security
> risk. GitHub's Security Hardening guide recommends pinning actions to
> full length commit.
> 
> - [GitHub Security
> Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)
> - [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security
> Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)
> ### Harden Runner
> 
> [Harden-Runner](https://github.com/step-security/harden-runner) is an
> open-source security agent for the GitHub-hosted runner to prevent
> software supply chain attacks. It prevents exfiltration of credentials,
> detects tampering of source code during build, and enables running jobs
> without `sudo` access. See how popular open-source projects use
> Harden-Runner
> [here](https://docs.stepsecurity.io/whos-using-harden-runner).
> 
> <details>
> <summary>Harden runner usage</summary>
>

> details.
> </details>
> 
> ### Keeping your actions up to date with Dependabot
> 
> With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated
> dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the
> latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well
> as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).
> 
> - [GitHub Security
> Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/keeping-your-actions-up-to-date-with-dependabot)
> - [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security
> Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dependency-update-tool)
> ### Add Dependency Review Workflow
> 
> The Dependency Review Workflow enforces dependency reviews on your pull
> requests. The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies
> introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you
> about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better
> visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent
> vulnerabilities being added to your repository.
> 
> - [Github Guide about Dependency
> Review](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/about-dependency-review)

> ### Add OpenSSF Scorecard Workflow

- 4e34294c13466ebf5b31f712b96ad254c598c939 — https://github.com/altair-graphql/altair/commit/4e34294c13466ebf5b31f712b96ad254c598c939

> ### Changes proposed in this pull request:
> <!-- Describe the changes being introduced in this PR -->
> 
> ## Summary by Sourcery
> 
> Improve Altair Cloud API around auth, teams, workspaces, AI chat, query
> collections, credits, and real‑time events, while tightening security,
> rate limiting, and configuration.
> 
> New Features:
> - Add team invitation model and API (create, list, accept, revoke) with
> email notifications and event broadcasts.
> - Introduce public query sharing via share links, including a public
> shared query endpoint and client helpers.
> - Extend AI chat API and client with session management (list, rename,
> delete, resume), message streaming, and smarter context handling with
> automatic summarization.
> - Implement full CRUD for workspaces with ownership and safety checks
> around deletion for personal and team workspaces.
> - Expose credit transaction history with cursor‑based pagination via API
> and client, and broadcast credit updates over SSE.
> - Add auth refresh token and email verification flows, including
> verification email sending and token‑based confirmation.
> - Support moving, exporting, and importing query collections (including
> nested structures) across workspaces via API and client.
> - Enhance SSE event streams with additional event types for team
> membership, plan, and credit updates and tie client subscriptions to
> sign‑out.
> 
> Bug Fixes:
> - Clamp credit purchases to the configured minimum amount instead of the
> maximum.
> - Prevent AI chat session race conditions by using database transactions
> when switching the active session.
> - Fix query collection subcollections observable to actually return the
> observable and correct local collection lookup when using alternate IDs.
> - Handle non‑JSON HTTP error responses in the app by falling back to raw
> text parsing.
> - Ensure various endpoints consistently derive user IDs from
> authenticated requests and return proper Unauthorized/Forbidden errors
> instead of generic BadRequest or NotFound in those cases.
> - Avoid failing SSE streams on transient EventSource errors and clean up
> event listeners when connections close.
> 
> Enhancements:
> - Add richer team role handling (including derived OWNER role), shared
> helpers for role assertions, and use them across team, workspace, and
> membership operations.
> - Emit structured events for plan, credit, and team membership changes
> and use them to drive SSE notifications.
> - Improve AI chat internals by factoring shared send logic, adding
> context truncation with LLM‑based summarization, and refactoring prompt
> chain building for reuse and streaming.
> - Refine credit usage and monthly refill logic to run atomically in
> transactions, emit balance updates, and log refill failures instead of
> failing the whole job.
> - Tighten workspace and team authorization rules so only appropriate
> roles can update/delete teams and workspaces, with clear validation
> around team ownership and workspace contents.
> - Improve OAuth strategies and JWT strategies by validating required
> environment configuration up front and logging failures with Nest logger
> instead of console.
> - Use a shared helper to extract authenticated user IDs from requests
> and standardize Unauthorized behavior across controllers.
> - Make Stripe checkout success and cancel URLs configurable via app
> config instead of hard‑coding them.
> - Switch API logging and email flows to use structured Nest logging and
> more precise New Relic metrics for successes and failures.
> - Upgrade NestJS, LangChain, Stripe auth, and related dependencies and
> config to newer major versions and align Rate Limiter and Swagger
> behavior with environment configuration.
> 
> Build:
> - Upgrade core backend dependencies (NestJS, LangChain packages,
> @types/node, Google auth library, jsonwebtoken, and throttler) and wire
> new versions into the app module and config.
> - Add pnpm override for jsonwebtoken and adjust Vitest coverage plugin
> placement in package configuration.
> 
> Tests:
> - Remove the SlowBuffer polyfill from custom test matchers now that
> dependencies no longer require it.
>

>   * Import/export/move collections and expanded workspace CRUD
>   * Viewable, paginated credit transaction history

- d3f494ca3d70e4e09d9f7e3b0131c51cc41b3e92 — https://github.com/altair-graphql/altair/commit/d3f494ca3d70e4e09d9f7e3b0131c51cc41b3e92
> Make search filters type-safe and config-driven (#2993)
> 
> ## Refactoring: Type-Safe and Maintainable Search Filters
> 
> ### Changes Implemented
> 
> #### 1. **Type Safety** (`models/index.ts`)
> Created strongly-typed filter system:
> ```typescript
> export type DocSearchFilterKey = 
>   | 'types' | 'fields' | 'queries' 
>   | 'mutations' | 'subscriptions' | 'directives';
> 
> export interface DocSearchFilter {
>   key: DocSearchFilterKey;
>   translationKey: string;
> }
> 
> export const DOC_SEARCH_FILTERS: readonly DocSearchFilter[] = [
>   { key: 'types', translationKey: 'DOCS_TYPES_TEXT' },
>   { key: 'fields', translationKey: 'DOCS_FIELDS_TEXT' },
>   // ... etc
> ] as const;
> ```
> 
> #### 2. **Translations Moved** (`default.json`)
> Moved all filter translation keys from `en-US.json` to `default.json`:
> - `DOCS_TYPES_TEXT`, `DOCS_FIELDS_TEXT`, `DOCS_QUERIES_TEXT`
> - `DOCS_MUTATIONS_TEXT`, `DOCS_SUBSCRIPTIONS_TEXT`,
> `DOCS_FILTER_BY_TEXT`
> 
> #### 3. **Config-Driven Template** (`doc-viewer.component.html`)
> **Before (48 lines of duplicated code):**
> ```html
> <button (click)="toggleSearchFilter('types')">
>   {{ 'DOCS_TYPES_TEXT' | translate }}
> </button>
> <button (click)="toggleSearchFilter('fields')">
>   {{ 'DOCS_FIELDS_TEXT' | translate }}
> </button>
> <!-- ... 4 more buttons ... -->
> ```
> 
> **After (17 lines, single loop):**
> ```html
> @for (filter of availableSearchFilters; track filter.key) {
>   <button (click)="toggleSearchFilter(filter.key)">
>     {{ filter.translationKey | translate }}
>   </button>
> }
> ```
> 
> #### 4. **Type-Safe Components**
> - `doc-viewer.component.ts`: Uses `Set<DocSearchFilterKey>` instead of
> `Set<string>`
> - `doc-viewer-search-results.component.ts`: Uses typed filter parameter
> - All method signatures use `DocSearchFilterKey` type
> 
> #### 5. **Updated Tests**
> - Added `DocSearchFilterKey` import to test files
> - Updated test expectations to use typed Sets
> - All tests remain passing with improved type safety
> 
> #### 6. **Style Adjustments** (`_doc-viewer.scss`)
> - Adjusted filter button padding from `5px 10px` to `2px 5px` for more
> compact appearance
> - Changed button border from `1px solid` to `0px` for cleaner look
> - Removed `border-color` transitions in hover and active states
> - Removed `font-weight: bold` from active state for consistency
> - Updated filter container margin from `margin-top: 15px` to `margin:
> 10px 0`
> 
> ### Benefits
> 
> ✅ **Type Safety**: Compiler catches typos and invalid filter keys at
> build time
> 
> ✅ **Maintainability**: Adding new filters only requires updating the
> `DOC_SEARCH_FILTERS` array
> 
> ✅ **DRY Principle**: Reduced template code duplication from 48 lines to
> 17 lines (64% reduction)
> 
> ✅ **Single Source of Truth**: Filter configuration centralized in one
> location
> 
> ✅ **Better i18n Structure**: Translation keys properly organized in
> `default.json`
> 
> ✅ **Cleaner UI**: More compact button styling with simplified visual
> states
> 
> ✅ **No Behavior Changes**: Purely refactoring - no runtime behavior
> changes
> 
> ### Files Changed
> -
> `packages/altair-app/src/app/modules/altair/components/doc-viewer/models/index.ts`
> - Added types and config
> -
> `packages/altair-app/src/app/modules/altair/components/doc-viewer/doc-viewer/doc-viewer.component.ts`
> - Type-safe implementation
> -
> `packages/altair-app/src/app/modules/altair/components/doc-viewer/doc-viewer/doc-viewer.component.html`
> - Config-driven template
> -
> `packages/altair-app/src/app/modules/altair/components/doc-viewer/doc-viewer-search-results/doc-viewer-search-results.component.ts`
> - Typed filters
> - `packages/altair-app/src/scss/components/_doc-viewer.scss` - Style
> adjustments
> - `packages/altair-app/src/assets/i18n/default.json` - Added
> translations
> - `packages/altair-app/src/assets/i18n/en-US.json` - Removed duplicate
> translations
> - Test files updated with typed imports

> Use dynamic offset for doc viewer sticky headers (#2991)
> 
> Sticky section headers in the doc viewer weren't flush to the scrollable
> viewport top due to `.app-doc-viewer`'s 20px padding.
> 
> ## Changes
> 
> - Define `--doc-viewer-padding` CSS custom property on `.app-doc-viewer`
> - Calculate sticky header offset dynamically: `top:
> calc(var(--doc-viewer-padding) * -1)`
> 
> ```scss
> .app-doc-viewer {
>   --doc-viewer-padding: 20px;
>   padding: var(--doc-viewer-padding);
>   // ...
> }
> 
> .doc-viewer-section-title {
>   position: sticky;
>   top: calc(var(--doc-viewer-padding) * -1);  // Was: top: 0
>   // ...
> }
> ```
> 
> Headers now stick flush to the viewport edge. If padding changes, the
> offset adjusts automatically without code modification.
>

> [StepSecurity] Apply security best practices (#3061)
> 
> ## Summary
> 
> This pull request is created by
> [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo) at the request of
> @imolorhe. Please merge the Pull Request to incorporate the requested
> changes. Please tag @imolorhe on your message if you have any questions
> related to the PR.
> ## Security Fixes
> 
> ### Least Privileged GitHub Actions Token Permissions
> 
> The GITHUB_TOKEN is an automatically generated secret to make
> authenticated calls to the GitHub API. GitHub recommends setting minimum
> token permissions for the GITHUB_TOKEN.
> 
> - [GitHub Security
> Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication#using-the-github_token-in-a-workflow)
> - [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security
> Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#token-permissions)
> ### Pinned Dependencies
> 
> GitHub Action tags and Docker tags are mutable. This poses a security
> risk. GitHub's Security Hardening guide recommends pinning actions to
> full length commit.
> 
> - [GitHub Security
> Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)
> - [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security
> Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)
> ### Harden Runner
> 
> [Harden-Runner](https://github.com/step-security/harden-runner) is an
> open-source security agent for the GitHub-hosted runner to prevent
> software supply chain attacks. It prevents exfiltration of credentials,
> detects tampering of source code during build, and enables running jobs
> without `sudo` access. See how popular open-source projects use
> Harden-Runner
> [here](https://docs.stepsecurity.io/whos-using-harden-runner).
> 
> <details>
> <summary>Harden runner usage</summary>
> 
> You can find link to view insights and policy recommendation in the
> build log
> 
> <img
> src="https://github.com/step-security/harden-runner/blob/main/images/buildlog1.png?raw=true"
> width="60%" height="60%">
> 
> Please refer to
> [documentation](https://docs.stepsecurity.io/harden-runner) to find more
> details.
> </details>
> 
> ### Keeping your actions up to date with Dependabot
> 
> With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated
> dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the
> latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well
> as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).
> 
> - [GitHub Security
> Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/keeping-your-actions-up-to-date-with-dependabot)
> - [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security
> Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dependency-update-tool)
> ### Add Dependency Review Workflow
> 
> The Dependency Review Workflow enforces dependency reviews on your pull
> requests. The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies
> introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you
> about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better
> visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent
> vulnerabilities being added to your repository.
> 
> - [Github Guide about Dependency
> Review](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/about-dependency-review)
> - [Github Guide for Configuring Dependency Review
> Action](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/configuring-dependency-review#using-inline-configuration-to-set-up-the-dependency-review-action)
> ### Add OpenSSF Scorecard Workflow
> 
> OpenSSF Scorecard is an automated tool that assesses a number of
> important heuristics ("checks") associated with software security and
> assigns each check a score of 0-10. You can use these scores to
> understand specific areas to improve in order to strengthen the security
> posture of your project.
> 
> Scorecard workflow also allows maintainers to display a Scorecard badge
> on their repository to show off their hard work.
> 
> - [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF)
> Scorecard](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard)
> 
> 
> ## Feedback
> For bug reports, feature requests, and general feedback; please email
> support@stepsecurity.io. To create such PRs, please visit
> https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo.
> 
> 
> Signed-off-by: StepSecurity Bot <bot@stepsecurity.io>
> 
> ## Summary by Sourcery
> 
> Improve CI and dependency management security across the repository.
> 
> Build:
> - Extend Dependabot configuration to cover GitHub Actions, Cargo,
> Docker, and all npm workspaces with daily update checks.
> 
> CI:
> - Add StepSecurity harden-runner to all major workflows to audit
> outbound calls from GitHub-hosted runners.
> - Restrict GitHub Actions GITHUB_TOKEN permissions explicitly in CodeQL,
> Firebase hosting, and new security workflows.
> - Introduce an OpenSSF Scorecard workflow to regularly assess and
> publish the project’s supply-chain security posture.
> - Add a Dependency Review workflow to scan pull requests for newly
> introduced vulnerable dependencies.
>

> ## Summary by Sourcery

> Improve Altair Cloud API around auth, teams, workspaces, AI chat, query
> collections, credits, and real‑time events, while tightening security,
> rate limiting, and configuration.
> 
> New Features:
> - Add team invitation model and API (create, list, accept, revoke) with
> email notifications and event broadcasts.
> - Introduce public query sharing via share links, including a public
> shared query endpoint and client helpers.
> - Extend AI chat API and client with session management (list, rename,
> delete, resume), message streaming, and smarter context handling with
> automatic summarization.
> - Implement full CRUD for workspaces with ownership and safety checks
> around deletion for personal and team workspaces.
> - Expose credit transaction history with cursor‑based pagination via API
> and client, and broadcast credit updates over SSE.
> - Add auth refresh token and email verification flows, including
> verification email sending and token‑based confirmation.
> - Support moving, exporting, and importing query collections (including
> nested structures) across workspaces via API and client.
> - Enhance SSE event streams with additional event types for team
> membership, plan, and credit updates and tie client subscriptions to
> sign‑out.
> 
> Bug Fixes:
> - Clamp credit purchases to the configured minimum amount instead of the
> maximum.
> - Prevent AI chat session race conditions by using database transactions
> when switching the active session.
> - Fix query collection subcollections observable to actually return the
> observable and correct local collection lookup when using alternate IDs.
> - Handle non‑JSON HTTP error responses in the app by falling back to raw
> text parsing.
> - Ensure various endpoints consistently derive user IDs from
> authenticated requests and return proper Unauthorized/Forbidden errors
> instead of generic BadRequest or NotFound in those cases.
> - Avoid failing SSE streams on transient EventSource errors and clean up
> event listeners when connections close.
> 
> Enhancements:
> - Add richer team role handling (including derived OWNER role), shared
> helpers for role assertions, and use them across team, workspace, and
> membership operations.
> - Emit structured events for plan, credit, and team membership changes
> and use them to drive SSE notifications.
> - Improve AI chat internals by factoring shared send logic, adding
> context truncation with LLM‑based summarization, and refactoring prompt
> chain building for reuse and streaming.
> - Refine credit usage and monthly refill logic to run atomically in
> transactions, emit balance updates, and log refill failures instead of
> failing the whole job.
> - Tighten workspace and team authorization rules so only appropriate
> roles can update/delete teams and workspaces, with clear validation
> around team ownership and workspace contents.
> - Improve OAuth strategies and JWT strategies by validating required
> environment configuration up front and logging failures with Nest logger
> instead of console.
> - Use a shared helper to extract authenticated user IDs from requests
> and standardize Unauthorized behavior across controllers.
> - Make Stripe checkout success and cancel URLs configurable via app
> config instead of hard‑coding them.
> - Switch API logging and email flows to use structured Nest logging and
> more precise New Relic metrics for successes and failures.
> - Upgrade NestJS, LangChain, Stripe auth, and related dependencies and
> config to newer major versions and align Rate Limiter and Swagger
> behavior with environment configuration.

> placement in package configuration.

item_id: amazon-science/chronos-forecasting::release::255743723
Data: 2025-10-20T13:48:29Z
URL: https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/releases/tag/v2.0.0

Release notes (texto original):

> ## 🚀 Introducing Chronos-2: From univariate to universal forecasting
> 
> This release adds support for [**Chronos-2**](https://www.arxiv.org/abs/2510.15821). It is a 120M-parameter time series foundation model that offers zero-shot support for univariate, multivariate, and covariate-informed forecasting tasks. Chronos-2 delivers state-of-the-art zero-shot performance across multiple benchmarks (including fev-bench and GIFT-Eval), with the largest improvements observed on tasks that include exogenous features. In head-to-head comparisons, it outperforms its predecessor, Chronos-Bolt, over 90% of times.
> 
> 📌 Get started with Chronos-2: [Chronos-2 Quick Start](https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/blob/main/notebooks/chronos-2-quickstart.ipynb)
> 
> Chronos-2 offers significant improvements in capabilities and can handle diverse forecasting scenarios not supported by earlier models.
> 
> | Capability | Chronos | Chronos-Bolt | Chronos-2 |
> |------------|---------|--------------|-----------|
> | Univariate Forecasting | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
> | Cross-learning across items | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
> | Multivariate Forecasting | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
> | Past-only (real/categorical) covariates | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
> | Known future (real/categorical) covariates | 🧩 | 🧩 | ✅ |
> | Fine-tuning support | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
> | Max. Context Length | 512 | 2048 | 8192 |
> 
> 🧩 Chronos/Chronos-Bolt do not natively support future covariates, but they can be combined with external covariate regressors (see [AutoGluon tutorial](https://auto.gluon.ai/stable/tutorials/timeseries/forecasting-chronos.html#incorporating-the-covariates)). This only models per-timestep effects, not effects across time. In contrast, Chronos-2 supports all covariate types natively.
> 
> ![fig1](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ab82fce-45ad-431e-a58c-189ed0d3359f)
> *Figure 1: The complete Chronos-2 pipeline. Input time series (targets and covariates) are first normalized using a robust scaling scheme, after which a time index and mask meta features are added. The resulting sequences are split into non-overlapping patches and mapped to high-dimensional embeddings via a residual network. The core transformer stack operates on these patch embeddings and produces multi-patch quantile outputs corresponding to the future patches masked out in the input. Each transformer block alternates between time and group attention layers: the time attention layer aggregates information across patches within a single time series, while the group attention layer aggregates information across all series within a group at each patch index. The figure illustrates two multivariate time series with one known covariate each, with corresponding groups highlighted in blue and red. This example is for illustration purposes only; Chronos-2 supports arbitrary numbers of targets and optional covariates.*
> 
> ![fig2](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/994d47c7-e197-4644-b16f-14f7aa853627)
> *Figure 2: Results of experiments on the fev-bench time series benchmark. The average win rate and skill score are computed with respect to the scaled quantile loss (SQL) metric, which evaluates probabilistic forecasting performance. Higher values are better for both. Chronos-2 outperforms all existing pretrained models by a substantial margin on this comprehensive benchmark, which includes univariate, multivariate, and covariate-informed forecasting tasks.*
> 
> ![fig3](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9046081b-2d9d-4588-a274-8dc70ad47a56)
> *Figure 3: Chronos-2 results in univariate mode and the corresponding gains from in-context learning (ICL), shown as stacked bars on the covariates subset of fev-bench. ICL delivers large gains on tasks with covariates, demonstrating Chronos-2’s ability to effectively use covariates through ICL. Besides Chronos-2, only TabPFN-TS and COSMIC support covariates, and Chronos-2 outperforms all baselines (including TabPFN-TS and COSMIC) by a wide margin.*
> 
> ![fig4](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4373e257-08af-4a8e-9700-1b77d2cc3a4b)
> *Figure 4: Results on the GIFT-Eval time series benchmark. The average win rate and skill score with respect to the (a) probabilistic and (b) point forecasting metrics. Higher values are better for both win rate and skill score. Chronos-2 outperforms the previously best-performing models, TimesFM-2.5 and TiRex.*
> 
> ## What's Changed
> * Add Chronos-2 by @abdulfatir in https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/319
> * Remove ALWAYS_DOWNLOAD from CF and S3 by @abdulfatir in https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/322
> * Use dynamic versioning and bump version by @abdulfatir in https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/320
> * Add example notebook for Chronos-2 by @shchur in https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/325
> * Update README for Chronos-2 by @abdulfatir in https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/324
> * Bump version to 2.0.0 by @abdulfatir in https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/323
> 
> 
> **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/compare/v1.5.3...v2.0.0

item_id: amazon-science/chronos-forecasting::release::341353060
Data: 2026-06-18T11:30:31Z
URL: https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/releases/tag/v2.3.0

Release notes (texto original):

> ## What's Changed
> 
> ### 🚀 Highlights
> * New [cloud deployment guide](https://auto.gluon.ai/cloud/stable/tutorials/foundation-model-timeseries.html): run Chronos-2 on AWS in 3 lines of code
> * Fine-tuning with `Chronos2Pipeline.fit()` now supports larger-than-memory datasets
> * New efficient preprocessing module `chronos.chronos2.preprocess` resulting in up to 20x faster input preprocessing for Chronos-2
> * Support for `transformers>=5` and `pandas>=3`
> 
> ### ❗Deprecations & breaking changes
> * When providing inputs to `Chronos2Pipeline` as a `list[dict]`, all dictionaries must share the same schema (same number of `target` dimensions and same covariate keys). To forecast inputs with different schemas, loop over them and call the model once per schema.
>   ```python
>   # ❌ Different covariate keys across items — no longer allowed
>   pipeline.predict([
>       {"target": [...], "past_covariates": {"price": [...], "promo": [...]}},
>       {"target": [...], "past_covariates": {"price": [...]}},
>   ])
> 
>   # ❌ Mixed univariate and multivariate targets — no longer allowed
>   pipeline.predict([
>       {"target": np.zeros(100)},       # shape (history_length,)
>       {"target": np.zeros((3, 100))},  # shape (n_variates, history_length)
>   ])
>   ```
> * Following methods have been deprecated. Please use `chronos.chronos2.preprocess.from_*` and helpers from `chronos.df_utils` instead.
>   * Input preparation methods in `chronos.chronos2.dataset`:.
>     * `Chronos2Dataset.convert_inputs`
>     * `validate_and_prepare_single_dict_task`
>     * `convert_list_of_tensors_input_to_list_of_dicts_input`
>     * `convert_tensor_input_to_list_of_dicts_input`
>     * `convert_fev_window_to_list_of_dicts_input`
>   * DataFrame utilities in `chronos.df_utils`:
>     * `convert_df_input_to_list_of_dicts_input` 
>     * `validate_df_inputs` 
> * Removed dependency on `scikit-learn`
> 
> ### ✨ New features
> * Add support for `transformers>=5.0` by @kashif in https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/416
> * New module `chronos.chronos2.preprocess` with efficient preprocessing methods for Chronos-2 by @shchur in https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/466, https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/493, https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/506
> * Public API of `Chronos2Pipeline` now accepts preprocessed data (e.g. backed by a memory-mapped Hugging Face `datasets.Dataset`) by @shchur in https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/507, https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/512
> 
> ### 🐛 Bugfixes & improvements
> * Allow explicitly passing the frequency to `pipeline.predict_df` by @shchur in https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/449
> * Fix `XDG_CACHE_HOME` typo in `boto_utils` by @shaun0927 in https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/488
> * Defer boto3 import and raise actionable `ImportError` for s3:// loads by @shaun0927 in https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/489
> * Fix pip install command for chronos-forecasting by @Arseni1919 in https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/481
> * Minor fixes and improvements by @abdulfatir, @shchur in https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/467, https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/505, https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/510, https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/511, 
> 
> ### 📚 Documentation
> * Describe deployment options via AutoGluon-Cloud by @shchur in https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/503
> * Update notebook on Chronos-2 deployment to SageMaker by @shchur in https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/444
> 
> ## New Contributors
> * @Arseni1919 made their first contribution in https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/481
> * @shaun0927 made their first contribution in https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/pull/488
>

- 0e9db70afc1c046867b4925e881c89458d3dda94 — https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/commit/0e9db70afc1c046867b4925e881c89458d3dda94
> Move input preparation outside of Chronos2Dataset (#466)
> 
> *Issue #, if available:*
> 
> This PR enables fine-tuning on datasets that don't fit into memory. The
> main idea is to decouple the preprocessing logic from the
> `Chronos2Dataset` class.
> 
> The workflow is as follows:
> 1. Preprocess raw data once using `prepare_tasks()` → save to any
> `Sequence[PreparedTask]` container like `datasets.Dataset`
>   2. During training, load tasks lazily via memory-mapped Arrow files
> 3. Pass data to `pipeline.fit(..., convert_inputs=False)` to skip
> redundant preprocessing
> 
> *Description of changes:*
> - Added `PreparedTask` `TypedDict` defining the preprocessed task schema
> (context, future_covariates, n_targets, n_covariates,
> n_future_covariates as torch.Tensor/int)
> - Extracted `prepare_tasks()` as a standalone function so it can be used
> in preprocessing scripts
> - Added `convert_inputs` parameter to `Chronos2Dataset` and
> `Chronos2Pipeline.fit()` to toggle between raw input preprocessing
> (default) and pre-processed input passthrough.
>

> choice.

> Defer boto3 import and raise actionable ImportError for s3:// loads (#489)
> 
> *Issue #, if available:*
> 
> *Description of changes:*
> - `boto3` lives in `[project.optional-dependencies].extras`, but
> `src/chronos/boto_utils.py` imported it (and `botocore`) at module top.
> A user who installs the package with `pip install chronos-forecasting`
> (no extras) and then calls `from_pretrained("s3://...")` currently hits
> a bare `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'boto3'` with no hint about
> the `extras` group.
> - Defer `boto3` / `botocore` imports in `src/chronos/boto_utils.py` into
> the single function that actually uses them
> (`download_model_files_from_s3`) and move the `boto3.Session` annotation
> behind `from __future__ import annotations` + a `TYPE_CHECKING` block,
> so importing the package no longer fails when `boto3` is absent.
> - In `src/chronos/base.py` (inside
> `BaseChronosPipeline.from_pretrained`, around line 349) wrap the
> `cache_model_from_s3(...)` call in `try/except ImportError` and re-raise
> with a message that tells the user to run `pip install
> 'chronos-forecasting[extras]'`. HuggingFace Hub and local-path loads are
> unaffected.
> - Verified locally in a fresh venv (no `[extras]`): `from chronos import
> BaseChronosPipeline` succeeds,
> `BaseChronosPipeline.from_pretrained("s3://...")` now raises the
> actionable `ImportError` instead of the bare `ModuleNotFoundError`.
>

- b7a82da527cca4da3868d7be969f6a5f59d01d1c — https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/commit/b7a82da527cca4da3868d7be969f6a5f59d01d1c
> Clean up user-facing API touching DataFrames (#507)
> 
> *Issue #, if available:*
> 
> ### Summary
> Reworks the DataFrame prediction path to be simpler, faster, and built
> from small reusable helpers. The old monolithic
> `convert_df_input_to_list_of_dicts_input` — which validated, sorted,
> built list-of-dicts, *and* generated prediction timestamps in a single
> pass — is replaced by focused functions in `df_utils.py`, and
> `predict_df` now assembles its output directly.
> 
> ### Changes
> - **Rewrote `df_utils.py` helpers**, each with a single responsibility:
> - `normalize_df` — coerce timestamps to datetime, group rows by id
> (first-appearance order), sort by timestamp within each group. Skips the
> sort when the data is already in that layout.
> - `infer_freq_from_df` — infer the shared frequency across series; skips
> series with <3 points and errors only if no series can pin down a
> frequency.
> - `make_future_df` — build the forecast-horizon timestamps (long format,
> `n_series * prediction_length` rows) for a normalized df.
> - `validate_df` — validate structure (required columns, numeric targets,
> known covariates, future_df shape/ids/lengths).
> - `validate_and_normalize_df` — single orchestrator that runs
> `validate_df` then `normalize_df`, used as the one source of truth for
> df preparation.
> - **Rewrote `predict_df`** (`base.py`, `chronos2/pipeline.py`):
> - Builds context tensors directly and assembles the output by attaching
> predictions to a `make_future_df` frame, instead of round-tripping
> through list-of-dicts.
> - Validates/normalizes once up front, then passes
> `validate_inputs=False` downstream to avoid redundant re-validation.
> - **Input auto-detection** (`chronos2/dataset.py`):
> - Removed the `convert_inputs` flag from `Chronos2Dataset` and
> `Chronos2Pipeline.fit`. Input kind is now auto-detected from structure:
> tensor / list-of-tensors / pre-processed (`"context"` key present) /
> list-of-dicts.
> - **Renames & deprecations:**
>   - `from_dataframe` → `from_data_frame`.
> - Removed duplicated `_normalize_df` / `_validate_dataframe` from
> `preprocess.py` (now in `df_utils.py`).
> - `validate_df_inputs` now raises `RuntimeError` pointing to the new
> API.
> - `convert_df_input_to_list_of_dicts_input` (with
> `validate_inputs=True`) now prints a FutureWarning
> - **Docs**:
> - Update `chronos-2-quickstart` to use the new recommended preprocessing
> path for fine-tuning.
> 
> ## Behavior changes
> - If the user provides `freq` to `pedict_df`, we skip freq inference on
> `df` and just use the provided `freq` to generate future timestamps.
> 
> ## Tests
> - Rewrote `test_df_utils.py` against the new API.
> - Renamed `from_dataframe` tests in `test_preprocess.py`.
> - Added `test_predict_df_matches_manual_preprocess_path` validating
> `predict_df` output against manual assembly via the public
> `from_data_frame` + `make_future_df` helpers.
> - Added `test_predict_df_accepts_short_series_with_explicit_freq`.
> 
>

- ec362e39081a59d664131856667bdd5fb3e7598b — https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/commit/ec362e39081a59d664131856667bdd5fb3e7598b
> Refactor preprocessing logic for Chronos-2 (#493)
> 
> ## Problem
> 
> Converting raw data to `list[PreparedInput]` is extremely slow when
> categorical covariates are present. For M5 (30K items, 50M rows, 7
> categorical columns), preprocessing takes ~8 minutes. The bottlenecks:
> 1. Per-item target encoding loop using sklearn
> 2. Redundant validation across `validate_df_inputs` and
> `validate_and_prepare_single_dict_input`
> 
> ## Changes
> 
> This PR speeds up the **list-of-dicts** and **tensor** inputs to
> `Chronos2Pipeline.fit` / `predict` / `predict_quantiles`. The
> `predict_df` path still goes through the old `df_utils` helper. We will
> change that path in a follow-up PR.
> 
> New module `chronos/chronos2/preprocess.py` with four entry points:
> 
> | Entry point | Input format |
> |-------------|--------------|
> | `from_tensor()` | 3D tensor |
> | `from_list_of_tensors()` | list of 1D/2D tensors |
> | `from_dataframe()` | pd.DataFrame + optional future_df |
> | `from_list_of_dicts()` | list[dict] |
> 
> Each method produces `list[PreparedInput]` that can directly be used by
> `Chronos2Dataset`.
> 
> Key implementation details:
> - **Direct tensor conversion** — no intermediate dict representation, no
> redundant validation
> - **Vectorized target encoding** — `_target_encode()` uses `np.bincount`
> across all items at once instead of per-item sklearn calls
> - **Single validation point** — each entry point validates once,
> internal helpers assume valid input
> - **Removes sklearn dependency** from the encoding hot path
> 
> On 1K, 2K, 5K items of the M5 dataset, we get the following speedups
> 
> | n_items | rows | old `list[dict]` (s) | `from_dataframe` (s) | speedup
> |
> 
> |--------:|-----:|---------------------:|---------------------:|--------:|
> | 1,000 | 1.7M | 11.21 | 0.68 | 16.6× |
> | 2,000 | 3.4M | 22.20 | 1.45 | 15.4× |
> | 5,000 | 7.7M | 53.22 | 4.80 | 11.1× |
> 
> ## Backwards compatibility
> 
> The four removed helpers (`prepare_inputs`,
> `validate_and_prepare_single_dict_input`,
> `convert_tensor_input_to_list_of_dicts_input`,
> `convert_list_of_tensors_input_to_list_of_dicts_input`) are kept as
> re-exports in `chronos.chronos2.dataset` and emit a `DeprecationWarning`
> pointing to the new `preprocess.from_*` entry points. Existing imports
> keep working.
> 
> ## Breaking changes
> 
> - `list[dict]` inputs must now be homogeneous: all dicts must share the
> same `n_targets`, the same `past_covariates` keys, the same
> `future_covariates` keys, and agree per key on whether each
> future-covariate value is provided or `None`/empty. Heterogeneous lists
> raise an actionable `ValueError` directing users to loop per item.
> (Mixing tasks of different shapes never composed cleanly with vectorized
> preprocessing.)
> 
> ## Tests
> 
> - New `test/test_preprocess.py` (30 tests) covering each entry point,
> validation errors, ordering invariants, target/ordinal encoding, and the
> unseen-future-category fallback.
> - Existing `test_chronos2.py` heterogeneous-list fixtures replaced with
> homogeneous fixtures that still exercise categorical covariates with
> known-future values.
> 
> By submitting this pull request, I confirm that you can use, modify,
> copy, and redistribute this contribution, under the terms of your
> choice.

- 80f62c71e87fe4506fb08647ac814a82725ba45d — https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/commit/80f62c71e87fe4506fb08647ac814a82725ba45d
> Pass import_allowlist when loading LoRA adapters with peft>=0.20 (#524)
> 
> ## Fix
> 
> `peft` 0.20
> ([huggingface/peft#3090](https://github.com/huggingface/peft/pull/3090))
> enforces an import allowlist when resolving a LoRA adapter's
> `auto_mapping.parent_library`. For Chronos-2 adapters this is
> `chronos.chronos2.model`, which is not in the default allowlist, so
> `Chronos2Pipeline.from_pretrained` on an adapter raises:
> 
> ```
> ValueError: The auto mapping wants to import 'chronos.chronos2.model' which is not in the import allowlist.
> ```
> 
> This broke `test_chronos2_lora_pipeline_loads_from_disk` in CI once
> `peft` 0.20 was pulled in.
> 
> We now pass `import_allowlist=["chronos"]` (peft matches on the module
> prefix, so this covers any submodule under our own package) when loading
> an adapter. The call is guarded on `peft>=0.20.0` since the kwarg does
> not exist in older versions within our supported range (`peft>=0.18.1`);
> the guard can be dropped once the minimum is 0.20.
> 
> ## Testing
> 
> `test/test_chronos2.py::test_chronos2_lora_pipeline_loads_from_disk`
> passes with `peft` 0.20.0 installed.
> 
> 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
> 
> Co-authored-by: Abdul Fatir Ansari <ansarnd@amazon.de>
> Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
- 8589d1988e9676817548e9626738ff06b6ca6370 — https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/commit/8589d1988e9676817548e9626738ff06b6ca6370
> Handle missing is_decoder in Transformers 5 (#520)
> 
> ## Summary
> 
> - guard the encoder and encoder-block decoder checks when `is_decoder`
> is absent
> - preserve the assertion when a config explicitly sets `is_decoder=True`
> - add a regression test that constructs `Chronos2Encoder` without the
> removed attribute
> 
> Fixes #519.
> 
> ## Root cause
> 
> Transformers 5 removed `PretrainedConfig.is_decoder`, while Chronos 2
> accessed the attribute directly in both encoder constructors. Since the
> package supports `transformers<6`, a fresh `Chronos2CoreConfig` on
> Transformers 5 raised `AttributeError` before the encoder could be
> constructed.
> 
> ## Validation
> 
> - reproduced with Transformers 5.14.1 and confirmed `Chronos2CoreConfig`
> has no `is_decoder` attribute
> - constructed a two-layer `Chronos2Encoder` successfully after the
> change
> - `python -m compileall -q src/chronos/chronos2/model.py
> test/test_chronos2.py`
> - `git diff --check`
> 
> ---------
> 
> Co-authored-by: Abdul Fatir <Abdulfatirs@gmail.com>
- ff27460c184635a991c4fa1ec1f3edc114a3d008 — https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting/commit/ff27460c184635a991c4fa1ec1f3edc114a3d008
> Preserve precision when unscaling Chronos-2 and Chronos-Bolt forecasts (#532)
> 
> ## Problem
> 
> Inverse normalization is computed in float32, but its result was cast
> back to the model dtype. For bfloat16 models, this discards low-order
> bits when the time-series level is large relative to its variation.
> Converting predictions to float32 later in the pipeline cannot recover
> that information.
> 
> ## Reproduction
> 
> ```python
> import torch
> from chronos.chronos_bolt import InstanceNorm
> 
> scaler, base = InstanceNorm(), torch.linspace(-2, 2, 9)[None]
> 
> for level, variation in [(1e4, 100), (1e5, 100), (1e6, 100), (1e6, 1e3), (1e6, 1e4), (1e7, 1e4)]:
>     x = level + variation * base
>     normalized, stats = scaler(x)
>     bf16 = normalized.bfloat16()
>     reference = scaler.inverse(normalized, stats, torch.float32)
>     outputs = (scaler.inverse(bf16, stats).float(), scaler.inverse(bf16, stats, torch.float32))
>     print(level, variation, *((output - reference).abs().max().item() for output in outputs))
> ```
> 
> The table shows the maximum absolute delta relative to performing both
> normalization and inverse normalization in float32:
> 
> | Series level | Series variation | Max delta before | Max delta after |
> |---:|---:|---:|---:|
> | 10,000 | 100 | 30.000 | 0.299 |
> | 100,000 | 100 | 252.000 | 0.297 |
> | 1,000,000 | 100 | 776.000 | 0.312 |
> | 1,000,000 | 1,000 | 2,020.000 | 3.000 |
> | 1,000,000 | 10,000 | 1,960.000 | 29.938 |
> | 10,000,000 | 10,000 | 32,008.000 | 30.000 |
> 
> ## Changes
> 
> - Add an optional output dtype to InstanceNorm inverse scaling while
> preserving its existing default behavior.
> - Keep inverse-scaled Chronos-2 and Chronos-Bolt predictions in float32.
> - Add bfloat16 model-level regression tests and a numerical precision
> test.
> 
> ## Testing
> 
> - Focused Chronos-2, Chronos-Bolt, and InstanceNorm suite: 16 passed.
> - Verified that the Chronos-2 regression test fails on the previous code
> because model predictions are returned as bfloat16.

> Fix Range.ExtractContent to follow the DOM Standard
> 
> extractContents() deviated from https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-range-extractcontents
> in several ways:
> 
> - Contained children were computed as *all descendants* of the common
>   ancestor that *intersect* the range, instead of the *direct children*
>   that are *contained* in it. Partially contained nodes and nested
>   descendants were therefore moved into the fragment a second time,
>   corrupting both the fragment and the source tree.
> - The first/last partially contained child was searched among all
>   descendants instead of the direct children of the common ancestor.
> - Partially contained elements were cloned deeply and their subrange
>   fragment was appended to the outer fragment instead of the clone,
>   flattening and duplicating content.
> - The new boundary computation climbed one level too far and swapped
>   node/offset arguments, throwing NullReferenceException when the common
>   ancestor has no parent (detached subtrees) and collapsing the range to
>   a wrong position otherwise. It now mirrors the correct logic already
>   used by ClearContent.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- 4302ffe3885cd598e20fd70082b46683fac55a92 — https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp/commit/4302ffe3885cd598e20fd70082b46683fac55a92
> Fix swapped END_TO_END and END_TO_START in Range.CompareBoundaryTo
> 
> Per https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-range-compareboundarypoints
> END_TO_END compares this range's end to the source range's end, and
> END_TO_START compares this range's start to the source range's end.
> The two cases used the opposite boundary of this range, which only
> surfaces with overlapping ranges (for disjoint ranges both mappings
> happen to produce the same result).
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- 4edb5232e4b5b6cb0e219da2265b112d530251bd — https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp/commit/4edb5232e4b5b6cb0e219da2265b112d530251bd

> Merge pull request #1258 from ivandrofly/fix/range-compare-boundary-points

> Updated changelog
- f042125cf9fd56f3c1be1b33de0569acf37dc37a — https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp/commit/f042125cf9fd56f3c1be1b33de0569acf37dc37a
> Fix O(n^2) regression when tokenizing large plain-text runs
> 
> The ScanDataText bulk-append optimization (added in 1.5.0) scanned the
> remaining buffer with IndexOfAny on every character. When no DataText
> terminator ('<', '&', '\0', '\r', '\n') was present before EOF, IndexOfAny
> returned -1, which `found <= 0 ? 0 : found` collapsed to a zero-length run.
> The tokenizer then advanced a single character and re-scanned the entire
> remaining buffer again, making tag-less text O(n^2): a 2 MB plain-text body
> took ~70s to parse (vs a few ms in 1.4.0).
> Treat the "no terminator" result as a run extending to the end of the
> buffer so the whole remainder is appended in one pass. Parsing is now
> linear (and faster than 1.4.0, since the run is appended via a single span).
> Add a regression test covering both ReadOnlyMemoryTextSource and
> CharArrayTextSource that asserts correct token output and guards against
> the quadratic behaviour returning.
- f0f2114677b4b02e7a9c6d814d2b5748f6ba47ec — https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp/commit/f0f2114677b4b02e7a9c6d814d2b5748f6ba47ec
> Fix Range.IsCollapsed to also compare offsets
> 
> Per https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#range-collapsed a range is collapsed
> only if its start and end are the same boundary point. The property
> only compared the nodes, so e.g. selectNode() reported a collapsed
> range even though it selected a whole node.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- f7177e0175f3c15d78b700bf8ee9148102ee3765 — https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp/commit/f7177e0175f3c15d78b700bf8ee9148102ee3765
> Fix NodeIterator pre-removing steps to use the first following node
> 
> Per https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#nodeiterator-pre-removing-steps the
> replacement reference is the removed node's first *following* node
> within the root that is not an inclusive descendant of the removed
> node. The search started from the beginning of the root's subtree, so
> it could move the reference *backwards* to an already visited node
> (nextNode() then re-returned visited nodes) and never reached the
> pointer-before/previous-sibling fallback.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- ff9ded2fc573bdbee38b937b682b000312953318 — https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp/commit/ff9ded2fc573bdbee38b937b682b000312953318
> Merge pull request #1257 from ivandrofly/fix/range-clone-contents

> Fix Range.CopyContent to follow the DOM Standard

- 06f047071748fc1f5dea763e02cf1d75fa07d2a3 — https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp/commit/06f047071748fc1f5dea763e02cf1d75fa07d2a3
> Improved selector matching performance
> 
> Profiling QuerySelector/QuerySelectorAll with ETW sampling showed the cost was
> concentrated in the traversal machinery rather than in the selectors themselves:
> array covariance checks pushing onto the node stack, an iterator state machine
> with a delegate filter, per-candidate interface casts, and a quadratic sibling
> walk.
> 
> - MatchAny/MatchAll no longer route through the GetDescendantsAndSelf iterator
>   with a Stack<INode> and a delegate filter. QuerySelector was slower than
>   QuerySelectorAll while doing strictly less work.
> - Added ElementTreeEnumerator, a depth-first pre-order walk over parent links
>   keeping a stack of child indices rather than nodes. No covariance checks, and
>   the working set is bounded by tree depth instead of tree width. Used by
>   QuerySelectorAll, MatchAny and MatchAll.
> - Added INodeListAccessor.TryGetElement, which tests NodeType instead of casting
>   to IElement, for the nth-child and nth-of-type selectors.
> - Previous/NextElementSibling hoist the child list out of the loop and drop the
>   interface casts; ParentElement avoids the interface cast helper, which is on
>   the ancestor walk of every descendant and child combinator candidate;
>   SiblingCombinator scans the parent child list once instead of re-locating the
>   element for every sibling.
> - Added TextContainsMatcher, streaming :contains over descendant text nodes with
>   Knuth-Morris-Pratt instead of materializing TextContent per candidate. Matches
>   spanning a node boundary are still found. Element.TextContent also drops its
>   nested LINQ iterators.
> 
> Benchmarks (BenchmarkDotNet, Ryzen 9 5950X, idle machine, StdDev under 1%):
> 
> Issue #929, not-found case, versus the hand-rolled GetElementsByTagName plus
> TextContent.Contains baseline:
>   net10.0  63.182 us (1.93x slower) -> 26.902 us (0.78x), 23.14 KB -> 176 B
>   net8.0  100.43 us (2.49x slower) -> 29.451 us (0.77x), 23.3 KB -> 184 B
> 
> QuerySelector, net10.0: up to 27.6x faster (div 3,998 -> 145 ns,
> p:nth-child(2n+1) 4,418 -> 160 ns), allocation 16,808 B -> 176 B per call.
> 
> QuerySelectorAll, net10.0: div ~ p 4.5x, p:nth-child 1.7x, p:contains 1.5x with
> allocation 235.75 KB -> 1,256 B.
> 
> Existing 42-selector SelectorBenchmark sweep: no regressions on either target
> framework, smallest gain 1.13x.
> 
> SelectorBenchmark only covered QuerySelectorAll, so the slower path had no
> coverage. Added QuerySelectorBenchmark (both entry points, default job) and
> Issue929Benchmark, and net10.0 to the benchmark target frameworks.
> 
> Fixes #929
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

> Generate the package with `dotnet pack` instead of the hand-written nuspec
> 
> Mirrors AngleSharp/AngleSharp.Js#134 so the two repositories package the same
> way.
> 
> src/AngleSharp.nuspec had drifted from what the project builds: it declared
> net6.0 and net7.0 dependency groups for frameworks that are not in
> TargetFrameworks. Generating the metadata from the csproj means the groups
> follow TargetFrameworks by construction, and System.Text.Encoding.CodePages
> lands only on the TFMs whose condition selects it.
> 
> Package versions move to src/Directory.Packages.props (CPM). CHANGELOG.md
> becomes the single version authority: nuke/Build.cs already parsed it for the
> package version and now passes it as -p:Version, so <Version> in
> Directory.Build.props is just a fallback for builds that bypass the script.
> 
> Moves the test project to net10.0, which raises it to the .NET 10 AnalysisLevel
> and surfaced CA2022 in two places that ignored a Stream.Read return value.
> Both are fixed rather than suppressed.
> 
> Verified against the package devel produces: identical file listing, identical
> dependency ranges, and unchanged assembly identity (Version=1.7.0.0,
> PublicKeyToken=e83494dcdc6d31ea, same FileVersion and InformationalVersion).
> 3741 tests pass on net10.0, net462 and net472 in both prefetched modes.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

> Assert the WPT origin field where the data provides one
> 
> Roughly half of the WPT url entries carry an "origin" key; the harness
> parsed it into the entry model but never compared it, leaving Origin
> computation untested. It is now checked, matching the WPT runners, which
> only assert origin when the key is present.
> 
> An opaque origin is the literal string "null" in the data, so a null
> Url.Origin is normalised to "null" before comparing. Presence of the key is
> tracked separately, since an absent key is otherwise indistinguishable from
> a null value once deserialised.
> 
> This surfaces 12 origin mismatches, of which one is a newly failing entry -
> gopher://foo:443/ - so the baseline moves from 521 to 520. The rest already
> failed on other fields. The mismatches are IPv6 compression, and gopher:
> and blob: origins that should be opaque.

> Allocate auxiliary-context storage lazily and release closed contexts
> 
> Follow-up to the previous commit, addressing review feedback.
> 
> Every document was allocating an empty auxiliary-context list even though
> the vast majority never open a window, which is wasteful on the parse and
> navigation hot path. The backing list is now allocated on first use, and
> typed as List<IBrowsingContext> rather than List<Object> so the storage is
> type-safe at the point of use.
> 
> Closed contexts were also retained for the whole lifetime of the opener.
> BrowsingContext.Dispose now detaches the context from the document that
> opened it, and Document.Dispose drops the strong roots it holds. Disposing
> the opener only releases the references - an opened window is not closed by
> its opener - so the observable behaviour is unchanged.
> 
> Adds BrowsingContextLifetime covering the three properties that matter: an
> open context survives a collection while its opener is alive (the original
> CI flake), an open context is retained by its opener, and closed contexts
> are collectible across repeated open/close cycles. The contexts are acquired
> in non-inlined helpers because a Debug build keeps locals alive until the
> end of the enclosing method, which would otherwise mask a real leak.
> 
> Each test was mutation-checked against the code it covers: removing the
> attach fails the first two, removing the detach fails the third.

> 
> The WPT url tests previously ran as one NUnit case per entry, each emitting
> per-mismatch console lines and an Assert.Warn, which buried the rest of the

> They now run as a single test that reports one informational line:
> 
>     WPT url tests: 521 of 891 pass (58.5%), 370 fail, baseline is 521.
> 
> The pass count is asserted against a MinimumPassing baseline so regressions
> fail the build, while improvements stay green and are visible in the summary.
> Per-entry mismatch detail is only emitted on a regression, capped at 25
> entries. The baseline is 521 because that is the net10.0 count; net462 and
> net472 pass 530 of the same entries.
>

> assembly rather than being downloaded from the wpt master branch on every
> run, so the baseline cannot drift with upstream edits and the tests no longer
> need network access.

> 
> Runs fallout-migrate to swap the Nuke.* namespaces for Fallout.*, rename
> .nuke/ to .fallout/ and update the bootstrap scripts. Fallout is the
> maintained continuation of NUKE, so the target graph and the [Parameter] /
> [Solution] / [GitHubActions] attributes are unchanged.
> 
> Three fixes were needed on top of the migration tool's output:
> 
> - Pin Fallout.Common to 10.3.49. The tool preserved the NUKE version
>   verbatim, but Fallout.Common publishes no 10.1.0 (the package starts at
>   10.2.12), so the reference did not restore.
> - Remove the telemetry property rather than renaming it.
> - Remove the Nuke Enterprise feed blocks from build.ps1 / build.sh.
> 
> Also renames nuke/ to the conventional build/. Note .gitignore carries a
> bare "build" rule inherited from a stale Python template, which would have
> left the entire build project untracked, so it is re-included with an
> explicit !/build/ negation.
> 
> CI needs no changes: ci.yml only invokes the bootstrap scripts.
> 
> Verified with the full suite on net10.0, net462 and net472 in both the
> prefetched=false and prefetched=true modes.

> Match the annotation-xml encoding case-insensitively (#1283)
> 
> An annotation-xml element in the MathML namespace is an HTML integration point
> when its encoding attribute is an ASCII case-insensitive match for text/html or
> application/xhtml+xml. IsHtmlTip compared the raw attribute value with ordinal
> equality, so TEXT/HTML and any other case variant were not recognised and the
> children were parsed as foreign content.
> 
> ForeignNormalTag already runs the same test with Isi a few hundred lines up, so
> this makes the dispatcher agree with it, and reads the value through
> GetAttribute with the interned AttributeNames.Encoding the way that call does.
> 
> A value carrying parameters, such as text/html; charset=utf-8, is still not an
> integration point. The specification matches the literal string rather than
> parsing a MIME type, and the added tests pin that down along with the absent
> attribute.
> 
> Signed-off-by: Arpit Jain <arpitjain099@gmail.com>

>

> instead of treating everything as opaque scheme data, aligning with the
> WHATWG URL Standard. Return opaque scheme data as PathName for non-authority
> URLs (data:, mailto:, etc.). Omit empty credentials from serialized href

- faf199ebc52439591e8017397827d1600d130266 — https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp/commit/faf199ebc52439591e8017397827d1600d130266
> Keep auxiliary browsing contexts alive until their opener is gone
> 
> A browsing context opened as a new window (target=, window.open) was only
> ever reachable through weak references: the name-keyed _children map and
> the _contextGroup list on the opener, plus Document._attachedReferences.
> Unlike a frame context - which its owning HtmlFrameElementBase roots via a
> strong _context field - an auxiliary context has no owning element, so once
> DefaultNavigationHandler.NavigateAsync completed, the new context and its
> active document formed an isolated cycle with no strong root. Any GC could
> then collect it, and a subsequent FindChild would return null for a window
> that logically still exists.
> 
> Root the auxiliary context in the opening document instead, mirroring the
> lifetime an opener/opened pair should have. Frame contexts and the existing
> weak lookup structures are left untouched, so search semantics are unchanged
> - only the lifetime differs.
> 
> This was surfacing as intermittent CI failures in IframeTargets, most often
> AnchorTargetsSelfAsParentInNewWindow, where the new window document has no
> iframes to incidentally keep it alive. The tests could not be fixed on their
> own: DoClick is fire-and-forget, and there is nothing to hold a strong
> reference to until FindChild returns, which is the racing call itself.
> Reproduced deterministically by forcing a collection between the click and
> the lookup: 5/5 failures before, 0/5 after.
- fe73d27b74a3771db65eeadab1096d8b027f1dae — https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp/commit/fe73d27b74a3771db65eeadab1096d8b027f1dae
> Own auxiliary context lifetime in the browsing context group
> 
> Reworks the previous two commits after review: the browsing context, not the
> document, is what knows whether a context is a frame descendant or a window
> opened from another document, so it is where the lifetime belongs.
> 
> Document is reverted to its original state - AttachAuxiliaryContext,
> DetachAuxiliaryContext and the Dispose clearing are all gone.
> 
> Rooting a window in the opening *document* was not just misplaced, it was
> wrong: a document is per-navigation while a window outlives every document
> that loads into its opener, so navigating the opener destroyed the window it
> had opened. AuxiliaryContextSurvivesTheOpenerNavigatingAway covers that.
> 
> _contextGroup already carried this intent - its comment says an auxiliary
> context belongs to the top-most browsing context - but it was never finished:
> it held weak references, each context had a private list rather than sharing
> one, and the `_contextGroup is null` branch was unreachable because the field
> is readonly and always initialised. It is now a single list shared by
> reference across the group, holding its auxiliary contexts strongly, and the
> dead branch is gone.
> 
> The lifetime falls out of the sharing: every context in a group references the
> same list, so holding any one of them keeps the group reachable, and dropping
> them all makes the whole graph collectible at once. Frame contexts stay out of
> the group - their frame element already roots them. Dispose removes a closed
> context from the group. Threading the group through the constructor chain
> avoids assigning the readonly field twice and allocating a list per child.
> 
> The group probe in the navigation test goes through a non-inlined helper that
> returns a Boolean. Calling FindChild in the test body left the context
> reachable from that frame, and the test passed even with the fix removed.
> 
> Mutation-checked: removing the group Add fails the three retention tests,
> removing the Dispose removal fails the collectibility test.

### Releases sorteadas

#### 1. v25.11.0-trunk.351 / Weekly digest

item_id: armbian/build::release::255670969
Data: 2025-10-20T06:41:41Z
URL: https://github.com/armbian/build/releases/tag/v25.11.0-trunk.351

Release notes (texto original):

> This week’s Armbian development saw a series of notable updates across build scripts, kernel versions, and board support. Key improvements include the addition of wget to host preparation scripts and expanded zram compression options for meson64 configurations. The build system now allows for minimal btrfs compressed images and introduces kernel bumps to version 6.18 for multiple platforms, including qcs6490, meson64, rockchip64, and UEFI. The BPI-R4/filogic platform received a kernel reorganization, while a new CSC board, Luckfox Lyra Zero W, was added for rockchip devices. Several build machinery fixes and driver updates were also implemented, alongside corrections in module documentation. These changes collectively enhance Armbian’s flexibility, hardware compatibility, and overall reliability.
> 
> ## 
> * Add wget to prepare-host.sh.  by @HeyMeco in [armbian/build#8779](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8779)
> * add zstd and lzo as zram compression to meson64 current and edge configs.  by @Migelo in [armbian/build#8767](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8767)
> * allow building a minimal btrfs compressed image.  by @amazingfate in [armbian/build#8751](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8751)
> * armsom-forge1: rename dtb name to match mainline.  by @amazingfate in [armbian/build#8768](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8768)
> * BPI-R4/filogic - demote current kernel to legacy, introduce frank-w kernel for current/edge.  by @tabrisnet in [armbian/build#8746](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8746)
> * build machinery - fixup compilation for uboot/atf BRANCH=edge, pass --no-warn-rwx-segments to linker, not compiler.  by @tabrisnet in [armbian/build#8757](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8757)
> * build machinery - replace wget with curl cuz reasons .  by @tabrisnet in [armbian/build#8765](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8765)
> * Bump qcs6490 edge to 6.18.  by @amazingfate in [armbian/build#8770](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8770)

#### 2. v25.11.0-trunk.414 / Weekly digest

item_id: armbian/build::release::259153696
Data: 2025-11-03T06:44:24Z
URL: https://github.com/armbian/build/releases/tag/v25.11.0-trunk.414

Release notes (texto original):

> This week’s Armbian development saw significant progress across multiple fronts, including expanded hardware support and key software enhancements. Notable additions include support for new boards such as the Radxa E54C and Hardkernel ODROID M1S, as well as the integration of Debian Forky as a CSC target. Kernel updates were prominent, with bumps to versions 6.17 and 6.18, alongside improved configuration management for various devices. Bootloader improvements were made, including enhanced BTRFS support and more reliable local version settings in U-Boot. Several bug fixes addressed build errors and kernel configurations, particularly for IMX8 and Filogic/BPI-R4. The release also featured updates to documentation and board maintenance, ensuring smoother development workflows and broader compatibility.
> 
> ## 
> * add CRYPTROOT_AUTOUNLOCK option and fix CRYPTROOT for uefi builds.  by @sashasimkin in [armbian/build#8805](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8805)
> * add Debian Forky as CSC target.  by @timsurber in [armbian/build#8814](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8814)
> * add description for .conf.  by @EvilOlaf in [armbian/build#8847](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8847)
> * add new board radxa-e54c.  by @kamilsaigol in [armbian/build#8849](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8849)
> * Add support for Hardkernel ODROID M1S.  by @Jojo-A in [armbian/build#8846](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8846)
> * change from frank-w's tree to just a git-format-patches from his tree.  by @tabrisnet in [armbian/build#8850](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8850)
> * filogic/bpi-r4 - fix edge kernel config.  by @tabrisnet in [armbian/build#8772](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8772)
> * Ghost: use latest version v6.  by @igorpecovnik in [armbian/configng#692](https://github.com/armbian/configng/pull/692)
> * grub: don't set CLOUD_INIT_CONFIG_LOCATION.  by @rpardini in [armbian/build#8852](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8852)
> * IMX8: fix ATF build error (again).  by @schmiedelm in [armbian/build#8843](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8843)
> * mainline-kernel: bump 6.18 to 6.18-rc3.  by @rpardini in [armbian/build#8830](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8830)
> * Move kernel config changes from board to kernel config.  by @igorpecovnik in [armbian/build#8858](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8858)
> * nanopct6(-lts): u-boot: enable BTRFS support.  by @rpardini in [armbian/build#8856](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8856)
> * odroidm1: u-boot: bump to 2025.10; enable BTRFS support.  by @rpardini in [armbian/build#8857](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8857)
> * rockchip64: add rk3318-box overlay for T98_RK3318 boards.  by @paolosabatino in [armbian/build#8848](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8848)
> * rpi maint: bump edge to 6.17.y.  by @EvilOlaf in [armbian/build#8837](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8837)
> * rpi4b: bump _edge_ to 6.18.  by @EvilOlaf in [armbian/build#8845](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8845)
> * RPI: Increase UEFISIZE from 256 MiB to 512 MiB.  by @igorpecovnik in [armbian/build#8842](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8842)
> * thinkpad-x13s: 6.17: .config: NFS_V4_2, ISCSI_TCP, NFSD =m.  by @rpardini in [armbian/build#8853](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8853)
> * ti: configs: boards: Update maintainer on board configs.  by @jonaswood01 in [armbian/build#8838](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8838)
> * uboot: set CONFIG_LOCALVERSION more reliably on script/config-enabled uboot sources.  by @rpardini in [armbian/build#8854](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8854)
> * uboot: `uboot-config` now prints diff with pre-menuconfig defconfig.  by @rpardini in [armbian/build#8855](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8855)
> #

#### 3. v26.2.0-trunk.32 / Weekly digest

item_id: armbian/build::release::266288553
Data: 2025-12-01T06:48:23Z
URL: https://github.com/armbian/build/releases/tag/v26.2.0-trunk.32

Release notes (texto original):

> This week’s Armbian development saw significant progress in board support and configuration updates. Notable additions include support for the Radxa CM5 IO and Youyeetoo YY3588 boards, alongside improvements for existing hardware such as the Youyeetoo R1 V3 and NanoPi R76S. Several boards, including the Radxa Rock 2A & F, were promoted to standard support status, while video output configurations were refined for BananaPi R4 and Radxa E52c. The team also made kernel advancements by bumping the edge branch to version 6.18-rc7 and updating Helios4 to the latest mainline U-Boot. Additional changes focused on package definitions, Thunderbolt support adjustments, and enhanced boot order and filesystem support, reflecting ongoing efforts to streamline and expand Armbian’s hardware compatibility.
> 
> ## 
> * add new board radxa-cm5-io.  by @amazingfate in [armbian/build#9009](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9009)
> * bananapi-r4 bpi-r4 board config - no video output.  by @tabrisnet in [armbian/build#8990](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8990)
> * board: add Youyeetoo YY3588 support.  by @SuperKali in [armbian/build#9003](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9003)
> * board: youyeetoo-r1-v3: fix boot order to prioritize SD card over eMMC.  by @SuperKali in [armbian/build#9006](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9006)
> * config: drop questing and resolute symlinks for package definitions.  by @leggewie in [armbian/build#8983](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8983)
> * Drop Thunderbolt in desktop packages, but enable in minimal, arch amd64 only.  by @igorpecovnik in [armbian/build#8982](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8982)
> * enable uboot btrfs for N2.  by @leggewie in [armbian/build#9011](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9011)
> * KERNEL_TEST_TARGET is just override. We won't both targets, so we have both..  by @igorpecovnik in [armbian/build#8998](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8998)
> * mainline: bump `edge` 6.18 to rc7.  by @EvilOlaf in [armbian/build#8989](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8989)
> * Radxa E54c: change board support status.  by @igorpecovnik in [armbian/build#8992](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8992)
> * Radxa Rock 2A & F: promote board to standard support.  by @igorpecovnik in [armbian/build#8986](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8986)
> * rk3576: nanopi-r76s: add mainline u-boot and fix USB3.0 host.  by @SuperKali in [armbian/build#8997](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8997)
> * Rock-5B-Plus: Use upstream device-tree name.  by @HeyMeco in [armbian/build#8994](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8994)
> * uboot btrfs support.  by @leggewie in [armbian/build#9010](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9010)
> * update Helios4 to u-boot mainline v2025.10.  by @leggewie in [armbian/build#8980](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8980)
> * Update radxa-e52c.conf - add HAS_VIDEO_OUTPUT="no".  by @schwar3kat in [armbian/build#8984](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8984)
> * Update SHA1 for armbian/linux-rockchip source.  by @HeyMeco in [armbian/build#8995](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/8995)
> #
