- ce584a7b147e067c959c95dda88ffd01181c1d3e — https://github.com/armbian/build/commit/ce584a7b147e067c959c95dda88ffd01181c1d3e
> board: youyeetoo-r1-v3: fix boot order to prioritize SD card over eMMC (#9006)
> 
> The device tree aliases show:
> - mmc0 = sdhci (eMMC, 8-bit, non-removable)
> - mmc1 = sdmmc (SD card, 4-bit, removable)
> 
> Previous boot order (mmc0, nvme, mmc1) caused the system to always
> boot from eMMC when multiple storage devices were present, ignoring
> bootable SD cards.
> 
> New boot order (mmc1, nvme, mmc0) now correctly prioritizes:
> 1. SD card
> 2. NVMe
> 3. eMMC
> 
> This ensures consistent boot behavior when using SD card as primary
> boot device.

#### 4. v26.2.0-trunk.146 / Weekly digest

item_id: armbian/build::release::273139910
Data: 2025-12-29T06:49:33Z
URL: https://github.com/armbian/build/releases/tag/v26.2.0-trunk.146

Release notes (texto original):

> This week in Armbian development saw a series of refinements and maintenance updates across the build and configuration repositories. Contributors focused on workflow standardization, cosmetic improvements such as board name adjustments, and documentation enhancements, including a README update promoting the Armbian Imager. Several technical fixes addressed typos, property mispellings, and package issues, while platform support was expanded with kernel and boot improvements for devices like the Mekotronics R58-4x4 and MusePi Pro. Notable changes also included vendor reorganization and the addition of fallback logic for Ubuntu LTS releases. Overall, the activity reflects ongoing efforts to streamline processes and bolster hardware compatibility.
> 
> ## 
> * Adjusting board names - cosmetic issue.  by @igorpecovnik in [armbian/build#9116](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9116)
> * chore: cleanup mirror_to_codeberg.yml workflow.  by @igorpecovnik in [armbian/build#9133](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9133)
> * chore: standardize workflow names.  by @igorpecovnik in [armbian/build#9130](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9130)
> * chore: update copyright years to 2026.  by @igorpecovnik in [armbian/build#9129](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9129)
> * Create mirror_to_codeberg.yml.  by @EvilOlaf in [armbian/build#9131](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9131)
> * docs: improve README and add Armbian Imager promotion.  by @igorpecovnik in [armbian/build#9128](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9128)
> * dts: orangepi-4-lts: fix mispelled disable properites.  by @EvilOlaf in [armbian/build#9123](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9123)
> * Fix dialog typo.  by @SergeantSerk in [armbian/configng#716](https://github.com/armbian/configng/pull/716)
> * fix(apt-utils): add fallback for Ubuntu LTS releases without -updates suffix in JSON.  by @adeepn in [armbian/build#9117](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9117)
> * fix(rootfs): unset GIT_FIXED_WORKDIR after debootstrap/mmdebstrap clone.  by @QwaSeeK in [armbian/build#9132](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9132)
> * Genio: Change INSTALL_ARMBIAN_FIRMWARE to 'yes'.  by @HeyMeco in [armbian/build#9134](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9134)
> * gha: check-pr-pictures: allow `declare -g BOARD_VENDOR=`.  by @rpardini in [armbian/build#9142](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9142)
> * mekotronics-r58-4x4: enable edge branch with mainline kernel & u-boot.  by @rpardini in [armbian/build#9127](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9127)

> 
> * fix(rootfs): pass GIT_FIXED_WORKDIR inline to fetch_from_repo
> 
> Instead of using 'export GIT_FIXED_WORKDIR' and then 'unset' after,
> pass the variable inline to the fetch_from_repo call. This ensures
> the variable only exists in the context of that specific command
> and doesn't leak into subsequent calls.
> 
> This follows the same pattern used in uboot-git.sh and kernel-git.sh.
> ---------
>

- 492b96aeeb251e52b86408d59366a29eabf34adc — https://github.com/armbian/build/commit/492b96aeeb251e52b86408d59366a29eabf34adc
> fix(apt-utils): add fallback for Ubuntu LTS releases without -updates suffix in JSON
> 
> Problem: armbian-base-files artifact for jammy fails to build because
> apt_find_upstream_package_version_and_download_url() looks for 'jammy-updates'
> in https://github.armbian.com/base-files.json, but only 'jammy' key exists.
> 
> Root cause:
> - For Ubuntu LTS (focal, jammy), code sets package_download_release to '${RELEASE}-updates'
> - JSON file from github.armbian.com only has base release keys (jammy, noble, etc)
> - jq query returns null for 'jammy-updates'
> - Artifact excluded from build matrix after 10 retries
> 
> Solution: Add fallback logic
> - First try with '-updates' suffix (jammy-updates)
> - If not found and release ends with '-updates', retry with base release (jammy)
> - This allows using base release data when -updates is not available
> 
> Impact:
> - Fixes jammy base-files artifact build
> - Allows jammy images to build (they depend on this artifact)
> - Maintains preference for -updates when available
> - No impact on other releases (Debian, non-LTS Ubuntu)

#### 5. v26.2.0-trunk.623 / Weekly digest

item_id: armbian/build::release::300071135
Data: 2026-03-23T07:24:46Z
URL: https://github.com/armbian/build/releases/tag/v26.2.0-trunk.623

Release notes (texto original):

> This week in Armbian development saw significant enhancements across multiple areas, including expanded board support and improved hardware compatibility. Notable additions include new images and configurations for Qidi X-6, X-7, and Ariaboard Photonicat2 mainboards, as well as refined kernel patch maintenance and updates for various platforms. The build system received important fixes, such as resolving compilation errors and device tree issues, alongside improvements in Docker utilities and offline mode detection. Several refactoring efforts streamlined backend processes and enhanced user interface elements. The team also introduced automatic fallback mechanisms for Hetzner server types, optimizing runner scaling. Overall, these updates reinforce Armbian's commitment to stability, broader hardware support, and a smoother user experience.
> 
> ## Changes
> 
> * Add automatic fallback to smaller Hetzner server types with runner count scaling. by @igorpecovnik in [armbian/actions#15](https://github.com/armbian/actions/pull/15)
> * Add board and board vendror image for Ariaboard Photonicat2. by @HackingGate in [armbian/armbian.github.io#255](https://github.com/armbian/armbian.github.io/pull/255)
> * Add image for Qidi X-7 Mainboard. by @Shadowrom2020 in [armbian/armbian.github.io#257](https://github.com/armbian/armbian.github.io/pull/257)
> * Add some board image. by @retro98boy in [armbian/armbian.github.io#258](https://github.com/armbian/armbian.github.io/pull/258)
> * Add support for dialog via new wrapper functions. by @igorpecovnik in [armbian/configng#762](https://github.com/armbian/configng/pull/762)
> * Add support for qidi x-* boards. by @Shadowrom2020 in [armbian/build#9564](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9564)
> * Change unit tests badge link in documentation. by @igorpecovnik in [armbian/documentation#885](https://github.com/armbian/documentation/pull/885)
> * Drop patches that landed upstream and fix two. by @igorpecovnik in [armbian/build#9544](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9544)
> * edge: bump 7.0 to rc5. by @EvilOlaf in [armbian/build#9580](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9580)
> * Enable BCACHE on Raspberry Pi build. by @aulanov in [armbian/build#9550](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9550)
> * feat: offline mode detection with local asset cache. by @SuperKali in [armbian/imager#117](https://github.com/armbian/imager/pull/117)
> * feat: settings refactoring, DiskArbitration device detection, and filename parser improvements. by @SuperKali in [armbian/imager#114](https://github.com/armbian/imager/pull/114)
> * fix race condition and NULL ptr deref in PCIe threaded probe. by @AlomeProg in [armbian/linux-rockchip#458](https://github.com/armbian/linux-rockchip/pull/458)
> * fix(docker): add trixie support for upstream docker-ce to fix HomeAssistant installation. by @igorpecovnik in [armbian/configng#765](https://github.com/armbian/configng/pull/765)
> * fix: correct dialog argument order causing box option errors. by @igorpecovnik in [armbian/configng#768](https://github.com/armbian/configng/pull/768)
> * fix: resolve Phytium stmmac compilation errors for kernel 6.19. by @igorpecovnik in [armbian/build#9545](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9545)
> * fix: settings modal reset, custom image manufacturer, and board detection setting. by @SuperKali in [armbian/imager#116](https://github.com/armbian/imager/pull/116)
> * Image for Qidi X-6 Mainboard. by @Shadowrom2020 in [armbian/armbian.github.io#256](https://github.com/armbian/armbian.github.io/pull/256)
> * kernel patch maintenance. by @EvilOlaf in [armbian/build#9562](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9562)
> * meson64-6.18: rewrite kernel config. by @EvilOlaf in [armbian/build#9581](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9581)
> * mksklipad50: fix devicetree opp voltage settings. by @torte71 in [armbian/build#9569](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9569)
> * OrangePi-RV2/R2S: rename board config from wip to csc. by @sven-ola in [armbian/build#9560](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9560)
> * Qidi X-6: fix defconfig patch. by @Shadowrom2020 in [armbian/build#9567](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9567)
> * refactor: add comprehensive Docker wrapper utilities with progress display. by @igorpecovnik in [armbian/configng#769](https://github.com/armbian/configng/pull/769)
> * refactor: deduplicate hooks, add CSS design tokens, clean up backend. by @SuperKali in [armbian/imager#115](https://github.com/armbian/imager/pull/115)
> * rockchip64-7.0: mekotronics-r58x-pro: analog sound: use SuperKali's new clock. by @rpardini in [armbian/build#9554](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9554)
> * rockchip64: rk3588: add I2S MCLK output gate clocks for audio codec support. by @SuperKali in [armbian/build#9548](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9548)
> * rockchip64: rk3588: update I2S MCLK gate patches to match upstream v3 and add u-boot clock IDs. by @SuperKali in [armbian/build#9568](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9568)
> * sm8250: Fix application of Retroid Pocket 5/mini device trees. by @kay-lambdadelta in [armbian/build#9572](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9572)
> * SpacemiT: Update ATFSOURCE, BOOTSOURCE and SD card support.. by @pyavitz in [armbian/build#9552](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9552)
> * sunxi-6.18: remove stray commit from patch. by @EvilOlaf in [armbian/build#9556](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9556)
> * sunxi: bump `edge` to 6.19.y, `current` to 6.18.y and `legacy` to 6.12.y. by @EvilOlaf in [armbian/build#9381](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9381)
> * Update odroidxu4-current to 6.6.129. by @belegdol in [armbian/build#9558](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9558)
> * Update VERSION. by @EvilOlaf in [armbian/build#9553](https://github.com/armbian/build/pull/9553)

> rockchip64-7.0: mekotronics-r58x-pro: analog sound: use SuperKali's new clock
> 
> > This series fixes ES8388 audio on the Mekotronics R58X-Pro (RK3588).
> >
> > Without these patches, the i2s0_8ch_mclkout_to_io gate remains closed
> > (enable_count=0 in the clk_summary), and the codec receives no master
> > clock. DAPM reports all widgets as powered on and playback streams run
> > without errors, but the hardware produces no sound — a rather
> > frustrating failure mode to debug.
> >
> > With the series applied and the board DTS updated to reference
> > I2S0_8CH_MCLKOUT_TO_IO from the codec node:
> >
> >     es8388: audio-codec@10 {
> >         compatible = "everest,es8388", "everest,es8328";
> >         reg = <0x10>;
> >         clocks = <&cru I2S0_8CH_MCLKOUT_TO_IO>;
> >         assigned-clocks = <&cru I2S0_8CH_MCLKOUT>;
> >         assigned-clock-rates = <12288000>;
> >         ...
> >     };
> >
> > audio playback works correctly, tested via headphones output.
> >
> > Tested-by: Ricardo Pardini <ricardo@pardini.net>

> rockchip64: rk3588: split I2S MCLK output gate patches to match upstream (#9548)
> 
> Replace the single combined MCLK gate patch with three separate patches
> matching the upstream series submitted to LKML:
> 
>   1. dt-bindings: add I2S MCLK output to IO clock IDs (722-725)
>   2. clk: rockchip: allow grf_type_sys lookup in aux_grf_table
>   3. clk: rockchip: rk3588: add GATE_GRF clocks for I2S MCLK output
> 
> Key changes from the previous combined patch:
>   - Use grf_type_sys instead of grf_type_ioc
>   - Add all four I2S MCLK output gates (not just I2S0)
>   - Use GFLAGS macro for consistency
>   - Place each GATE_GRF after its parent MCLKOUT
>   - No subscope in init function
> 
> 6.18 uses kzalloc(sizeof(...)) as kzalloc_obj is not available.

#### 1. v2.0.12 / v2.0.12

item_id: arvidn/libtorrent::release::296896493
Data: 2026-03-13T22:23:52Z
URL: https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/releases/tag/v2.0.12

Release notes (texto original):

> 2.0.12 released
> 
> * fix issue where file priorities could be cleared by force recheck
> * fix issue in XML parser
> * when building against OpenSSL, require at least version 1.1.1
> * add setting to set no-copy-on-write flag on new files
> * add performance counters to file pool
> * add high_priority flag to torrent_handle::force_reannounce()
> * update default DSCP value and update docs
> * fix python binding for set_notify_function()
> * fix error handling in mmap disk I/O when hashing files
> * improve copy_file_range() fallback
> * don't overwrite existing files when renaming
> * add option to send host header in HTTP proxy CONNECT command
> * cache DNS failures for a shorter time
> * file_renamed_alert is always posted, regardless of alert mask
> * add feature to request resume data synchronously
> * don't leak file descriptors to child processes (O_CLOEXEC)
> * optimize the utp resend
> * optimize tracker announcements
> * fix handling of invalid filenames
> * add support for I2CP inbound.lengthVariance and outbound.lengthVariance tunnel settings
> * add natpmp_gateway setting to manually set the default gateway for the NAT-PMP protocol
> 
> 
> ## What's Changed
> * fix publish to pypi by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/7836
> * fix warning in posix_storage and TORRENT_RVO by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/7846

> Optimize the utp resend loop in `utp_socket_impl::send_pkt`
> 
> There has been a TODO message there for over 10 years now saying that the
> current implementation isn't very efficient, and it isn't.
> 
> This commit adds a new `std::vector` `m_needs_resend` for each utp connection to
> track the packets that need to be resent. I've kept the behaviour the same as
> the previous implementation - the packets at `m_acked_seq_nr` (last acked packet)
> and `m_seq_nr` (FIN packet) will never be added to `m_needs_resend`.
> 
> Whoops, forgot to commit this
> 
> Caught the segfault
> 
> Account for `resend_packet` erasing the packet from `m_needs_resend`
> 
> Uncomment sequence number assertions
> 
> Move some assignments so invariant checks pass
> 
> Update src/utp_stream.cpp
> 
> Co-authored-by: Arvid Norberg <arvid.norberg@gmail.com>
> 
> Make a `need_resend` variable `const`
> 
> Co-authored-by: Arvid Norberg <arvid.norberg@gmail.com>

> * Drop support for Python <3.9 (EOL)
> * Add Python 3.12 & 3.13 support
> * Updated URL for "supported python versions"
> * Remove PyEval_InitThreads() call for Python 3.7 and later as Python calls it automatically now.
> This removes a deprecation warning when using Python 3.9.
> https://docs.python.org/3/c-api/init.html#c.PyEval_InitThreads

> require payload data before marking peer as last-seen-complete
> 
> Only update last_seen_complete timestamp when a peer claiming to be
> a seed has actually sent us payload data (total_payload_download > 0).
> 
> This prevents malicious or broken peers from polluting the
> last_seen_complete timestamp by connecting, claiming 100% via their
> bitfield, and immediately disconnecting without transferring any data.
> 
> Also reverts the previous is_seed() change as the original implementation
> was correct - the bitfield is properly initialized to zeroes.
> 
> Fixes #8118

#### 2. v2.0.13 / v2.0.13

Release notes (texto original):

> 2.0.13 released
> 
> * stricter basic auth handling for web seed
> * fix bug in tracker announcements involving i2p trackers
> * improve performance of disk job pool
> * fix race when removing an auto managed torrent
> * fix bug in post_download_queue() when a torrent complete
> * in create_torrent, store symbolic links according to BEP 47
> * strengthen peer encryption (obfuscation)
> * improve HTTP response parsing
> * optimize sanitization of symlinks when loading torrents
> * stricter checking of tracker URLs
> * fixed piece-picker accounting issue for filtered pieces
> * add setting for NAT-PMP lease duration
> * optimize v2 request sizes
> * fix socks5 issues
> * fix issue in loading v2 resume data merkle trees
> 
>

#### 3. v2.1.0 / v2.1.0

item_id: arvidn/libtorrent::release::351482123
Data: 2026-07-09T11:08:01Z
URL: https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/releases/tag/v2.1.0

Release notes (texto original):

> There are some changes to the API in this version. They are documented [here](https://libtorrent.org/upgrade_to_2.1-ref.html
> ). The headline features for this release are:
> 
> ## webtorrent support
> 
> Thanks to Paul-Louis Ageneau https://github.com/paullouisageneau, and apologies for this feature having been unreleased for so long.
> This feature is now enabled by default. The last push to get this ready has been to add fuzz targets for WebRTC specific features, rtc_parse_endpoint, rtc_peer_conn, rtc_tracker_offer and sdp_offer. The dependencies for webtorrent support are pulled in as submodules in the repository. webtorrent also adds a new dependency on boost-json.
> 
> Note that the webtorrent support significantly widens the attack surface of libtorrent, if you don't need this feature, it's probably best disabled (webtorrent=off / -Dwebtorrent=OFF)
> 
> ## pread_disk_io
> 
> A new disk I/O backend that uses pwritev and preadv (and windows counterparts). This is hopefully addressing the misstep of transitioning all disk I/O over to memory mapped files. The mmap disk backend is still available and is probably more efficient for local NVMe drives. But for spinning disks, network mounts or FUSE drives, regular I/O calls should be a lot more efficient. pread_disk_io is now the default.
> 
> One of the main challenges with the new disk I/O has been to get the multi-threading right. It computes piece hashes on dedicated threads, separate from those making the I/O calls. This lets us advertise and upload pieces before they're flushed to disk, maintaining high throughput.
> 
> Other highlights are:
> 
> * add max_directory_depth limit to load_torrent_limits to bound file path depth when loading torrents
> * fix race in wait_for_alert(), and update its return value
> * optimize torrent_handle::torrent_file()
> * add option to not validate v1 hashes for hybrid torrents
> * add post_file_status() to query them asynchronously
> * add post_file_priorities() to query them asynchronously
> * fix local service discovery not being correctly staggered
> * make the save path for part files configurable
> * retry failed SAM connection (for i2p)
> * deprecated remap_files(), and prevent it from breaking v2 torrents
> * fix peer_info holding an i2p destination
> * implement i2p_pex, peer exchange support for i2p torrents
> * deprecate torrent_alert::torrent_name()
> * requires OpenSSL minimum version 1.1.0 with SNI support
> * try harder to bind TCP and UDP sockets to the same port
> * made disk_interface's status_t type a flags type
> * optimize resume data format to use less space
> * add a simpler overload to bencode() returning a vector<char>
> * introduced a new API for creating torrents, enabling file_storage optimizations
> * default build to not include functions deprecated in libtorrent 1.1 and earlier
> * add comment, created_by and creation_date to add_torrent_params
> * move session_flags to session_params
> * the entry class is now a standard variant type
> * use std::string_view instead of boost counterpart
> * libtorrent now requires C++17 to build
> * removed support for BEP 17 web seeds (in favor of BEP 19)
> * fix bug where torrent_status::total was not set for seeds
> 
> ## full commit log
> * bump C++ version to 17 by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/4167
> * Use time_duration instead of int for predictive pieces by @vktr in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/4707
> * remove some noexcept-movable hacks that are no longer necessary by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/4708
> * [clang-tidy] use bool literals by @neheb in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/4757

- 6683f95153134a9cb93c1b7c3bdd05020d7efbf1 — https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/commit/6683f95153134a9cb93c1b7c3bdd05020d7efbf1
> Add Linux CA certificate probing in start_session()
> 
> On macOS, start_session() already probes /etc/ssl/cert.pem and
> /etc/ssl/certs for CA certificates. On Linux, only
> set_default_verify_paths() was called, which relies on OpenSSL's
> compiled-in OPENSSLDIR. When OpenSSL is statically linked or
> cross-compiled, OPENSSLDIR often points to a non-existent build-time
> path, leaving the SSL context with no trusted CAs.
> 
> Add a Linux-specific block that probes the standard CA bundle files:
> 
>   /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt  (Debian, Ubuntu, Alpine, openSUSE)
>   /etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt    (RHEL, Fedora, CentOS)
> 
> Mirrors the existing macOS probing pattern — all errors are logged
> and cleared, no-op when paths don't exist.

> 
> * Stop calling `is_i2p_url` so often by caching its value
>

> 
> Routing table nodes can sometimes contain hundreds of nodes, fully sorting them

> 
> This commit changes it to only partition the node list into the best 8 on the

Release notes (texto original):

> Changelog 2.0.14
> 
> * fix issue in merkle tree
> * fix use of a stack buffer past its lifetime when sending i2p SAM commands
> * fix issues with active_time, seeding_time and finished_time
> * fix torrent updates for idle torrents
> * improve dont-count-slow-torrents
> * fix external_ip_alert not being posted under some conditions when UPnP/NAT-PMP is enabled
> * fix issue with stuck trackers on session pause
> * fix windows disk read, possibly causing short-read errors
> * fix blocking UDP socket in LSD and NAT-PMP
> * fix web seed requests for single-file torrents in multi-file mode
> * fix duplicate filenames in magnet links
> * fix blocking UDP socket in UPnP
> * fix corruption bug in mmap_storage
> * fix bug where torrent_status::total was not set for seeds
> 
> ## What's Changed
> * harden merkle_tree proof validation by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8466
> * Fix web seed Host header ports by @hussainarslan in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8460
> * use the new host_header functions in more places by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8471
> * Add Linux CA certificate probing in start_session() by @trim21 in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8488
> * torrent_status::total by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8524
> * fix use-after-free in uTP failure socket shutdown path by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8528
> * fix incorrect hint in mmap_storage::write that could cause corruption by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8542
> * disk_write_mode setting by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8546
> * fix blocking UDP socket in UPnP by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8555
> * backport: fix duplicate filenames in magnet links by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8556
> * fix web seed requests for single-file torrents in multi-file mode by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8559
> * fix integer overflow in download_queue_time() by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8560
> * non-blocking UDP socket in LSD and NAT-PMP by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8566
> * persist BEP-21 upload_only on peer_list entry (RC_2_0) by @reardonia in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8557
> * Optimize CPU usage in the DH key exchange hot path by @anthonyryan1 in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8565
> * back-port want_peers_finished() invariant check failure by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8575
> * fix mistake in workflows syntax by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8577
> * handle ReadFile() returning a short read, by retrying by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8597
> * fix undefined std::toupper on signed char in base32decode by @isl-Ramzi in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8600
> * Abort trackers 2.0 by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8604
> * fix out of bounds read in from_hex on odd number of digits by @isl-Ramzi in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8611
> * fix external_ip_alert not being posted when UPnP/NAT-PMP succeeds by @rts-kotori in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8607
> * inactive torrent fix, back-port by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8617
> * don't report a utf8 sequence length longer than the input by @isl-Ramzi in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8618
> * fix torrent updates for idle torrents by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8620
> * Fix empty tracker tiers are incorrectly saved by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8625
> * factor out fragile logic to track active, seeding and finished time by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8623
> * fix out of bounds write in hashes_rejected on block hash requests by @isl-Ramzi in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8630
> * reject all-zero node hashes in merkle_validate_and_insert_proofs by @isl-Ramzi in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8635
> * back-port: don't hand a stack buffer to async_write in i2p_stream by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8641
> * back-port Fix wrapped packet buffer range checks by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8661
> * back-port web seed chunk size check by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8672
> * bump 2.0.14 version by @arvidn in https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/pull/8684

### Releases sorteadas

#### 1. v1.10.0 / v1.10.0

item_id: bisq-network/bisq::release::323553144
Data: 2026-07-31T15:28:20Z
URL: https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/releases/tag/v1.10.0

Release notes (texto original):

> Bisq 1.10.0 follows the recent security incident with a focused hardening release that improves trade protocol security, network message validation, release verification, and hardening against supply chain attacks.
> 
> A detailed post-mortem covering the incident, investigation, impact assessment, and the security improvements introduced with this release will be published in the coming days on the Bisq webpage.
> 
> Note: As this release adds support for both Intel and Apple Silicon macOS binaries, the in-app download for macOS binaries will not work for this release. Please download, install, and verify the macOS binaries manually.
> 
> 
> ## Release notes
> 
> ### Security Improvements
> 
> - Hardened validation of trade protocol messages, deposit transactions, payout transactions, trade contract data, and peer-provided wallet data.
> - Improved protection against supply chain attacks by adding PGP signature verification to dependency resolution.
> - Updated Java, JavaFX, Tor, bitcoinj, and other dependencies to their latest stable versions.
> - Improved the build process with additional verification of the build toolchain.
> - Added Docker-based DAO and end-to-end trade tests to GitHub Actions. This work will continue over the coming weeks.
> 
> ### Security Improvements Affecting the Trading Experience
> 
> - The maximum trade amount is now limited to `0.125 BTC`.
> - Offers and trades are now restricted to a maximum price deviation of `25%`.
> - Disabled XMR auto-confirmation. No issues have been identified, but a more in-depth security audit is planned for this area.
> - Removed the webcam library used for QR code scanning to reduce security risks. A more secure replacement will be introduced in the next release.
> - Removed dispute chat attachments and dispute log file transfers for security reasons.
> - Added a popup reminder advising users not to use the Bisq wallet as a long-term storage wallet when holding higher balances.
> 
> ### UX
> 
> - Improved performance by updating JavaFX and Java versions.
> 
> ### Network And Runtime
> 
> - The DAO full-node bitcoind RPC layer was migrated for Bitcoin Core 29.2 support, with updated bitcoind targets and reorg-test coverage.
> - Bundled DAO and network resource snapshots were refreshed for the release.
> 
> ### Deployment
> 
> - macOS releases now support both Apple Silicon and Intel-based Macs.
> - The reproducible build system is now partially in place, though not yet applied to this release. The next release will fully benefit from it.
> 
> 
> ## Installation
> 
> ### macOS
> Bisq does not use Apple's notarization process (see [why](https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/discussions/6341)). 
> For that reason you will see that (misleading) alert:
> <img src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e058c34c-38f5-4329-8fc5-f48b3f2ba4dd" width="180"/>
> Grant permissions by: 
> - run `sudo xattr -rd com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Bisq.app` in a terminal (type Terminal in the Apple search box)
> - open `Bisq` again
> 
> More details can be found [here](https://bisq.wiki/Downloading_and_installing#OS-specific_install_notes).
> 
> ### Windows
> For similar reasons you will get that warning at Windows: _**Windows protected your PC**_
> 
> - Click the `More info` button when prompted
> - Click the `Run anyway` button when prompted
> 
> More details can be found [here](https://bisq.wiki/Downloading_and_installing#OS-specific_install_notes).
> 
> ### Verify download
> See the [verification and installation instructions](https://bisq.wiki/Downloading_and_installing) in the Bisq Wiki.
> 
> 
> ### Context to the binary signing process used for that release:
> 
> Alejandro García (key ID E222AA02) built all binaries except the new aarch64 macOS target, as he does not yet have a VM configured for it. Therefore, Henrik Jannsen (key ID 387C8307) provided the aarch64 macOS binary and signed the binaries he received from Alejandro.
> 
> Our in-app verification tool does not currently support mixed keys or signatures. It reads the key ID specified in `signingkey.asc` and applies it uniformly to all binaries. For this reason, Henrik re-signed all binaries using his own key so that the verification process remains consistent and compatible with the current implementation.
> 
> Please note that both Alejandro García and Henrik Jannsen are official release managers for Bisq 1 and Bisq 2. Their public keys have been included in the source code for a long time and are distributed with the application to enable independent key verification and cross-checking.
> 
> The partial_signatures_by_E222AA02.zip contains the original signatures provided by Alejandro. User can use those to verify using  key E222AA02.
> 
> Relevant references:
> 
> * `github.com/bisq-network/bisq/tree/master/desktop/src/main/resources/keys`
> * `https://bisq.network/pubkey/E222AA02.asc`
> * `https://bisq.network/pubkey/387C8307.asc`
> 
> The release process will be further improved in the next version through the introduction of reproducible builds.
>

> Verify the release build runtime
> 
> Add pinned release Java and Gradle versions to `gradle.properties` and a
> `verifyReleaseEnvironment` task that fails when a release verification is run
> with a different Gradle or Java runtime.
> 
> Wire the environment check into `verifyReleaseBuild` and `verifyReleaseManifest`
> so both the CI evidence build and local manifest comparison use the same runtime
> policy. Include the expected values in `build-info.json`.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> ./gradlew verifyReleaseEnvironment
> ./gradlew clean verifyReleaseBuild
> ./gradlew verifyReleaseManifest -PreleaseManifest=/path/to/release-manifest.tsv
> git diff --check
> ```
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenrikJannsen <boilingfrog@gmx.com>
- 0451a927199fa94ddd723bb359924c00bff5e754 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/0451a927199fa94ddd723bb359924c00bff5e754
> Pin release-builder apt snapshot
> 
> Pin the Linux release-builder Dockerfile package installation to a reviewed
> Ubuntu apt snapshot with `UBUNTU_APT_SNAPSHOT`. The image already pins the Azul
> Zulu base image by digest; this also freezes Ubuntu package repository
> resolution for the Linux builder and documents how to test a newer snapshot
> before changing the default.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> docker build --pull=false -t bisq-release-builder-linux:java-21.0.6 docker/release-builder/linux
> docker build --pull=false \
>   --build-arg UBUNTU_APT_SNAPSHOT=20260501T000000Z \
>   -t bisq-release-builder-linux:java-21.0.6 \
>   docker/release-builder/linux
> ./gradlew help --task verifyReleaseBuild --stacktrace
> git diff --check
> ```
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenrikJannsen <boilingfrog@gmx.com>

> Restore JFXProgressBarSkin shadow class
>

> 
> Commit 56e7d68973 added a local override at the same fully-qualified name to shadow the broken class on the classpath. Commit a16fdc4735 ("Remove unused class") later deleted it - it had no Java references but was load-bearing because it shadows a third-party class.

> fix(offer): address review issues from #7636 max price deviation enforcement
> 
> - OpenOfferManager: replace one-shot 30s timer with priceFeed-update listener
>   so newly-arrived market prices for offers in untocked currencies are still
>   evaluated and reported to the user. Listener auto-deregisters once every
>   open offer has been evaluated. Fix field name typo Time -> Timer.
> - OfferBook: stop self-removing the price feed listener; re-prune on every
>   tick so feed recovery and late-arriving currency prices are honoured. Log
>   removed-offer count instead of full toString of the list.
> - OfferValidation: drop exception-as-control-flow on the hot path. Internal
>   helper returns a nullable error string; isPriceInBounds returns false on
>   null inputs instead of warn-logging an NPE. verifyPriceDeviation no longer
>   eagerly formats the error string when the check passes.
> - PreferencesPayload: log a warning when a persisted maxPriceDistanceInPercent
>   is clamped on load so silent migration from the old 0.3 default to 0.25 is
>   observable in logs.
> - TradeManager: drop the @Getter on priceFeedService that was added solely to
>   feed MakerProcessesInputsForDepositTxRequest. Pass the dep through the trade
>   Provider/ProcessModel instead, matching the pattern used for every other
>   task-side service.
> - TradePriceValidation: document that the 1.5 multiplier resolves to an
>   absolute deviation of 37.5%.
> - handleOfferAvailabilityRequest: comment that narrowing Throwable -> Exception
>   is intentional so JVM Errors propagate rather than being downgraded to a
>   PRICE_CHECK_FAILED.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

- 15f1b1155a824d222608d81e720edebb3d0b486c — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/15f1b1155a824d222608d81e720edebb3d0b486c
> Bound taker-supplied trade tx fee
> 
> The taker-supplied txFee in InputsForDepositTxRequest was only checked
> > 0. A malicious taker could pick a value too low (deposit tx never
> confirms, locking maker funds) or too high (excess miner-fee burn).
> 
> Add an absolute-sat envelope of 100..600000 sat as a sanity floor and
> ceiling against absurd values. Applied in two places:
> 
>   - TradeValidation.checkTradeTxFee(Coin/long), so every caller of the
>     central validation helper (including Trade.setTradeTxFee and the
>     tolerance checks invoked from checkInputsForDepositTxRequest) gets
>     bounds enforcement for free.
>   - InputsForDepositTxRequest.validate(), the message-level integrity
>     check that runs at deserialisation before any trade context is
>     available.
> 
> The tighter check against the local fee estimate
> (checkTradeTxFeeIsInTolerance) remains the primary defence; these bounds
> are a defence-in-depth backstop for callers without a FeeService and for
> cases where the fee estimate itself could be skewed.
> 
> Tests added in TradeValidationTest and BisqV1MessageIntegrityTest cover
> the new boundary, below-min, and above-max cases.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash

> The first command should return no floating runner or Java major-version
> entries. The second command lists the pinned runner and Java settings for
> review.

> Verify Gradle wrapper inputs
> 
> Add a checked-in `gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.sha256` manifest for the Gradle
> wrapper scripts, wrapper jar, and wrapper properties file.
> 
> Add `verifyGradleWrapperSecurity` to verify those hashes and require the wrapper
> distribution URL plus `distributionSha256Sum` to stay pinned.
> 
> Run the checksum manifest directly in GitHub Actions before Gradle starts, then
> run the Gradle task during the normal build. Pin `gradlew` and
> `gradle-wrapper.properties` line endings so the wrapper checksums are stable
> across OS checkouts.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> ./gradlew verifyGradleWrapperSecurity
> shasum -a 256 -c gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.sha256
> git diff --check
> ```
> 
> When upgrading Gradle, regenerate the wrapper, review the changed wrapper files,
> update `gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.sha256`, and run the verification commands
> again.
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenrikJannsen <boilingfrog@gmx.com>

> Record precise Debian tar metadata
> 
> Make Debian installer structure reports use GNU tar's full timestamp and
> numeric ownership output when listing the inner `control.tar` and `data.tar`
> archives. This keeps the existing diagnostic-only flow while making timestamp,
> owner, group, mode, and ordering differences easier to compare across `.deb`
> rebuilds.
> 
> Document that Debian structure reports include full timestamps and numeric
> ownership when GNU tar is available.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> ./gradlew help --task generateInstallerStructureReport --stacktrace
> ./gradlew generateInstallerStructureReport --stacktrace
> ./gradlew generateInstallerEvidenceBundle --stacktrace
> git diff --check
> ```
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenrikJannsen <boilingfrog@gmx.com>

> Fix Linux installer evidence bundle validation
> 
> Coerce generated installer-structure ZIP entry names to plain strings before
> comparing TreeSets, avoiding a Groovy GString cast failure seen on Linux
> installer evidence with multiple structure reports.

> --version flag.

> 
> ```bash
> ./gradlew help --task generateInstallerEvidenceBundle --stacktrace
> git diff --check

> Trust Gradle source distribution signature
> 
> Allow Gradle dependency verification to accept the Gradle 8.9 source
> distribution requested during IDE sync.
> 
> The artifact `gradle:gradle:8.9` / `gradle-8.9-src.zip` was already pinned by
> SHA-256 in `gradle/verification-metadata.xml`, and the cached file matches the
> official Gradle distribution checksum:
> 
> ```text
> cfeccc3375aa0ea1b7838361ec9acdb291bd36dd10c46ea0777c8508a40684ae
> ```
> 
> The sync failure was caused by the artifact's detached signature being made by
> Gradle Inc.'s key `1BD97A6A154E7810EE0BC832E2F38302C8075E3D`, while that key
> was only trusted for `org.gradle.kotlin:gradle-kotlin-dsl-plugins:4.4.0`.
> 
> Scope the same key to `gradle:gradle:8.9` and record the PGP signer on the
> `gradle-8.9-src.zip` artifact.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> ./gradlew resolveAndVerifyDependencies
> ```
> 
> The task should report:
> 
> ```text
> Resolved and verified 169 configurations.
> ```
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenrikJannsen <boilingfrog@gmx.com>

> Bound peer input count, parentTransaction size, and dedup outpoints
> 
> A peer can supply a large parentTransaction byte blob and duplicate
> outpoints in their RawTransactionInput list. The previous validator
> caught the financial-equality requirement but did not bound memory
> or detect duplicates explicitly.
> 
> In DepositTxValidation.validatePeersInputs / getValidatedInputValue:
> - cap input count at 100;
> - cap parentTransaction length at 100 KiB;
> - dedup by outpoint string and reject duplicates.
> 
> Addresses risk #11 in /findings/07_risks_ranked.md.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

> Document reproducible release verification
> 
> Add a reproducible release build guide that explains the current Java payload
> verification scope, release-manager workflow, CI manifest comparison, signing
> recommendation, independent verifier workflow, and remaining gaps.
> 
> Link the guide from the developer docs index and the release process checklist so
> the release manager has one canonical place for the new reproducible-build
> checks.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> git submodule update --init --recursive
> shasum -a 256 -c gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.sha256
> ./gradlew clean build verifyGradleWrapperSecurity verifyGithubActionsSecurity verifyDependencySignaturePolicy verifyReproducibleArchives generateReleaseManifest
> ./gradlew verifyReleaseManifest -PreleaseManifest=/path/to/release-manifest.tsv
> git diff --check
> ```

> Enforce price to be inside the max price bounds of 25%.
> 
> Makers offers which are outside the boundary will trigger a popup to tell the user to edit the offer to adjust the price.
> 
> Offers in offerbook outside the boundary will get filtered out.
> 
> At take offer requests and at trade we fail if the offers price is outside of boundary.
> 
> We apply different tolerance levels depending on the use case.
> Trade: 50%
> My offers: 0%
> Accept take offer: 10 %
> Filter offers: 5 %
> Added offers: 10%
> 
> Those tolerance level should avoid that market price fluctuations have too much impact on the boundary calculation.

> Add e2e DAO + trade test suite running in Docker via GitHub Actions
> 
> Introduces a headless Dao gRPC service (passthrough to DaoFacade) covering
> every proposal type, vote action, blind-vote, reveal, and result inspection,
> plus a getRawTransaction helper that lets tests deterministically inject
> Bisq-broadcast txs into bitcoind's mempool. Phase advancement is driven by
> bitcoin-cli generatetoaddress, so the suite has no wall-clock dependence.
> 
> The new apitest package bisq.apitest.dao exercises proposal/blind-vote/
> reveal/result phases, full multi-cycle scenarios, vote edge cases (quorum,
> tie, no-vote, all-ignore, single-voter), and v1 BTC + BSQ-swap trade flows
> with balance-delta assertions. End-to-end governance loop (propose →
> vote → result → param flip) is verified via getDaoParamValue.
> 
> Stack is 5 containers (bitcoind + seednode + arb + alice + bob) on a
> docker-compose bridge network. LocalhostNetworkNode now honours
> BISQ_P2P_LOCALHOST_NAME so each daemon announces a peer-resolvable
> hostname instead of the hardcoded "localhost".
> 
> Workflow .github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml runs the suite on PRs touching
> core/daemon/cli/proto/apitest/seednode, with Gradle + Docker buildx layer
> caches for ~3 min hot-run CI time. Pre-existing apitest tests remain
> @Disabled and are unaffected.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

- 4690a9f5ade798322b5072f08e34d950ef9ed2f3 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/4690a9f5ade798322b5072f08e34d950ef9ed2f3
> # macOS Dual Architecture Support
> 
> ## Scope
> 
> Bisq now needs separate macOS installer artifacts for Intel and Apple Silicon.
> The app update downloader, macOS packaging output, and release finalization flow
> were still assuming a single macOS DMG named `Bisq-<version>.dmg`.
> 
> ## Changes Applied
> 
> - Updated the in-app installer descriptor to select a macOS DMG by runtime
>   architecture:
>   - Intel: `Bisq-x86_64-<version>.dmg`
>   - Apple Silicon: `Bisq-aarch64-<version>.dmg`
> - Added focused tests for macOS updater filename selection using common JVM
>   architecture strings: `x86_64`, `amd64`, `aarch64`, and `arm64`.
> - Updated Gradle packaging so a macOS `generateInstallers` run renames the
>   generated DMG to the same architecture-qualified filename that the app
>   downloader expects.
> - Updated the macOS library hash filename and hash content label to include the
>   macOS architecture, preventing Intel and Apple Silicon builds from producing
>   colliding `desktop-<version>-all-mac.jar.SHA-256` files.
> - Updated `desktop/package/macosx/finalize.sh` to copy, sign, verify, and
>   include both macOS DMGs and both macOS library hash files.
> 
> ## Release Inputs Expected By `finalize.sh`
> 
> - Intel macOS build directory:
>   - Defaults to `$BISQ_VM_PATH/vm_shared_macosx`
>   - Can be overridden with `BISQ_MACOS_X86_64_PATH`
>   - Must contain `Bisq-x86_64-<version>.dmg`
>   - Must contain `desktop-<version>-all-mac-x86_64.jar.SHA-256`
> - Apple Silicon macOS build directory:
>   - Defaults to `$BISQ_VM_PATH/vm_shared_macosx_aarch64`
>   - Can be overridden with `BISQ_MACOS_AARCH64_PATH`
>   - Must contain `Bisq-aarch64-<version>.dmg`
>   - Must contain `desktop-<version>-all-mac-aarch64.jar.SHA-256`
> 
> ## x86 Test Plan
> 
> Run this on the Intel macOS machine:
> 
> ```sh
> ./gradlew :desktop:generateInstallers
> ```
> 
> Expected artifacts:
> 
> ```text
> desktop/build/packaging/jpackage/packages/Bisq-x86_64-1.10.0.dmg
> desktop/build/packaging/jpackage/packages/desktop-1.10.0-all-mac-x86_64.jar.SHA-256
> ```
> 
> Then install and launch the DMG on the Intel machine. After the Apple Silicon
> DMG is also available, run `desktop/package/macosx/finalize.sh` with both macOS
> build directories available and verify that the release folder contains both
> macOS DMGs and `.asc` signatures.
> 
> ## Notes
> 
> - No Rosetta-dependent test was added or run. The Intel build path should be
>   validated on the separate x86 machine.
> - Reproducible-build comparison logic was not expanded beyond accepting the
>   generated installer filenames; the core reproducible-build workflow was left
>   unchanged.
> 
> ## Verification Performed
> 
> On the Apple Silicon machine:
> 
> ```sh
> bash -n desktop/package/macosx/finalize.sh
> ./gradlew :desktop:test --tests bisq.desktop.main.overlays.windows.downloadupdate.BisqInstallerTest
> ./gradlew :desktop:generateHashes
> ./gradlew :desktop:generateInstallers
> ```
> 
> The focused test passed, packaging build logic compiled, and
> `:desktop:generateHashes` produced:
> 
> ```text
> desktop/build/packaging/jpackage/packages/desktop-1.10.0-all-mac-aarch64.jar.SHA-256
> ```
> 
> The generated hash file uses `macOS-aarch64` as its entry prefix.
> `:desktop:generateInstallers` also completed successfully and produced:
> 
> ```text
> desktop/build/packaging/jpackage/packages/Bisq-aarch64-1.10.0.dmg
> ```
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenrikJannsen <boilingfrog@gmx.com>

> Verify GitHub Actions workflow hardening
> 
> Add a root `verifyGithubActionsSecurity` task that scans GitHub Actions
> workflow files and fails if they reintroduce common CI supply-chain drift.
> 
> The task checks for:
> 
> - action references that are not pinned to full 40-character commit SHAs
> - floating `ubuntu-latest`, `macos-latest`, or `windows-latest` runner labels
> - floating Java major versions such as `java-version: 21`
> - `check-latest: true`
> 
> Wire the task into the main GitHub build workflow so PR CI enforces the policy
> before publishing release-manifest artifacts.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> ./gradlew verifyGithubActionsSecurity
> rg -n "uses:.*@[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$|uses:.*@v[0-9]|ubuntu-latest|macOS-latest|macos-latest|windows-latest|java-version: '21'|java: \\[ '21' \\]" .github/workflows
> git diff --check
> ```
> 
> The Gradle task should report:
> 
> ```text
> Verified 3 GitHub Actions workflow files.
> ```
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenrikJannsen <boilingfrog@gmx.com>

> Add missing P2WSH witness validation for DPT
> 
> Prevent the peer from rendering the DPT invalid by supplying a bogus MS
> signature, since it turns out that bitcoinj 'Script::correctlySpends'
> only provides partial validation for segwit. Specifically, only P2WPKH
> signatures are checked and P2WSH witnesses aren't checked at all. This
> makes it necessary to check the buyer and seller signatures manually
> against their respective pubkeys and the DPT input sighash.
> 
> Also canonicalise the signatures (that is, force them to be low-S) prior
> to the check, to ensure that the finalised DPT will actually be standard
> and not merely valid at the consensus level.

> Verify encrypted message sender addresses at network layer
> 
> Introduce SendersNodeAddressAwarePayload for encrypted payloads that already
> carry a sender node address, and apply it to TradeMessage and MailboxMessage.
> 
> Validate sender consistency before dispatching encrypted direct messages:
> the decrypted payload sender must match the PrefixedSealedAndSignedMessage
> sender, and the outer sender must match the connection peer address. Also
> reject outbound encrypted direct and mailbox messages before encryption if
> their payload sender does not match the local node address.
> 
> Move mailbox decrypted payload validation into MailboxItem so persisted
> mailbox entries are checked as well. Invalid decrypted entries are dropped if
> the payload is not a MailboxMessage or if its sender address does not match
> the enclosing mailbox envelope.
> 
> Add focused tests for direct encrypted receive/send validation, sender-aware
> payload helper behavior, mailbox outbound rejection, and persisted mailbox
> item validation.
> 
> Motivation: prevent peers from mixing inconsistent sender identities across
> the connection, outer encrypted envelope, and decrypted payload layers. This
> hardens messages that already include sender addresses without requiring any
> protobuf schema changes.

- 4d57133fea30b4ce905bbfb42d02f90a9ac49a3d — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/4d57133fea30b4ce905bbfb42d02f90a9ac49a3d
> Reject legacy UTXOs at deposit funding to prevent mid-trade abort
> 
> PR #7655 added checkTransactionIsUnsigned which rejects any input with a
> non-empty scriptSig or witness. The buyer-side deposit-tx flows witness-strip
> via bitcoinSerialize(false) before sending to the peer, but do not strip
> scriptSig. For legacy P2PK/P2PKH inputs the scriptSig persists after
> witness-strip, so the peer's validator rejects the deposit tx mid-protocol
> after funds may already be locked.
> 
> Add WalletService.assertAllInputsSpendP2WPKH and call it at the local
> funding step in TradeWalletService (takerCreatesDepositTxInputs and
> makerCreatesDepositTx). Users with legacy UTXOs now see a clear error
> before any peer messaging starts, instead of aborting mid-trade.
> 
> Also document that checkDerEncodedEcdsaSignature expects raw DER without
> a trailing sighash byte, and add a verify() test for duplicate outpoints.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

> the allowlist as `<group:name:version>\t<artifact-file-name>\t<review-rationale>`
> and fails when an entry is malformed, duplicated, missing, or stale.

> Add rationales for the existing checksum-only artifacts, include those
> rationales in the generated dependency signature report, and document the
> allowlist format in the Gradle and reproducible release build docs.
> 
> Usage:

> ./gradlew verifyDependencySignaturePolicy --stacktrace

> git diff --check

> Remove dead legacy P2SH branches in payout signing
> 
> Deposit outputs have been P2WSH-only since v1.5.0 and PR #7676 made
> get2of2MultiSigOutputScript unconditionally P2WSH. The new defense
> gate verifyDepositTxMultiSigOutput rejects any deposit whose output[0]
> is not the agreed P2WSH script, so the legacy P2SH branches in
> payout signing were unreachable.
> 
> Cleanup:
> - buyerSignsPayoutTx, sellerSignsAndFinalizesPayoutTx,
>   signMediatedPayoutTx, finalizeMediatedPayoutTx: drop the
>   isP2SH sigHash branch and the createP2SHMultiSigInputScript
>   scriptSig branch. Witness-only paths remain.
> - traderSignAndFinalizeDisputedPayoutTx and get2of3MultiSigRedeemScript:
>   removed. Only caller was the legacy-arbitrator dispute publishing
>   branch in ArbitrationManager, which has been broken since v1.5.0
>   due to inverted isP2SH polarity.
> - ArbitrationManager: legacy-arbitrator publishing branch replaced
>   with a graceful warn-and-close. Unused imports and catch blocks
>   removed.
> 
> Emergency support tools (BuildPane / SignPane) keep the legacy flag;
> they are user-driven recovery tools outside the protocol path.

> Add cold storage reminder popup for high wallet balances
> 
> Warns users holding more than 0.5 BTC in their Bisq wallet to treat it
> as a hot wallet and move idle funds to cold storage. Threshold and
> cooldown are constants in WalletColdStorageReminder for easy tuning.
> 
> Triggers:
> - On every app launch (after splash) when total wallet balance exceeds
>   the threshold.
> - On every navigation event, throttled by a 6-hour cooldown.
> 
> This is intentionally persistent until the user reduces the on-wallet
> balance, given the elevated risk of a future Bisq-side zero-day.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
- 5cddcae77e8dc2d213246044b942c0362b669414 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/5cddcae77e8dc2d213246044b942c0362b669414
> Drop asymmetric return values from mediated payout validation
> 
> `checkMediatedPayoutAmounts` returned the buyer amount and
> `checkMediatedPayoutAddresses` returned the buyer address; callers stored
> them as `validatedBuyer...` and passed them downstream instead of the raw
> inputs. The returned value is always equal to the input (the helpers
> either throw or pass through), so the wrapping suggested an asymmetric
> "more validated" treatment of buyer vs. seller that did not exist.
> 
> Make both helpers return void and update all callers to use the original
> inputs. No behavior change.
>

> Add release payload manifests and verification
> 
> Add root release-manifest tasks for the Java payload used by the desktop
> binary build.
> 
> `generateReleaseManifest` builds the project JARs and desktop
> `installDist/lib` payload, then writes:
> 
> - `build/reports/release/SHA256SUMS`
> - `build/reports/release/release-manifest.tsv`
> - `build/reports/release/build-info.json`
> 
> `verifyReleaseManifest` rebuilds the local payload manifest and compares it
> against a previously generated `release-manifest.tsv`, failing on missing,
> extra, or changed files.
> 
> `build-info.json` records the manifest checksum, Git commit/submodule state,
> Gradle wrapper details, Java runtime, OS, `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, and Gradle
> invocation context so release managers and CI can publish comparable build
> metadata.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> ./gradlew generateReleaseManifest
> shasum -a 256 -c build/reports/release/SHA256SUMS
> ./gradlew verifyReleaseManifest -PreleaseManifest=/path/to/release-manifest.tsv
> ```
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenrikJannsen <boilingfrog@gmx.com>

> Add Linux release-builder image definition
> 
> Add a Linux release-builder Dockerfile for independent Java payload
> verification. The image uses the linux/amd64 Azul Zulu OpenJDK 21.0.6 base
> image pinned by digest, sets release-sensitive defaults for
> `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, timezone, and locale, and installs the Linux package tools
> needed for payload verification and installer investigation.
> 
> Document how to build and run the container without wiring installer generation
> into CI, and keep package repository snapshot pinning listed as a remaining
> hardening step.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> docker build --pull=false -t bisq-release-builder-linux:java-21.0.6 docker/release-builder/linux
> docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 \
>   --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
>   -v "$PWD:/workspace" \
>   -w /workspace \

> Verify release-builder image definition
> 
> Add `verifyReleaseBuilderImage` to check that the Linux release-builder
> Dockerfile keeps its base image pinned by linux/amd64 digest, uses an exact apt
> snapshot argument, preserves release-sensitive environment defaults, installs
> the expected package/archive tools, avoids apt upgrades, and keeps its default
> command on `verifyReleaseBuild`.
> 
> Wire the new verifier into `verifyReleaseBuild` so CI and local release checks
> fail quickly if the release-builder definition drifts. Document the verifier in
> the reproducible release build guide.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> ./gradlew verifyReleaseBuilderImage --stacktrace
> ./gradlew verifyReleaseBuild --dry-run --stacktrace
> git diff --check
> ```
>

> Harden BSQ swap fee/payout arithmetic
> 
> Fail fast on malformed BSQ swap arithmetic before wallet commits inputs:
> 
> - getAdjustedTxFee: use Math.multiplyExact and assert non-negative result.
>   Negative adjusted fee inverts buyer BTC payout, producing tx with
>   outputs > inputs. Add lenient variant for UI estimation paths
>   (BsqSwapOfferModel) so display still works when wallet is underfunded.
> - ProcessTxInputsMessage: reject seller BSQ payout that is non-positive
>   or below dust. Sub-dust output is non-standard; without the guard the
>   seller commits BSQ inputs to a tx miners will drop.

- 7c5bd333555642698bf9e9f97e51b0ecdd33dd54 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/7c5bd333555642698bf9e9f97e51b0ecdd33dd54
> Verify encrypted message sender addresses at network layer
> 
> Introduce SendersNodeAddressAwarePayload for encrypted payloads that already
> carry a sender node address, and apply it to TradeMessage and MailboxMessage.
> 
> Validate sender consistency before dispatching encrypted direct messages:
> the decrypted payload sender must match the PrefixedSealedAndSignedMessage
> sender, and the outer sender must match the connection peer address. Also
> reject outbound encrypted direct and mailbox messages before encryption if
> their payload sender does not match the local node address.
> 
> Move mailbox decrypted payload validation into MailboxItem so persisted
> mailbox entries are checked as well. Invalid decrypted entries are dropped if
> the payload is not a MailboxMessage or if its sender address does not match
> the enclosing mailbox envelope.
> 
> Add focused tests for direct encrypted receive/send validation, sender-aware
> payload helper behavior, mailbox outbound rejection, and persisted mailbox
> item validation.
> 
> Motivation: prevent peers from mixing inconsistent sender identities across
> the connection, outer encrypted envelope, and decrypted payload layers. This
> hardens messages that already include sender addresses without requiring any
> protobuf schema changes.

> Add Gradle dependency signature verification report
> 
>  Enable Gradle dependency signature verification with an armored
>  verification keyring, add tasks to resolve/verify dependencies, refresh
>  the keyring from key servers, and generate a dependency signature report.
> 
>  The report lists signed vs checksum-only artifacts, signer key metadata,
>  and how direct/transitive dependencies are handled. Check in the armored
>  public keyring for deterministic verification and ignore the binary GPG
>  keyring format.
> 
>  Usage:
>  - ./gradlew resolveAndVerifyDependencies
>  - ./gradlew resolveAndVerifyDependencies --write-verification-metadata pgp,sha256
>  - ./gradlew refreshDependencyVerificationKeyring
>  - ./gradlew dependencySignatureReport
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenrikJannsen <boilingfrog@gmx.com>

> Add installer evidence bundle task
> 
> Add `generateInstallerEvidenceBundle` to package installer evidence into a
> separate reproducible ZIP for signing and publishing. The task depends on
> `generateInstallerManifest`, includes `installer-manifest.tsv` and
> `INSTALLER-SHA256SUMS`, and keeps installer evidence separate from the Java
> payload release evidence bundle.
> 
> Document the new installer evidence bundle workflow and signature verification
> without wiring installer generation into `verifyReleaseBuild` or CI.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> ./gradlew help --task generateInstallerEvidenceBundle --stacktrace
> ./gradlew generateInstallerEvidenceBundle --dry-run --stacktrace
> git diff --check
> ```
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenrikJannsen <boilingfrog@gmx.com>

> Record Windows MSI properties
> 
> Add optional MSI Property table diagnostics to Windows installer structure
> reports. The PowerShell inspector now records sorted `Property=Value` entries
> for `.msi` artifacts when the Windows Installer COM API can read the package,
> alongside the existing file metadata, version info, and Authenticode evidence.
> 
> Keep the MSI table read optional so the structure report still succeeds when
> the COM API is unavailable or a package cannot be opened for inspection.
> Document the new MSI Property table evidence in the reproducible release guide.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> ./gradlew help --task generateInstallerStructureReport --stacktrace
> ./gradlew generateInstallerEvidenceBundle --stacktrace
> git diff --check
> ```
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenrikJannsen <boilingfrog@gmx.com>

> Record Windows PE header metadata
> 
> Add optional PE/COFF header diagnostics to Windows `.exe` installer structure
> reports. The PowerShell inspector reads the PE header offset, signature,
> machine, section count, raw TimeDateStamp, UTC TimeDateStamp, optional header
> size, and characteristics so timestamp-related Windows installer drift is easier
> to identify.
> 
> Keep the PE header read optional so non-PE or unreadable artifacts do not fail
> otherwise valid structure evidence. Document the new `.exe` PE/COFF timestamp
> metadata in the reproducible release guide.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> ./gradlew help --task generateInstallerStructureReport --stacktrace
> ./gradlew generateInstallerEvidenceBundle --stacktrace
> git diff --check
> ```
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenrikJannsen <boilingfrog@gmx.com>

> Add aggregate release verification task
> 
> Add a root `verifyReleaseBuild` task that runs the Java release payload build,
> wrapper checks, GitHub Actions policy checks, dependency signature policy,
> reproducible archive checks, and release manifest generation.
> 
> Use the aggregate task from GitHub Actions and the reproducible release build
> guide so CI and release managers run the same verification entry point.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> git submodule update --init --recursive
> shasum -a 256 -c gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.sha256
> ./gradlew clean verifyReleaseBuild
> ./gradlew verifyReleaseManifest -PreleaseManifest=/path/to/release-manifest.tsv
> git diff --check
> ```
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenrikJannsen <boilingfrog@gmx.com>

> Re-clamp trade amount against MAX_TRADE_AMOUNT in checkTradeAmount
> 
> The 0.125 BTC cap (TradeLimits.MAX_TRADE_AMOUNT) is enforced at offer
> creation but not at take-offer. Legacy offers persisted with a larger
> amount can still be taken at the old size, defeating the cap.
> 
> Apply the cap in TradeAmountValidation.checkTradeAmount, which is
> invoked by both InputsForDepositTxRequestValidation (taker path via
> TradeManager) and MakerProcessesInputsForDepositTxRequest (maker path),
> covering both sides of the take-offer flow.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

> Avoid eager startBisqApp realization
> 
> Make `AppStartPlugin` configure `startBisqApp` without reading the installed
> application `lib` directory during task creation. The runtime classpath is now
> resolved lazily after `installDist`, and missing `mainClass` or install output
> fails with a clear `GradleException` instead of a null pointer.
> 
> Also change the root release verification task collector so it looks up named
> tasks directly instead of iterating every task in every project, which avoids
> realizing unrelated tasks such as `:apitest:startBisqApp` while building the
> `verifyReleaseBuild` dependency graph.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> ./gradlew :apitest:clean
> ./gradlew :apitest:startBisqApp --dry-run --stacktrace
> ./gradlew verifyReleaseBuild --dry-run --stacktrace
> ./gradlew verifyReleaseBuild
> git diff --check
> ```
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenrikJannsen <boilingfrog@gmx.com>

> 
> Add `hdiutil checksum -type SHA256` output to DMG installer structure reports.
> This records the platform tool's image checksum result alongside `hdiutil
> imageinfo` and `hdiutil verify`, giving macOS installer evidence another
> diagnostic signal without changing generated artifacts.
> 
> Document that DMG reports include `hdiutil` SHA-256 checksum output on macOS.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> ./gradlew help --task generateInstallerStructureReport --stacktrace
> ./gradlew generateInstallerEvidenceBundle --stacktrace
> git diff --check
> ```
>

> Accept evidence ZIPs for manifest verification
> 
> Allow `verifyReleaseManifest` and `verifyInstallerManifest` to accept signed
> evidence ZIP files directly. The manifest resolver now extracts exactly one
> matching manifest from a ZIP into `build/tmp/manifest-inputs` before running the
> existing canonical manifest comparison.
> 
> Document that release and installer verification properties can point to a raw
> manifest, an extracted evidence directory, or the corresponding evidence ZIP.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> ./gradlew help --task verifyReleaseManifest --stacktrace
> ./gradlew help --task verifyInstallerManifest --stacktrace
> ./gradlew generateReleaseEvidenceBundle --stacktrace
> ./gradlew generateInstallerEvidenceBundle --stacktrace
> ./gradlew verifyReleaseManifest -PreleaseManifest=build/reports/release/release-evidence.zip --stacktrace
> ./gradlew verifyInstallerManifest -PinstallerManifest=build/reports/release/installer-evidence.zip --stacktrace
> git diff --check
> ```
>

> Fix follow-ups from #7642 sender pub key verification review
> 
> - BsqSwapRequest: checkNotNull(takerPubKeyRing) in constructor;
>   drop defensive null-guard in getSenderSignaturePubKey to match
>   the InputsForDepositTxRequest convention. Asymmetry was the bug,
>   not the absence of null support: PubKeyRing constructors already
>   enforce non-null signaturePubKey, so the guard was unreachable.
> 
> - SendersNodeAddressProvidingPayload, SendersSignaturePubKeyProvidingPayload:
>   restore @Nullable on isSender*Matching parameters lost during
>   the rename refactor. Behavior unchanged; static-analysis hint
>   preserved.
> 
> - MailboxItem.getValidDecryptedMessageWithPubKey: cast decryptedPayload
>   to MailboxMessage instead of SendersNodeAddressProvidingPayload.
>   Cast safety becomes a compile-time guarantee (MailboxMessage is
>   already verified via instanceof above) rather than relying on
>   the MailboxMessage interface continuing to extend
>   SendersNodeAddressProvidingPayload.
> 
> - P2PService.doSendEncryptedDirectMessage: pass CryptoException to
>   log.error so the stack trace is retained on encryption failure.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

> Add installer structure evidence report
> 
> Add `generateInstallerStructureReport` as an investigation aid for installer
> internals. The task records a canonical TSV summary and writes per-installer
> tool output for supported package formats, using `dpkg-deb`, `rpm`, or
> `hdiutil` when available. Unsupported formats are recorded as skipped instead
> of failing installer evidence generation.
> 
> Include the structure summary and reports in `installer-evidence.zip`, upload
> them from the manual installer evidence workflow, and document how they relate
> to the canonical installer manifest.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> ./gradlew help --task generateInstallerStructureReport --stacktrace
> ./gradlew generateInstallerStructureReport --stacktrace
> ./gradlew generateInstallerEvidenceBundle --dry-run --stacktrace
> ./gradlew generateInstallerEvidenceBundle --stacktrace
> ./gradlew verifyGithubActionsSecurity --stacktrace
> unzip -l build/reports/release/installer-evidence.zip
> git diff --check
> ```
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenrikJannsen <boilingfrog@gmx.com>

> Accept release manifest directories
> 
> Allow `verifyReleaseManifest` to accept either a direct
> `release-manifest.tsv` path or a directory containing exactly one
> `release-manifest.tsv`.
> 
> This lets a release manager point the task at an extracted GitHub Actions
> artifact or release evidence bundle without manually copying the inner manifest
> path. The task fails if the directory contains no manifest or multiple manifests.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> ./gradlew clean verifyReleaseBuild
> ./gradlew verifyReleaseManifest -PreleaseManifest=/path/to/release-manifest.tsv
> ./gradlew verifyReleaseManifest -PreleaseManifest=/path/to/extracted-ci-artifact
> git diff --check
> ```
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenrikJannsen <boilingfrog@gmx.com>

> Check if deposit tx is valid before taker publish the taker fee tx.
> 
> The check at TakerProcessesInputsForDepositTxResponse.java:85 happened before TakerPublishFeeTx, and it only verified “unsigned,” so a bad maker tx could still make the taker publish their fee and then fail later.
> Implemented the early fix:
> •
> Added DepositTxValidation.checkMakersPreparedDepositTx(...) in DepositTxValidation.java.
> •
> Wired it into TakerProcessesInputsForDepositTxResponse.java, before processModel.setPreparedDepositTx(...) and before fee publication.
> •
> Validation now checks canonical tx shape, input count/order/outpoints, maker/taker input amounts, multisig output script and value, maker change output rules, output count, and implied deposit tx fee.
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenrikJannsen <boilingfrog@gmx.com>

> Pin GitHub Actions to commit SHAs
> 
> Pin all GitHub Actions workflow dependencies to immutable full commit SHAs.
> Keep the original action version tags as inline comments so updates remain
> auditable.
> 
> Pinned actions:
> 
> - `actions/checkout` `v6.0.2`
> - `actions/setup-java` `v5.2.0`
> - `gradle/gradle-build-action` `v3.5.0`
> - `actions/upload-artifact` `v4.6.2`
> - `codacy/codacy-coverage-reporter-action` `v1.3.0`
> - `actions/stale` `v10.2.0`
> 
> This avoids mutable tag references in CI, including the release-manifest upload
> path used for reproducible-build verification.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> rg -n "uses:.*@[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$|uses:.*@v[0-9]" .github/workflows
> rg -n "uses:" .github/workflows
> git diff --check
> ```
> 
> The first command should return no unpinned `uses:` entries. The second command
> lists the pinned actions for review.
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenrikJannsen <boilingfrog@gmx.com>

> Document installer structure report statuses
> 
> Explain the `installer-structure-report.tsv` status column so release managers
> and independent verifiers can interpret installer evidence consistently.
> 
> Document that `generated` means required inspectors ran successfully, `failed`
> means a required inspector command failed and the report should be inspected,
> and `skipped` means no required structure inspector is configured for that
> artifact on the current OS. Clarify that skipped structure diagnostics do not
> prevent comparison through the canonical installer manifest.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> git diff -- docs/reproducible-release-builds.md
> git diff --check
> ```
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenrikJannsen <boilingfrog@gmx.com>

> 
> Expand Debian installer structure evidence with listings for the inner

> metadata, package fields, and package payload contents; these additional
> sections make timestamp, ownership, ordering, and mode differences easier to
> inspect when comparing `.deb` builds.
>

> artifacts are unchanged. Document that Debian structure reports include the
> outer archive, package fields, payload listing, and inner control/data archive
> listings.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> ./gradlew help --task generateInstallerStructureReport --stacktrace
> ./gradlew generateInstallerStructureReport --stacktrace

> ```

> Re-verify deposit-tx multisig output in payout-signing tasks
> 
> Defence-in-depth gate at the last step before money moves: every
> payout-signing task now re-derives the agreed 2-of-2 multisig script
> from the trade's pubkey pair and asserts depositTx.output[0] equals it.
> 
> If any upstream regression were ever to leave a tampered
> trade.getDepositTx() in place, this gate stops the local node from
> signing a payout that pays an attacker. Today the gate is redundant
> with the take-offer-time check at TradeWalletService.takerSignsDepositTx
> :551-560, but defence-in-depth at the last gate is the single highest-
> value mitigation against the original drain class.
> 
> Script-only by design: a value-substituted deposit tx would yield a
> sighash valid only for that tx, which has no on-chain prevout to spend,
> so broadcast fails. Redirect-to-attacker (script swap) is the actual
> drain vector this gate blocks.
> 
> Adds public verifyDepositTxMultiSigOutput on TradeWalletService and
> calls it in BuyerSignPayoutTx, SellerSignAndFinalizePayoutTx,
> SignMediatedPayoutTx, FinalizeMediatedPayoutTx.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

> Implements the validation/commit cleanup for Bisq v1 trade-message processing.
> 
> Key changes:
> 
> Kept message validate() methods structural only; no domain validation moved there.
> 
> Reordered maker/taker deposit-input handling so untrusted values are validated first, returned checked values are used, then model fields are committed.
> 
> Added missing validation before commit for DER signatures, delayed-payout/deposit tx matching, payout message peer-address updates, counter-currency tx id/extra-data length rejection, and optional payment-account payload hash checks.
> 
> Prevented the previous behavior where invalid long counter-currency data was silently ignored while the rest of the message still committed.
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenrikJannsen <boilingfrog@gmx.com>

- e741eb046209abd77bd07df87b0f57cc135c48d5 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/e741eb046209abd77bd07df87b0f57cc135c48d5
> Apply CRAI suggestion: check multisig keys decompress without error
> 
> Make sure the peer's multisig key decompresses to a valid curve point,
> and not just that it has the correct length of 33 and a leading byte of
> 0x02 or 0x03 (since only half of such byte arrays are valid compressed
> curve point encodings), in the 'MakerProcessesInputsForDepositTxRequest'
> and 'TakerProcessesInputsForDepositTxResponse' trade tasks.
> 
> This makes their calls to 'ECKey::isPubKeyCanonical' redundant, since it
> was just checking the leading byte, where a full decompression attempt
> should be performed. So remove those method calls.
> 
> (Note that only the length check is actually security-critical, since in
> both cases an invalid compressed pubkey encoding just leads to failure
> later in the round, when the deposit tx is created or signed.)

> Record installer file type diagnostics
> 
> Add generic `file` command diagnostics to installer evidence without changing

> output with Linux archive tools, and installer structure reports include a
> non-blocking `file <artifact>` section before format-specific inspectors.

> turn otherwise valid package structure reports into failures. Format-specific
> inspectors still determine whether a report row is generated, failed, or

> that build-info captures Linux package and archive tool diagnostics.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash

> ```

- eea51b76275560a22bc6a3d2055da73771081c74 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/eea51b76275560a22bc6a3d2055da73771081c74
> Gate checksum-only dependency artifacts
> 
> Add a `verifyDependencySignaturePolicy` task that resolves all dependency
> configurations, lets Gradle dependency verification check the artifacts, and
> then fails if any checksum-only artifact is not present in the reviewed
> allowlist.
> 
> The allowlist is intentionally artifact-level in
> `gradle/dependency-checksum-fallback-allowlist.tsv`, so a newly introduced
> unsigned jar, pom, module metadata file, or plugin marker requires an explicit
> review before CI accepts it.
> 
> Wire the task into the main GitHub build workflow so dependency verification
> policy is enforced before release manifest artifacts are uploaded.
> 
> Usage:
> 
> ```bash
> ./gradlew verifyDependencySignaturePolicy
> ./gradlew dependencySignatureReport
> git diff --check
> ```
> 
> When a dependency update adds or removes checksum-only artifacts, review the
> metadata diff, update `gradle/dependency-checksum-fallback-allowlist.tsv`, and
> regenerate `docs/dependency-signature-report.md`.
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenrikJannsen <boilingfrog@gmx.com>

> Publish release manifests from CI

> The workflow now uploads the generated release manifest files as a CI artifact
> named for the OS and Java matrix entry:

> - `build/reports/release/build-info.json`

> ./gradlew verifyReleaseManifest -PreleaseManifest=/path/to/ci/release-manifest.tsv

> artifact from the successful workflow run and use its `release-manifest.tsv` as
> the `-PreleaseManifest` input.
