- f1dd86b82fd5ec03e98a15c2bb636125fe465495 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/f1dd86b82fd5ec03e98a15c2bb636125fe465495
> Reject non-P2WPKH maker inputs and non-default sequence/lockTime
> 
> verifyPreparedDepositTxFrom*AsMaker only checked the change output.
> A malicious maker could supply a legacy P2PKH or P2WSH input, making
> the deposit tx malleable. The buyer-signed delayed payout tx (DPT)
> references the deposit txid, so a malleated tx breaks DPT recovery
> and locks funds in the multisig output until manual mediation.
> 
> Add a verifyMakerInputsAreP2WPKHAndTxIsNonMalleable check in both
> BuyerAsTakerSignsDepositTx and SellerAsTakerSignsDepositTx that asserts:
> - every maker input scriptPubKey is strictly P2WPKH;
> - preparedDepositTx.lockTime == 0;
> - every input sequence is 0xfffffffe or 0xffffffff.
> 
> Addresses risk #3 in /findings/07_risks_ranked.md.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
- f20f521eddbfc4ca1462e3c587c26991ecccfa05 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/f20f521eddbfc4ca1462e3c587c26991ecccfa05
> Add installer build info evidence
> 
> Write `installer-build-info.json` alongside the installer manifest and checksum
> file so per-OS installer evidence records the build environment used to create

> and installer manifests, include the installer build-info file in the
> reproducible installer evidence bundle, and upload it from each manual
> installer evidence workflow job.
> 
> Keep manifest-generation tasks non-incremental so their git and environment
> diagnostics are refreshed whenever the evidence tasks run.
> 
> Usage:

> ./gradlew verifyGithubActionsSecurity --stacktrace
> ./gradlew generateReleaseManifest --stacktrace
> ./gradlew generateInstallerEvidenceBundle --stacktrace
> unzip -l build/reports/release/installer-evidence.zip
> git diff --check
> ```
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenrikJannsen <boilingfrog@gmx.com>

> Add installer manifest verification

> byte size, and repo-relative path for the generated installer artifacts to
> `build/reports/release/installer-manifest.tsv` and

> 
> ```bash

> shasum -a 256 -c build/reports/release/INSTALLER-SHA256SUMS

> ```

> Unreserve open offer when take-offer request fails
> 
> If MakerProcessesInputsForDepositTxRequest (or any subsequent task in
> MakerProtocol.handleTakeOfferRequest) fails after TradeManager has already
> called reserveOpenOffer, the offer stayed RESERVED for the full
> OpenOffer.TIMEOUT (60s) before self-healing.
> 
> This window is reachable in practice because TradeManager re-runs the
> full InputsForDepositTxRequest validation a second time inside the task
> (intentional defense-in-depth from PR #7644). Block-height advances or
> price-feed updates between the two validations can flip a request from
> valid to invalid, leaving the offer stuck.
> 
> Add OpenOfferManager.unreserveOpenOffer and call it from the error
> handler so a retry can proceed immediately.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

#### 2. v1.10.1 / v1.10.1

item_id: bisq-network/bisq::release::331041306
Data: 2026-07-31T15:30:49Z
URL: https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/releases/tag/v1.10.1

Release notes (texto original):

> This release addresses concerns about the overly restrictive trade amount limits introduced in the previous release and fixes a bug affecting BSQ swap trades.
> 
> ## Release notes
> 
> ### Trading And Wallet Safety
> 
> * Maximum trade limits were increased to 0.250 BTC.
> * The risk-based reduction factors for the 4 risk classes were changed from `1, 2, 4, 8` to `1, 2, 3, 4`. This results in trade limits of up to 0.250 BTC for Altcoins and up to 0.0625 BTC for higher-risk fiat payment methods such as SEPA or Zelle.
> * Fixed a bug in BSQ swap fee validation and added additional validation checks.
> * Trade statistics validation was adjusted for the reduced trade limits introduced in the previous release.
> 
> ### UX And Settings
> 
> * Updated the user agreement.
> * Trade rules are now shown when users create or take an offer for the first time.
> * Trade rules and the user agreement are now available from Settings → About.
> * The cold-storage reminder threshold is now configurable in preferences.
> 
> ### Release Process And CI
> 
> * Debian package dependency generation now relaxes `t64` dependencies while preserving the original constraint or qualifier on the non-`t64` alternative.
> 
> See full release notes at: https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/tree/release/v1.10.1/release-notes/1.10.1
> 
> 
> ## Installation
> 
> ### macOS
> Bisq does not use Apple's notarization process (see [why](https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/discussions/6341)). 
> For that reason you will see that (misleading) alert:
> <img src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e058c34c-38f5-4329-8fc5-f48b3f2ba4dd" width="180"/>
> Grant permissions by: 
> - run `sudo xattr -rd com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Bisq.app` in a terminal (type Terminal in the Apple search box)
> - open `Bisq` again
> 
> More details can be found [here](https://bisq.wiki/Downloading_and_installing#OS-specific_install_notes).
> 
> ### Windows
> For similar reasons you will get that warning at Windows: _**Windows protected your PC**_
> 
> - Click the `More info` button when prompted
> - Click the `Run anyway` button when prompted
> 
> More details can be found [here](https://bisq.wiki/Downloading_and_installing#OS-specific_install_notes).
> 
> ### Verify download
> See the [verification and installation instructions](https://bisq.wiki/Downloading_and_installing) in the Bisq Wiki.

- 1c3773adbd07ffd5a7d52e59af4ad9fcdcc2a652 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/1c3773adbd07ffd5a7d52e59af4ad9fcdcc2a652
> Relax t64 dependencies in generated .deb
> 
> Debian/Ubuntu 24.04 renamed many libraries during the 64-bit time_t transition, appending a `t64` suffix (e.g. libasound2 -> libasound2t64).
> jpackage inherits whatever names dpkg-shlibdeps picks up on the build host, so a .deb produced on a t64-transitioned system pins `libasound2t64` and refuses to install on Ubuntu 22.04 where only the un-suffixed name exists.
> 
> Post-process the generated .deb to rewrite each `<pkg>t64` entry in the Depends field as `<pkg>t64 | <pkg>`, satisfying the requirement on both old and new releases without overriding jpackage's auto-detected dependency list.
> 
> Fixes #7819

> test(apitest): poll for BSQ balance changes in TradeScenarioTest
> 
> CI surfaced a flaky failure in TradeScenarioTest.aliceBuysBtcForBsq_bobTakes_swap:
> 
>     org.opentest4j.AssertionFailedError: bob BSQ must increase:
>     before=149974597 after=149974597 ==> expected: <true> but was: <false>
> 
> After the swap tx is mined the test reads each side's available_confirmed BSQ
> balance once and asserts the expected direction. The BSQ parser updates the
> confirmed balance asynchronously after the block arrives, so a single one-shot
> read races the parser and can observe stale values. Same race could in
> principle affect the BTC totals via reserved->available flow.
> 
> Gate the four post-swap balance assertions on the observable state change
> (DaoTestUtils.await) with a 30s safety-net timeout, matching the pattern used
> elsewhere in this test for tx-id and confirmation waits. No protocol change;
> test-only.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

- 5a23970079e0b4f35a937446131781f5bc66e613 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/5a23970079e0b4f35a937446131781f5bc66e613
> Surface async offer/wallet failures through the gRPC observer
> 
> Several gRPC RPCs were returning success while async side-effects continued
> on a different thread (a wallet broadcast callback, a UserThread offerbook
> listener) — failures on those threads were logged but the gRPC reply had
> already been sent, so the client saw a successful create/edit/cancel/send
> on a broken outcome. The OpenBsqSwapOffer ctor crash on SELL bsq-swap offers
> made this concrete: createBsqSwapOffer always replied OK even though the
> wallet listener never got attached.
> 
> - OpenBsqSwapOfferService: extract the per-offer registration into
>   registerOpenBsqSwapOffer and run it synchronously from placeBsqSwapOffer
>   before signalling success; on RuntimeException, roll back the offerbook
>   publish and route the error to the gRPC errorMessageHandler. The
>   observable-list listener now dedups against the synchronous registration
>   to avoid double-construction and leaked wallet listeners.
> - CoreApi / CoreOffersService: thread Consumer<String> errorHandler through
>   createAndPlaceBsqSwapOffer, createAndPlaceOffer, editOffer, cancelOffer,
>   placeOffer, placeBsqSwapOffer; remove the racy post-call
>   `offer.getErrorMessage()` checks (the field is set on a later thread).
>   editOffer now chains editOpenOfferPublish from editOpenOfferStart's
>   success handler so the gRPC reply fires only after both phases land.
> - GrpcOffersService: pass an error handler that calls
>   exceptionHandler.handleErrorMessage(...) so the client gets onError when
>   the async path fails.
> - GrpcWalletsService: sendBsq.onFailure and sendBtc.onSuccess(null) /
>   .onFailure previously threw new IllegalStateException from the broadcast
>   callback thread, which the surrounding try/catch could not see and which
>   left the gRPC stream open. Route through exceptionHandler.handleException
>   so the client sees the failure.
- 5a75a48785a2c97ff51593f5de60db906c20c3a0 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/5a75a48785a2c97ff51593f5de60db906c20c3a0
> Fix BSQ swap take-offer crash by clamping BTC miner contribution at 0
> 
> When the BSQ trade fee already covers this side's share of the miner
> cost, our BTC miner contribution should be 0 — the excess BSQ simply
> burns into the miner-fee pool and the tx slightly overpays the miner.
> Previously getAdjustedTxFee threw IllegalArgumentException on a
> negative result, which is correct as a guard against an invalid tx
> (outputs > inputs) but the calculation itself can be made valid by
> clamping at 0 instead. The thrown exception killed the take-offer
> dialog under realistic conditions: with DEFAULT_TAKER_FEE_BSQ
> (1.5 BSQ/BTC) a 1 BTC swap produces a 150 BSQ-sat trade fee, while
> 1 sat/vbyte × ~73 vbytes (single segwit input) is only ~73 sat miner
> portion — the invariant breaks in normal use.
> 
> Economic rationale: the BSQ trade fee burns regardless (DAO accounting
> unchanged). The constructed tx now satisfies sum(inputs) >= sum(outputs)
> in every case, and at low fee rates with small inputs the miner ends
> up overpaid by at most (tradeFee - vBytes * txFeePerVbyte) sat per
> side — well within MAX_FEE_DEVIATION_FACTOR=2 for the rate-tolerance
> check in BsqSwapTakeOfferRequestVerification.
> 
> - BsqSwapCalculation.getAdjustedTxFee: clamp at 0 when tradeFee
>   exceeds the miner-fee portion. Math.multiplyExact still trips loudly
>   on absurd txFeePerVbyte, preserving the overflow guard from the
>   previous hardening pass.
> - BsqSwapCalculation.getAdjustedTxFeeForEstimate: removed — the single
>   variant now serves both broadcast and UI estimation paths.
> - BsqSwapOfferModel.getEstimatedTxFee: reverted to call the unified
>   getAdjustedTxFee (still never throws on the no-overflow path).
> - BsqSwapOfferModel.calculateInputAndPayout and
>   BsqSwapOfferViewModel.getTxFee: removed the IllegalArgumentException
>   catches added in the earlier symptom-only fix; with the proper fix
>   no exception is thrown, so the UI try/catch only needs to handle the
>   pre-existing InsufficientMoneyException case.
> - BsqSwapCalculationTest: replaced the "rejects tradeFee above miner
>   portion" assertions with clamp-at-zero assertions covering the raw
>   function and both seller/buyer wrappers used in production.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

- 66cc2d85fe47a1a3326a6a0f03157a57a06609f6 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/66cc2d85fe47a1a3326a6a0f03157a57a06609f6
> Clamp FeeService rates at the network minimum on updateFeeInfo
> 
> Defense-in-depth follow-up to the BSQ swap take-offer fix. The fee provider
> is external and untrusted; a misbehaving or malicious feed could push the
> stored txFeePerVbyte / minFeePerVByte below the network's documented minimum.
> Downstream code (BSQ swap arithmetic, BTC trade fee deposit checks) assumes
> txFeePerVbyte >= minFeePerVByte >= networkMin and does not re-check this at
> each use site.
> 
> In particular the BsqSwapCalculation.getAdjustedTxFee clamp-at-0 semantics
> relies on this invariant to prove min-relay viability: when one side's BSQ
> trade fee exceeds its miner-portion, the BSQ burn alone is only guaranteed
> to cover the side's share of the network minimum if txFeePerVbyte was at
> least networkMin to begin with.
> 
> - FeeService.updateFeeInfo: clamp both fields to
>   Config.baseCurrencyNetwork().getDefaultMinFeePerVbyte() before storing.
>   Log a warning when clamping actually fires so a bad feed is visible in
>   the logs rather than silently degrading every downstream fee calculation.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

> fix(apitest): de-flake TradeScenarioTest, fail CI on timeout, add DAO-sync test
> 
> Three related e2e fixes, found via repeated local runs (1 failure in 8):
> 
> 1. TradeScenarioTest intermittently failed all four trades at
>    takeOffer/takeBsqSwapOffer with gRPC "timeout reached: peer has not
>    responded". Root cause: it ran in the shared-stack DAO phase, after the
>    governance tests churn proposals/votes whose payloads reach the seed node
>    and Alice on slightly different schedules. That leaves Alice's
>    DaoStateMonitoringService in a persistent block-hash conflict with the seed
>    node (isInConflictWithSeedNode), so isDaoStateReadyAndInSync stays false.
>    OpenOfferManager.handleOfferAvailabilityRequest then answers a take with
>    only a NACK AckMessage and no OfferAvailabilityResponse; the taker's protocol
>    only resolves on the response, so it hits the 90s timeout.
> 
>    Fix: run TradeScenarioTest on a freshly reset stack (@Tag("freshstack")),
>    like the sibling method.trade.* take-offer tests — a pristine stack has no
>    governance-induced seed-node divergence. Confirmed by repeated fresh-stack
>    runs passing where shared-stack runs flaked. Also add awaitMakerReadyToRespond
>    before each take as a defensive fast-fail (getDaoStatus + non-pending
>    maker-fee tx) so any residual maker-sync lag surfaces with a clear message
>    instead of the opaque 90s gRPC timeout.
> 
> 2. run-e2e-tests.sh could exit 0 on a global-timeout abort: the watchdog
>    SIGTERMs the script mid-command and the cleanup trap captured $? of whatever
>    trivial command was running (often 0), so an aborted run reported success
>    and CI stayed green. The watchdog now drops a marker that cleanup turns into
>    exit 124. Also raise GLOBAL_TIMEOUT_SECS 1800->3600 (a healthy run on a
>    2-core CI runner can approach 30min, so 1800 sat on the edge), and capture
>    the shared-stack containers' logs on failure before the fresh-stack loop
>    tears that stack down.
> 
> 3. Add DaoStaysInSyncTest (freshstack): a regression guard asserting a correctly
>    gated proposal + blind-vote + reveal + result cycle leaves every daemon in
>    sync with the seed node (getDaoStatus() == true) at each milestone, not just
>    producing the right vote outcome — pinning down the consensus property whose
>    violation caused the flake above. Validated deterministic: 12/12 fresh-stack
>    runs green.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

> Fix trade statistics validation after limit reductions
> 
> TradeStatistics3.isValid() was checking post-2021 trade amounts against the current payment-method trade limit. That limit is DAO-adjusted and can be reduced after a trade was executed, so valid historical trade statistics above the new limit could be rejected when loading persisted stats, receiving P2P stats, or republishing missing stats.
> 
> Keep trade statistics validation independent of mutable current limits by using a stable 2 BTC historical sanity cap. This preserves old valid statistics while still filtering implausibly large amounts.
> 
> Add regression coverage for a 0.25 BTC statistic, which is above the current 0.125 BTC cap but should remain valid historical data, and for rejecting amounts above the historical sanity cap.
> 
> Verification: ./gradlew :core:test --tests bisq.core.trade.statistics.TradeStatistics3Test

> test(apitest): port legacy disabled tests to docker stack
> 
> Replace Scaffold-spawned subprocess harness with a docker-compose-based
> suite that runs against the e2e stack introduced in 3f51f9b850.
> 
> - DockerMethodTest / DockerOfferTest / DockerTradeTest bases: connect via
>   system properties, expose state-gated awaitCond/awaitOffer/awaitOfferActivated
>   helpers, reuse DaoTestUtils for chain ops.
> - Port 22 previously @Disabled classes (offer create/cancel/edit, payment
>   account, wallet protection, xmr trade, etc.); drop classes redundant with
>   the DAO+trade scenario suite (BTC v1 trades, BSQ v1 trades superseded by
>   swaps, scenario composites, long-running perf loops).
> - Fresh-stack phase: classes annotated @Tag("freshstack") run in their own
>   reset stack via reset_stack helper. Discovery is grep-driven from the
>   source — single source of truth, no list to keep in sync.
> - Deterministic waits: every async test gates on the daemon's own state
>   signal (DaoTestUtils.await, 250ms poll, 60s safety timeout); sleeps only
>   remain where the test exercises a wall-clock contract (unlock-timeout).
> - run-e2e-tests.sh refactored into lifecycle helpers (teardown_stack,
>   start_stack, wait_for_daemons, reset_stack) — single source of truth for
>   stack ops, used by both initial bring-up and the fresh-stack loop.
> - e2e-tests.yml path filter widened to include common, p2p, persistence,
>   assets, bridge, bitcoind, gradle/libs.versions.toml — regressions in
>   transitive deps now trigger the suite.
>

#### 3. v1.10.4 / v1.10.4

item_id: bisq-network/bisq::release::358911643
Data: 2026-07-31T15:33:24Z
URL: https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/releases/tag/v1.10.4

Release notes (texto original):

> ## Release notes
> 
> This is an important security update that fixes vulnerabilities identified during our recent security audit.
> Updating to this version is required to continue trading. BSQ Swaps have also been re-enabled.
> 
> #### Security
> 
> - **DAO block signatures**: DAO blocks received from the network can now be signed by trusted BSQ block providers. Bisq verifies these signatures before accepting the blocks. 
> - **Blind-vote validation**: Bisq rejects blind votes whose encrypted payload does not match the on-chain commitment, and decrypts vote results only from the ballots that match the majority hash. 
> - **Dispute-opening validation**: New dispute cases are validated before being accepted. Disputes that fail validation are rejected.
> - **Arbitrator-witness signatures**: Signed witness records are now checked for valid DSA signatures before being used for account aging.
> - **Seed-only data filtering**: Network data that is intended to come only from seed nodes is now rejected when received from non-seed peers.
> - **Price-zero offer rejection**: Offers with a price of zero are rejected and not added to the offer book.
> - **Burning Man fee routing**: The Burning Man distribution address list is now used when selecting BTC fee receivers.
> - **Trusted seeds**: Trusted seed nodes are used during network bootstrap.
> 
> #### Other changes
> 
> - Alert authors can remove all alerts they created.
> - Legacy arbitrator data has been removed from trade and deposit flows.
> 
> #### Credits to reporters of vulnerabilities
> - https://github.com/Kevandrew
> - https://github.com/0xEr3n
> - https://github.com/woodser
> 
> ## Installation
> 
> ### macOS
> Bisq does not use Apple's notarization process (see [why](https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/discussions/6341)). 
> For that reason you will see that (misleading) alert:
> <img src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e058c34c-38f5-4329-8fc5-f48b3f2ba4dd" width="180"/>
> Grant permissions by: 
> - run `sudo xattr -rd com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Bisq.app` in a terminal (type Terminal in the Apple search box)
> - open `Bisq` again
> 
> More details can be found [here](https://bisq.wiki/Downloading_and_installing#OS-specific_install_notes).
> 
> ### Windows
> For similar reasons you will get that warning at Windows: _**Windows protected your PC**_
> 
> - Click the `More info` button when prompted
> - Click the `Run anyway` button when prompted
> 
> More details can be found [here](https://bisq.wiki/Downloading_and_installing#OS-specific_install_notes).
> 
> ### Verify download
> See the [verification and installation instructions](https://bisq.wiki/Downloading_and_installing) in the Bisq Wiki.

> fix: reject malformed price=0 offer to prevent offer-book DoS
> 
> A fixed-price OfferPayload with price<=0 is malformed. If accepted it
> crashes the offer-book render path: Offer.getVolumeByAmount -> bitcoinj
> ExchangeRate(checkArgument(isPositive())) throws on the JavaFX thread for
> every client viewing the affected market (security report F2-1).
> 
> - OfferPayload.fromProto: reject a fixed-price offer with price<=0 so the
>   malformed entry never enters the P2P store or the offer book. A
>   market-based offer legitimately carries price==0 (price derived from the
>   margin), so only the fixed-price case is gated.
> - Offer.getVolumeByAmount: treat a non-positive price as no volume
>   (defense in depth) so a bad entry can never crash the FX thread.

>

> or encoder change that diverged from protobuf-java's default-omit

> fix: restore mediation broken by fail-closed dispute validation
> 
> Commit 8b432c6e94 moved DisputeValidation ahead of the side effects in
> onOpenNewDisputeMessage and made every failure fail-closed. Two problems:
> 
> 1. testIfDisputeTriesReplay assumed the dispute under test was already in
>    the list (pre-1.10.3 order validated after disputeList.add). Run before
>    the add, the first legitimate dispute for a trade hit a null trade-id
>    set and threw "more then 2 disputes", so the agent silently dropped it
>    and mediation never progressed.
> 
> 2. Fail-closing on advisory data checks (donation address, node address)
>    silently discarded legitimate disputes and stopped surfacing the agent
>    popup those cases rely on, while still exposing a popup-flood vector for
>    incorrect payloads.
> 
> Fixes:
> - testIfDisputeTriesReplay now counts the dispute under test via an
>   idempotent uid injection, so the <= 2 limit holds regardless of whether
>   the caller validates before or after adding to the list.
> - Split ingest validation: integrity checks (contract data,
>   replay) stay fail-closed and drop silently (log only, no popup);
>   advisory checks (node/donation address) store and forward the dispute
>   and alert the agent via validationExceptions, matching pre-1.10.3
>   behavior and the sibling peerOpenedDisputeForTrade handler.
> 
> Tests: DisputeValidationTest replay regressions; DisputeManagerAuthTest
> hard-drop vs advisory-store paths.

> test(apitest): add long-running trade e2e tests + regtest wallet-sync fixes
> 
> Add two opt-in long-running e2e tests under a shared v1-trade helper, plus the
> regtest-scoped wallet fixes needed to make them pass reliably.
> 
> Tests (apitest/.../dao):
> - AllAccountTypesTradeScenarioTest: every CLI-creatable account type
>   (F2F, Revolut, AdvancedCash, JapanBank, BrazilNationalBank) x all four role
>   combinations (each peer as maker+taker, BTC buyer+seller).
> - F2FStabilityTradeScenarioTest: 100-round F2F soak alternating maker/taker and
>   direction each round.
> - V1TradeFlow: reusable take-offer -> payment -> payout flow both tests drive.
> 
> Both are @Tag("longrunning") (+ freshstack) and opt-in only: the runner skips
> them unless RUN_LONG_RUNNING_TESTS=true, in which case it runs ONLY them
> (shared-stack/other-freshstack/policy phases skipped). Exposed as a
> workflow_dispatch boolean input in e2e-tests.yml and e2e-tests-compat.yml, so
> normal PR and compat CI never run them.
> 
> Wallet fixes (regtest only, mainnet/testnet untouched):
> - WalletsSetup.isChainHeightSyncedWithinTolerance: the symmetric
>   Math.abs(peers - best) <= 3 check spuriously reported "not synced" when our own
>   downloaded chain ran ahead of the height the PeerGroup last tracked for the peer
>   (routine under burst mining), making makers NACK offer-availability with "chain
>   is not synced" despite being fully at the tip. On regtest, treat at-or-ahead as
>   synced (best >= peers - 3, peers > 0); only a genuine lag is unsynced. At
>   mainnet/testnet block cadence the tracking lag never reaches the tolerance, so
>   the original symmetric check is kept there.
> - WalletConfig: force bitcoinj bloom-filter false-positive rate to 1.0 on regtest
>   so a freshly broadcast wallet tx (trade deposit/payout) is never omitted from
>   the confirming block's merkleblock (the bloom-filter race that left deposits
>   buried on-chain but unconfirmed in the wallet). No effect off regtest.
> 
> Supporting:
> - New GetWalletSyncStatus gRPC (proto -> CoreWalletsService -> GrpcWalletsService
>   -> cli) exposing the bitcoinj wallet's chain-sync flag + best height.
> - DaoTestUtils.confirmTxAfterFilterPropagation and a take-retry/maker-sync gate in
>   V1TradeFlow as additional robustness.

> Cover canonical payment account parity for locally created payloads
> 
> Every existing parity case decodes through CoreProtoResolver.fromProto, which
> hides three production code paths from the canonical schema:
> 
> - PaymentAccountPayload's no-arg constructor leaves maxTradePeriod at -1, while
>   the matrix always seeds the protobuf with maxTradePeriod=12345.
> - The constructor auto-injects a SALT entry into excludeFromJsonDataMap and
>   PaymentAccountPayloadExcludeFromJsonMap then enforces LEGACY_HASHMAP_ORDER,
>   whereas fromProto always picks the preserveInsertionOrder branch.
> - setHolderName on PaymentAccountPayload subclasses that have no holderName
>   field of their own (AliPay etc.) feeds the HOLDER_NAME entry into the same
>   map and forces the legacy reorder to put HOLDER_NAME ahead of SALT.
> 
> Add a parity matrix that builds AliPayAccountPayload, NationalBankAccountPayload
> and SepaAccountPayload directly through their public Java constructors, mutates
> them the way producers do, and asserts canonical bytes, serializeForHash bytes
> and the ripemd160 contract hash stay byte-compatible with the roundtripped
> protobuf bytes. This covers the default signed-int64 maxTradePeriod path, the
> auto-salt LEGACY_HASHMAP_ORDER path, an empty repeated-string field (Sepa
> acceptedCountryCodes) and the nested CountryBased -> Bank -> NationalBank
> wrapper for a payload that only sets the required holder name.

> Fix Windows backup failing on locked bisq.spvchain
> 
> The data-dir backup ("Backup now") aborts on Windows since v1.9.22 with
> "The process cannot access the file because another process has locked a
> portion of the file", producing no backup at all.
> 
> Root cause: commons-io was bumped 2.6 -> 2.22.0. Since 2.7,
> FileUtils.copyDirectory copies each file via java.nio.file.Files.copy,
> which on Windows routes to the Win32 CopyFileEx API. CopyFileEx respects
> byte-range locks and fails on the FileLock bitcoinj's SPVBlockStore holds
> on bisq.spvchain. The old 2.6 stream copy (FileInputStream) read through
> the lock.
> 
> Replace FileUtil.copyDirectory with an in-tree recursive copy that reads
> each file through a FileInputStream (Guava Files.copy), restoring the
> pre-upgrade tolerant behaviour without reverting the dependency bump.
> 
> Keep the rest of commons-io copyDirectory's semantics so it stays a
> drop-in: missing source throws FileNotFoundException, a non-directory
> source throws IllegalArgumentException, a destination inside the source is
> excluded from the walk (no endless self-copy, backups configured under the
> data dir keep working), a directory whose listFiles() returns null raises
> IOException instead of being treated as empty, last-modified times are
> preserved for files and directories, and per-file IO errors propagate.
> 
> Add FileUtilTest covering nested-file copy correctness, file and directory
> last-modified preservation, and the missing-source, non-directory-source,
> destination-inside-source, and directory-listing-failure paths.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
- 836a6b5528ee11d05f5e5b0afb5a85cbe178297c — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/836a6b5528ee11d05f5e5b0afb5a85cbe178297c
> Remove obsolete TradeStatistics2 handling
> 
> TradeStatistics3 has been the active trade statistics format since the v1.4.0 migration, and the remaining TradeStatistics2 code only supported stale local conversion and very old network payload conversion.

- 859b1daa226c0602f0b5190b5ef8b55def53c2bf — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/859b1daa226c0602f0b5190b5ef8b55def53c2bf
> Re-send payment started message at startup when it was never ACKed
> 
> The buyer re-sends CounterCurrencyTransferStartedMessage on a timer until the seller ACKs it. The timer only lives in memory, so a restart kills it. The STARTUP rule in BuyerProtocol#onInitialized re-ran the send task only for the STORED_IN_MAILBOX and SEND_FAILED states. It skipped BUYER_SENT_FIAT_PAYMENT_INITIATED_MSG (sent, but no ACK yet). Such a trade never re-sent the message. The buyer stayed stuck at "Please send confirmation again". The seller never learned the payment was started. This often ended in needless mediation.
> 
> Fix: include BUYER_SENT_FIAT_PAYMENT_INITIATED_MSG in the STARTUP re-send condition. Re-sending is safe: the message has a deterministic uid, so re-sends deduplicate, and the seller side tolerates repeated delivery.
> 
> Also skip the send when the persisted message state is already ACKNOWLEDGED. That happens when the ACK arrives while no task is listening (right after a restart). In that case only apply the BUYER_SAW_ARRIVED state transition.
> 
> Fixes the buyer side of #7243. Also reported in #6715 and #3372.

> fix(filter): defer no-filter warning until seed data received
> 
> The "no filter object received" warning was triggered synchronously in
> onAllServicesInitialized(), before the initial P2P data request to the
> seed nodes had completed. On slow networks the filter had simply not
> arrived yet, producing a false-positive popup asking users to contact
> the developers.
> 
> Move the check into the onDataReceived() listener, which fires after the
> seed-node data handshake completes; by then any network filter has been
> applied via the onAdded listener. A one-shot guard prevents repeat
> warnings. When no seed node is reachable onDataReceived never fires, so
> the unrelated "No seed nodes available" path handles that case instead.
> 
> Also fix grammar typo in the warning string ("a not expected situation"
> -> "an unexpected situation") in the English source.

> test(apitest): add cross-version e2e compat test + fix DAO/trade flakes
> 
> Add a dispatch-only e2e variant that runs the full DAO + trade suite against a
> mixed-version stack: seednode/arb/alice on the current tree, bob on the latest
> tagged release. Exercises release<->master P2P/DAO/trade compatibility.
> 
> Infra:
> - Dockerfile.bisq-release: inherit the master harness image (entrypoint,
>   dao-setup, javafx) and swap only the Bisq app binaries for a release build.
> - dao-compose.compat.yml: override pointing bob at bisq-daemon:release.
> - run-e2e-tests.sh: COMPOSE_OVERRIDE_FILE support so the override layers over
>   up/down/build; require bisq-daemon:release when the override is active.
> - e2e-tests-compat.yml: workflow_dispatch-only CI job that builds the release
>   dists in a git worktree, builds the release image, and runs the suite with
>   the override. Skips the deny-list policy phase (injects the master-only
>   --denyListResource flag an older release peer does not recognize). The
>   release_ref input is passed via env and validated with git rev-parse to avoid
>   shell injection.
> - run-e2e-tests-compat.sh: local runner mirroring the workflow.
> - .dockerignore/.gitignore: whitelist + ignore the staged .release-dist.
> 
> Flakiness fixes surfaced by the e2e runs:
> - Dispute-agent race: on a freshly reset stack the maker's first createoffer
>   could run before the mediator/refund-agent payloads registered on the arb
>   node propagated over P2P, failing ValidateOffer. ValidateOffer precedes funds
>   reservation, so a rejected attempt is side-effect free. Add
>   DaoTestUtils.placeV1OfferWhenReady (bounded retry on that transient, gate on
>   success) and apply it to every freshstack positive v1 offer creation.
> - Vote-reveal counting race: confirming each voter's reveal tx in its own block
>   (confirmAutoRevealsFor per voter) mined a second block that crossed out of the
>   2-block regtest VOTE_REVEAL phase, silently dropping the later voter's vote
>   from the tally. Add DaoTestUtils.confirmAutoRevealsForAll, which stages all
>   reveals into the mempool and confirms them in a single in-phase block, and use
>   it at every two-voter result-counting site.
> - WalletProtectionTest.testUnlockWalletTimeoutOverride: only 1.5s slack before
>   the 3s re-lock deadline could flake under CI stall. Widen the override window
>   to 60s, keeping the 1.5s probe that proves the override past the original 1s.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

> refactor(proto): extract gRPC services into separate :proto-grpc module
> 
> Split the proto module so that gRPC service stubs and their runtime
> dependencies (grpc-stub, grpc-protobuf and transitives) no longer leak
> onto the runtime classpath of modules that only need protobuf messages.
> 
> The :proto module now generates messages only: the `service` blocks were
> moved out of grpc.proto and bridge.proto into grpc_services.proto and
> bridge_services.proto in the new :proto-grpc module, which imports the
> message definitions from proto.jar (import-only, no recompilation) and
> owns the gRPC codegen and dependencies.
> 
> Only cli, daemon, apitest and bridge consume the service stubs and now
> depend on :proto-grpc; core (messages only) and all other modules
> (desktop, seednode, p2p, persistence, common, inventory, btcnodemonitor,
> restapi, statsnode) stay on the grpc-free :proto.

> Filter same-txid forged blind vote duplicates by merit decryption
> 
> Before matching the local blind vote list against the majority hash,
> drop any payload whose encryptedMeritList does not decrypt under its
> on-chain secret key. Random ciphertext cannot decrypt under a key the
> attacker did not know at blind-vote-phase publication time, so this
> neutralizes the forged duplicate. Payloads for which no vote reveal is
> observable on-chain are kept because they may still be needed to
> reconstruct the majority hash.
> 
> The filtered list is now threaded into findBlindVoteListMatchingMajorityHash
> and findPermutatedListMatchingMajority, replacing the previous inline
> BlindVoteConsensus.getSortedBlindVoteListOfCycle(blindVoteListService) call
> at each site. The existing empty-merit fallback in getDecryptedBallotsWithMerits
> is retained as defense in depth for merit-format regressions from honest voters.
> 
> Tests added:
> - getMeritDecryptableBlindVoteListDropsPayloadWithMalformedMerit
> - getMeritDecryptableBlindVoteListKeepsHonestPayload
> - getMeritDecryptableBlindVoteListKeepsPayloadWithoutObservedVoteReveal
> - malformedMeritDuplicateDoesNotPreventVoteResultCalculation (regression
>   covering the report19 end-to-end scenario)

> Cover canonical payment account parity for null optional fields
> 
> The previous parity matrix populated every protobuf field, so the canonical
> schemas were never exercised against BankAccountPayload and
> CashDepositAccountPayload instances whose nullable bank-level fields fromProto
> decoded as null. The schemas read those fields directly through lambdas, so a
> regression that introduced an NPE or wrote an empty string instead of skipping
> the field would silently drift away from the legacy protobuf hash preimage.
> 
> Add a focused parity matrix that exercises:
> 
> - NationalBank and SpecificBanks with only the required holderName populated.
> - CashDepositAccountPayload with only the required holderName populated.
> - Sepa with the deprecated email field unset.
> - SepaInstant with the acceptedCountryCodes list left empty.
> 
> For each shape we re-decode through CoreProtoResolver and assert that the
> canonical bytes, serializeForHash bytes and ripemd160 contract hash match the
> roundtripped protobuf bytes, so the canonical encoder must continue handling
> null lambda returns, empty repeated string lists and missing deprecated string
> fields exactly the way protobuf does.

> build: remove obsolete macOS JDK overrides and runtime image setup
> 
> Simplify the packaging configuration by removing legacy workarounds that
> are no longer required now that the project has upgraded to JDK 21.
> 
> 1. Remove JDK 16 override for macOS:
> The previous JavaFX version was incompatible with JDK 11 on macOS and
> caused system crashes, triggering a workaround that forced JDK 16 on
> macOS while other operating systems used the default project JDK. This
> override is no longer necessary.
> 
> 2. Remove custom JDK 11 runtime image creation:
> We previously used JDK 17's jpackage to build a runtime image for JDK 11
> because JDK 11 lacked built-in jpackage support. Since the project is
> now on JDK 21, this custom pipeline is obsolete.

- dc51d41b01efd4ba16722f1180e749f348851bea — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/dc51d41b01efd4ba16722f1180e749f348851bea
> Lock canonical encoding for opReturn, tx input, block header
> 
> Report 16 warns that if the canonical schema for RawBlock/RawTx were
> to silently drop a field, a full node could sign a benign-looking
> encoding while a peer distributed a poisoned raw block hashing to
> the same value. RawBlockCanonicalEncoderTest already covered tx
> output value, tx output address, and tx set size; extend it to lock
> the fields that most directly drive DAO-state classification:
> 
> - opReturnData: distinguishes BSQ operation types in the parser.
>   A regression here would let an attacker swap the OP_RETURN
>   marker under a valid block signature.
> - TxInput.connectedTxOutputTxId / connectedTxOutputIndex: a tx is
>   classified BSQ iff it consumes a locally-BSQ output. Rebinding
>   the input is exactly the primitive that would recolor an
>   unrelated tx as BSQ.
> - Block header (height, time, previousBlockHash): schema regressions
>   here would let a signed block be replayed at a different position
>   in the chain.
> 
> Pure test additions; no production code changes.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

> Add RawBlock canonical encoding tests
> 
> The signed DAO block feature signs the canonical encoding of a
> RawBlock (see DaoBlockSignatureHash). If the canonical schema for
> RawBlock/RawTx were to accidentally omit a field, a full node could
> sign a benign-looking encoding while a peer distributed a poisoned
> raw block that hashes identically - reintroducing the attack path
> that the signature is meant to close.
> 
> Add regression tests that:
> 
> - Confirm canonical encoding is deterministic for equal content.
> - Confirm proto round-trip preserves the canonical encoding.
> - Confirm changing a tx output value produces a different encoding.
> - Confirm changing a tx output address produces a different encoding.
> - Confirm adding an extra tx into the block produces a different
>   encoding.
> 
> These lock the invariant that a signed RawBlock's hash covers all
> DAO-relevant content so future schema edits cannot silently open a
> signature-collision path.

> 
> Several pure-JavaFX control replacements diverged from the CSS contract /

>   whenever a pseudo-class change re-ran the box CSS (-fx-background-color:
>   transparent). Re-assert the fill via a guarded backgroundProperty listener.
> 
> - Offer input underlines overflowed the field and floated above the box
>   border. Restore jfoenix geometry in BisqTextFieldSkin/BisqComboBoxSkin:
>   line width = fieldWidth + inputLineExtension (right-only, not both sides)
>   and y = controlHeight so the line rests on the box's bottom border.
>

>   shared -bs-color-gray-line so it reads clearly, matching jfoenix.
> 
> - Remove the dead `.jfx-checkbox` rule (typo for `.jfx-check-box`; carried a
>   removed-jfoenix `-jfx-checked-color` property and never matched).
> 
> - Add the `.indeterminate-mark` node to BisqCheckBoxSkin so the indeterminate
>   state renders per the existing CSS (jfoenix-faithful drop-in).
> 
> - Restore ComboBox validation: BisqJfxComboBox gets getValidators()/validate()/
>   errorMessageProperty() and toggles the :error pseudo-class; BisqComboBoxSkin
>   renders the .error-label; add the matching combo error CSS (error-label rules
>   + light-theme :error underline).
> 
> - Tabs scrolled off-screen on window resize (e.g. open-trades): BisqTabPaneSkin
>   let the content's min height propagate, making the pane and its ancestors
>   unshrinkable. Clip the pane to its bounds and override computeMinHeight to the
>   header height so content clips instead of pushing the chrome off-screen
>   (mirrors jfoenix's clipped JFXTabPaneSkin).

> The tests confirm that:
> 
> - A message whose signed and unsigned block hashes disagree is
>   dropped without notifying listeners or re-broadcasting.
> - A message whose Bitcoin block hash matches but whose DAO

>   unsigned copy) is also dropped.

>   the content-hash based blockUid key.

> consuming an unsigned poisoned block that came bundled with a
> signed decoy would be silently regressable.

#### 4. v1.10.5 / v1.10.5

item_id: bisq-network/bisq::release::373471904

URL: https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/releases/tag/v1.10.5

Release notes (texto original):

> ## Release notes
> 
> This is an important security update that fixes vulnerabilities identified during our recent security audit.
> Updating to this version is required to continue trading and using BSQ and the Bisq DAO.
> 
> ### DAO and Network Integrity
> 
> - Canonical hash/signature encodings reduce ambiguity across DAO and P2P payloads.
> - DAO block signatures, trusted providers, lite-node checks, checkpoints, and payload hash commitments are strengthened.
> - BSQ block bridge delivery requires contiguous state and recovers gaps.
> - Malformed decrypted votes are isolated per voter, while malformed merit can no longer remove a majority-committed blind vote.
> - Proposal validation is consistent across startup and live nodes and applies to the entire activating cycle.
> 
> ### Reputation and Bonded Roles
> 
> - Account-age and signed-witness bridge validation is bound to ownership and trusted witness chains.
> - Bonded-role registrations and lockups are checked against the correct proposal and collateral lifecycle.
> - Merit issuance and Burning Man accounting receive additional integrity checks and refreshed release data.
> 
> ### Trading and Messaging
> 
> - Fiat buyer-account validation, deposit/DPT binding, support-message authentication, and dispute-agent authentication are hardened.
> 
> 
> #### Credits to reporters of vulnerabilities
> - https://github.com/Kevandrew
> - https://github.com/stejbac
> - https://github.com/woodser
> 
> ## Installation
> 
> ### macOS
> Bisq does not use Apple's notarization process (see [why](https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/discussions/6341)). 
> For that reason you will see that (misleading) alert:
> <img src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e058c34c-38f5-4329-8fc5-f48b3f2ba4dd" width="180"/>
> Grant permissions by: 
> - run `sudo xattr -rd com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Bisq.app` in a terminal (type Terminal in the Apple search box)
> - open `Bisq` again
> 
> More details can be found [here](https://bisq.wiki/Downloading_and_installing#OS-specific_install_notes).
> 
> ### Windows
> For similar reasons you will get that warning at Windows: _**Windows protected your PC**_
> 
> - Click the `More info` button when prompted
> - Click the `Run anyway` button when prompted
> 
> More details can be found [here](https://bisq.wiki/Downloading_and_installing#OS-specific_install_notes).
> 
> ### Verify download
> See the [verification and installation instructions](https://bisq.wiki/Downloading_and_installing) in the Bisq Wiki.

- 002c5a29d83ceb6bdcdc4e146f6370471f68cc6e — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/002c5a29d83ceb6bdcdc4e146f6370471f68cc6e
> Use audited height for legacy role registrations
> 
> The legacy cutoff reused the hard-fork-3 activation height, which is in
> the future. Every lockup published between now and that height would
> therefore be legacy eligible, so anyone could bond an accepted role today
> and register as its holder in Bisq 2 through the version 0 path. That is
> the vulnerability the bound format closes, reopened by its own
> compatibility rule.
> 
> A compatibility cutoff has to be historical, so that the set of keys it
> admits is already fixed and can be audited. Use mainnet height 941000,
> below which the role lockups have been checked to contain no conflicting
> lockups, and disable legacy verification entirely on the other networks,
> where that assertion does not apply.
> 
> The cutoff must not be advanced with the release height. Advancing it
> adds lockup keys to the legacy authority set and requires a new audit and
> an explicit protocol decision.
- 01d3f8e7646844864dcdb1d110b973854eb0a96b — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/01d3f8e7646844864dcdb1d110b973854eb0a96b
> Harden duplicate ballot reconstruction and audits
> 
> Vote-result reconstruction still used a merge-free local ballot map after malformed decrypted voters were isolated. A duplicated persisted ballot transaction ID could therefore escape the per-voter boundary and abort result processing.
> 
> Merge byte-identical canonical proposals because the decrypted vote replaces local vote state, but raise a named integrity failure when the proposals differ. Add persisted-ballot regressions for both outcomes without broadening the malformed-voter catch.
> 
> Make the bundled blind-vote compatibility claims reproducible by resolving all reveal transactions, decrypting vote and merit payloads, and asserting the 947 stored / 935 revealed snapshot counts and proposal-ID uniqueness. Update the DAO voting, proposal, and merit specifications with the audit commands, activation rationale, and remaining post-snapshot obligations.
> 
> Verification: :core: VoteResultServiceTest and the opt-in bundled block/blind-vote audit passed.
- 038a07975d8480d194614d1578a85431831f1922 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/038a07975d8480d194614d1578a85431831f1922
> Document the merit vote weight rules
> 
> Merit is the part of a vote weight which is claimed inside the encrypted
> blind vote payload rather than being visible on chain, so the rules which
> make a claim trustworthy are worth stating independently of the code that
> currently implements them.
> 
> The specification records what a claim must prove against DAO state, why
> the verification key must be taken from DAO state rather than from the
> claim, how decay and the two relevant block heights work, that an
> issuance may back merit at most once per cycle, and that the rules are
> selected by the vote result evaluation height.
> 
> It also records the known gap that uniqueness is currently enforced only
> within a single merit list and not across the blind votes of a cycle, and
> what closing that gap requires.
- 0471fc73c29da4940a4a8cbf749a0909f913530c — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/0471fc73c29da4940a4a8cbf749a0909f913530c
> Refactoring: Extract the merit claim validation of one claim
> 
> The checks which decide whether an untrusted merit claim is backed by a
> real compensation issuance were inlined in the loop which sums the merit
> of one merit list. Enforcing uniqueness over a wider scope than a single
> merit list needs the same checks, and a second copy of them would be free
> to drift away from this one.
> 
> The loop keeps its structure, so validation, weighting and the checked
> addition still happen in the same order and an overflow still aborts at
> the same point.

> Preserve fail-open handling for verifier faults
> 
> Per-registration IllegalArgumentException results represent authoritative domain rejection and may deactivate a Bisq 2 role. An unexpected repository failure is not evidence that the registration is invalid and must therefore reject the whole batch so the oracle retains existing authority and retries later.
> 
> Specify that distinction and add coverage proving an unexpected verifier exception becomes an INTERNAL RPC failure without emitting a partial batch response. This guards against turning bridge defects into destructive deauthorization decisions.

> Avoid shutdown-hook re-entry on controlled exit
> 
> Unregister the common JVM shutdown hook only after graceful service
> shutdown and persistence have completed, then run the final exit on a
> dedicated thread. This avoids the UserThread/System.exit/hook wait cycle
> without restoring unsupported platform signal APIs.
> 
> Share one exit scheduler across normal, timeout, and error paths so the
> first completed path retains its status. Cover the hook lifecycle and
> document the shutdown invariant.
- 1248eda6d099f6e93f840c8f0b2914fff6ad39bc — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/1248eda6d099f6e93f840c8f0b2914fff6ad39bc
> Release the trade statistics table on deactivate
> 
> The market trade statistics view is kept in the CachingViewLoader
> for the whole session. Its table holds one list item per trade
> statistic, so with Show all selected it retains the full set,
> hundreds of thousands of rows, even while the screen is not shown.
> That memory is never released.
> 
> We clear the table and drop the sorted list on deactivate so the
> rows are collected, and rebuild them on activate. The async list
> build is guarded so a build finishing after the user left does not
> repopulate the released table on the cached view.
> 
> Reference: https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/pull/8020
> Author: https://github.com/fenlark
- 1697b04e6f0952058d4a91f3d298d5dbdc473a33 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/1697b04e6f0952058d4a91f3d298d5dbdc473a33
> Avoid materializing a Price per trade statistic
> 
> onAllServicesInitialized seeded PriceFeedService with the newest price
> per currency by calling getTradePrice() on every trade statistic.
> getTradePrice() lazily builds and caches a Price on the element, so this
> loop pinned a Price (plus its Monetary) on every row for the whole
> session even though only the latest price per currency is used.
> 
> The statistics set is sorted by date, so iterate it newest-first and
> keep the first price seen per currency with computeIfAbsent. The
> resulting map is identical, but getTradePrice() runs once per currency
> instead of once per element. On a full mainnet store this drops the
> retained Price instances from about 410k to a few hundred, freeing
> roughly 19 MiB at startup.
> 
> Reference: https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/pull/8024
> Author: https://github.com/fenlark

> Allow proposal owners to create additional role lockups
> 
> The lockup action was offered only while the role had no lockup at all,
> and the publishing guard refused once any lockup existed. Since anyone
> can publish a lockup for an accepted role, a third party could
> permanently prevent the role holder from bonding their own collateral,
> and the holder could not add a second lockup or re-lock after unlocking.
> 
> Proposal ownership, not the absence of a lockup, decides whether the
> action is offered. The role level action is now attached to one row per
> role and gated on the accepted proposal, and the guard only refuses while
> the wallet's own lockup transaction for that role is still unconfirmed,
> which prevents accidental duplicate publication.

> Classify bonded reputation by lockup reason
> 
> Bonded reputation was defined as every lockup output which no bonded role
> bond claimed. That made the reputation set a function of role bond
> selection: a BONDED_ROLE lockup which no role claimed, for instance one
> whose hash matches no accepted proposal, silently became a bonded
> reputation, and the set changed whenever role selection changed.
> 
> The lockup reason in the OP_RETURN is the only correct selector, and the
> two reasons are disjoint, so select REPUTATION directly. The repository
> then no longer depends on BondedRolesRepository, which also removes the
> listener that existed only to order the two updates.
> 
> The Bisq 2 reputation export is built from the same stream, so a
> BONDED_ROLE or UNDEFINED lockup with a lock time of at least the export
> minimum which was previously exported as reputation is no longer
> exported. This needs a check against the bundled mainnet DAO state before
> release.

> Track bonded-role lockups independently
> 
> A role had exactly one bond, chosen from the lockups carrying its role
> hash. Because publishing a lockup is permissionless, that made a third
> party's lockup able to change the role holder's bond state, and it hid
> the real lifecycle of every lockup which was not selected.
> 
> There is no reason to select. Build one BondedRole per valid role lockup,
> each with its own lifecycle, plus one READY_FOR_LOCKUP entry for an
> accepted role which has no valid lockup yet. Unlocking, illegally
> spending or confiscating one lockup then changes only that lockup, and
> several confirmed lockups for one role coexist without precedence.
> 
> Pending wallet states are applied per lockup afterwards, using the exact
> lockup transaction id, and the whole collection is rebuilt from DAO state
> on every update and cleared if a rebuild fails.

> Accept a signed witness from a trade only if it matches that trade
> 
> A malicious seller could embed a SignedWitness with an arbitrary date in
> the PayoutTxPublishedMessage. BuyerProcessPayoutTxPublishedMessage handed
> it to publishOwnSignedWitness, which published it with
> P2PService.addPersistableNetworkPayload. That API is meant for locally
> created data and skips the date tolerance check which remotely received
> payloads get in P2PDataStorage. The record was then added to the signed
> witness maps and to the persisted append-only store, which has no removal
> path. As no read path compares a stored witness date against the wall
> clock, the forged date became permanent local state. It falsifies the
> local sign age and trade limit, and it would be exported over the Bisq 2
> bridge if a bridge node ever processed trade messages.
> 
> The witness is not arbitrary data: it is exactly the witness the seller
> creates in signAndPublishAccountAgeWitness for this trade. Instead of
> checking the received fields one by one we therefore build that expected
> witness from our own validated trade data and accept the received one
> only if it is equal to it. The field list stays in one place, at the
> constructor, so a field added later is covered without changing the
> validation.
> 
> Two fields cannot be derived from the trade data:
> 
> - The signature. It is the reason why we cannot create the witness
>   ourselves, and it is verified against the now trusted account age
>   witness hash and signer key.
> - The date. A tolerance check against the current time is not applicable
>   here, because the message can be delivered late over the mailbox and
>   the date is then legitimately old. The seller signs when the payout
>   transaction gets published, so we require instead that the date is not
>   before the start of the trade and not in the future, with a one day
>   tolerance for clock differences between the peers. The bounds are
>   compared directly, so an extreme date value cannot overflow.
> 
> verifySigner asked whether the receiver of the signature is a signer.
> That is not the question at this point and it excluded the case that our
> first account gets signed, so that exactly the users who need the
> republish never got it. It now asks whether the signer was allowed to
> sign, looking up the witnesses owned by the signer key, the same way
> isValidSignerWitnessInternal walks up the chain and the same condition
> the seller checks in isSignWitnessTrade before signing. verifySigner has
> only this one call site, so no other behaviour changes.
> 
> AccountAgeWitnessService takes the expected values from the contract and
> the trade and passes them on. SignedWitnessService gets the Clock which
> is already bound in P2PModule and injected into AccountAgeWitnessService.

> Audit the bundled DAO state for duplicated merit issuances
> 
> Checks the shipped mainnet DAO state for a compensation issuance which is
> claimed by more than one blind vote of the same cycle, which is what the
> cycle wide uniqueness rule rejects from its activation height on. This
> answers whether the weakness was exploited before the rule exists, and it
> keeps answering that question whenever the bundled resource is updated.
> 
> The claims are validated with the production rules so that the audit
> cannot disagree with the implementation about which claim counts. The
> blind vote cycle is resolved through the vote reveal transaction which
> spent the blind vote stake output, so no block data is needed.
> 
> Two reported numbers guard against a vacuous result: a grouping which put
> every blind vote into its own group would report no duplicates whatever
> the data contains, so the audit also asserts that cycles do contain
> several blind votes and that issuances are claimed again in later cycles.

> Only allow a bond lockup output to be spent by an unlock tx
> 
> A lockup output is an ordinary P2WPKH output of the bond owner's wallet.
> Nothing in Bitcoin holds it, the lock time lives in the OP_RETURN and is
> applied by the parser, and only when the spend has the canonical unlock
> shape. Every other spend of a lockup output was accepted as an ordinary
> BSQ transfer, so the owner could recover the collateral in the next block
> with no lock time, and confiscateBond was left with no unlocking unspent
> output to reach.
> 
> That defeats the purpose of a bond. Confiscation needs a full DAO cycle
> and names its target in plaintext from the proposal phase on, while the
> recovery confirms in one block, so an owner who did not cooperate always
> won the race and did not even need to wait for a proposal to appear. The
> honest exit was protected by the lock time exactly as designed; the
> dishonest one had no lock time at all.
> 
> From the hard fork 3 activation height on, a tx which spends a lockup
> output and is not an unlock tx is invalid, so its BSQ is burnt rather
> than recovered. Burning costs the owner exactly what confiscation would,
> which restores the incentive the bond exists to create. One rule covers
> splitting the value, adding another input to break the exact value match,
> rolling the bond forward into a new lockup, spending several lockup
> outputs at once, spending in the same block as the lockup, and the
> boundary case where a lockup spend happens to match the unlock value
> pattern, which before produced a tx typed LOCKUP whose first output was
> an unlock output for a declared bond that did not exist.
> 
> Supporting changes which the rule requires to be watertight:
> 
> - BlockParser rejects a block whose transactions or transaction outputs
> carry block metadata other than that of the containing block, by
> throwing InvalidParsingConditionException before any state is mutated.
> The parser applies height gated consensus rules, including the
> activation check of this fork, to the height the tx and the output
> themselves claim, and the tx output key which addresses the UTXO set is
> derived from the output's own txId. Without the check an output could
> enter the UTXO set under a foreign key and replace a lockup output
> entry with an ordinary BSQ output, reopening the recovery this fork
> forbids. RpcService always stamps both levels from the containing block
> and tx, so only hand crafted data can trip this and no historical block
> is affected.
> 
> - A spend of a zero valued lockup output no longer falls out of parsing
> at the "no BSQ inputs" early return, from the activation height on.
> Otherwise the lockup output would be removed from the UTXO set without
> recording the tx which ended the bond as invalid.
> 
> - The burnt BSQ of an invalid tx now includes the value of prematurely
> spent unlock inputs, from the activation height on. TxInputParser moves
> that value from accumulatedInputValue to burntBondValue, so it was
> missing from the invalid tx accounting, while valid txs already
> included it. Before the fork the historical undercounting is preserved
> because burntBsq is part of the persisted and hashed DAO state.
> 
> - The activation height lookup is an exhaustive switch over
> BaseCurrencyNetwork, so the DAO dev networks map to the regtest height
> explicitly and a newly added network cannot be forgotten silently. The
> mapping is unchanged from the isMainnet/isTestnet ternary used by the
> earlier hard forks.
> 
> No Bisq client can produce any of the rejected shapes: isTxOutputSpendable
> returns false for a lockup output, so wallet coin selection never picks
> one. A scan of the shipped mainnet DAO state confirms the rule
> reclassifies nothing: of 187 lockup outputs, 85 have been spent and all 85
> by a formal unlock tx, and no tx has the boundary shape.
> 
> The tests drive real RawBlocks through the production BlockParser,
> TxParser and DaoStateService against a real DaoState; only PeriodService
> is a stub which is never consulted for the tx types used.
> LockupOutputSpendTest pins the pre fork behaviour, including the recovery
> this change forbids and the confiscation race the owner won.
> LockupOutputSpendHardForkTest covers the same shapes from the activation
> height on, and each burn is followed by the confiscation a pending
> proposal would still trigger, which must be a no-op rather than an error.
> It also covers the activation boundary itself, the honest unlock with an
> unrelated BTC fee input and change output, an illegal spend later in the
> same block, the combined lockup and premature unlock spend accounting,
> the zero valued lockup spend, and the block metadata validation at both
> the tx and the output level.
> 
> docs/specifications/dao/bond-lockup-spend.md records the resulting spend
> rules, the invariant they restore, the block data integrity requirements
> they depend on, and the activation and compatibility constraints.

> Preserve legacy bonded-role registrations before the cutoff
> 
> Requiring the bound registration format for every request invalidates
> every Bisq 2 bonded-role registration which exists today, including
> ORACLE_NODE, from which Bisq 2 bootstraps its authority. Those
> registrations were signed with a lockup key over the profile id alone,
> and there is no way for a holder to re-sign them before the bridge which
> verifies them is updated.
> 
> Accept protocol version 0 as the historical unbound format, bounded by
> the height of the lockup which backs it. A version 0 request must carry
> no transaction bindings and is accepted only if some confirmed valid
> lockup of the canonical accepted role matching the claimed name and role
> type was mined below the cutoff and has a first input key which verifies
> the signature over the profile id. A missing protobuf version selects it,
> so an unmodified Bisq 2 keeps working, and the previous REST route is
> restored for the same reason.
> 
> Version 1 stays the only format which can authorize a lockup at or above
> the cutoff.

> Make the payload date tolerance check overflow safe
> 
> SignedWitness.isDateInTolerance and AccountAgeWitness.isDateInTolerance
> used Math.abs(clock.millis() - date) <= TOLERANCE. The date is taken
> from a network payload, so a peer can choose any long value. For
> date = now + Long.MIN_VALUE the subtraction overflows to Long.MIN_VALUE,
> and Math.abs(Long.MIN_VALUE) is still negative, so the comparison
> returned true and the payload passed the date check of the P2P layer.
> 
> Exploiting this requires hitting the recipient's clock at millisecond
> precision, but repeated attempts with different date candidates raise
> the chance, and input validation should reject the whole hostile value
> range deterministically.
> 
> Replace the difference calculation with two direct bound comparisons
> (now - TOLERANCE <= date <= now + TOLERANCE). These cannot overflow
> because only the trusted clock value takes part in the arithmetic.
> 
> Add boundary tests for both classes covering the exact tolerance
> bounds, one millisecond outside each bound, Long.MIN_VALUE,
> Long.MAX_VALUE and the overflowing date value.

> Discard superseded trade statistics async results
> 
> The trade statistics screen runs asynchronous refilter and chart
> calculations in the view model and builds the table rows in the
> view, from several triggers: currency change, tick unit change, the
> trade statistics set change and activate. An older calculation could
> complete after a newer request and overwrite the model data, the
> chart items or the table with an outdated result.
> 
> Each refilter, chart calculation and table build now takes a
> generation when it starts on the user thread and applies its result
> only if the generation is still current, so superseded results are
> dropped. The table build also snapshots the observable list and the
> sort comparator on the user thread and sorts off it, so it no longer
> reads JavaFX state from the background thread.
> 
> Fixes #8018
> 
> Reference: https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/pull/8022
> Author: https://github.com/fenlark

> Protect witness privacy in bridge exports
> 
> Successful account-age and signed-witness ownership responses exposed the public Bisq 1 witness hash indirectly through authorized Bisq 2 data and returned millisecond-precise dates, creating direct cross-network correlation handles.
> 
> After ownership and trust-chain verification, derive a shared domain-separated 32-byte nullifier from the exact historical witness preimage and return only the fixed one-day UTC bucket containing the authoritative date. Keep the raw hash and exact date private for proof verification and oracle-local duplicate handling. Bisq 2 uses the bucket's latest millisecond for conservative scoring, limiting under-credit to at most one whole day while documenting the remaining correlation tradeoff.
> 
> Reserve the retired exact-date response name and field number, and place dateBucket and witnessNullifier on new tags. Old oracles therefore see their required date as absent, while current oracles reject legacy responses missing the new fields, making staggered upgrades fail closed in both directions.
> 
> Update both bridge services, protobuf responses, specifications, golden vectors, bucket checks, and ownership-response tests. This changes the coordinated, not-yet-activated version-2 bridge contract and requires the matching Bisq 2 oracle deployment.
>

> 
> The proposal display showed the required bond but left the unlock time as
> a TODO, so the two bond terms which a role proposal carries were only
> half visible. Both are attacker-chosen fields of the proposal payload
> below the hard-fork-3 activation height, and the required bond is the

> could therefore not see that an otherwise normal looking role proposal
> carried a one-block unlock time instead of the role type's term.

> bond details window. Both fields are read from the proposal rather than
> from the role type constants, so a proposal whose terms deviate from its
> role type shows the deviating value instead of the expected one.

> box it observes rather than after one of them.

> Fix empty trade statistics chart regression
> 
> The activate() handler gated the corrective chart recompute behind
> task2Done.getNow(false). An early refilter during activation could then
> compute a chart while the USD-average maps were still empty, hitting an
> NPE in ChartCalculations.getUpdateChartResult, and the gate skipped the
> recompute that would have repaired it, leaving the chart empty for the
> session. Call applyAsyncChartData unconditionally (chartGeneration drops
> superseded results) and use getOrDefault so a not-yet-populated map does
> not NPE. A regression test covers the empty-map path.
> 
> Also tighten the async lifecycle: deactivate() now advances the refilter,
> chart, and USD-map generations, and the USD-map apply gains a generation
> guard like the other two, so an in-flight result cannot repopulate the
> model after cleanup. Drop the view's now-redundant deactivateCalled field
> and the two stale volatile modifiers, since the generation guard alone
> drops stale builds.
> 
> Reference: https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/pull/8022
> Author: https://github.com/fenlark

> Add fail-closed DAO signature verification
> 
> Callers which have to try several candidate keys cannot use verify()
> directly, because a wrong key, a malformed key and a malformed signature
> throw different exceptions and only one of them means "not this key".
> 
> Add isValidSignature() which catches every exception and returns false,
> so a caller can try candidates uniformly without special casing, and no
> caller can accidentally treat a malformed input as a successful
> verification.

> Enforce consistent locale and encoding for reproducible builds
> 
> If a build is executed on machines with different native locales or
> character sets, the resulting binary artifacts can differ. Tools like
> Javadoc or code generators might output different date formats,
> alphabetical sorting, or localized text.
> 
> This pins the Gradle JVM's system properties to UTF-8 and en_US,
> aligning with the JVM guidelines from reproducible-builds.org.
> This ensures our build artifacts remain bit-for-bit identical
> regardless of the host environment (CI or local developer machine).

> Authorize bonded roles with proposal keys
> 
> Verification accepted a signature from the first input key of any
> confirmed lockup carrying the role hash. Publishing a lockup is
> permissionless, so anyone could bond an accepted role and then register
> as its holder in Bisq 2, ORACLE_NODE included.
> 
> A lockup proves only that someone published a transaction carrying the
> role hash. The DAO accepted binding of a name and role type to an
> identity is the role proposal, so the first input key of the canonical
> accepted proposal transaction is the only identity, with no fallback.
> 
> verifyBondedRole now takes the whole registration and requires the
> protocol version, resolves the proposal transaction id to the canonical
> accepted proposal, checks that its role matches the claimed name and
> type, resolves the named lockup as a valid lockup of that exact role,
> requires it to be LOCKUP_TX_CONFIRMED, and verifies the signature over
> the canonical message. Naming the proposal also disambiguates roles which
> share a name and role type, so the previous rule of accepting any of
> several candidate keys is no longer needed.
- b0d84440c19a37c6993c158ac4043b599b24dc07 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/b0d84440c19a37c6993c158ac4043b599b24dc07
> common: replace SignalHandler with ShutdownHook
> 
> The current shutdown implementation traps INT and TERM signals
> using the internal JDK classes Signal and SignalHandler.
> 
> These APIs are part of the internal JDK and are strongly
> encapsulated starting with JDK 17, making them inaccessible on
> modern JVMs. In addition, this mechanism only works on Unix-like
> systems (macOS and Linux) where these signals are available.
> 
> Replace the signal-based shutdown handling with a JVM
> ShutdownHook. This provides a supported and portable way to
> perform graceful shutdown across JVM versions and platforms.

> Validate peer timestamps with overflow-safe bounds
> 
> Several validators compared a peer controlled timestamp with the local time by
> calculating a difference: Math.abs(now - peerTimestamp) <= tolerance. That check is
> not correct for extreme values. The subtraction overflows, and Math.abs(Long.MIN_VALUE)
> stays negative, so a peer date of now + Long.MIN_VALUE passed a positive tolerance
> check. Affected were TradeValidation.checkPeersDate (4 hours),
> AccountAgeWitnessService.verifyPeersCurrentDate (1 day) and
> BsqSwapTakeOfferRequestVerification.isDateInTolerance (10 minutes). The peer has to hit
> the local clock of the victim to the exact millisecond, but the BSQ swap path can be
> retried by the peer.
> 
> Changed code paths:
> 
> - DateUtil.isWithinBounds(timestamp, lowerBound, upperBound) compares a value with
>   explicit inclusive bounds. An inverted range contains no value, thus it accepts
>   nothing instead of throwing. Bounds can come from independent sources, for instance
>   a stored trade date and the local clock, and validation of untrusted data must fail
>   closed instead of letting the caller fail with an exception.
> - DateUtil.isWithinTolerance(timestamp, reference, tolerance) derives the bounds from a
>   reference value and saturates them at Long.MIN_VALUE and Long.MAX_VALUE, so no
>   subtraction on peer data can overflow.
> - The three validators listed above use isWithinTolerance now, as do the freshness
>   checks of the SignedWitness and AccountAgeWitness payloads, which already compared
>   bounds directly. SignedWitnessService.isSignDateInTradeRange uses isWithinBounds for
>   its asymmetric window and now rejects instead of throwing if the local clock is more
>   than two days behind the stored trade date.
> - verifyPeersCurrentDate uses the injected clock instead of a new Date(), so it can be
>   verified with a controlled clock. It is package scope for that reason.
> - XmrTxProofParser keeps the one sided rule for the timestamp of the Monero transaction
>   used as payment proof: the transaction must not be older than the trade date minus the
>   tolerance of 2 hours, which prevents that an already existing transaction is presented
>   as payment proof. The subtraction is done on the local trade date, thus a hostile
>   explorer API cannot drive it into an overflow. A symmetric window would reject the
>   normal case of a buyer paying more than 2 hours after taking the offer and would break
>   the automatic confirmation for a large part of the XMR trades.
> 
> Behaviour change: the BSQ swap tolerance boundary moves from exclusive to inclusive, so
> a request which is exactly 10 minutes off is accepted now. This makes the check
> consistent with the account age and signed witness checks, which are inclusive. No
> protocol message, persisted data or serialized format is affected.
> 
> Specifications: docs/specifications/network/peer-timestamp-validation.md defines the
> invariant for peer supplied freshness timestamps, the current tolerances and the fail
> closed rule for bounds validation. docs/specifications/trade/xmr-payment-proof-timestamp.md
> defines the one sided rule of the XMR payment proof and why it has no upper bound.
> 
> Tests: DateUtilTest covers the bounds, the saturation edges, a zero tolerance, the
> inverted range and the value which defeats a Math.abs based check. TradeValidationTest,
> BsqSwapTakeOfferRequestVerificationTest and AccountAgeWitnessServiceTest reject extreme
> peer dates. SignedWitnessServiceTest covers the case of a local clock behind the trade
> start date. XmrTxProofParserTest asserts that a transaction confirmed 20 hours after the
> trade start is accepted and that an extreme timestamp is rejected. The disabled test
> AccountAgeWitnessServiceTest.testIsTradeDateAfterReleaseDate is active again;
> isDateAfterReleaseDate keeps its exclusive boundary and its direct comparison, which
> carries no overflow risk. ./gradlew :common:test :core:test passes.

> the exception and log a warning instead.

> removing it and belongs next to the known gap in bonded-roles.md 7.

> is always built with BONDED_ROLE or REPUTATION, but the reason byte is
> only checked for mapping to a known enum value, so a hand-built
> transaction can. Whether any such output exists in mainnet history is
> unverified.
