- d198101751263174b3ce574cd6881beece29454e — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/d198101751263174b3ce574cd6881beece29454e
> Count a merit issuance at most once per cycle
> 
> Merit consensus V2 rejects a merit list which claims the same issuance
> twice, but it evaluates each blind vote on its own. A contributor could
> therefore publish several blind votes in one cycle, each carrying a merit
> list re-signed for its own blind vote transaction id, and have the same
> merit counted once per blind vote. Every list is genuine, so no rule of
> V2 is violated. The extra vote weight costs only the blind vote fee per
> blind vote and does not scale with the merit being multiplied, so a past
> contributor could buy an arbitrary multiple of their own merit.
> 
> An issuance claimed by more than one blind vote of the cycle is now
> counted for none of them. Awarding it to one blind vote instead would let
> whoever holds a stolen issuance key take the merit, and a tie break on
> transaction ids would be grindable, so dropping every copy is the option
> which leaves nothing to gain.
> 
> Only claims which passed the full validation take part in the duplicate
> detection. Collecting the claimed issuance ids before validating them
> would let anyone name other voters' issuances with invalid signatures and
> thereby erase their merit, which would be a cheaper attack than the one
> this rule closes.
> 
> The rule activates with hard fork 3. The V2 activation height has passed
> and cycles have been evaluated under its rules, so tightening those rules
> in place would change results which are already derived and persisted.
> 
> This is only the consensus rule; it is not applied by the vote result
> calculation yet.

> Define versioned bonded-role registration messages
> 
> A Bisq 2 bonded-role registration currently proves only that the signer
> holds the key of some lockup carrying the role hash. Binding it to one
> exact lockup requires a canonical message which Bisq 1 and Bisq 2 both
> compute the same way, and a version so the two formats can be told apart
> rather than inferred from empty fields.
> 
> BondedRoleRegistration carries the request fields including the protocol
> version. BondedRoleRegistrationSignature builds the signed message as the
> SHA-256 digest of the domain tag, proposal transaction id, lockup
> transaction id and profile id, each UTF-8 encoded and prefixed by its
> four-byte big-endian length.
> 
> The message carries no network or DAO instance identifier, because both
> transaction ids are resolved against the verifier's own DAO state and a
> signature made against another chain cannot verify there. The test pins
> the digest rather than recomputing it, since Bisq 2 has to reproduce the
> preimage byte for byte.

> 
> The merit stake is a property of the blind vote, not of the individual
> ballot, so it has the same value for every ballot of that blind vote.
> It was recomputed inside the ballot loop, which repeated the ECDSA
> verification of every merit entry once per ballot. The merit list is
> attacker supplied and this runs in the consensus critical vote result
> calculation, so the repetition is unnecessary work proportional to the
> number of proposals in the cycle.

> Behaviour is unchanged: the merit stake is still derived only when the
> blind vote has at least one ballot, with the same arguments, and an
> exception from the derivation still aborts the vote result calculation.
> 
> This addresses the concern behind the external patch which introduced a
> signature verification cache on the Merit object. Caching inside Merit
> is not applicable here because the verification key is taken from the
> DAO state issuance rather than from the untrusted embedded issuance.
- e5d6c181f8563a353ee6cb093defb33579547504 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/e5d6c181f8563a353ee6cb093defb33579547504
> Let the max heap scale with the machine RAM
> 
> The desktop ships -XX:MaxRAM=8g without an explicit -Xmx. HotSpot
> ergonomics size the max heap at 25% of MaxRAM, and an explicit
> MaxRAM replaces the detected physical RAM, so every installation
> runs with a 2 GiB max heap regardless of the machine. This matches
> the "Max memory: 2 GB" Profiler lines in the recent heap space
> reports. Verified with -XX:+PrintFlagsFinal: MaxRAM=8g yields
> MaxHeapSize 2 GiB regardless of the installed RAM.
> 
> With -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=50 the max heap scales with the machine:
> 2 GiB on a 4 GB machine as before, 4 GiB on 8 GB and so on.
> Machines below 4 GB get a smaller max heap; the old setting
> promised them a heap larger than their physical RAM, which ends in
> swapping or the OS OOM killer rather than useful headroom.
> -XX:MaxHeapFreeRatio=10 keeps returning unused memory to the OS as
> before.
> 
> The explicit -XX:+UseCompressedOops caps the ergonomic heap at the
> compressed oops limit of about 30 GiB. Without it machines with
> more than about 60 GB RAM would get a larger heap with compressed
> oops silently disabled, which doubles the reference size.
> 
> The packaging and app start plugins both read
> applicationDefaultJvmArgs, so the installer and run-from-source
> pick up the change alike. Seed nodes already run with a fixed
> 4 GiB heap and are not affected.
> 
> Same approach as the MaxRAM bumps after the 2021 OOM wave (#5550,
> #5609).

> Run node-specific shutdown once and keep the requested exit status
> 
> SeedNodeMain and BridgeMain overrode gracefulShutDown, shut down their
> own services and only then called super. The guard against a repeated
> request sits inside the parent method, so the service shutdown of the
> subclass ran before the guard and therefore ran again on every repeated
> request. Both now override the new shutDownAdditionalServices() hook,
> which the parent calls after the guard and inside its try block, and
> gracefulShutDown is final so the mistake cannot come back. An exception
> in that hook no longer prevents the final persistence flush and the
> exit.
> 
> The exit status was a volatile field shared by all requests, so a
> failure request arriving while a normal shutdown was still running
> replaced the status of that shutdown. It is now a parameter of a private
> gracefulShutDown overload: the first request fixes the value and a later
> request only joins. A failure status that gets dropped that way is
> logged.
> 
> Failure paths exit with status 1 instead of 0: an uncaught error and a
> DAO state checkpoint mismatch. seednode/bisq.service sets
> Restart=on-failure, so with status 0 systemd did not restart a node that
> ran out of memory. handleUncaughtException also logs the throwable
> instead of always reporting an OutOfMemoryError.
> 
> shutDown and checkMemory no longer take a GracefulShutDownHandler. Every
> caller passed this, and the branch for a different handler dropped the
> requested failure status without notice.
> 
> BtcNodeMonitorMain memoizes the shutdown future, so a repeated request
> joins the running service shutdown instead of starting a second one. The
> join is separated from the completion handler because ProxySetup and
> PeerGroupService complete their future with an error in normal
> situations; a Tor shutdown regularly needs longer than the 2 second
> timeout used there. Before, the exception from join skipped the
> completion handler, so the JVM shutdown hook waited its full 2 minutes
> on every such shutdown. A termination signal that arrives before the
> constructor assigned the monitor is handled as well, in the same way as
> SeedNodeMain handles it for its seed node.
> 
> RestApi stops its http server through the new hook. A shutdown started
> inside the application (checkpoint failure, memory limit, periodic
> restart, connection loss) does not pass RestApiMain and left the
> endpoints answering while the services behind them were already closed.
> 
> The specification states the two rules that were missing: the
> single-entry rule covers the service shutdown of subclasses, and a later
> failure request must not change the exit status captured by a running
> normal shutdown. New tests cover the repeated request, both orders of a
> normal and a failure request, a failing subclass shutdown, and the two
> BtcNodeMonitorMain cases.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

> lockup.

> and the protocol version. It also rejects requests while the DAO state is
> not ready and in sync, with FAILED_PRECONDITION, so a node which is
> behind cannot answer an authorization question, and it no longer logs the
> signature.

#### 5. v1.10.8 / v1.10.8

item_id: bisq-network/bisq::release::389797327
Data: 2026-09-16T14:57:35Z
URL: https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/releases/tag/v1.10.8

Release notes (texto original):

> ## Release notes
> 
> This is an important security update that fixes vulnerabilities identified during our recent security audit.
> Updating to this version is required to continue trading.
> 
> ## Security
> 
> - Refund payouts require validated escrow evidence and authenticated claimant/agent authorization.
> - Replayed refund receipts and cross-chain payout reservations are blocked.
> - Refund transaction provenance, finality, receiver outputs, and transaction IDs are validated.
> - Burning Man proposal inputs and address-list resources fail closed when invalid or obsolete.
> - DAO readiness is revoked after checkpoint failure, and BSQ swap signatures require exact publication handoffs.
> - Update to latest tor version
> 
> ## Trading
> 
> - Altcoin amounts honor registered precision and zero-rounded amounts are rejected.
> - Deposit liveness handling uses broadcast evidence and configured explorer scope.
> - Withdrawals complete after commit, obsolete mediation results are ignored, and unknown BTC fee receivers are rejected.
> - Security deposits remain editable down to the minimum floor.
> 
> ## Reliability and Builds
> 
> - Shutdown sequencing is safer across JavaFX, network, Tor, broadcaster, and desktop components.
> - Store checks avoid copying the full store.
> - Reproducible Debian packaging, Docker builds, Gradle configuration cache, and Gradle 9.0.0 support are included.
> 
> ## Installation
> 
> ### macOS
> 
> Bisq does not use Apple's notarization process (see [why](https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/discussions/6341)).
> For that reason you will see that (misleading) alert:
> \<img src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e058c34c-38f5-4329-8fc5-f48b3f2ba4dd" width="180"/>
> Grant permissions by:
> 
> - run `sudo xattr -rd com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Bisq.app` in a terminal (type Terminal in the Apple search box)
> - open `Bisq` again
> 
> More details can be found [here](https://bisq.wiki/Downloading_and_installing#OS-specific_install_notes).
> 
> ### Windows
> 
> For similar reasons you will get that warning at Windows: _**Windows protected your PC**_
> 
> - Click the `More info` button when prompted
> - Click the `Run anyway` button when prompted
> 
> More details can be found [here](https://bisq.wiki/Downloading_and_installing#OS-specific_install_notes).
> 
> ### Verify download
> 
> See the [verification and installation instructions](https://bisq.wiki/Downloading_and_installing) in the Bisq Wiki.

> Abort destructive flows when offer removal failed
> 
> removeAllOpenOffers scheduled its completion handler after a drain
> delay regardless of the removal outcomes, and a failed removal leaves
> the offer locally persisted and alive on the offer book. Restoring the
> wallet from seed words and emptying the wallet, which promise the user
> that the open offers are removed first, proceeded anyway; the BSQ swap
> proof-of-work redo minted and published a mutated-id replacement next
> to the old offer, creating a duplicate the periodic refresh keeps
> alive. Before this branch a pre-bootstrap removal failure aborted
> those flows by accident, through the synchronous exception thrown
> before the completion was scheduled; converting it into an error
> report widened the window, and a removal rejected by the local store
> took the unsafe continuation already on master.
> 
> Aggregate the removal outcomes: the batch removal reports success only
> when every single removal succeeded, decided after the existing drain
> delay, and names the failed offers otherwise. Wallet restore and
> wallet emptying abort with a popup on the error outcome; the redo
> mints the replacement only from the removal success handler and
> otherwise leaves the old offer for the next activation to retry. The
> fire-and-forget removal overload is gone, its only caller was the
> redo. The wallet-empty exception logging switches from printStackTrace
> to the standard logger call along the way.

> Do not copy the whole store to test membership
> 
> Every incoming AddPersistableNetworkPayloadMessage is checked for a
> duplicate hash before it is stored, in addPersistableNetworkPayload.
> The check went through AppendOnlyDataStoreService.getMap(payload), which
> for a HistoricalDataStoreService returns getMapOfAllData(): a fresh
> HashMap holding a copy of the live map plus every historical payload.
> The two historical stores, TradeStatistics3 and AccountAgeWitness, hold
> hundreds of thousands of entries, so a single message allocated a
> full-store copy on the user thread only to answer one containsKey.
> 
> The message runs on the user thread, the JavaFX thread on desktop, so
> the copy competes with the UI, and it happens before the payload is
> otherwise validated, so a rejected payload costs the same as a stored
> one. A peer can keep this up within the normal message rate.
> 
> Add AppendOnlyDataStoreService.containsKey, which delegates to the
> service that handles the payload. HistoricalDataStoreService overrides
> it to look the hash up in the live map and the historical map directly,
> without merging them, the same test its own put and putIfAbsent already
> used. getMap stays for the callers that need the map itself.

> Reject altcoin volume that rounds to zero
> 
> An altcoin volume below half of one on-chain unit rounds to zero and
> getAdjustedAltcoinVolume documents that callers must reject it, but no
> core caller did. A fixed-price offer priced far enough above the market
> could therefore be placed and taken with no payment obligation.
> 
> Reject the zero at the three trust boundaries:
> 
> - ValidateOffer checks volume and min volume at offer placement,
>   covering the desktop, API and cloned offers. Rounding is monotonic in
>   the amount, so a positive min volume also keeps every partial take
>   amount of a compliant offer above zero at an unchanged price.
> - TakeOfferModel rejects the taker side, covering the API take path for
>   offers that bypassed placement validation, e.g. crafted ones, edited
>   ones or market-priced offers whose price has risen far since
>   placement.
> - MakerProcessesInputsForDepositTxRequest rejects the trade volume on
>   the maker for take requests from modified clients against such
>   offers. The maker trade has no price until the taker's validated
>   price is applied, so the check runs after that point.
> 
> The desktop take screen additionally disables the take button and shows
> a validation message instead of failing later in the protocol.

> TxBroadcaster tracked only one timer per transaction ID. After an attempt timed out, a late result from it could remove a newer attempt's timer and suppress the newer callback. > Prevent replayed refund receipts from creating repeat payouts
> 
> Refund-agent payouts were guarded only by a transient flag on one dispute row, while the dispute replay check intentionally permits the two peer rows sharing a deposit and delayed-payout transaction. A second row or restart could therefore create another refund-wallet spend from the same evidence. > Publish the deposit from the buyer account reveal for fiat trades only
> 
> Deferring deposit publication until the buyer payment account is validated
> applies to fiat trades. For a crypto trade the publisher has no gate, so the
> deposit is broadcast as soon as the delayed-payout signature response has
> been processed.
> 
> The reveal handler decided to append SellerPublishesDepositTx from the trade
> phase and the prepared deposit transaction alone. The phase advances only in
> the asynchronous broadcast callback, so while the first broadcast was still
> pending the handler saw an unpublished trade and appended the publisher
> again. The buyer sends ShareBuyerPaymentAccountMessage for every trade
> directly after it processed the deposit message, which arrives well inside
> the broadcast timeout. A crypto trade taken by a BTC seller therefore
> requested a second broadcast of the deposit transaction almost every time.
> 
> Restrict the decision to fiat offers, which is the only case where
> publication was deferred and where the reveal is a publication prerequisite.
> 
> The specification already scoped this mechanism to fiat trades and required
> that repeated messages must not cause a second logical publication. State
> both explicitly, together with the requirement that a second publication
> attempt must not disturb a pending broadcast.
>

> Require verified trader contract signatures on refund disputes
> 
> DisputeValidation.validateDisputeData called Sig.verify for the maker and
> taker contract signatures but ignored its boolean result, so any well-formed
> signature passed. It also accepted a refund dispute that carried only the
> opener's signature. The refund agent pays a direct refund to the payout
> addresses of the dispute-carried contract; the contract hash, the escrow
> script and the escrow value do not commit those addresses independently of
> the opener. A dispute opener with a modified client could therefore present
> a self-consistent contract with the peer's payout address replaced and
> collect the peer's refund share. Report 8b listed both trader signatures as
> a required fix; this closes that gap.

> (MakerCreateAndSignContract, TakerVerifyAndSignContract,
> BuyerProcessDepositTxAndDelayedPayoutTxMessage,
> SellerProcessShareBuyerPaymentAccountMessage), and the agent forwards both to
> the peer, so legitimate refund cases are unaffected. Mediation disputes keep
> optional signatures because the mediated payout is built by the traders from
> their own contract.

> updated in refund-delayed-payout-validation.md and referenced from

> Report sync P2P failures via offer book handlers
> 
> P2PService throws NetworkNotReadyException synchronously while the
> network is not bootstrapped. OfferBookService passed that exception
> through to its callers, bypassing their error handlers: an edit of an
> active offer then left the offer stuck in edit mode until restart,
> because editOpenOfferStart never reached the error path clearing
> offersToBeEdited.
> 
> Convert the exception to an operation-specific error message directly
> at the P2P call in addOffer, removeOffer and refreshTTL. This keeps
> the handling at the boundary, so an exception thrown by a success
> callback is not misreported as a failure of the operation itself.
> 
> Call sites that passed no-op or null error handlers now log the
> failure with the offer id: the shutdown removal, the single-argument
> removeOpenOffer used by removeAllOpenOffers and the wallet-restore
> path, and the not-in-list removal fallback. Before, a pre-bootstrap
> failure on those paths disappeared without a trace once the exception
> no longer reached the global exception handler; on the wallet-restore
> path that let the restore replace the wallet while the open offers
> were never withdrawn.
> 
> Behaviour note: a pre-bootstrap publish failure in the edit flow now
> routes into the existing republish retry path instead of aborting the
> edit, so an API edit returns OK once the offer is edited locally; the
> offer is published by the bootstrap republish. activateOffer's
> parameters are no longer marked nullable, matching addOffer which it
> delegates to.
> 
> Covered by OfferBookServiceTest for the three conversions, asserting
> the exact operation-specific messages and that the P2P call was
> attempted, and by OpenOfferManagerTest for the edit flow.

> Resolve the bitcoinj listener executor at dispatch time
> 
> WalletsSetup captured UserThread.getExecutor() into Threading.USER_THREAD
> once at wallet setup. bitcoinj resolves that executor when a listener is
> registered, so every wallet and peer-group listener stayed bound to the
> JavaFX Platform.runLater executor. After UserThread.executeAtShutdown moved
> the UserThread to the shutdown executor, wallet events raised by
> walletsSetup.shutDown() on the JVM-hook path still ran domain listeners on
> the JavaFX thread while the shutdown executor serialised the same state for
> the persistence flush.
> 
> Assign UserThread::execute instead, which resolves the current UserThread
> executor per dispatch. Before the transition this is the same JavaFX
> executor; after it the listeners follow the shutdown executor as the
> graceful-shutdown specification requires. The specification records the
> rule for library callbacks registered before the transition.
> 
> No behaviour change on the controlled shutdown path or at runtime.
> 
> Verification: ./gradlew :core:test --tests 'bisq.core.support.dispute.refund.*'

> Accept deposit-tx message in DEPOSIT_CONFIRMED
> 
> The buyer's handler for DepositTxAndDelayedPayoutTxMessage accepts the
> message only in the TAKER_FEE_PUBLISHED and DEPOSIT_PUBLISHED phases.
> The deposit can confirm independently through the wallet listener,
> moving the trade to DEPOSIT_CONFIRMED before the (mailbox) message is
> processed. The phase gate then rejects it: no ACK is sent and the
> mailbox entry is not removed, so it is redelivered and re-rejected on
> every restart until its TTL. As a result the seller's payment account
> payload is never stored, both sides keep a hash-only contract, and the
> trade is permanently stuck.
> 
> The symmetric seller handler for ShareBuyerPaymentAccountMessage already
> accepts DEPOSIT_CONFIRMED. Add the same phase to the buyer gate. The
> existing preCondition still prevents reprocessing: it proceeds only
> while the payment account payload is missing and otherwise just resends
> the ACK.
> 
> The accepted phases move to a @VisibleForTesting constant, and a
> regression test pins the list (including DEPOSIT_CONFIRMED), mirroring
> STARTUP_RESEND_PAYMENT_STARTED_STATES.

> fix(bridge): serialize snapshot subscription setup with block publication
> 
> subscribeWithSnapshot registered the observer inside a task submitted to
> notifyObserversExecutor. onParseBlockCompleteAfterBatchProcessing checks the
> observer sets on the caller thread and returns early when both are empty, so a
> block parsed while the registration task was still queued was never delivered to
> that subscriber. The client recovered it through the backfill, since the ready
> height was read after the registration, but the ordering was invisible to
> subscribeWithSnapshot callers and left BsqBlockGrpcServiceTest flaky.
> 
> Register the observer and read the chain height on the calling thread, and keep
> only the subscriptionReadyHeight event on the executor. Registering before
> reading the height means a block parsed in between is delivered on the stream and
> may also fall within the snapshot range, which is a duplicate rather than a gap.
> 
> That alone would let a block queue ahead of the ready event, because the observer
> becomes visible to the block capture before its ready task is submitted. Guard
> both sequences with snapshotSubscriptionLock so that registration and readiness
> submission are atomic against observer capture and block submission. An observer
> present in the capture therefore already has its ready event queued, and the
> single threaded executor delivers it first.
> 
> Snapshot observers are captured when the block is raised, so a client subscribing
> afterwards cannot receive the block ahead of its ready event; the height it gets
> already covers the block, so it backfills via requestBsqBlocks. Plain subscribers
> keep live iteration since they have no such handshake and no backfill signal.

> Handle malformed historical refund receipt rows safely
> 
> Older releases could retain refund disputes with malformed funding transaction IDs. Strictly parsing every stored row made one bad row abort reservation for unrelated tickets, while treating the whole row as unmatchable discarded valid prior-payout evidence when only one ID was malformed.
> 
> For paid stored rows, compare both funding IDs independently and ignore only malformed fields. A valid matching ID remains receipt-consumption evidence, while rows without a complete funding chain are not marked during reservation. Continue to parse the selected payout ticket strictly, so malformed tickets cannot authorize funds.
>

> floors the actual deposit at the minimum BTC amount (shown next to the

> view models: those views are cached and reused, so a lock left behind
> by a previous session would otherwise block editing of perfectly valid
> offers, and an unchanged amount string would leave the field stuck in
> the locked state.

> Gate the dead-deposit verdict on broadcast evidence
> 
> The unknown-to-all-explorers verdict was derived from the trade age
> and a single lookup. Both are wrong ways to measure it:
> 
> - The seller sends DepositTxAndDelayedPayoutTxMessage before
>   publishing the deposit tx, and fiat publication even waits for its
>   delivery, so a buyer can hold a signed deposit tx which was never
>   broadcast. The explorers truthfully not knowing it is no evidence
>   of death then; the seller can still publish it later. The verdict
>   now requires broadcast evidence on the buyer: the network-sighting
>   state when the wallet saw the tx before the message arrived, or
>   broadcast peers observed on the committed tx afterwards. That
>   evidence is persisted with the wallet; an SPV resync wipes it, in
>   which case no verdict is derived. The seller has evidence by
>   construction, since he reaches the confirmation step only by
>   broadcasting himself. The 24 hour threshold remains as a trigger
>   heuristic for the lookup.
> - A tx broadcast moments ago may not have reached the explorers, and
>   the verdict could be arbitrarily old by the time the user acts on
>   it. Moving the trade now re-checks the explorers when the action is
>   invoked and is only authorized by a fresh unanimous not-found
>   answer arriving at least 30 minutes after the first one. A
>   transport failure blocks the action, a provider knowing the tx
>   cancels the verdict, and a verdict revoked by a concurrent lookup
>   while the re-check was running is treated as found.
> 
> The confirmation dialog no longer claims that funds are locked: the
> dead-deposit case gets its own text stating that the verdict is
> external and the move reversible.

>

> when the callback is attached, so the callback runs synchronously at

> included, while the API contract pinned by the e2e suite is that the
> memo is not yet persisted before confirmation. Restore the original
> relative order. With every step guarded on its own, attaching the
> callback first no longer risks a synchronously thrown handler failure
> suppressing the mempool publish, which was the reason it had been
> moved to the end.

> fix(bridge): keep observer error signalling best effort
> 
> An already closed gRPC stream rejects onError, which is the state reached right
> after onNext failed on a disconnected client. ManagedStreamObserver ran its
> deregistration callback only after delegate.onError returned, so a rejecting
> delegate left the dead observer registered and it failed again on every later
> block. The throw also escaped the notification loop, skipping the remaining
> observers, and then escaped publishBlock into an unobserved CompletableFuture.
> 
> Deregister in a finally so cleanup no longer depends on the delegate, and let
> notifyOnError swallow and log a failed signal so one observer cannot stop the
> others from being notified.
> 
> The interleaving test now records uncaught exceptions from its threads, so a
> thread dying surfaces directly instead of as an invocation count mismatch.

> Show update popup only once per session
> 
> The software update alert can be delivered to a running node more
> than once. When its P2P storage entry expires or gets removed,
> AlertManager clears alertMessageProperty or falls back to another
> alert, and a later re-receipt sets the property again with an alert
> for an update that was already shown. The listener in BisqSetup
> then fires again and queues another update popup, so the user gets
> the same update window again right after closing the first one.
> 
> The normal message alert branch already guards against repeats by
> comparing user.getDisplayedAlert(), but the update branch has no
> such check and the persisted displayedAlert cannot be used for it
> as the popup should be shown again in a new session as a reminder.
> 
> We keep track of the alert versions shown in this session and skip
> repeated popups for them. The session guard uses the same version
> key as the persisted dont-show-again preference. Opening the popup
> from the footer link is not affected and an alert for a new version
> still shows.
> 
> BisqSetupTest covers the guard behavior.
> 
> Fixes #7936

> Report a late broadcast failure as a notification
> 
> onWithdrawRequest invoked the result handler once the withdraw tx was
> committed and additionally the fault handler when the broadcast failed
> later, so one request could produce two terminal outcomes: the desktop
> path showed a success and then a failure popup, and the API threw from
> a future callback into a call it had already answered, swallowed by
> the executor. The trade was closed by then, so the fault suggested a
> failure which could no longer be acted on.
> 
> Give the late broadcast failure its own handler. The fault handler is
> now strictly for a failed commit, which leaves the trade open and
> retryable; an unchecked failure before the commit propagates to the
> caller as the single outcome. The broadcast failure handler is a
> notification about an already completed withdrawal: the desktop shows
> a popup on the UserThread saying the tx remains in the wallet as
> pending, the API logs it. Pending txs are re-broadcast at startup and
> published via mempool nodes right away.
> 
> Also guard the post-commit steps inside both sendFunds variants, so an
> unchecked exception from the best-effort memo, mempool publish or
> callback attach cannot surface a committed send as a failure. The
> callback is attached last, so an already failed future whose handler
> throws synchronously cannot suppress the mempool publish.

> Keep a pending tx broadcast intact when it is requested twice
> 
> Calling TxBroadcaster.broadcastTx twice with the same transaction is API
> misuse, but the reaction to it destroyed the state of the call that was
> already in flight. The duplicate call ran stopAndRemoveTimer for the txId,
> so the first call lost its timeout timer. The timeout could then no longer
> fire, and the peer group success handler skips a broadcast whose timer is
> gone. The first caller therefore never received any callback, even though
> the transaction had been committed to the wallet and propagated to the
> network. On top of that the duplicate call committed and broadcast the same
> transaction again.
> 
> For the seller deposit publication this turned a harmless duplicate request
> into a permanently stuck trade: the deposit transaction was mined while
> Trade.applyDepositTx was never executed, leaving depositTxId and the
> wallet-resolved depositTx null. Any other caller, for example a payout
> broadcast, is exposed to the same loss of its callback.
> 
> A duplicate request now reports the misuse to the second caller only and
> returns. The pending broadcast keeps its timer and its callback, and the
> transaction is not committed or broadcast a second time.
> 
> Add a test that issues a duplicate broadcast while the first one is pending
> and verifies that only the second caller fails, that wallet commit and peer
> group broadcast happen once, and that the first caller still receives its
> success callback when the broadcast completes.
> 
> Verification: ./gradlew :core:test

> Make refund payout reservations durable and isolated
> 
> A reservation marks refund rows before asynchronous persistence so the serialized state contains the payout transaction ID. If that write failed, temporary marks remained in memory and could later become phantom paid state even though no transaction was committed or broadcast. A second concurrent reservation could also serialize the first temporary marker and resurrect it after failure.
> 
> Track every row marked by a reservation, clear those marks on persistence error, and request cleanup persistence before reporting that no funds were spent. Permit only one reservation awaiting persistence at a time and release the guard on either callback. Wallet commit and broadcast remain reachable only after successful durable persistence.
> 
> Add persistence callback contract tests, reservation rollback and overlap coverage, and regression coverage for restoring the persisted payout latch. Update the specification and operator error text.
> 
> Compatibility: this changes only local refund-agent coordination and persisted values; it introduces no schema or network protocol change.
> 
> Verification: ./gradlew :common:test --tests bisq.common.persistence.PersistenceManagerTest :core:test --tests bisq.core.support.dispute.refund.RefundPayoutReceiptServiceTest --tests bisq.core.support.dispute.messages.DisputeOpenMessageTest --offline

> Keep seller deposit publication single-flight
> 
> The idempotence check in SellerPublishesDepositTx reads the trade phase,
> which advances only when the broadcast callback runs. Overlapping task
> runners that reach publication before that callback therefore all passed the
> check. The seller can reach publication more than once, for instance from
> the startup recovery and from a stored buyer account reveal that is
> processed shortly afterwards.
> 
> Add a transient single-flight flag to ProcessModel and acquire it in
> SellerPublishesDepositTx after the prerequisite and canonical transaction
> checks. An overlapping task runner now completes without a second wallet
> broadcast, and the first attempt stays responsible for applying the
> transaction and advancing the trade. Success, broadcast failure and a
> synchronous failure of the broadcast call release the flag, so publication
> can be retried. The flag is not persisted, which keeps restart recovery and
> the persisted data and wire format unchanged.
> 
> Add tests for an overlapping task runner while the first callback is
> pending, and for the release of the flag after a failed broadcast.
> 
> Verification: ./gradlew :core:test

> Bound refund payouts by the validated escrow instead of the DPT output sum
> 
> RefundManager.verifyRefundPayoutAmount capped the refund at the minimum of the
> contract pot and the sum of the delayed payout transaction outputs. The close
> dialog and the wallet boundary use a different limit, the deposit output 0
> value minus the recorded trade fee, which equals the contract pot for every
> deposit that passed the escrow equation. The DPT outputs are smaller than the
> escrow by the DPT miner fee (fee rate times 51 + 32 x receivers vbytes, more
> than the trade fee for the usual receiver count), so every refund that used
> the default full-pot allocation was accepted in the form and rejected at
> close with "Proposed refund amount exceeds verified maximum". The two
> specifications also contradicted each other on this bound.
> 
> Use the same deposit-based bound at close time through
> RefundPayoutReceiptService.calculateMaximumPayoutAmount, computed from the
> validated deposit output and the trade fee verified by verifyDepositTx. Drop
> the corresponding invariant from RefundValidationResult; the DPT output sum
> stays part of the binding. The deposit output is bound to the contract pot,
> multisig script and trade fee before the bound is used, and the DPT is still
> required to spend that exact output to the protocol receivers, so the refund
> wallet remains bounded by escrow evidence. Covering the DPT miner fee in the
> refund is the pre-existing behaviour.
> 
> Specification updated in refund-delayed-payout-validation.md.
> 
> Verification: ./gradlew :core:test --tests 'bisq.core.support.dispute.refund.*'
> --tests bisq.core.support.dispute.DisputeValidationTest :desktop:compileJava
> --offline; the amount tests now assert acceptance at the pot above the DPT
> output sum and rejection one satoshi above the pot.

> Report a consumed refund payout reservation when the recheck fails
> 
> The authorization recheck added after the durable payout reservation
> correctly refused to commit the wallet transaction, but it only logged a
> warning and completed the close attempt with false. By then the
> reservation had already marked every row of the funding chain as paid and
> persisted the payout transaction ID, so the receipt was consumed without
> any transaction. The operator saw nothing when the dialog row had changed,

> attempt "a payout transaction has already been created", which was false.

>

> so the recheck can run them without the generic popup, and show one
> dedicated popup that states no transaction was committed or broadcast,
> names the reserved transaction ID that now blocks a replacement payout,
> and asks for manual investigation. The close attempt completes only when
> the operator dismisses that popup. The already-paid popup additionally
> says when the wallet holds no transaction with the recorded ID, so a
> reserved-but-unpublished receipt is not reported as a created payout.
> Fail-closed behaviour is unchanged: the reservation stays consumed.
> 
> Update the durable-reservation specification to require this operator
> feedback. Extend the dialog test so all three rejection cases assert the
> single popup, the reserved transaction ID and the deferred completion.

> Complete trade once withdraw tx is committed
> 
> TradeManager.onWithdrawRequest completed the trade only inside the
> onSuccess callback of the BitcoinJ broadcastComplete future. That
> future only completes once enough connected peers have announced
> the tx back to us, which over Tor can take a long time or never
> happen. The trade then stayed in open trades although the withdraw
> tx was committed to the wallet and usually confirms on-chain.
> 
> The desktop withdraw-to-external-wallet step was removed from the
> trade completion screen in 1162060e28, so today this path is only
> reachable through the api withdrawfunds call. A headless daemon
> hitting the stalled future is left with a trade that never leaves
> open trades.
> 
> We complete the trade once sendFunds has committed the tx to the
> wallet. This is consistent with the trade completion screen, which
> completes the trade without any broadcast, and with the api
> closeTrade call, and matches the TxBroadcaster policy that
> committing the tx and broadcasting it later is the least risky
> option. Still pending txs are handed to the broadcaster again at
> startup and the tx is additionally published to mempool nodes for
> redundancy.
> 
> The broadcast callback is kept for logging and error reporting.
> 
> Fixes #5523

> Validate all refund DPT receiver outputs
> 
> Exact escrow-outpoint validation is necessary but not sufficient: colluding
> traders can co-sign a spend of that output to an address they control. The
> modern Burning Man branch validated fetched outputs, while the legacy branch
> trusted an opener-supplied donation-address string and never inspected the
> transaction outputs.
> 
> Apply equally strict receiver rules to both branches. Legacy transactions must
> have exactly one output to the dispute's donation address, and that address
> must be a current or past DAO donation parameter. Modern transactions must
> exactly match the protocol receiver schedule. Expand regression coverage for
> input shape, output count, address, and value failures, and document the
> validated invariants and remaining limitations in the canonical specification.
> 
> Valid historical legacy transactions already use the required single donation
> output. Malformed evidence is rejected; serialization, persistence, and the
> network protocol are unchanged. Verification covers RefundManagerTest, the
> core test suite, and desktop compilation.

> Accept foreign mobile numbers for SBP
> 
> The SBP validator pins the mobile number to the Russian dialing
> code as SbpValidator extends PhoneNumberValidator with country RU.
> Russian banks now allow registering the service with a foreign
> mobile number, so such accounts cannot be entered in Bisq.
> 
> We accept numbers with an explicit non-Russian dialing code and
> validate them as international numbers with E.164 length bounds.
> Zone 7 numbers and numbers without a dialing code are validated
> against the Russian rules as before, so existing accounts and
> local format entries are not affected.
> 
> A + is only valid as the single leading character: a second or
> misplaced + is rejected on both the Russian and the international
> path (the base validator would strip it silently), while formatting
> between the + and the digits is accepted the same way it is for
> Russian numbers. The structural rejections use a dedicated error
> message instead of reporting invalid characters.
> 
> The account info text keeps the historical +7-only fact next to the
> new foreign-number option, and the buyer payment step notes that
> paying a foreign number depends on the buyer's own bank supporting
> it in SBP.
> 
> SbpValidatorTest covers the new and the unchanged cases.
> 
> Fixes #7988

> the resulting deprecation warnings to keep the build output clean while
> we migrate to the new implementation
- f552b0f36a4207f713804d987ccad1c95d095f99 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/f552b0f36a4207f713804d987ccad1c95d095f99
> Suppress legacy DaoState serialization warnings
> 
> The method DaoState.getSerializedStateForHashChainLegacy was recently
> deprecated, but it is still used until the canonical encoding migration
> verification is complete.
> 
> This change temporarily suppresses the resulting deprecation warnings
> to keep the build output clean while we migrate to the new
> implementation.
- f5848f040a54255ebaf49c2599f72c658e401e35 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/f5848f040a54255ebaf49c2599f72c658e401e35
> Prevent refund payout markers from crossing funding chains
> 
> Receipt conflict detection intentionally matches either funding transaction ID, but using that same OR relation to propagate payout markers created transitive paid state. A crafted bridge row combining the deposit from trade A with the delayed payout from trade B could acquire A payout marker and then make B appear paid.
> 
> Distinguish conflict detection from funding-chain identity. Continue blocking a payout when either ID matches a consumed receipt, but mark only rows where both IDs identify the same funding chain. At close time, report a prior payout without copying its marker into a potentially conflicting row.
> 
> Peer rows for the same trade remain marked together; bridge rows remain blocked but cannot become new marker sources. Update the specification and add the crafted-row regression test.
> 
> Verification: ./gradlew :core:test --tests bisq.core.support.dispute.refund.RefundPayoutReceiptServiceTest :desktop:compileJava --offline
- f58b74c81d8e369e997c92cc9ce88a25c192203d — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/f58b74c81d8e369e997c92cc9ce88a25c192203d
> Extract the manual test timer for reuse
> 
> The deterministic UserThread timer replacement was nested inside
> TxBroadcasterTest and inaccessible to other tests. Move it to a shared
> test utility unchanged, with accessors instead of the private field
> reads.
- f61d0600a1355cc8ab37a2113c66cb24249b61d2 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/f61d0600a1355cc8ab37a2113c66cb24249b61d2
> fix(bridge): keep burningman error signalling best effort
> 
> BurningmanGrpcService carries its own copy of notifyOnError with the same defect
> just fixed in BsqBlockGrpcService: it is used from two forEach loops, so an
> observer whose already closed stream rejects onError aborted the loop and left
> the remaining observers unsignalled.
> 
> Guard the signal the same way. The deregistration half is already covered, since
> both services share ManagedStreamObserver.
- f65b76c10698d92e54a11aa6a1d2f3cb57af6fd0 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/f65b76c10698d92e54a11aa6a1d2f3cb57af6fd0
> fix(bridge): keep snapshot observer registration consistent on failure
> 
> Two gaps around snapshot subscription lifetime.
> 
> subscribeWithSnapshot registered the observer and only then read the chain height
> and submitted the readiness task. A throw from either, such as a rejected
> submission during shutdown, left an observer registered that would never receive
> its readiness event, while the client saw the RPC fail. Route a setup failure
> through notifyOnError, which also deregisters the observer.
> 
> Snapshot observers are captured when the block is raised, so an observer removed
> in between, typically by its own readiness event failing, was still invoked by
> the queued block task on an already terminated stream. Check captured observers
> against the live set before notifying. That only excludes further and never
> re-includes an observer registered after the capture, so the publication ordering
> is unaffected.
> 
> The plain subscriber path is left alone: it iterates the live set within a single
> dispatch and has no readiness event that can remove an observer mid flight.
- f6e294972d1ad62881b7a1b31b0a3f5c9dcdf9a3 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/f6e294972d1ad62881b7a1b31b0a3f5c9dcdf9a3
> Suppress deprecation warnings for Venmo
> 
> Venmo was deprecated and removed as an active payment method due to
> high chargeback risk. This change suppresses the resulting
> deprecation warnings to keep the build output clean.
- f6e6ced378506c12a6f8971750f07d4edf202605 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/f6e6ced378506c12a6f8971750f07d4edf202605
> Re-enable the dependency verification tasks that were were disabled with the surrounding build logic.
- f8d83e9d7e777d791fa9ca51efbb4bf6058d9eff — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/f8d83e9d7e777d791fa9ca51efbb4bf6058d9eff
> Merge pull request #8043 from alvasw/Suppress_deprecation_warnings_for_ArbitrationManager
> 
> Suppress deprecation warnings for ArbitrationManager
- f98c5dc6a0fca3cb1366f2a1bb5c43754513727a — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/f98c5dc6a0fca3cb1366f2a1bb5c43754513727a
> Replace deprecated URL constructor with URI.toURL()
> 
> The java.net.URL constructors were deprecated in Java 20.
> This updates the code to use the recommended approach:
> parsing a URI string and converting it via URI.toURL(),
> which ensures better syntax validation.
- ff88a2f15f487bd540c177dfe5e88011fbddb456 — https://github.com/bisq-network/bisq/commit/ff88a2f15f487bd540c177dfe5e88011fbddb456
> Round altcoin trade amounts to coin precision
> 
> Altcoin volumes are stored at 10^-8 precision, but coins with fewer
> decimals cannot receive such amounts: a taker paying 0.123457 USDC for
> a stated volume of 0.12345678 USDC cannot settle the trade exactly.
> 
> Round the volume to the coin's chain precision on the payment path:
> Offer, TakeOfferModel, Contract, Trade and the create/take models. The
> rounding is half up in exact integer arithmetic with an overflow guard.
> A volume below half of one on-chain unit rounds to zero and callers
> must reject it as below the coin's minimum; inflating it to one unit
> would silently change the agreed rate. Derived analytics
> (TradeStatistics3, JSON exports) intentionally stay raw: the payment
> instruction is rounded to chain precision, derived data is not.
> 
> The per-offer-row precision lookup is cached in CurrencyUtil next to
> the existing isCryptoCurrency cache.

- 89cd7476a7db4a176c611688baa4584a0b92b27c — https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/commit/89cd7476a7db4a176c611688baa4584a0b92b27c
> Accelerate FP16 attention via cblas_sgemm for Apple AMX (#346)
> 
> * Accelerate FP16 attention via cblas_sgemm for Apple AMX
> 
> Batch query positions into real GEMMs so cblas_sgemm can use AMX,
> same approach as the matmul kernel (#340). Parallelizes over
> batch * num_q_heads instead of batch * num_q_heads * seq_len,
> with each work item processing all seq_len positions for one head.
> 
> Benchmark (1024x16x64): 8.7ms / 246 GFLOPS -> 4.4ms / 490 GFLOPS (~2x)
> 
> Falls back to existing NEON path for seq_len < 64.
> 
> Signed-off-by: Kayaan Tharani <kayaan.tharani@gmail.com>
> 
> * Add ACCELERATE_NEW_LAPACK definition for improved LAPACK support
> 
> Signed-off-by: HenryNdubuaku <ndubuakuhenry@gmail.com>
> 
> ---------
> 
> Signed-off-by: Kayaan Tharani <kayaan.tharani@gmail.com>
> Signed-off-by: HenryNdubuaku <ndubuakuhenry@gmail.com>
> Co-authored-by: HenryNdubuaku <ndubuakuhenry@gmail.com>

> Add optional cloud key prompt for transcribe (#359)
> 
> * Add optional cloud key prompt for transcribe
> 
> Prompts user for cloud API key on first run or whenever key is not set.
> If provided, key is saved to ~/.cactus/config.json and exported as
> CACTUS_CLOUD_API_KEY env var for C++ cloud code. If skipped, user is
> prompted again on next run. Env var takes precedence over config file.

> fix: replace NSLog with CACTUS_LOG in NPU code for iOS debuggability (#321) (#328)
> 
> On physical iOS devices, stdout/stderr is redirected to cactus_test.log
> but NSLog goes to the system log, making all CoreML/ANE errors invisible.
> This replaces all NSLog calls with CACTUS_LOG_ERROR (which writes to
> stderr), adds load/path diagnostics, mlpackage directory validation,
> and fixes silent file copy failures in the iOS test harness.
> 
> Signed-off-by: Kayaan Tharani <kayaan.tharani@gmail.com>

item_id: cactus-compute/cactus::release::289669608
Data: 2026-02-24T02:06:48Z
URL: https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/releases/tag/v1.8

Release notes (texto original):

> ## What's Changed
> * Kernel optimisations by @HenryNdubuaku in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/397
> * Improve INT4 by @ncylich and @jrajala6 in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/343
> * add einops dependency to requirements by @jakmro in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/371
> * Add language parameter support for Whisper transcription by @rshemet in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/384
> * added moe support for lfm by @kar-m in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/374
> * Add raw FFI binding for Rust by @yujonglee in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/382
> * fix: handle spaces in paths when running shell commands by @adithya-n05 in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/377
> * fixing sentencepiece detection for transformers 5.0+ (still backwards compatible) by @ncylich in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/373
> * Improve Telemetry by @mhayes853 in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/372
> * proprietry commit by @HenryNdubuaku 
> * Update performance metrics for iPhone 13 Mini and Galaxy A56 by @jakmro in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/386
> * fix: improve version sorting and enhance model export tagging by @jakmro in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/387
> * Add Rust SDK and language parameter documentation by @rshemet in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/389
> * Basic addition of int4 functionality by @jrajala6 in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/343
> * add scalar log by @yujonglee in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/390
> * fix assertion and linux build in rust test by @yujonglee in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/392
> * Justin/api fixes by @justinl66 in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/380
> * Update telemetry by @justinl66 in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/394
> * docs: add compatibility guidelines for runtime and weights by @jakmro in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/398
> * add STFT_COMPLEX, derive stft_magnitude via graph composition by @yujonglee in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/395
> 
> ## New Contributors
> * @yujonglee made their first contribution in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/382
> * @adithya-n05 made their first contribution in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/377
> 
> **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/compare/v1.7...v1.8
>

> This breaks the weights.

- d1616c3b6c2ef7b9e8398de6811d945419268978 — https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/commit/d1616c3b6c2ef7b9e8398de6811d945419268978
> fix: handle spaces in paths when running shell commands (#377)
> 
> * fix: handle spaces in paths when running shell commands
> 
> Added shlex.quote() to properly escape paths with spaces in run_command().
> This fixes build failures when the cactus repo is cloned into a directory
> path containing spaces (e.g., 'Programming Projects').
> 
> Signed-off-by: Adithya Narayanan <adithya.narayanan01@gmail.com>
> 
> * fix: use shell=False to handle spaces in paths safely
> 
> Improved fix based on code review feedback:
> - Removed shlex.quote() approach which has Windows compatibility issues
> - Use subprocess.run with shell=False by converting string paths to lists
> - This is more robust, secure, and cross-platform
> 
> The shell=False approach:
> - Handles paths with spaces correctly without quoting
> - Works on both Unix and Windows
> - Avoids shell injection risks
> - Respects script shebangs when execute bit is set
> 
> Signed-off-by: Adithya Narayanan <adithya.narayanan01@gmail.com>
> 
> ---------
> 
> Signed-off-by: Adithya Narayanan <adithya.narayanan01@gmail.com>

Release notes (texto original):

> ## What's Changed
> * Enhance model publishing workflow with detailed metadata and licenses by @jakmro in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/459
> * Added parakeet to publish to hf yaml by @ParkiratS in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/464
> * Update telemetry for supported platforms by @justinl66 in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/465
> * added back moe weight conversion by @kar-m in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/468
> * adjust manual workflow for model publish by @jakmro in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/470
> * Parakeet blog by @ammesatyajit in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/467
> * perf: add FP16 fast path for LayerNorm by @yujonglee in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/433
> * Issue #406: Bilinear + Depthwise Optimizations by @PiyawanChaiprasit2006 in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/466
> * ARM SME2: Accelerate MatMul FP16 by @aarav18 in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/457
> * build: add Objective-C ARC support for NPU sources by @jakmro in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/475
> * long transcription by @jakmro in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/482
> * Language detection by @ParkiratS in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/471
> * Parakeet tdt by @ParkiratS in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/476
> * kotlin: expose forceTools in CompletionOptions by @rshemet in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/484
> * Update model list in README and publish_to_hf.yml with new LiquidAI m… by @jakmro in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/487
> * test: updated rag test conditions by @nshejwalkar in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/488
> * optimize scale correction in cactus_attention_f16_h64 by @jakmro in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/485
> * fix greedy sampler ignoring logit suppression by @jakmro in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/486
> 
> ## New Contributors
> * @PiyawanChaiprasit2006 made their first contribution in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/466
> * @aarav18 made their first contribution in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/457
> 
> **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/compare/v1.9...v1.10

#### 4. v1.13 / v1.13

item_id: cactus-compute/cactus::release::308617111
Data: 2026-04-14T01:54:31Z
URL: https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/releases/tag/v1.13

Release notes (texto original):

> ## What's Changed
> * Improve model publishing error handling in workflow by @jakmro in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/546
> * Fix VLM prefill cache reuse image path slicing by @KayaanT in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/545
> * Add cache cleanup for Hugging Face models in export_and_publish_model by @jakmro in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/547
> * Add branch override option to publish workflow by @ncylich in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/548
> * Fix Gemma 3n conversion memory usage by @ncylich in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/549
> * Update blog URL in README.md by @amerkld in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/544
> * Parakeet streaming fix by @ParkiratS in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/551
> * Tool call prompt formatting by @jakmro in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/558
> * Feature Cleanup by @ParkiratS in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/559
> * Add Whisper v3 (large-v3) support by @ncylich in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/557
> * Add LFM2.5 VL 450M by @yujonglee in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/567
> * LFM2-VL-450M: fix garbled output (vision tower, template, kernel) by @ncylich in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/565
> * Change default transcribe model to parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 by @rshemet in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/566
> * Expose min_p and repetition_penalty in completion options by @DuFanYin in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/560
> * Graph save load by @cattermelon1234 in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/556
> * Pyannote features and optimizations by @jakmro in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/571
> * Karen/needle by @kar-m in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/574
> * fix apple i8mm detection to use runtime sysctl check by @DuFanYin in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/562
> * Fix streaming transcribe by @jakmro in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/576
> 
> ## New Contributors
> * @amerkld made their first contribution in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/544
> * @DuFanYin made their first contribution in https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/pull/560
> 
> **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/compare/v1.12...v1.13

- f2385f31a432d4668a9aa54275a3ad116a5a5ca5 — https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/commit/f2385f31a432d4668a9aa54275a3ad116a5a5ca5
> LFM2-VL-450M: fix garbled output (vision tower, template, kernel) (#565)
> 
> * graph: reserve node id 0 as a sentinel for 'no node'
> 
> Node id 0 used to be a valid, allocatable id, which made it impossible
> for downstream code to distinguish 'node not loaded/set' from 'node is
> the first one I allocated'. For example, LFM2-VL's projector layernorm
> weight would be assigned id 0 on a fresh graph, and the code guarding
> its use via 'id != 0' would silently skip the layernorm.
> 
> Reserve 0 as a sentinel by starting next_node_id_ at 1 in both the
> constructor and hard_reset. Existing checks of the form 'id != 0' now
> correctly mean 'id is loaded'.
> 
> Signed-off-by: Noah Cylich <noahcylich@gmail.com>
> 
> * engine/tokenizer: emit image tokens before text in LFM2-VL user turns
> 
> HF's LFM2-VL chat template iterates the message content list in order,
> so a user turn of [image, text] produces '<|image_start|>...<|image_end|>'
> before the text. cactus was unconditionally writing msg.content first and
> then appending the image block, which is the opposite order. The model
> was trained image-first, and the text-first prompt degraded generation
> quality (often producing incoherent output for an otherwise-correct
> vision tower / projector).
> 
> Swap the order so the image block is emitted before msg.content within
> each turn. Verified byte-identical to HF's processor output across the
> entire LFM VL family (LFM2-VL-450M, LFM2-VL-1.6B, LFM2.5-VL-1.6B): same
> <|image_start|> / <|img_row_R_col_C|> / <|img_thumbnail|> / <|image_end|>
> structure, same 2837-token prompt for the banner.jpg test case.
> 
> Signed-off-by: Noah Cylich <noahcylich@gmail.com>
> 
> * graph: add align_corners option to bilinear_interpolation (matches HF/PyTorch)
> 
> cactus_bilinear_interpolation_f16 previously hardcoded align_corners=True
> semantics: scale=(src-1)/(dst-1), src=dst*scale. That is the wrong
> convention for Siglip2 vision towers (and most HF/PyTorch vision models),
> whose reference implementations use F.interpolate(..., align_corners=False):
> scale=src/dst, src=(dst+0.5)*scale-0.5 with edge clamping.
> 
> Using the wrong convention produced systematically-incorrect position
> embeddings at the edges, concentrated in the channels with the largest
> magnitudes (e.g. channel 720 of LFM2-VL-450M's position embedding has
> max |v|=23.25). The error was carried straight into the transformer
> and amplified by every subsequent layer.
> 
> Add align_corners as a per-call option plumbed end-to-end through:
>   - cactus_bilinear_interpolation_f16 (kernel)
>   - OpParams and CactusGraph::bilinear_interpolation (graph)
>   - compute_bilinear_interpolation_node (executor)
> 
> The default is align_corners=true so every existing caller (including
> the FFI cactus_graph_bilinear_interpolation) keeps its current behavior.
> Siglip2VisionModel::build_vision_embeddings opts into align_corners=false
> to match HF's resize_positional_embeddings, which works for the whole
> LFM2-VL / LFM2.5-VL family.
> 
> Also drop unused Siglip2VisionModel::get_image_features{,_node} overloads
> that had no callers anywhere in cactus, the FFI, tests, or any language
> binding.
> 
> Signed-off-by: Noah Cylich <noahcylich@gmail.com>
> 
> * removing the old debugger methods
> 
> Signed-off-by: Noah Cylich <noahcylich@gmail.com>
> 
> * kernel: replace fast_tanh Padé with Cephes 13/6 rational + dual-vector path
> 
> The previous fast_tanh_f32x4 used a 3rd-order Padé (27+x^2)/(27+9x^2)
> with a hard saturation at +/-4.5. Max abs error was 0.024 (relative
> error up to 2.6%) in the [1, 4.5] range, and the saturation cutoff
> produced a visible discontinuity at the clamp boundary. That level of
> inaccuracy materially degraded GELU outputs (e.g. Siglip2 vision MLP,
> ~18% norm error per layer) and any LSTM/BiLSTM path that uses tanh.
> 
> Switch to the Cephes 13/6 rational polynomial (same coefficients as
> Eigen's generic_fast_tanh_float):
>   - max abs error 3.2e-7 over [-9, 9] (~7 decimal digits, parity with
>     libm tanhf to well below FP16 epsilon)
>   - strictly bounded in [-1, 1] unlike the Padé which overshoots to
>     1.016 just before its clamp and then jumps back down
>   - no discontinuity at the clamp boundary (natural value at +/-9 is
>     already 1 - 3e-8)
> 
> Coefficients are stored as static splatted float[4] arrays so the
> compiler loads each with a single pc-relative ldr instead of the
> mov+movk+dup sequence it emits for vdupq_n_f32 literals.
> 
> Add fast_tanh_f32x4_x2 that processes two input vectors with fully
> interleaved dependency chains. Apple Silicon's out-of-order scheduler
> can hide the divide latency of one vector behind the other's
> polynomial evaluation, giving ~2.4x the throughput of two back-to-back
> fast_tanh_f32x4 calls.
> 
> Use the dual-vector variant from cactus_gelu_f16, which already loads
> the low/high halves of a float16x8_t per iteration. No other callers
> are required to change; fast_tanh_f32x4 remains drop-in compatible.
> 
> Signed-off-by: Noah Cylich <noahcylich@gmail.com>
> 
> * removing debug print
> 
> Signed-off-by: Noah Cylich <noahcylich@gmail.com>
> 
> * graph: tidy next_node_id_ sentinel comment and restore stray whitespace
> 
> Move the 'node id 0 is a sentinel for no node' explanation from the two
> definition sites to the single member declaration in graph.h. Same
> information, half the comment footprint, less repetition in blame.
> 
> Also revert an accidental trailing-whitespace strip on a 'try {' line in
> model_lfm2vl.cpp so the file is no-op vs origin/main.
> 
> Signed-off-by: Noah Cylich <noahcylich@gmail.com>
> 
> * tests/kernel: pin fast_tanh_f32x4_x2 against libm tanhf
> 
> Sweep x in [-10, 10] step 1e-3 and compare each lane against std::tanh
> to within 1e-5. The Cephes 13/6 rational has ~3e-7 max abs error so
> the tolerance leaves ~30x slack while still firing immediately on the
> ~2.4e-2 worst-case error of the previous (broken) Pade approximation.
> 
> Also pins lane symmetry of the pair-with-self call pattern that the
> lone f32 BiLSTM gate sites use, so any future drift between the two
> output halves is caught at build-test time rather than as a model-level
> regression.
> 
> Signed-off-by: Noah Cylich <noahcylich@gmail.com>
> 
> * kernel: drop fast_tanh_f32x4_x2 in favor of the single-vector form
> 
> The dual-vector variant existed to manually interleave two dependency
> chains so the OoO scheduler could hide the vdiv latency, but a
> consolidated benchmark shows clang at -O3 schedules two back-to-back
> fast_tanh_f32x4 calls just as well (~4 G elem/s on Apple M3). The
> extra API surface and ~45 lines of near-duplicated Cephes polynomial
> body weren't buying anything.
> 
> Remove fast_tanh_f32x4_x2, revert cactus_gelu_f16 to two single-vector
> calls, and simplify the pin test in tests/test_kernel.cpp to exercise
> fast_tanh_f32x4 directly. Projector cos sim vs HF on LFM2-VL-450M
> unchanged at 0.999299.
> 
> Signed-off-by: Noah Cylich <noahcylich@gmail.com>
> 
> ---------
> 
> Signed-off-by: Noah Cylich <noahcylich@gmail.com>

> 
> * enforce required params and prevent duplicate keys in Needle constrained generation
> 
> - Extract `required` array from JSON schema and propagate to `ToolConstraintSpec`
> - Precompute `needle_arg_close_tokens_` covering combined BPE tokens that exit
>   a string value and close the arguments object in one step
> - Track `needle_between_pairs_` to distinguish "between key-value pairs" from
>   "mid-value" so force-close fires only after a complete value, not after a key
> - Block `needle_arg_close_tokens_` while inside a string value when required
>   params are unsatisfied (covers combined tokens like `engineer"}`)
> - Force close arguments when all parameter names have been seen and we are
>   between pairs, preventing hallucinated extra keys (e.g. "sunday":"Sunday")
> - Track `needle_seen_arg_keys_` to block duplicate parameter keys
> - Remove dead `QWEN_EXPECT_CLOSE_BRACE` state; clear `generated_text_` in
>   QWEN/Gemma IN_ARGUMENTS states to prevent unbounded accumulation
> - Add `extract_schema_required()` parser for the JSON schema `required` array
> - Expand test coverage: no-params, optional-only, boolean params, 5/10-tool
>   haystack, buried key info, long irrelevant preamble, numeric required,
>   non-obvious param names, 1k-context-with-tool tests
> - Add docs/constrained_generation.md documenting current logic, flaws, and
>   proposed improvements

Release notes (texto original):

> 
> ### Bug Fixes
> 
> * 修复1:: 形式的ipv6校验失败的bug ([8b96f21](https://github.com/certd/certd/commit/8b96f218d5284033f10c186c0ce18e4c16d8e9b2))
> * 修复阿里云esa超过免费配额之后无法部署证书的bug，改成删除最旧的那张证书 ([32de8d9](https://github.com/certd/certd/commit/32de8d9ccb08d26414adbdde950d7cd405dc344a))
> 
> ### Performance Improvements
> 
> * 当ip证书天数太小时，自动调整更新天数，避免每次运行都重新申请ip证书 ([433e98b](https://github.com/certd/certd/commit/433e98b6450fa7d0491151f159e432bf3dfe4feb))

> * 验证码支持 Cloudflare Turnstile ，谨慎启用，国内被墙了 ([ca43c77](https://github.com/certd/certd/commit/ca43c775250154def63c4acd96d65dc95d1c0c2b))
> * 优化证书未过期时的任务日志提示 ([ac85488](https://github.com/certd/certd/commit/ac85488245197694560aad7df9425ca215ef7ff7))
> * 支持部署到阿里云GA ([1a0d3ee](https://github.com/certd/certd/commit/1a0d3eeb1b0b5ce08f05af84b6161e00c1fe1815))

> * 支持部署到AcePanel ([1661cae](https://github.com/certd/certd/commit/1661caed05e3413dc3e2b14ce62b75aa03ad90e0))

### Releases sorteadas

#### 1. @ark-ui/vue@5.26.0 / @ark-ui/vue@5.26.0

item_id: chakra-ui/ark::release::253159810
Data: 2025-10-08T20:52:24Z
URL: https://github.com/chakra-ui/ark/releases/tag/%40ark-ui/vue%405.26.0

Release notes (texto original):

> ### Added
> 
> - **Collapsible**: Add support for `collapsedHeight` and `collapsedWidth` props to control the dimensions of the
>   collapsible content when in its collapsed state.
> 
> - **Focus Trap**: Allow elements referenced by `aria-controls` to be included in the trap scope. This makes it possible
>   for menus, popovers, etc. to be portalled and work correctly.
> 
> - **Pagination**: Add `getPageUrl` prop for generating `href` attributes when using pagination as links.
> 
> ```ts
> const service = useMachine(pagination.machine, {
>   type: 'link',
>   getPageUrl: ({ page, pageSize }) => `/products?page=${page}&size=${pageSize}`,
> })
> ```
> 
> - **Select**: Add `SelectRootComponentProps` type export for better component type composition.
> 
> - **Listbox**: Add `ListboxRootComponentProps` type export for better component type composition.
> 
> - **Combobox**: Add `ComboboxRootComponentProps` type export for better component type composition.
> 
> - **TreeView**:
>   - Add `TreeViewRootComponentProps` type export for better component type composition.
>   - (Experimental) Add support for node renaming functionality:
>     - Add `TreeViewNodeRenameInput` component for inline node label editing
>     - Add `canRename` prop to control which nodes can be renamed
>     - Add `renameStart`, `beforeRename`, and `renameComplete` event emitters for rename lifecycle
>     - Add `CheckedChangeDetails`, `LoadChildrenErrorDetails`, `RenameStartDetails`, and `RenameCompleteDetails` type exports
> 
> ### Fixed
> 
> - **Scroll Area**: Fix RTL horizontal scrollbar positioning on Safari
> 
> - **Slider**: Fix issue where slider continues dragging when disabled during drag operation.
>
