> Stabilize hardware E2E input capture and audio routing (#1595)
> 
> * test(e2e): treat shell access to the device as optional
> 
> A unit with developer mode off has no SSH, and the suite should still run
> against it and report what it covered. deviceShellAvailable() answers once
> per worker, from JETKVM_DEVICE_SSH=0 or a five second probe, and sshExec
> short-circuits on it so best-effort calls return immediately instead of
> waiting out the connect timeout. The nine specs that need the shell skip
> with a reason; the global teardown skips log capture and reset.
> 
> Test titles carry what they need: @ssh, @serial, @tls, @audio, @ota, so
> subsets can be picked with --grep and --grep-invert.
> 
> The remote agent deploy no longer falls back to a hardcoded user name;
> JETKVM_REMOTE_HOST is required. The unused prebuilt agent binary under
> e2e/remote-agent/bin is removed and ignored; the agent is built from its
> source at the repo root as before.
> 
> The login rate-limit spec runs in its own project after ui instead of
> relying on a zz- filename prefix.
> 
> * fix(e2e): guard serial setup before accessing the device shell
> 
> * test(e2e): clean up and verify uploads and serial settings over RPC
> 
> upload-cancel used the shell for three things the device already exposes:
> the size of the partial file (listStorageFiles lists it under its
> .incomplete name), removing test images (deleteStorageFile accepts the
> partial name), and the final hash. The first two go through RPC; the
> byte-for-byte hash stays behind deviceShellAvailable and the fallback is
> the final size, which still catches a truncated or doubled resume.
> 
> serial-console-takeover checked for the settings file over the shell to
> know whether to restore or delete it. It now reads the settings through
> getSerialSettings, falls back to the defaults when that fails, and
> restores through setSerialSettings. The one difference is that a device
> that had no settings file ends up with one holding the defaults.
> 
> Both specs drop the @ssh tag and run on a device without a shell.
> 
> * test(e2e): skip feature tests the device reports as unavailable
> 
> The suite also runs against older firmware during upgrade testing, and a
> method the device does not implement answers "Method not found". That
> is a version fact, not a regression, so the audio, serial console, TLS
> and network settings tests now probe their getter through rpcAvailable()
> and skip with the method name in the reason. The timesync spec no longer
> tries to restore settings it never read. Network tests carry @network.
> 
> * test(e2e): split ra-all and helpers by area
> 
> ra-all.spec.ts held 54 tests in one 125 KB file behind one describe, so
> one early failure in serial mode took every later area with it. It is now
> seven specs, one per area: keyboard, mouse, virtual media, USB gadget
> config, display, TLS, factory reset. The page, agent, macro setup and log
> capture they shared live in remote-agent/shared.ts; each spec registers
> its session with registerSharedSession() and keeps serial mode. The
> factory reset spec reboots the device into setup, so it runs in its own
> project after the rest of the remote-agent project.
> 
> helpers.ts, 1,600 lines, is now e2e/helpers/ with device, hid, video,
> auth, ssh and ota modules and an index that re-exports all of them, so
> every existing import path still resolves.
> 
> Test bodies and helper bodies are moved, not edited. playwright test
> --list reports the same 95 tests.
> 
> * fix(e2e): retain display and virtual media fixtures in split specs
> 
> * test(e2e): focus serial console across reconnect
> 
> * fix(e2e): synchronize input monitors across USB reconnects
> 
> * test(e2e): retain keyboard delivery diagnostics
> 
> * test(e2e): wait for keyboard delivery before checking events
> 
> * test(e2e): target the selected ALSA card by PipeWire node name
> 
> * test(e2e): check complete keyboard sequence after host settles
> 
> * test(e2e): use event sequence for release ordering

> seven specs, one per area: keyboard, mouse, virtual media, USB gadget
> config, display, TLS, factory reset. The page, agent, macro setup and log
> capture they shared live in remote-agent/shared.ts; each spec registers
> its session with registerSharedSession() and keeps serial mode. The
> factory reset spec reboots the device into setup, so it runs in its own
> project after the rest of the remote-agent project.
> 
> helpers.ts, 1,600 lines, is now e2e/helpers/ with device, hid, video,
> auth, ssh and ota modules and an index that re-exports all of them, so
> every existing import path still resolves.
> 
> Test bodies and helper bodies are moved, not edited. playwright test
> --list reports the same 95 tests.
> 
> * fix(e2e): retain display and virtual media fixtures in split specs

- c2e29cd3c8218596ab43a1aaf123b09abd43dfbf — https://github.com/jetkvm/kvm/commit/c2e29cd3c8218596ab43a1aaf123b09abd43dfbf
> fix(video): signal limited-range BT.709/BT.601 colorimetry in encoder VUI (#1460)
> 
> Annotate the H.264/H.265 bitstream with proper VUI colour_primaries,
> transfer_characteristics, and matrix_coefficients (BT.709 for >576p,
> SMPTE 170M otherwise) plus video_full_range_flag=0. Without this,
> browser WebRTC decoders fall back to BT.601/full-range guesses,
> producing tinted output on HD sources.
> 
> Also set the matching V4L2 capture colorimetry hints and hoist
> constant per-stream fields out of the per-frame SendFrame loop.

> Fix tzdata generator to emit go fmt formatted file (#1442)
> 
> Regeneration added "America/Coyhaique"
- d58e6e44d795b34969d4b5e35511ff2adc577afb — https://github.com/jetkvm/kvm/commit/d58e6e44d795b34969d4b5e35511ff2adc577afb
> fix(usbgadget): stop the mass storage oops and avoid needless USB rebinds (#1579)
> 
> * usbgadget: skip the disconnect and rebind when nothing changed
> 
> configureUsbGadget(true) always soft-disconnected the host session and
> rebound the UDC, even on every app start with a gadget that was already
> bound, attached and configured identically. Each disconnect races the
> mass storage function's kernel thread and can leave the gadget dead
> until a power cycle (#1360).
> 
> Resolve the staged configfs changes first. If none would touch the tree
> and the gadget is live, commit the no-op transaction and leave the USB
> link alone. Otherwise disconnect and rebind as before.
> 
> * usbgadget: make the configfs no-op check actually pass
> 
> checkIfSymlinksInOrder used os.ReadDir, which sorts entries by name, so
> the actual order never matched the configured order once uac1 sat
> before mass_storage. configfs lists entries newest first, so read the
> raw directory order and reverse it.
> 
> The audio c_chmask attribute was written as "0x3" while the kernel
> reads it back as "3", so it resolved to an update on every start.
> Write the value in the form the kernel reports.
> 
> Together these made every start rewrite the symlinks and rebind.
> 
> * usbgadget: only skip the rebind on process start
> 
> UpdateGadgetConfig is the fallback in the USB recovery path and the
> entry point for config changes, so it has to rebind unconditionally.
> Restrict the no-op shortcut to Init.
> 
> * test(e2e): import rebootDeviceViaSSH in the remote-agent spec
> 
> The UDC unbind recovery test calls it from its cleanup path, which
> threw ReferenceError instead of rebooting the device.
> 
> * usbgadget: disable bulk endpoint stalls on the mass storage function
> 
> Every halt_bulk_in_endpoint call in f_mass_storage is gated by
> can_stall. On the RV1106 dwc3 that halt races the disconnect path and
> oopses in __dwc3_gadget_ep_set_halt (#1360), leaving the gadget dead
> until a power cycle. With stalls disabled the function sends a
> zero-length packet instead, which the Bulk-Only Transport hosts handle
> through the CSW residue.
> 
> * usbgadget: close HID descriptors before rebinding the UDC
> 
> f_hid re-initialises the same embedded cdev on every bind. Descriptors
> still open from the previous bind drop the fresh refcount to zero when
> they are closed afterwards, and every open of /dev/hidg* then fails
> with ENXIO until the next rebind. The recovery path hit this on every
> UDC rebind: eight reopen attempts over 20 s, then a full reconfigure
> as the workaround. Close the descriptors first, and log the reopen
> error instead of swallowing it.
> 
> * usbgadget: release inherited inputs and carry LED state over on adoption
> 
> When Init keeps the previous instance's gadget bound, the host sees no
> disconnect. It still holds whatever the old process left pressed, and it
> does not resend its LED report. Keep the last LED byte and any unreleased
> absolute mouse press in a tmpfs handover file, and on adoption send
> neutral keyboard and mouse reports and restore the LED state. A rebind
> resets the file, since re-enumeration handles both.
> 
> * test(e2e): cover app restart with the gadget adopted
> 
> Hold two keys, restart the app, and require the host to see releases
> while the gadget's device number stays the same. Toggle Caps Lock,
> restart, and require the new process to report the same LED state
> without a new toggle.
> 
> * usbgadget: clear a failed transaction and persist the adopted mouse release
> 
> WithTransaction left u.tx set when the callback returned an error, so
> every later transaction failed with "transaction already exists". That
> path was unreachable before HasPendingChanges could fail. Clear it on
> every exit.
> 
> adoptLiveGadget sent the absolute mouse release with the press state
> still false, so the edge in AbsMouseReport never cleared the handover
> entry and the next adoption replayed the release. Seed the press state
> first.
> 
> * test(e2e): an adopted absolute mouse release is sent once
> 
> Hold a button, restart, require the host release. Park the cursor
> elsewhere, restart again, require no mouse event: a replayed release
> would show up as a move back to the press position.
> 
> * usbgadget: do not adopt a gadget whose pull-up is off
> 
> The adoption check looked at the UDC binding and the gadget's UDC file.
> Both still hold after a soft disconnect, so a process that died between
> its soft disconnect and the rebind left a gadget the host could not see,
> and the next start kept it that way.
> 
> The sysfs state and speed files keep their last value across a soft
> disconnect. DCTL.RUN_STOP in the dwc3 register dump under debugfs does
> not: soft_connect clears and sets it. Require it before adopting. Without
> a readable dump the start rebinds, as it did before adoption existed.
> 
> Also drop a missing optional attribute from the pending-change check.
> On kernels without wakeup_on_write the staged write resolved to a create
> on every start, which forced a rebind that Commit would then have
> ignored the failure of.
> 
> Reset the HID handover after every rebind, not only in Init. A forced
> rebind from a config write re-enumerates the gadget, which releases
> every input on the host, but the recorded absolute mouse press survived
> and the next adoption replayed its release.
> 
> * test(e2e): rebind a soft-disconnected gadget, drop the press across a forced rebind
> 
> * usbgadget: persist unchanged LED reports, hold the mouse lock through the reset
> 
> After a rebind the host resends its LED state. Had it repeated the state
> the process already held, the early return would have skipped
> persisting it, and the handover the rebind had just reset would have
> carried all-off into the next adoption. A Linux host sends an all-off
> report before the real state on a fresh device, so this did not
> reproduce on the rig; persisting every report costs nothing and does
> not depend on the host's sequence.
> 
> A press reported between the mouse state reset and the file write was
> persisted and then overwritten, leaving a held button the next adoption
> would not release. Hold the lock through the write.
> 
> * usbgadget: reset the HID handover on soft reconnects too
> 
> A soft reconnect re-enumerates the gadget on the host just like a
> rebind: the recovery loop's SoftReconnect and the forced eject that
> unmount falls back to when the host holds the medium. Neither reset
> the handover, so a press recorded before one could still be replayed
> at the next adoption.
> 
> * usbgadget: reset the HID handover after a failed rebind too
> 
> A commit that fails after the soft disconnect falls back to a soft
> connect, which re-enumerates the host just like the rebind would have.
> The reset ran only on success.

- ec8ca4a55daeb1213a113a61466d8cb31db39f88 — https://github.com/jetkvm/kvm/commit/ec8ca4a55daeb1213a113a61466d8cb31db39f88
> feat(cloud): send X-Device-SKU on the cloud signaling connection (#1568)
> 
> The cloud keeps the device version from X-App-Version in memory for the
> lifetime of the connection and now does the same for the hardware SKU,
> so it can tell hardware variants apart without inferring it from the
> version string. Reuse GetDeviceSKU(), which reads /etc/jetkvm-sku and
> defaults to jetkvm-v2, the same value already sent on the update check.
- f13f34623ab9092d9f0c3ac81b516497fb89eb7f — https://github.com/jetkvm/kvm/commit/f13f34623ab9092d9f0c3ac81b516497fb89eb7f
> test(e2e): move codec retry coverage into the video suite (#1601)
- f14bd10245a545d46316582e1bd338596937395f — https://github.com/jetkvm/kvm/commit/f14bd10245a545d46316582e1bd338596937395f
> test(e2e): clean up and verify uploads and serial settings over RPC (#1588)
> 
> * test(e2e): treat shell access to the device as optional
> 
> A unit with developer mode off has no SSH, and the suite should still run
> against it and report what it covered. deviceShellAvailable() answers once
> per worker, from JETKVM_DEVICE_SSH=0 or a five second probe, and sshExec
> short-circuits on it so best-effort calls return immediately instead of
> waiting out the connect timeout. The nine specs that need the shell skip
> with a reason; the global teardown skips log capture and reset.
> 
> Test titles carry what they need: @ssh, @serial, @tls, @audio, @ota, so
> subsets can be picked with --grep and --grep-invert.
> 
> The remote agent deploy no longer falls back to a hardcoded user name;
> JETKVM_REMOTE_HOST is required. The unused prebuilt agent binary under
> e2e/remote-agent/bin is removed and ignored; the agent is built from its
> source at the repo root as before.
> 
> The login rate-limit spec runs in its own project after ui instead of
> relying on a zz- filename prefix.
> 
> * fix(e2e): guard serial setup before accessing the device shell
> 
> * test(e2e): clean up and verify uploads and serial settings over RPC
> 
> upload-cancel used the shell for three things the device already exposes:
> the size of the partial file (listStorageFiles lists it under its
> .incomplete name), removing test images (deleteStorageFile accepts the
> partial name), and the final hash. The first two go through RPC; the
> byte-for-byte hash stays behind deviceShellAvailable and the fallback is
> the final size, which still catches a truncated or doubled resume.
> 
> serial-console-takeover checked for the settings file over the shell to
> know whether to restore or delete it. It now reads the settings through
> getSerialSettings, falls back to the defaults when that fails, and
> restores through setSerialSettings. The one difference is that a device
> that had no settings file ends up with one holding the defaults.
> 
> Both specs drop the @ssh tag and run on a device without a shell.

- fdc4fd8a3270d30d6f6f5620df39562d9e3614e1 — https://github.com/jetkvm/kvm/commit/fdc4fd8a3270d30d6f6f5620df39562d9e3614e1
> fix(ui): clear HID channels and protocol version when the device route unmounts (#1572)
> 
> The unmount cleanup reset the peer, rpc and terminal channels but left
> the three HID channels and the negotiated HID protocol version in the
> store. Navigating away and back showed the closed channels until the new
> peer opened its own. Reset them with the rest, and let the setters take
> null.

#### 1. 2.41.0 / 2.41.0

item_id: kimai/kimai::release::252372911
Data: 2025-11-11T15:17:21Z

Release notes (texto original):

> **Compatible with PHP 8.1 to 8.4**
> 
> - Added structured Customer address (#5519)
> - Added timesheet ID column for export templates (#5653)
> - Fix invoice rounding issues (#5653) see [documentation](https://www.kimai.org/documentation/rounding.html)
> - Group invoice items by project and activity (#5675)
> - Deactivate `autocomplete` on `duration` input field (caused invalid click issues in Firefox) (#5653)
> - Limit API calls to a page size of 500 items max (#5653)
> - Fix dispatching `create` and `update` events for `Customer`, `Project` and `Activity` (#5653)
> - Support for custom-fields for InvoiceTemplates (only programmatically) (#5519)
> - Prepare general support for returning a Paginator from the API endpoints for better DX (#5653)
> - Translations update from Hosted Weblate (#5649)
> 
> The following **BC BREAKS** are included:
> - Limit paginated API call to a page size of 500 items max
> - The customer address was previously stored as one single large text field. Structured invoices require that the address fields are split up into address line 1/2/3, city and postcode: these fields have been added to the customer. Please adapt your code (API, plugin) to use the new fields. The old address field will be removed soon.
> - Invoice templates are now linked to one customer, whose data is used for filling all the details of the invoice (like name, address and tax number). Currently configured invoice template fields (address, company name, vat id) will not be accessible any longer via UI, but used as fallback, until a customer account is linked.
> - Deprecate `internal rate` fields in invoices (#5653)
> 
> Involved in this release: @kevinpapst

- 002702ef4d94138bfcf4bfaf4c3128bf9d058a61 — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/002702ef4d94138bfcf4bfaf4c3128bf9d058a61
> fix(extract): strip internal rawHtml from agent response sources
> 
> rawHtml is internal fuel for schema extraction; it was never stripped, so
> on the schema path it shipped hundreds of KB of raw page HTML per source,
> and on the no-schema path it inflated enforceResponseEnvelope's token count
> (over-dropping evidence/sources). Strip it from every source before both
> the schema-return and the general return in the pipeline. Adds a test
> asserting sources[].rawHtml is undefined on both paths.
- 00587449b9ea474bc7a6803efe6a8a6fed7e62b1 — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/00587449b9ea474bc7a6803efe6a8a6fed7e62b1
> feat(research): fire local synthesis via the C0 opt-in local-model tier
> 
> Widen the research synthesis gate so the local-model path also runs when
> resolveLocalModelTier() is reachable, not only when a cloud key / explicit
> provider is configured. Slotted as the middle rung: host-sampling >
> local model > deterministic evidence assembly. Per-claim [n] citations
> stay index-aligned through the shared fetched-view remap. When the tier
> is null and no cloud key is set, synthesizeLocal is never called and the
> deterministic path is byte-for-byte identical.
- 0428e1faecd5292d0c03cdec8e550e19af8b0ba2 — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/0428e1faecd5292d0c03cdec8e550e19af8b0ba2
> feat(doctor): surface the opt-in local-model tier state
> 
> Add buildLocalTierDoctorLines + wire it into doctor after the existing ollama
> block: report WIGOLO_LOCAL_LLM=off (default, discoverable) vs auto with the
> resolved endpoint + model, or enabled-but-unreachable. The resolver (and its
> fast negative-cached probe) runs only when the flag is on; off never probes.
> Untrusted model names are terminal-sanitized. Component names allowed here.
- 066cce17869655676437155374bb80e4f1b37bad — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/066cce17869655676437155374bb80e4f1b37bad

> chore(release): v0.1.40-beta.1

> Merge branch 'feat/quality-r4-local-llm' into slice-C2-synthesis-local-llm
- 0ab4d5bdf65f6c42961990050a67b2cfc3e5a73a — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/0ab4d5bdf65f6c42961990050a67b2cfc3e5a73a
> feat(search): add domain context to cross-encoder rerank input
> 
> Title+snippet alone let a short off-topic snippet game the reranker into
> a high logit (junk saturation). Append the result host to the candidate
> text so the domain is a relevance signal. Shared rerankInputText helper
> used by both the fold path and the legacy rerank path.
- 0b6037ec89a016dea181b91fd963b717cf7a6b74 — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/0b6037ec89a016dea181b91fd963b717cf7a6b74

> Exercise handleResearch / handleAgent end-to-end with the C0 opt-in
> local-model tier: local-synthesized report with index-aligned per-claim
> [n] citations, and the keyless-default no-model-call path.
- 0bb14201763f6c126e1b8acd68b4c22f1fe7e2f0 — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/0bb14201763f6c126e1b8acd68b4c22f1fe7e2f0
> feat(research): synthesizeLocal accepts an opt-in local-model tier
> 
> Route runLlmText at the tier endpoint/model and bypass the keystore
> gate when a tier is supplied — enabling synthesis when only
> WIGOLO_LOCAL_LLM is on (no cloud key, no explicit WIGOLO_LLM_PROVIDER).
> The WIGOLO_LLM_PROVIDER env is scoped to the call and restored after
> success or failure.
- 0fda1abe0d3dcd592df0f90bdb87cce4b32a5c17 — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/0fda1abe0d3dcd592df0f90bdb87cce4b32a5c17
> merge(bench2-s2): extensionless PDF routing — content-type/magic-bytes sniff + browser download backstop (round2 item 2)
- 12679ac8a86bfb6ee977a96cd36d76ee8779de2c — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/12679ac8a86bfb6ee977a96cd36d76ee8779de2c
> merge(crawl-fetch): per-page markdown budget floor + PDF byte-tier routing (items 11,12)
- 12d3dd0e95a8f28ea74c75098b6c984afa1f5c73 — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/12d3dd0e95a8f28ea74c75098b6c984afa1f5c73
> merge(bench2-s5): engine latency tail — pool soft-deadline + session-chronic tighter budget (round2 item 5)
- 144d92b44f11f8e491d81feed2b18b1da75b9b67 — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/144d92b44f11f8e491d81feed2b18b1da75b9b67
> feat(agent): prose fallback on low-confidence schema grid match
> 
> When the agent's schema extraction locks onto a wrong-shape grid — the
> schema's item declares an array-typed property (e.g. key_features) but the
> matched grid left it unfilled, the name+price add-on dump masquerading as a
> tier list — reject the typed-but-wrong rows and fall back to prose synthesis
> with an explicit warning. The bench judged typed-but-wrong 3.0 vs honest
> prose 6.5. Generic: keys on schema shape vs filled columns via the matcher's
> confidence signal, never on any site or field name; a shape-complete grid
> (array property filled) still returns typed rows.
- 17da07e8c9c9f3ea09c412a20a477b691a9866e6 — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/17da07e8c9c9f3ea09c412a20a477b691a9866e6
> merge(search-s3): adaptive engine breaker — exponential in-call retry backoff + shared UA rotation on 403 (item 6)
- 1b2cd5b495d6a492645eb88340bc60fe7fa215cf — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/1b2cd5b495d6a492645eb88340bc60fe7fa215cf
> merge(bench3-s4): research boilerplate leak — filter nav/byline from key-finding candidates (round3 item 4)
- 1db5381821de093cf175c21c3455c356dd1a4d93 — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/1db5381821de093cf175c21c3455c356dd1a4d93
> fix(extraction): feed local model the deterministic pre-extraction, not raw HTML
> 
> extractWithLocalLlm built its prompt from a ~50KB raw HTML slice. Replace
> that with the structured brief from extractStructured (tables/lists/kv/
> JSON-LD, compactly serialized) plus trimmed page markdown bounded to a
> char budget — a single, bounded-context call. The endpoint/model come from
> the resolved local-model tier and are bridged onto WIGOLO_LLM_PROVIDER for
> exactly one runLlmJson call, then restored so no ambient env survives. Any
> failure (timeout, non-200, invalid JSON, transport) now returns null so the
> caller falls back deterministically instead of throwing.
- 1ea7ff0da2e0eced5ddbb6106bccb2f4837d1d8d — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/1ea7ff0da2e0eced5ddbb6106bccb2f4837d1d8d
> feat(extraction): generic repeated-sibling list detector
> 
> Detect <ol>/<ul> listings whose <li> children share a consistent inner
> shape and carry a record signal (anchor href or numeric metric), emitting
> one TableData row per item with the anchor href and typed numeric fields.
> Slotted as a third structural detector alongside extractTables and the
> div-grid detector at the mergeGridTables seam. Purely structural — no
> site-specific class or tag is special-cased; bare nav/prose lists, short
> lists below the >=3 gate, and non-uniform containers yield nothing.
- 2022829a15b2d8e8c943aa796755567e163e9e12 — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/2022829a15b2d8e8c943aa796755567e163e9e12
> fix(fetch): route extensionless PDFs to the byte tier by content-type
> 
> Round #1's PDF routing (commit 2bd0cd9) sniffed only the URL extension, so
> an extensionless PDF URL (e.g. arxiv.org/pdf/<id>) slipped past and reached
> the browser tier, dying with 'Download is starting'. Root cause is two-fold:
> 
> - The HTTP tier returns a PDF as empty html + rawBuffer. The auto-path
>   SPA-shell heuristic saw the empty html and escalated to the browser. Now a
>   PDF result (content-type application/pdf OR %PDF- magic bytes) short-circuits
>   and returns before any SPA/anti-bot escalation. The TLS tier had the same
>   latent misclassification (looksJsRequired('') is true) and is fixed the same
>   way.
> - On a preferPlaywright domain the extensionless PDF went straight to the
>   browser. A cheap HEAD content-type probe (first-chunk magic-bytes fallback)
>   now runs only on the browser-bound auto path, rerouting any PDF to the byte
>   tier. Extension-typed URLs still short-circuit upstream, so normal HTML
>   fetches never pay for the probe.
> - The HTTP and TLS tiers now also byte-buffer a PDF served with a generic /
>   absent content-type by sniffing the %PDF- magic marker, and normalise the
>   reported content-type to application/pdf so the extractor runs pdf-parse.
> - Browser-tier download backstop: goto can reject 'Download is starting'
>   before the download event is captured. Wait briefly via waitForEvent so a
>   mis-routed PDF is intercepted as bytes instead of hard-erroring.
> 
> Pattern-level (content-type / magic bytes for any PDF), never host-specific.

> perf(search): cap engine-dispatch latency tail with a pool soft deadline
> 
> runEnginesParallel awaited every engine via Promise.all, so one straggler
> hanging toward its 10s per-engine abort budget dragged the whole response to
> ~10s even when the fast engines returned in <1s. Add a soft deadline: once it
> elapses, engines still in flight are abandoned (not awaited) and recorded as a
> timedOut EngineOutcome; their request keeps running so a late result can still
> populate cache. Chronically-tripped engines (session-scoped breaker trip count
> >= threshold) get a tighter budget so the pool stops paying a perma-failing
> engine's straggler cost on every recovery probe. The down-weight is generic and
> data-driven (observed session trips) — no engine name is special-cased.
> 
> Legacy Promise.all behaviour is preserved when no soft deadline is passed. A
> timedOut outcome (ok:false, results:[]) is excluded from fusion, engines_used
> and pool-healthy counts, and surfaces honestly as an 'error'/'timeout' warning.
> 
> Wall-clock: a 9s hung straggler drops from 9002ms to 3502ms (pool budget) and a
> chronically-tripped hung engine to 1202ms (chronic budget); happy-path warm p50
> unchanged (~0.87s).

> fix(search): recover error-token queries with atomic-token dispatch + survival damp
> 
> Queries carrying an atomic error token (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, error[E0499],
> ERROR ... SQLSTATE) returned pure junk — err.ee broadcaster, dictionary "ERR"
> definitions, unrelated brands — because general engines substring-match the
> shortest fragment ("ERR"/"ERROR") against those pages, and on the long
> natural-language form only one engine survives while it returns only junk.
> 
> Diagnosis (live): for the bare atomic token, DuckDuckGo returns perfectly
> on-target fix pages but returns ZERO for the long form; Bing returns only junk
> for the token regardless of phrase-quoting. So the long form loses the good
> results that exist.
> 
> Fix, both in the core search path:
> - error-intent.ts: SHAPE-based atomic error-token detection (no allow-list).
>   Conservative gate — SCREAMING_SNAKE only when error-flavoured, bare errno
>   only with error context, compiler codes only bracketed or error-prefixed;
>   ordinary acronyms, env/config constants, hardware/codec tokens and the bare
>   words ERROR/STATUS never fire.
> - core-provider.ts: (1) one extra concurrent bare-token dispatch when
>   error-intent fires (recovers the on-target results the long form misses),
>   suppressing the redundant rare-term quoted variant; (2) a per-result survival
>   damp at the final-ordering seam — results mentioning none of the query's
>   atomic tokens are damped 0.15x then trimmed by the score floor. Single-query
>   only; per-result hit/miss predicate; never empties the set.

> fix(extraction): restore per-story segmentation for legacy nested-table listings
> 
> Legacy nested-table listings (HN-class front pages) lay out each story as a
> CYCLE of rows — a rank+title row, a points/comments meta row, then a spacer —
> inside one header-less <table>. extractTables synthesised col_1..col_N headers
> and emitted every physical <tr> as its own row, so a listing became an
> interleaved run-on dump ({col_1:"1.",col_3:"Title"} then {col_2:"342 points…"}
> then an all-empty spacer). That dump is useless to an agent AND, carrying only
> col_N headers, matches no schema field so schema mode returns {} on the page.
> 
> The multi-column interleaved case was never handled: the round-1 degenerate
> salvage only fired for single-column (headers.length<=1) run-on tables, and the
> round-2 div-grid detector explicitly excludes <table>/<tr>/<td> tags, so a
> multi-<tr>-per-record listing fell straight through to the raw col_N mapping.
> 
> Detect the pattern at the extractTables seam and collapse it to ONE row per
> record. The gate is per-structure and narrow: header-less table (no <th>) +
> >=3 rank-ordinal record starts that are a strict minority of rows + over half
> the row×column grid empty (sparsity). A dense data grid, a sparse non-ordinal
> layout, and a <2-record table all pass through untouched. Real legacy tables
> (DistroWatch rankings, FluxBB topic list, OpenBSD errata, the RFC index) do not
> fire. Schema mode returns clean records as a consequence, no schema.ts change.
> 
> The div-grid pricing path (divs, not tables) is structurally disjoint and stays
> green. Both behaviours are locked in a permanent both-ways regression test with
> non-HN fixtures so a future round cannot silently trade one for the other.

- cd501056b0f7a8f8925a2b5ca960e70e72dadf48 — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/cd501056b0f7a8f8925a2b5ca960e70e72dadf48
> perf(search): burst-load engine-pool resilience — failure-class breaker isolation + degraded re-dispatch
> 
> Round-3 blind benchmark exposed engine-pool collapse under burst: mojeek
> 403s (reputational, persistent) and marginalia 429s (rate-limit, transient)
> tripped breakers with identical 60s cooldowns that cascaded across
> consecutive searches. Within a burst the pool degraded to bing-only and
> result quality cratered (error-token + brand-collision queries returned
> dictionary/music-lyrics junk with a starved pool while passing minutes
> earlier with a healthy pool — the classifiers were correct both times;
> engine_pool state decided the outcome).
> 
> Root cause: (1) mojeek is a perma-403 on this network — 0 results, pure
> retry-latency + breaker-trip tax on every call; (2) a 429 (transient) was
> treated identically to a 403 (persistent) — same cooldown then exponential
> backoff; (3) once mojeek+marginalia breakers opened mid-burst, error/brand
> queries had only bing left and bing-alone substring-matched junk.
> 
> Fix (generic, no benchmark special-casing, no engine-name allowlists):
> - Failure-class-aware breaker cooldowns (engine-base.ts): classifyFailure()
>   reads the error class; a rate-limit/429 gets a short 5s cooldown, a
>   forbidden/403 or other keeps the full cooldown. Keyed on error class,
>   never on an engine name — a 429 breaker recovers faster than a 403 one.
> - Degraded-recovery wave (orchestrator.ts): when the primary dispatch wave
>   leaves fewer than half the dispatched engines healthy, run ONE recovery
>   wave that force-probes the held-back probe-only roster plus any
>   breaker-open primary engine, re-fusing per-result. Recovery happens within
>   the burst instead of waiting out the cooldown. Gated per-dispatch on the
>   observed healthy count; a healthy pool never triggers it.
> - Mojeek probe-only by default (verticals/general.ts + news.ts, config
>   searchMojeekProbeOnly / WIGOLO_MOJEEK_PROBE_ONLY): held out of the primary
>   wave so it stops taxing the happy path + cascading breakers, still pulled
>   by the recovery wave when the pool collapses. Config-overridable.
> 
> Live warm-process burst: before-fix wave-2 error queries collapsed to
> healthy=1/5 (bing-only) with junk; after-fix the pool stays healthy=2-4/4
> across the burst with all breakers closed at end, and happy-path p50 latency
> improves 490ms->276ms (mojeek's per-call retry tax removed from the primary
> wave, so the round-2 soft-deadline tail is tighter, not regressed).

> fix(extraction): semantic row-selection for schema plan/tier arrays
> 
> Root cause: matchArrayOfObjectsFromStructures returned the FIRST extracted
> grid clearing the 2-property match gate, with no ranking. A pricing page
> carries both plan tiers (name+price+features, a handful of rows) and an
> add-ons/resources section (name+price, many rows); first-wins let the add-on

> 
> Fix (all in the shared matcher, inherited by extract-schema and agent-schema):
> - Score every qualifying grid and return the best instead of first-wins.
>   Score = matched scalar props (dominant) + array props actually filled
>   (full-shape signal separating tiers-with-features from add-ons) + a SOFT
>   2-6-row plausibility prior. The prior is a tie-breaker only: it never
>   truncates rows or drops a legit >6-tier list.
> - Bind a name/title/label property from a tier-synonym header
>   (plan/tier/product/package), scoped to single-token identity columns so it
>   never widens price/feature matching or the no-false-positive gate.
> 
> Selection is now order-independent and prefers the fuller-shaped, plausibly
> -sized grid; the no-false-positive bar (both name and price must bind) is
> unchanged.

> merge(search-s4): search-phase fetch enrichment hardening — prewarm, narrow-set budget scaling, snippet fallback (item 7)

> merge(bench3-s1): engine-pool burst resilience — failure-class breaker isolation + degraded re-dispatch + mojeek probe-only (round3 item 1)
- dc6972d5dffef4388adf3f3614ddb8d5a522997d — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/dc6972d5dffef4388adf3f3614ddb8d5a522997d
> feat(search): docs vertical general-web fallback + brand-collision detector v2
> 
> Docs pool (was MDN + DevDocs only, guaranteed starvation on any docs subject
> they do not index) gains Bing + DuckDuckGo as secondary general-web signals so
> every docs query has web recall; the orchestrator's secondary-only demotion
> keeps them from outranking a real MDN/DevDocs hit.
> 
> Brand-collision detector rewritten to fire on a proper-noun-head + generic-tail
> query regardless of token count (old gate required <=2 tokens, all common
> nouns, so a 3-token "Entity + generic tail" collision never fired). The head is
> a Capitalized-word proper noun (structural casing signal, reusing the query
> entity extractor); a generic category noun anywhere after it triggers the
> collision. Error-token queries and bare acronyms are excluded. The duplicate
> predicate in query-understanding + brand-collision is unified into one export.
> The warning carries an entity-qualified rewrite that anchors the entity head
> verbatim, and core-provider dual-dispatches that rewrite concurrently,
> RRF-merging it and recording it in queries_executed so the fan-out is auditable.
- dc944dcda479210886b4ed356525b83e1be29c77 — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/dc944dcda479210886b4ed356525b83e1be29c77
> fix(extract): keyless schema fuzzy-matches nested array-of-objects onto grids
> 
> A pricing schema like {tiers:[{name,price,key_features}]} matched 0 fields
> through both extract and `wigolo agent` and fell back to prose, even against a
> page whose tier facts sat in a clean <table>/div-grid. The keyless fuzzy
> matcher only resolved a schema field NAME to a single scalar; a top-level
> array-of-objects field ("tiers") had no structure literally named "tiers", so
> it fell through to the crude class-name heuristic and returned run-on garbage.
> 
> Teach the shared extractWithSchemaDetailed engine to map an array-of-objects
> field onto the best-matching extracted grid: one item object per row, each
> scalar item property fuzzy-matched to a header, and array-typed item properties
> (key_features) harvesting the card's feature_* columns. The no-false-positive
> gate counts only scalar matches (MIN_ITEM_MATCHES), so an unrelated grid
> (weather/SERP) whose headers match nothing yields undefined, never junk rows.
> 
> The agent pipeline already carries rawHtml per source and calls this same
> engine, so the fix is unified — no forked second matcher.
- de2f3b760db3092c6fae169365c632c72355420a — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/de2f3b760db3092c6fae169365c632c72355420a
> feat(agent): fire synthesis via the C0 opt-in local-model tier
> 
> Add the local-model tier as the middle rung of the agent synthesis
> ladder (host-sampling > local model > deterministic). It runs only when
> no cloud key / explicit provider produced the result above and host
> sampling did not answer, so the existing explicit-provider precedence and
> sampling behavior are unchanged. Routes runLlmText at the tier
> endpoint/model via a scoped-and-restored WIGOLO_LLM_PROVIDER. Null tier
> (the keyless default) makes zero network calls and drops straight to the
> deterministic evidence fallback.
- de53ed14edb3e04a0f0d967c778827b1de5e5b4d — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/de53ed14edb3e04a0f0d967c778827b1de5e5b4d
> feat(search): orchestrator ranking rescue — error-token atomicity, dictionary demotion, domain-scoped backfill, undated news demotion, starvation re-dispatch
> 
> Fixes four core retrieval failures where wigolo scored last on a blind
> benchmark:
> 
> - Error-code queries: detect all-caps status/error tokens (ERR_*, ENOENT,
>   SQLSTATE, TypeError-style class names) and quote each in place so engines
>   match the code as one atom instead of a bare substring that lets glossary
>   junk rank. Error tokens no longer route into the docs vertical.
> - Dictionary demotion: per-result gate in domainQualityScore — a dictionary/
>   glossary host is dropped to 0.25 ONLY when the query carries an error token.
>   A normal query leaves the same host at 1.0 (hit/miss, never query-wide).
> - Domain scoping + backfill: inject a site: operator into the dispatched query
>   for a small include_domains set (engines that honour it narrow at source);
>   applyDomainFilters stays the hard post-filter. When the on-domain survivors
>   fall short of max_results, a broad backfill wave refills with on-domain hits.
> - News undated demotion: on a recency-bound news query, undated results are
>   demoted (x0.3) rather than dropped so dated in-window pages win top slots
>   without collapsing recall.
> - Per-result starvation re-dispatch: a thin non-general vertical that fuses
>   fewer than the floor pulls the general pool with the same query, RRF-merges
>   per-result, and re-scores. Gated on post-fusion COUNT, distinct from the
>   query-wide degraded fallback.
> 
> Adds SearchOutput.engine_pool { healthy, total, degraded, reasons? } as the
> single pool-health surface, populated from engine telemetry + dispatch degrade
> reasons (starvation_redispatch).
- e0cd1699404d458ef5d59e06f8e5e2e40a2768e7 — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/e0cd1699404d458ef5d59e06f8e5e2e40a2768e7
> fix(search): bare-zero cross-encoder logit no longer saturates tier-1
> 
> A logit at ~0 is the sigmoid midpoint (uncertain), yet the tier gate
> (logit >= 0) promoted it to the [0.5,1.0] confidently-relevant band; an
> all-near-zero (all-junk) batch, where the normaliser returns the neutral
> 0.5, mapped every result to 0.75. Require a logit above a small positive
> margin for tier-1 so uncertain/near-zero results fall to tier-0.
- e572926dd4bc0b2d43844793ec25d90a09d93a3e — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/e572926dd4bc0b2d43844793ec25d90a09d93a3e
> fix(extraction): skip chrome-landmark lists in list detector
> 
> A live over-fire probe showed the list detector firing 21 times on a docs
> page's <nav> sidebar link menus — linked lists that pass the anchor signal
> but are page chrome, not data feeds. Add the nav/footer/header/aside +
> role=navigation landmark guard the card detector already uses, so a nav menu
> is rejected while a genuine content feed (a <ul> of linked articles in
> <main>) still surfaces.
- e637c95b90dd63f4b8d987160754bca8a67bd5b3 — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/e637c95b90dd63f4b8d987160754bca8a67bd5b3
> merge(extract): degenerate-table fix + div/flex-grid detector + keyless schema fuzzy-match & agent wire (items 8,9,10)
- e68d830281505445d683f03cbf6cbeac55f56dc6 — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/e68d830281505445d683f03cbf6cbeac55f56dc6
> merge(search-s2): docs vertical general-web fallback + brand-collision detector v2 with gated entity-qualified dual-dispatch (items 1-docs, 3)
- e7761d79a1da0e4812386cc5e7a18b7f791158da — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/e7761d79a1da0e4812386cc5e7a18b7f791158da
> fix(crawl): scale per-page markdown budget so later pages are not starved
> 
> DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS_OUT was a shared aggregate cap across all crawled
> pages, so once early pages consumed it every later page was cleared to
> '' by applyAggregateMarkdownBudget. Scale the default with page count
> (bounded by max_total_chars and a ceiling) and add an opt-in
> minTokensPerItem floor to applyAggregateMarkdownBudget so a page with
> real content is never emptied while an earlier page kept content. The
> floor defaults to a no-op, keeping search/find_similar/research/agent/
> cache callers byte-identical.
- e93181f9e24d29eec0956c8abf43c537e5b61353 — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/e93181f9e24d29eec0956c8abf43c537e5b61353

> docs: add agent demo videos and rewrite benchmark section (#135)

> - Add live Claude Code demo (wigolo fetch-router) as MP4/WebM/poster
>   companions to the existing GIF
> - Add 4-way head-to-head (WebSearch, wigolo, Tavily, Firecrawl) video assets

>   'why it's different' close to lead with wigolo's strengths

- f075482aa1edf614fa8035ab590788b7e566552e — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/f075482aa1edf614fa8035ab590788b7e566552e
> fix(extraction): deterministic field binding for interleaved listings
> 
> Bind the interleaved multi-tr listing's title to the record's story anchor
> text (first non-metric anchor in DOM order), not the longest cell — the old
> longest-cell rule swapped title<->meta whenever the meta line ran longer than
> a short title. Capture the story anchor's href per row and surface numeric
> metrics (points/comments) as typed num_N fields instead of leaving them
> buried in the prose meta blob.
- f56e409ae4ff29bbb306fdf408323909ff436bb3 — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/f56e409ae4ff29bbb306fdf408323909ff436bb3
> feat(search): harden search-phase fetch enrichment (item 7)
> 
> Narrow candidate sets, cold browser pools, and empty-on-timeout content
> starved search enrichment. Three pattern-level fixes on the fetch path:
> 
> - Narrow-set per-URL budget scaling: when few candidates are hydrated,
>   each gets a proportionally larger per-URL budget (narrowSetBudgetMs /
>   candidateCount), floored at the base and clamped to the stage budget.
>   Keys on candidateCount (structural), never a domain allowlist. Computed
>   at the core-provider fetch call site from items.length.
> - Snippet fallback on timeout: a per-URL/stage/total timeout now promotes
>   the result's own snippet into markdown_content (content_from_snippet
>   flag) instead of leaving it empty. Scoped to timeout-class failures;
>   never fabricates; the failure stays recorded in fetch_failed.
> - Browser pool pre-warm: SmartRouter.prewarmBrowser() -> MultiBrowserPool
>   .warm() pre-launches the default browser type before enrichment on
>   balanced/deep with include_content, so the first hydration fetch does
>   not pay the cold start inline. Idempotent + best-effort.
> 
> The per-URL budget is enforced via the existing per-URL timeout signal
> already threaded through every SmartRouter.fetch tier (stealth, TLS-
> impersonation, browser, HTTP) — no new fetch option is threaded. Config
> knobs searchNarrowSetBudgetMs + searchPrewarmBrowser default to today's
> behavior for legacy paths (the legacy orchestrator omits the new context
> fields, so its enrichment is unchanged).
- f7de60d8dfa7309f9bcff0b08d35ca7f28c43682 — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/f7de60d8dfa7309f9bcff0b08d35ca7f28c43682
> merge(r4-C1): schema extraction via optional local language model — feeds the model the deterministic pre-extraction (main-content markdown) not raw HTML, schema-validated + evidence-filtered, deterministic fallback; endpoint threaded per-call via runLlm backend override (no process.env mutation, concurrency-safe); byte-for-byte when tier off
- f8d9864d1d3a20a21cf23869eb4fe29486ff96dc — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/f8d9864d1d3a20a21cf23869eb4fe29486ff96dc
> merge(bench2-s1): error-token recovery — atomic-token bare dispatch + per-result survival damp (round2 item 1)
- fdb40b4981d1d0e4b3eff4a3b9754cf52ff31538 — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/fdb40b4981d1d0e4b3eff4a3b9754cf52ff31538
> merge(r4-A): search ranking bugs — per-engine floor rescue (min-relevance gated) fixes kept-0; hook-family lexical + brand/entity collision auto-dispatch; rerank URL-context + tier-margin + compound junk-floor guard

- 197d4e2dceac2e598d60ed175c31f84e9e1427a0 — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/197d4e2dceac2e598d60ed175c31f84e9e1427a0
> fix(cli): make --agents optional in non-interactive init
> 
> Non-interactive init no longer requires --agents. Without it, wigolo sets
> up the local engine (on-device models, browser, cache) and skips agent
> wiring, so any MCP-capable agent (not just the built-in installers) can be
> pointed at the server by hand. --agents remains the auto-wire shortcut.
> 
> Also correct the site quickstart: the install command drops the mandatory
> --agents, and the answer-synthesis step now shows setting the provider AND
> its model (a provider alone is not enough).

> fix(serve): add server-level request + headers timeouts (slow-loris)
> 
> The daemon HTTP server never set requestTimeout / headersTimeout, so a
> slow-drip client stayed under the per-request byte cap yet held a
> connection — and, since /v1 acquires a concurrency slot before the body
> read, a slot — for Node's ~300s default. Set bounded defaults
> (requestTimeout 120s, headersTimeout 60s) on the http.Server in start(),
> env-overridable via WIGOLO_SERVE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS /
> WIGOLO_SERVE_HEADERS_TIMEOUT_MS. Room left for legit large
> crawls-over-REST.

> fix(repl): create shell history file owner-only, no chmod TOCTOU (LOW-2)
> 
> appendFileSync created the history file under the process umask, then chmodSync
> 0o600 only when fresh — a loose umask left a brief world/group-readable window
> between create and chmod. Pass { mode: 0o600 } to appendFileSync so the mode
> applies at creation; drop the follow-up chmod. Existing-file appends and the
> piped/json no-append behavior are unchanged.
- 214b099b38c10180a94c15383b1d704bc535f73a — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/214b099b38c10180a94c15383b1d704bc535f73a
> fix(search): skip max-normalisation for a weak top on a degraded pool
> 
> Max-normalisation divides every score by the top score, so a single-junk
> degraded pool's top becomes 1.0 by construction — the live-incident ~1.0
> mechanism. When the pool is degraded AND the top pre-normalised score is below
> an absolute confidence floor, skip the stretch so a low-confidence junk survivor
> is not manufactured into a 1.0 evidence score. Threads the degraded signal into
> the normalisation seam, closing the timing gap where the pool-health object was

> 
> The stealth acquisition/setup (acquireStealthSlot + launch + newContext +
> addInitScript + newPage) runs outside the main try/finally, so any throw
> there leaked the semaphore slot permanently and orphaned a launched browser.
> After maxBrowsers such failures acquireStealthSlot queued forever, hanging
> every later stealth fetch. Wrap the setup in a local try/catch that closes
> the throwaway browser and frees the slot before rethrowing; the happy-path
> finally stays the sole releaser (catch never runs on success). newPage's
> stealth path gets the same guard, keyed on `dedicated`.

> fix(searxng): pip self-upgrade on Windows, gate native bootstrap, accept podman
> 
> pip.exe cannot overwrite itself while running on Windows, so the venv
> bootstrap upgraded pip via `python -m pip` instead of invoking pip.exe
> directly. Separately, SearXNG's own `searx/valkeydb.py` unconditionally
> imports the POSIX-only `pwd` module, and upstream has confirmed native
> Windows support isn't a goal (github.com/searxng/searxng/discussions/4029) —
> native bootstrap now fails fast on win32 with an actionable message instead
> of burning minutes on a doomed install, and resolveSearchBackend() routes
> straight to a container or the core backend.
> 
> Since the fallback is a container either way, checkDockerAvailable() and
> DockerSearxng now resolve any docker-compatible CLI on PATH (docker or
> podman) instead of assuming Docker Desktop specifically.

> security: harden URL guards, plugin install, exec surface
> 
> Addresses the audit findings from L99's 2026-07-13 review of
> KnockOutEZ/wigolo commit 9a5c8d0:
> 
> 1. SSRF: extend guardUrl() with a fetch-friendly variant guardFetchUrl()
>    and wire it into fetch, crawl, extract, agent. Loopback stays allowed
>    (docs promise localhost:3000 works). 169.254/16 + metadata hostnames
>    blocked unconditionally. RFC 1918 + CGN blocked unless the user opts
>    in via WIGOLO_FETCH_ALLOW_PRIVATE=1.
> 
> 2. Plugin install: print the resolved repo name + target dir and require
>    interactive confirmation before git clone. --yes / WIGOLO_PLUGIN_AUTO_YES=1
>    bypass for scripted installs. Non-TTY without --yes now errors cleanly
>    instead of cloning silently.
> 
> 3. Exec surface: convert searxng/docker.ts and claude-code.ts from
>    execSync(string) to execFileSync(bin, [argv]) so shell metacharacters
>    in config values can't ever become command injection.
> 
> 4. SearXNG secret: generate a random 32-byte secret per install instead
>    of the hardcoded 'wigolo-local-only'. Stays inside 127.0.0.1 bind
>    but removes the known-string if the bind address ever changes.
> 
> 5. Dependency hygiene: add overrides block pinning hono >= 4.12.25 to
>    close the CORS-credential-reflection + serve-static path-traversal
>    CVEs that npm audit flagged in transitive deps.
> 
> Tests:
> - 53 ssrf tests (28 new for guardFetchUrl)
> - 27 plugin tests (3 new for the confirmation flow)
> - 16 claude-code tests (rewired to assert on argv array)
> 
> All watch + cli tests green. Tool tests not regressed by these changes
> (failures observed are pre-existing missing native binaries
> @anush008/tokenizers-linux-arm64-gnu and better-sqlite3 native binding).

- 94a48532f8ab993252f396359a47375cf3db0310 — https://github.com/KnockOutEZ/wigolo/commit/94a48532f8ab993252f396359a47375cf3db0310
> fix(search): tune breakers, reset chronic status, add throttle-as-skip
> 
> Rate-limit (429) failures no longer feed the exponential trips/sessionTrips
> counters: a 429 opens the breaker on the transient 5s window and repeated 429
> probe-failures stay capped at 30s instead of climbing the hard-failure ladder.
> Hard failures (403/5xx/other) are unchanged in kind but the exponential cap is
> lowered from 600s to 180s. sessionTrips now resets on a successful half-open
> recovery so chronic status is escapable.
> 
> Adds a public resetBreakers() (clears all breaker state incl. sessionTrips) with
> _resetBreakersForTest kept as a delegating alias for zero importer churn.
> 
> Adds throttle-as-skip: a per-engine minimum inter-request interval (marginalia
> 2s). A call inside the interval is skipped via ThrottledError (a BreakerOpenError
> subclass, so the pool maps it to skipped:true with no forwarding change) rather
> than waited on, keeping pool deadlines and multi-query fan-out uncoupled.

> fix(fetch): browser tier recognises modern-CF challenge (header trigger, body clear-check, cleared-result normalise)
> 
> The browser tier's challenge settle used only legacy body markers, so a
> modern Cloudflare 403 (cf-mitigated: challenge, body's only signal the
> /cdn-cgi/challenge-platform/ script) never entered the completion poll and
> its shell could leak as content.
> 
> - TRIGGER now uses the header-inclusive isChallengeResponse so a modern-CF
>   403 enters pollUntilCleared (the header fires even with no legacy markers).
> - CLEAR-CHECK is a new body-only stillShowingChallenge predicate keyed on the
>   RENDERED DOM (never the stale nav header): hasBrowserChallengeBody OR the
>   challenge-platform marker on a text-length skeleton. A real article that
>   references the path is not a skeleton, so a cleared page reports cleared.
> - On a cleared challenge the browser result is normalised (status -> 200,
>   stale cf-mitigated header dropped) so the router success guard won't
>   mislabel a genuine pass as blocked_by_challenge.

> replaced by doctor cold checks (presence/snapshot only), so a --no-warmup
> init writes zero model/browser bytes. --json now carries per-component
> status (browserEngine/embeddings/reranker) + the doctor results, using
> capability-language keys.

> fix(setup): lazy-aware setup-status classifier for engine-only init
> 
> Align the setup-status classifier with P0 lazy component acquisition and

> 
> - agents component is required ONLY when registration was requested
>   (--agents given or interactive selection). In engine-only mode
>   (non-interactive, no --agents) it reports 'skipped' with an engine-only

> fix(rest): cap concurrent running compat crawl jobs at 16
> 
> The job-store caps bound storage, not execution — rapid crawl POSTs could
> launch unbounded concurrent background crawls (each up to the max_pages
> clamp). Add a running-jobs cap (default 16, WIGOLO_SERVE_MAX_COMPAT_JOBS
> override) counting jobs in 'scraping'; an over-cap POST is refused with
> 429 {success:false} + Retry-After: 5, never queued. Capacity frees when a
> crawl settles (success, in-band error, or rejection).

> fix(rest): apply /v1 slot+deadline discipline to firecrawl-compat shim
> 
> The synchronous compat shim routes (scrape/search/map) and the crawl
> start/status routes bypassed the REST concurrency cap and per-route
> deadline — an unbounded escape hatch past D7/D11. Extract a shared
> runUnderSlotAndDeadline helper mirroring handleToolRequest (acquire slot
> before work, 429 on exhaustion, 504 on deadline, slot released only on
> settle, respond() double-write guarded, detached late-rejection catch)
> and wrap the shim branch in it. Scrape reuses the fetch deadline, search
> the search deadline, map the crawl deadline; crawl start/status take a
> short deadline. The background crawl job model (runningCrawlJobs) is
> unchanged — the POST holds a transient slot for its own work only.

> reference them.
> 
> Fixed by inlining table creation directly in each test function and removing
> the now-unused setup function.

Release notes (texto original):

> ## [2.6.0] — 2026-08-26 — Certification Consolidation + Engine Cleanup + v2.2 Promotion
> 
> ### 🏆 Certified — 12 Families · 26 Model/Quant Combinations
> 
> Shimmy's certification pipeline has been **consolidated from the old 5-gate + CHAT regime into a clean 3-box regimen** (MATH + INFERENCE + DETERMINISM), matching the airframe 0.4.0 release. The regression-causing chat box is gone, replaced with deterministic inference verification.
> 
> **The 3-box certification regimen:**
> 1. **MATH** — GPU dequant audit, structural peel, plan-vs-peel reds, numerical self-consistency
> 2. **INFERENCE** — 5-prompt battery (factual / creative / arithmetic / kv_cache / dev_question) on real GPU
> 3. **DETERMINISM** — two identical runs must produce identical text
> 
> **26 certified model/quant combinations across 12 families** — up from 25 in v2.4.0. New: llama-3.1-8b, qwen2-7b, gemma-2-2b (plus re-certification of all prior models under the new regimen).
> 
> ### Highlights
> 
> - **v2.2 release cleanup promoted to main** — Legacy engine code stripped (huggingface.rs, mlx.rs, universal.rs, rustchain_compat.rs removed — ~1,600 lines deleted). Feature flags cleaned. Shimmy is now a pure Airframe product.
> - **CI simplified** — Removed huggingface/mlx/llama references from CI/CD. Faster, cleaner builds.
> - **Certification alignment** — Shimmy's cert documentation, README, and supported-models tables now align with airframe's 3-box regimen and 26-model count.
> 
> ### Removals
> 
> - **`engine/huggingface.rs`** (428 lines) — removed
> - **`engine/mlx.rs`** (323 lines) — removed
> - **`engine/universal.rs`** (573 lines) — removed
> - **`src/rustchain_compat.rs`** (306 lines) — removed
> - **`docs/rustchain-provider.md`** (40 lines) — removed
> - All RustChain provider references scrubbed from docs, .gitignore, lib.rs
> 
> ### Documentation
> 
> - **v2-roadmap.md** added (131 lines) — current roadmap and release planning
> - Chinese user manuals updated
> - Safetensors release status clarified
> 
> ### Infrastructure
> 
> - **Beads issue tracking initialized** — `.beads/` Dolt-backed board for durable task tracking
> - **Cargo.lock refreshed** for path-sourced airframe patch
> 
> ### Commits
> 18 commits since v2.5.0 — see git log `v2.5.0..HEAD` for full list.
>

#### 1. v1.1.0 / v1.1.0

item_id: modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk::release::258488293
Data: 2025-10-30T14:32:21Z
URL: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/releases/tag/v1.1.0

Release notes (texto original):

> This release introduces a few new features, and includes improvements and bug fixes for the streamable transport. Notably, the default behavior of the streamable server transport is changed to disable streams resumption (see #580).
> 
> ## Behavior Changes
> 
> **Stream resumption disabled by default**. In the `StreamableServerTransport`, the default value of `nil` for the `EventStore` field now disables stream resumption, rather than defaulting to use an in-memory event store. Resumption is not desirable in many cases, particularly for servers that must serve a large number of users and/or streams.
> 
> If you want to enable resumption, set `StreamableHTTPOptions.EventStore`.
> 
> In general, we will avoid changing behaviors that may be relied upon by users, but in this case the old default was deemed to be an oversight/bug, and fixing it now will benefit future users.
> 
> ## API Additions
> 
> - **`IOTransport`** is a new general-purpose transport constructed from an `io.ReadCloser` and `io.WriteCloser` (#444 ).
> - **`ServerOptions.Logger`** and **`StreamableHTTPOptions.Logger`** enable server-side logging (#170).
> - **`StreamableHTTPOptions.EventStore`** enables stream resumption (#587).
> - **`StreamableHTTPOptions.SessionTimeout`** adds a timeout which, when set, causes idle sessions to be automatically closed (#499).
> 
> ## Experimental client-side oauth support
> 
> The `auth` package now includes experimental APIs when build with the `mcp_go_client_oauth` build tag. See [auth/client.go](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/blob/1a907bcd6fddbac1116145f81fa7bb9f76d59b1a/auth/client.go) for more details. These APIs may change before their official release.
> 
> ## New Contributors
> * @atomAltera made their first contribution in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/376
> * @Adebayo120 made their first contribution in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/555
> * @jhrozek made their first contribution in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/561
> * @AdrielVelazquez made their first contribution in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/566
> * @appleboy made their first contribution in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/567
> * @RyoKusnadi made their first contribution in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/563
> * @TomCN0803 made their first contribution in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/581
> * @rutu1717 made their first contribution in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/603
> 
> **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/compare/v1.0.0...v1.1.0

> mcp: fix goroutine leaks in unit tests (#496)
> 
> This PR fixes goroutine leaks in all unit tests.
> 
> To find the leaks I integrated https://github.com/uber-go/goleak and I
> suggest to keep using it to catch any future regressions.
> 
> I used the folowing script to more easily find individual tests which
> were leaking goroutines:
> 
> ```
> for t in $(go test -run=Nothing -list=. ./mcp | grep -v ok); do go test ./mcp -run="$t" > /dev/null && echo -n . || echo -e "\nDetected leak: $t"; done
> ```
- 069aae16df70ea254fe703c77b263d3b919f3e44 — https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/commit/069aae16df70ea254fe703c77b263d3b919f3e44
> mcp: add client-side OAuth flow (#544)
> 
> This is a preliminary implementation of OAuth 2.1 for the client.
> 
> When a StreamableClientTransport encounters a 401 Unauthorized response
> from the server, it initiates the OAuth flow described in thec
> authorization section of the MCP spec
> 
> (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/authorization).
> On success, the transport obtains an access token which it passes
> to all subsequent requests.
> 
> Much remains to be done here:
> 
> * Resource Indicators, as described in section 2.5.1 of the MCP spec.
> 
> * All of this is unexported, so it is available only to our own
> StreamingClientTransport. We should add API so people can use it
> with their own transports.
> 
> * And, of course, tests. We should test against fake implementations
> but also, if we can find any, real reference implementations.
> 
> For #19
> Co-authored-by: Jonathan Amsterdam <jba@google.com>
> 
> ---------
> 
> Co-authored-by: Jonathan Amsterdam <jba@google.com>
- 104d39c6099e0754b73c30084b7053d642713e86 — https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/commit/104d39c6099e0754b73c30084b7053d642713e86
> mcp: allow disabling stream replay; disable by default (#585)
> 
> This CL implements two changes that must be logically connected.
> 
> The first is to provide a mechanism for disabling stream replay.
> Previously, our documentation stated that if
> StreamableServerTransport.EventStore was nil, a default in-memory event
> store would be used. In that case, there would be no way to completely
> disable stream replay, and as described in #576, there are many cases
> where replay is undesirable.
> 
> But of course changing the behavior of the transport zero value
> implicitly affects its default behavior, and so this CL also implements
> the proposal #580: stream replay is disabled by default.
> 
> Implementing this change required a significant refactoring, as
> previously we were relying on the event store for serialized message
> delivery from the JSON-RPC layer to the MCP layer: the connection would
> write to the event store, and independently the stream (be it an
> incoming POST or replay GET) would iterate and serve messages in the
> stream.
> 
> In order to achieve the goals of this CL, it was necessary to decouple
> storage from delivery. The 'stream' abstraction now tracks a delivery
> callback that writes straight to the HTTP response. It would have been
> convenient to store the ongoing http.ResponseWriter directly in the
> stream (this is how typescript does it), but due to the design of our
> EventStore API, only the HTTP handler knows the next event index, so a
> 'deliver' abstraction was an unfortunate requirement (suggestions for
> how to further simplify this are welcome).
> 
> More simplification is possible: in particular, as a result of this
> refactoring it should be entirely possible to clean up streams once
> we've received all responses. Any replay would only need access to the
> EventStore, if at all. This is left to a follow-up CL, to limit this
> already significant change.
> 
> Furthermore, a nice consequence of this refactoring is that, when not
> using event storage, servers can get synchronous feedback that message
> delivery failed, which should avoid unnecessary work. We can
> additionally cancel ongoing requests on early client termination, but
> that is also left to a follow-up CL.
> 
> Throughout, the terminology 'standalone SSE stream' replaced 'hanging
> GET' when referring to the non-replay GET request issued by the client.
> This is consistent with other SDKs.
> 
> Fixes #576
> Updates #580
- 1059f59a27e9705c6b40d7e703176545cb72dc0f — https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/commit/1059f59a27e9705c6b40d7e703176545cb72dc0f
> internal/oauthex: fix GetProtectedResourceMetadataFromHeader validation (#561)

Release notes (texto original):

> _**This release is equivalent to v1.3.0-pre.1. Thank you to those who tested the pre-release.**_
> 
> This release includes several enhancements and bugfixes. Worth mentioning is the addition of schema caching, which significantly improves the performance in some stateless server deployment scenarios.
> 
> ## Dependency updates
> * go.mod: upgrade to jsonschema v0.4.2 by @jba in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/732
> 
> ## Enhancements
> * perf: add schema caching to avoid repeated reflection by @SamMorrowDrums in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/685
> * mcp: add DisableListening option to StreamableClientTransport by @zxxf18 in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/729
> * feat: deprecated logger in client & add Logger in ClientOption by @CocaineCong in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/738
> * feat: deleted the old logger in client by @CocaineCong in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/744
> * Export GetError and SetError methods by @jba in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/753
> 
> ## Bugfixes
> * fix: connectStandaloneSSE checking Content-Type header by @liushuangls in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/736
> * mcp: fix SSEClientTransport to report HTTP errors properly by @hassan123789 in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/740
> * mcp: add Allow header to 405 responses per RFC 9110 §15.5.6 by @SamMorrowDrums in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/757
> * mcp: fix a race condition in logging by @maciej-kisiel in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/761
> 
> ## Chores
> * docs: adds SDK version support matrix by @La002 in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/737
> * .github/workflows: add nightly conformance tests by @findleyr in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/752
> 
> ## New Contributors

- 52e03de6c86c413ddee4bf4991e558ab97a630b6 — https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/commit/52e03de6c86c413ddee4bf4991e558ab97a630b6
> mcp: add Allow header to 405 responses per RFC 9110 §15.5.6 (#757)
> 
> 405 Method Not Allowed responses MUST include an Allow header listing
> supported methods, per RFC 9110 Section 15.5.6. This fixes issues with
> strict HTTP gateways (like Apigee) that treat 405 responses without an
> Allow header as malformed, returning 502 Bad Gateway errors.
> 
> ## Changes
> 
> - **SSEHandler**: Add `Allow: GET, POST` header for unsupported methods
> - **StreamableHTTPHandler**: Add Allow header for GET-without-session case:
>   - Stateless mode: `Allow: POST, DELETE` (GET is never valid)
>   - Stateful mode: `Allow: GET, POST, DELETE` (GET is valid once you have
> a session)
> - Add tests to verify Allow header presence in all 405 responses
> 
> ## RFC 9110 Reference
> 
> [Section 15.5.6 (405 Method Not
> Allowed)](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9110.html#status.405):
> 
> > The origin server MUST generate an Allow header field in a 405
> response containing a list of the target resource's currently supported
> methods.
> 
> ## Testing
> 
> All existing tests pass, plus new tests added:
> - `TestSSE405AllowHeader` - verifies SSE handler compliance
> - `TestStreamable405AllowHeader` - verifies Streamable handler
> compliance in both stateful and stateless modes
> 
> ---------
> 
> Co-authored-by: omgitsads <4619+omgitsads@users.noreply.github.com>

- b4f957ff3c279051f9bcc88aa08e897add012a95 — https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/commit/b4f957ff3c279051f9bcc88aa08e897add012a95
> mcp: add DisableListening option to StreamableClientTransport (#729)
> 
> mcp: add DisableStandaloneSSE option to control standalone SSE stream
> 
> Currently, StreamableClientTransport always establishes a standalone SSE
> connection after initialization to receive server-initiated messages.
> While this is useful for receiving notifications like
> ToolListChangedNotification, it causes problems in several real-world
> scenarios:
> 
> 1. **Unnecessary resource usage**: Many use cases (for me), especially
> in scientific computing scenarios, only require simple request-response
> communication. Clients don't need server-initiated notifications, making
> the persistent SSE connection wasteful.
> 
> 2. **Server compatibility issues**: Some third-party MCP servers don't
> properly handle GET requests for SSE streams. When the client
> automatically tries to establish the SSE connection, it fails or hangs,
> blocking the entire connection process. This is particularly problematic
> when using third-party servers that cannot be modified. This issue is
> similar to what was discussed in issue #634.
> 
> 3. **Lack of user control**: The MCP specification states that the
> standalone SSE stream is optional ("The client MAY issue an HTTP GET"),
> but the current SDK implementation doesn't provide a way to opt out.
> This implementation is also inconsistent with other MCP SDKs like
> github.com/mark3labs/mcp-go, which provides getListeningEnabled control
> (defaults to false, requires explicit enablement).
> 
> Fixes #728
> 
> Co-authored-by: zhaoxin <zhaoxin@pjlab.org.cn>
- c2c7edc3f026a63ce82fa6a2bf5359c48b441502 — https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/commit/c2c7edc3f026a63ce82fa6a2bf5359c48b441502
> perf: add schema caching to avoid repeated reflection (#685)
> 
> ## Summary
> 
> This PR adds schema caching that dramatically reduces the cost of tool
> registration in stateless server patterns.
> 
> **Contributors:** Thanks to @omgitsads and @almaleksia for collaborating
> on and researching this solution!
> 
> ## Problem
> 
> In stateless deployments like `github/github-mcp-server`, a new
> `*mcp.Server` is created for each incoming request. This means `AddTool`
> is called repeatedly for the same tools, causing:
> 
> 1. **For typed handlers**: `jsonschema.ForType()` reflection is called
> every time
> 2. **For pre-defined schemas**: `schema.Resolve()` is called every time
> 
> ## Solution
> 
> Add a `schemaCache` that stores:
> - Schemas by `reflect.Type` (for auto-generated schemas from typed
> handlers)
> - Resolved schemas by schema pointer (for pre-defined schemas)
> 
> The cache is:
> - Concurrent-safe using `sync.Map`
> - Unbounded (typical MCP servers have &lt;100 tools)
> - Global (lives across server instances)
> 
> ## Benchmark Results
> 
> ```
> BenchmarkAddToolTypedHandler-22          977080    1223 ns/op     1208 B/op    21 allocs/op
> BenchmarkAddToolTypedHandlerNoCache-22    6764  161463 ns/op    39262 B/op  1072 allocs/op
> ```
> 
> | Metric | With Cache | Without Cache | Improvement |
> |--------|------------|---------------|-------------|
> | Time | 1,223 ns/op | 161,463 ns/op | **132x faster** |
> | Allocations | 21 allocs | 1,072 allocs | **51x fewer** |
> | Memory | 1,208 B/op | 39,262 B/op | **32x less** |
> 
> ## Files Changed
> 
> - `mcp/schema_cache.go` - New cache implementation
> - `mcp/server.go` - Modified `setSchema` to use cache
> - `mcp/schema_cache_test.go` - Unit tests for caching behavior
> - `mcp/schema_cache_benchmark_test.go` - Benchmarks
> 
> ## Impact for Integrators
> 
> **Automatic** - no code changes required. Integrators using:
> - Typed handlers (`AddTool[In, Out]`) → cache by type
> - Pre-defined schemas (`Tool{InputSchema: schema}`) → cache by pointer
> 
> Both patterns benefit from caching after the first call.
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Real-World Performance Validation
> 
> The following benchmarks were conducted using `github/github-mcp-server`
> (a production MCP server with ~130 tools) to validate the performance
> impact in a real-world scenario.
> 
> ### Test Environment
> - **Server:** github-mcp-server (stateless HTTP deployment)
> - **Tools registered per request:** ~130 tools
> - **Test methodology:** Python benchmark client, 30 iterations
> (latency), 100 iterations (stress)
> - **Date:** December 4, 2025
> 
> ### Configurations Tested
> 
> | Configuration | Description |
> |--------------|-------------|
> | **main (mcp-go)** | Original implementation using mcp-go library |
> | **go-sdk (no cache)** | go-sdk WITHOUT schema caching (broken) |
> | **go-sdk (with cache)** | go-sdk WITH this PR&#39;s schema caching fix
> |
> 
> ### Latency Test Results (n=30)
> 
> #### Operation: `initialize`
> 
> | Configuration | P50 | P99 | Status |
> |--------------|-----|-----|--------|
> | main (mcp-go) | 11.48ms | 14.00ms | ✅ Baseline |
> | go-sdk (no cache) | 20.47ms | 25.30ms | 🔴 **+78% REGRESSION** |
> | go-sdk (with cache) | 10.36ms | 14.33ms | ✅ **FIXED (-10%)** |
> 
> #### Operation: `tools/list`
> 
> | Configuration | P50 | P99 | Status |
> |--------------|-----|-----|--------|
> | main (mcp-go) | 13.46ms | 22.47ms | ✅ Baseline |
> | go-sdk (no cache) | 22.98ms | 29.11ms | 🔴 **+71% REGRESSION** |
> | go-sdk (with cache) | 14.15ms | 15.91ms | ✅ **FIXED (+5%)** |
> 
> #### Operation: `prompts/list`
> 
> | Configuration | P50 | P99 | Status |
> |--------------|-----|-----|--------|
> | main (mcp-go) | 11.56ms | 13.81ms | ✅ Baseline |
> | go-sdk (no cache) | 21.00ms | 26.42ms | 🔴 **+82% REGRESSION** |
> | go-sdk (with cache) | 10.77ms | 15.25ms | ✅ **FIXED (-7%)** |
> 
> ### Stress Test Results (n=100)
> 
> | Configuration | P50 (initialize) | P50 (tools/list) | P50
> (prompts/list) |
> 
> |--------------|------------------|------------------|-------------------|
> | main (mcp-go) | 12.06ms | 14.30ms | 11.34ms |
> | go-sdk (no cache) | 20.06ms | 23.44ms | 19.59ms |
> | go-sdk (with cache) | **11.83ms** | **14.58ms** | **11.05ms** |
> 
> ### Memory/Allocation Comparison (from pprof)
> 
> | Configuration | Total Allocations | Comparison |
> |--------------|-------------------|------------|
> | main (mcp-go) | 355.91 MB | Baseline |
> | go-sdk (no cache) | **1208.70 MB** | 🔴 **3.4x MORE allocations** |
> 
> #### Top Allocation Sources - go-sdk WITHOUT cache (broken)
> 
> | Function | Size | % | Issue |
> |----------|------|---|-------|
> | `jsonschema.UnmarshalJSON` | 324.60 MB | 27% | 🚨 Schema re-parsing |
> | `encoding/json.Unmarshal` | 341.10 MB | 28% | JSON deserialization |
> | `jsonschema.resolve` | 219.51 MB | 18% | 🚨 Schema re-resolution |
> | `jsonschema.MarshalJSON` | 92.52 MB | 8% | Schema JSON encoding |
> 
> ### Root Cause Analysis
> 
> The `google/jsonschema-go` library regenerates JSON schemas on every
> request instead of caching them. In a server with ~130 tools, this
> causes:
> - **70-80% latency regression** on all MCP operations
> - **3.4x more memory allocations** per request
> - **~70% of all allocations** are schema-related operations
> 
> ### Key Findings
> 
> 1. ✅ **REGRESSION CONFIRMED:** go-sdk without schema caching is 70-80%
> slower than mcp-go
> 2. ✅ **FIX VERIFIED:** Schema caching restores performance to baseline
> (or better)
> 3. ✅ **MEMORY IMPACT:** 3.4x reduction in allocations with caching
> 4. ✅ **PRODUCTION READY:** Fixed version performs equivalently to mcp-go
> baseline
> 
> ---------
>

> Co-authored-by: Ksenia Bobrova <1885174+almaleksia@users.noreply.github.com>

> mcp: fix connectStandaloneSSE checking Content-Type header (#736)
> 
> Issue encountered: the MCP server request was unexpectedly redirected to
> an HTML page. Because the client didn’t validate the response
> Content-Type, it still entered handleSSE, which then kept treating the
> HTML as an SSE stream and repeatedly re-requesting the same
> page—creating an infinite request loop.
