- 0c02b08645b2f8a2521308996fa569bdda7a4e2f — https://github.com/nyblnet/bento/commit/0c02b08645b2f8a2521308996fa569bdda7a4e2f
> spaces: an issue is a page — a Linear-shaped tracker in one file (#242)
> 
> * spaces: an issue is a page — the Linear-shaped tracker, first cut
> 
> An ISSUE IS A PAGE. Its fields are `prop` BLOCKS; the schema they draw on is
> `doc.fields`; a board is a `view` BLOCK. Nothing here is a new document type
> and nothing is a page-level key.
> 
> WHY SPACES RATHER THAN A NEW APP. A tracker is a pile of short documents with
> typed fields and a few saved queries. Spaces already has pages, rich bodies,
> links, backlinks, search, archive, print, nine languages and an agent surface —
> most of a tracker — and Linear's own model is "an issue is a document with
> fields". A separate app rebuilds all of that and lands where Jira is: a tracker
> whose issues cannot hold a real document.
> 
> WHY VALUES ARE BLOCKS. Everything in spaces that matters iterates page.blocks —
> search, find-and-replace, undo, the block registry, the static preview, the
> markdown export. A page-level key is invisible to every one of them and renders
> as NOTHING on a build that predates it. And under collaboration each block
> property is its own last-writer-wins register, so two people setting status and
> assignee at the same moment both win; one object on the page would have been
> one register and would have lost an edit silently. This was already the
> recorded ruling; the tracker is the first thing to need it.
> 
> WHY THE SCHEMA IS NOT A VALUE. Putting the status list on every issue would
> copy it into every page and let two pages disagree about what "Todo" means.
> `doc.fields` is document-level and additive: an older build ignores it and
> still renders each block's html.
> 
> EVERY PROP BLOCK CARRIES A READABLE `html`, always written with the value.
> "Status: In progress" is what an older build, a thumbnailer, a grep and the
> markdown export see. Pinned: an option this build does not know is shown
> VERBATIM rather than blanked, and the readable form is escaped, because it is
> html and the value is author data.
> 
> Fields render as a header strip by POSITION, not by a flag: prop blocks before
> the first non-prop block are drawn as one row under the title. An older build
> shows the same values in the same order, just stacked.
> 
> In this cut: the seven default fields, a board grouped by status in the
> schema's declared order (an unknown status gets an "Other" column rather than
> being dropped), a list layout, one-click field editing, ⌘⇧I for a new issue,
> and "Make this page an issue". A page carrying a board gets the width — the
> measure is for prose, and 720px shows two and a half columns of a six-column
> board.
> 
> NOT here, deliberately: no teams (the file is the team boundary), no per-user
> permissions (the file is the capability, PLATFORM §5), no notifications, no
> server-side automation. That is Buzz's shape — a Rust service with Postgres and
> a relay behind it. What Bento can do that neither Linear nor Buzz can is hand
> you the whole tracker as one file that opens offline, forever, with no account.
> 
> Ceiling 118 → 125 KiB, raised here with the reason.
> 
> * spaces: an agent can triage the backlog — fields, issues, setField, newIssue
> 
> The tracker shipped this morning with an agent surface that did not know fields
> existed. An agent could read `doc.fields` out of the JSON and write a `prop`
> block through insertBlocks — and get the `html` wrong, which is the one thing
> that must never happen: that string is what an older build, a file-manager
> thumbnail, a grep and the markdown export see, and it is ALL they see. A value
> written without it is a value none of them can read, forever, with nothing to
> notice it.
> 
> So the only supported way to write a value goes through fields.ts propHtml(),
> the same call the editor's field picker makes. Measured in a real saved file:
> after bento.setField(page, 'due', '2026-09-30') the .bento.html on disk carries
> the literal text "Due: 2026-09-30" — the degradation guarantee, not asserted but
> grepped.
> 
> WHAT IS NEW
> 
>   bento.fields()                     the schema in force, as a copy
>   bento.issues(query?)               the backlog: id, title, url, group, fields
>   bento.setField(pageId, key, value) one undoable step, value AND html
>   bento.newIssue({title, ...fields}) one page, seeded, in one step
> 
> fields() first, because a value is set by option ID and the ids are not the
> labels — 'doing', not 'In progress'. It hands back a COPY: fieldsOf() returns
> DEFAULT_FIELDS itself when a document declares no schema, and that array is
> module state shared by every document in the session, so one caller's push()
> would edit the schema of documents not yet opened.
> 
> THREE SHAPES SETTLED, recorded in DECISIONS.md
> 
> 1. An unknown value is WRITTEN and warned about, never refused. The format is
>    permanent and additive: a status a newer build declared has to round-trip
>    through this one, and refusing it would make an older build unable to edit a
>    document a newer one wrote. But an agent typing the label where the id
>    belongs is wrong and would otherwise stay confident, so the result carries
>    warning:{code:'unknown-option', options:[…]}. Refuse the shapes JSON cannot
>    carry; warn about the vocabulary.
> 
> 2. An unknown key in an ARGUMENT is a typo, not additivity — both write verbs
>    refuse it (err:'no-such-field', naming the keys that do exist). Unknown keys
>    in a document are how a future build's data survives; unknown keys in a call
>    are how an agent believes it set a priority it did not set.
> 
> 3. "Open" means NOT FINISHED — one predicate, so a status with no phase and a
>    status this build has never heard of both count as work (the latter reports
>    group:'unknown' rather than being folded in with the rest). An issue wrongly
>    shown in a backlog costs a glance; one wrongly hidden costs the issue.
>    issues({group:'open', where:{assignee:null}}) is the triage call.
> 
> VALIDATE LEARNS ABOUT FIELDS
> 
> prop-html-stale (warning) is the valuable one: a readable form that disagrees
> with its value. It deliberately STANDS DOWN when the value names no known
> option — the writer knew a label this build does not, so its html is right and
> ours would be the guess. Without that carve-out every document from a newer
> build reports a defect it does not have. Also: unknown-field-value and
> unknown-field-key at INFO (that is how newer data arrives, and it is kept),
> duplicate-prop and prop-no-key at warning, and bad-field-schema at ERROR — a
> doc.fields entry with no string label makes propHtml THROW, so the editor's
> field picker dies on click.
> 
> ISSUE_FIELDS moves to fields.ts: ⌘⇧I and bento.newIssue() must seed the same
> four fields, because `prop` is unlisted in the / menu and a field an issue does
> not start with is a field a human can never set.

> MEASURED

> link and nothing else: no way to move an issue between columns, no way to

> sync: let an app stamp a state without the text token history (#254)
> 
> `toJSON({ text: false })` omits `txt`. The default is unchanged and always will
> be — every bento/slides file in the field was written with it, and the
> equivalence gate compares those bytes. bento/spaces will use the lean form.
> 
> WHY. The token history is one entry per character, ~26 bytes each with an id,
> and a deletion cannot remove one: a tombstone is how "delete" reaches a replica
> that has not caught up. Measured — "hello" is 159 B of state; typing " world"
> takes it to 297 B; deleting " world" again takes it to 333 B; emptying the
> paragraph entirely takes it to 363 B, for a document with no text in it.
> 
> THE COST IS EDITING, NOT TEXT, which was not obvious and decides where it
> matters. Identical prose: 2,978 B of state when pasted (x0.2 of the text) and
> 479,825 B when typed in 40-character runs (x25.8). 161x apart for byte-identical
> content, because text arriving as one write never engages the RGA. Slides is
> fine — slide text is titles and bullets. A space IS typed prose.
> 
> NOT WHAT EVERYBODY DOES, and worth being accurate about: Yjs keeps its state and
> garbage-collects deleted content; Automerge keeps the whole history and pays for
> it with a binary encoding. Dropping the history is unusual. What makes it right
> HERE is Bento-specific — the state is JSON inside an HTML file rather than a
> binary blob, and there is no closed set of peers, so the causal cutoff that
> makes GC safe never arrives. A copy can come back out of a mailbox a year later.
> 
> THE PRECONDITION, found by testing rather than reasoning, and it is not a
> detail. A restored state with no token history does NOT fall back to whole-value
> sets as I first assumed: the differ re-seeds a generation from the current
> content, and the seed comes from that content plus the register stamp. Two
> replicas that both re-seed derive the same seed and still merge per character —
> measured on one shared paragraph, "Friday"→"Monday" from one side and an
> appended sentence from the other, both kept, byte-identical on both sides, from
> a stamp 10.9x smaller.
> 
> A replica that re-seeds meeting a peer that still holds the ORIGINAL generation
> is a different story: the generations duel as units and the two documents DO NOT
> CONVERGE. A live session holds the tokens in memory, so save-close-reopen-rejoin
> is exactly that case. A lean stamp is therefore safe only when every participant
> is lean, and the session layer must treat "restored without txt" as
> needs-a-snapshot rather than resume. That rule cannot be written yet — spaces has
> no session — so the evidence and the note live in the rig instead of in a
> comment nobody reads.
> 
> Verified: equivalence rig byte-identical at CI settings (slides' stamp is
> untouched, and its key ORDER too — txt is omitted in place, not appended);
> shape seam 23/23; test-sync.ts 46408 checks; delprop 22/22; spaces convergence
> 2/2; kernel and slides typecheck.

> agent.ts is ~900 lines and shipped with zero automated coverage — the slides
> validator has its own rig and the spaces model rig never imported this file.

> a person reading code rather than by anything that runs.
> 
> What it pins is what makes the surface worth trusting:

>  · validate() SILENT on documents that are correct but unusual — a page holding
>    only an image, a single empty paragraph, nested toggles, an unknown block
>    type from a newer build, a 500-page space. False positives are the failure
>    mode that makes a validator worthless, because an agent that gets warnings
>    for good documents learns to ignore warnings.
>  · …and specific on a broken one, with every finding carrying both a message
>    and a fix.
>  · Every write verb refusing what it cannot honour, with a machine-readable
>    code rather than a bare null an agent cannot distinguish from "no match".
>  · No verb producing a document this build could not have produced: html
>    sanitized on the way in, ids minted rather than taken from the caller, a
>    type change running the registry's init, a removed container taking its
>    children.
>  · Every walk over author-supplied parent links terminating.
> 
> Worth recording honestly: all four failures while writing this were wrong
> assumptions in the TEST, not defects in the code — the finding code is
> "unknown-block-type", outline returns counts plus a FLAT depth-tagged tree
> rather than nested children, and stats reports bytes as an object. The surface
> was in better shape than "no coverage" suggested; the rig's value is that it
> stays that way.
> 
> The termination probes run in CHILD PROCESSES with timeouts. The first version
> measured elapsed time after the call, which cannot report a call that never
> returns — it hung the rig, so CI would have timed out with nothing to read
> instead of naming the defect. Verified by removing the cycle guard: it now
> fails in eight seconds with the verb named.
> 
> * spaces: undo you can actually reach back through
> 
> Every checkpoint stringified the WHOLE document. Measured on a realistic
> 200-page, 2.5 MB handbook: fifty edits left an undo depth of NINE — nine
> snapshots of 2.5 MB exhaust the 24 MB budget — so a writer who spotted a
> mistake ten edits back could not reach it, and nothing said why.
> 
> A typing run is one block in the page in view, by definition, and it is by far
> the most common edit there is. It now records only that PAGE. Same document,
> same budget: 150 typing runs, all undoable, and each checkpoint costs 0.93ms
> instead of 1.8ms.
> 
> WHAT MAKES THIS DANGEROUS is that a page entry restores one page and leaves the
> rest of the document alone — correct only if the mutation touched nothing else.
> The store cannot check that cheaply, so scope is OPTED INTO and `doc` remains
> the default: a caller that forgets gets the slow, safe behaviour rather than a
> silently corrupted history.
> 
> scripts/test-spaces-undo.ts covers where a wrong scope would lose work: a page
> entry leaving every other page untouched, page and doc entries interleaved in
> the right order (a doc entry restores the whole document, so a page entry taken
> after it must not land on a document that no longer holds that page), redo
> returning exactly what undo took at both scopes, a new edit dropping the redo
> branch, and undo restoring the VIEW as well as the content.
> 
> Both negative controls fire: reverting to doc-scope drops the depth to 12, and
> making a page restore replace the page array trips three assertions.
> 
> * spaces: a block can be moved, duplicated and deleted — on every device
> 
> Four actions existed NOWHERE, on any device: move up, move down, duplicate,
> delete. Deletion was Backspace-into-the-previous-block and reordering was
> drag-only — and the drag gutter was display:none on touch, so on a phone a
> block could not be reordered or removed AT ALL.
> 
> One declared list feeds the desktop menu and the phone sheet, the same
> reasoning as the topbar's secondary actions: a second hand-maintained copy
> drifts the first time either changes, and the drift is invisible to whoever is
> not holding the other device.
> 
> The gutter now survives the drawer breakpoint. It was hidden there on the
> reasoning that there is no hover on touch — but hover was how you reached the
> only controls a block has, so removing it removed the controls. It is shown
> rather than hovered, with 40px targets, and the menu becomes a bottom sheet
> because a popover anchored to a 5px gutter button is not usable with a thumb.
> 
> Unavailable actions are disabled rather than removed: "move up" vanishing on
> the first block makes a menu that changes shape, and a menu that changes shape
> has to be re-read every time.
> 
> THE SUBTREE RULES are where this silently loses work, so each is verified:
>  · a block cannot be moved inside its own subtree
>  · a move lands after the target's WHOLE subtree. This was a real bug found in
>    testing: landing immediately after a container put the moved block between
>    that container and its children, so the child no longer followed its parent
>    contiguously and the renderer drew it at root — moving the first block down
>    past a toggle un-nested the toggle's body.
>  · a duplicate rewrites its copies' parent links, so the copy owns the copies

>  · a delete takes the subtree with it, and never leaves a page with nothing to

> 
> Shell 117,358 → 119,046 B, inside the 120,832 B ceiling. Seven new strings,

> webext: a package that can be uploaded, and the answers a reviewer asks for (#232)
> 
> * webext: a package that can be uploaded, and the answers a reviewer asks for
> 
> The extension worked but there was no way to SHIP it: nothing produced an
> upload, the version was still the scaffold's 0.0.1, and none of the listing
> answers existed.
> 
> scripts/pack-webext.mjs, and deliberately not `zip -r`:
> 
>   It refuses to ship the wrong files. tray/webext/ holds probe/ -- four
>   capability probes that open local files and talk across origins, harmless to
>   us and alarming to a reviewer -- plus 200 lines of internal reasoning in
>   README.md and now STORE.md. A recursive zip takes the lot. The payload is an
>   allow-list and anything unexpected in the tree is an error.
> 
>   It checks the manifest against the tree: every file named exists, every icon
>   is really the size it claims, no permission is declared but unused. Verified
>   by breaking it -- swapping the 16px icon for the 128 is caught by name and
>   size. A rejection for a wrong icon costs days of review latency for something
>   a regex catches in milliseconds.
> 
>   It is byte-reproducible: sorted entries, fixed timestamps, no filesystem
>   metadata. Built twice, identical sha256. This repo holds that line for the
>   document shell (signed locally, signed bytes are served bytes); an extension
>   going through a store cannot be signed by us, so reproducibility is what is
>   left -- "is the uploaded package the reviewed package?" stays answerable.
> 
> The zip is hand-written rather than shelled out, so I checked it is a real one
> and not merely a plausible one: unzip -t passes, unzip lists 13 files, and
> extracted manifest.json, background.js and icon-128.png each compare identical
> to source.
> 
> STORE.md carries the listing copy, the single-purpose statement, a
> justification per permission, and the data-usage answers -- all No, because the
> extension makes no network requests at all. In the repo so the answers a
> reviewer gets are the ones the code supports, and so the next submission does
> not reinvent them. Screenshots are the one item still missing and are marked as
> such.
> 
> Also closed: ID_SINCE. v1.0.14 carries no pickerIdFor and v1.0.15 carries it, so
> 1.0.15 is confirmed as the floor rather than assumed. Decks older than that get
> the browser's own picker, exactly as they do with no extension installed.
> 
> * Do not promise in-place saving while file access is off
> 
> Found by rendering the popup and the options page in every state rather than
> reading the code, which is the only way this kind of thing shows up.
> 
> With file access off, both surfaces printed a GREEN "Folder: Decks — decks in
> here save in place, with no dialog" directly beneath "nothing works until it is
> on". Two reassuring-looking signals contradicting each other, and the reassuring
> one was the false one: with file access off, nothing saves in place at all.
> 
> The folder row now reads "Ready, but nothing saves in place until local file
> access is on" and drops to amber whenever the other precondition is failing. The
> grant genuinely IS fine in that state -- it is not an error and should not be
> red -- it just cannot do anything yet, and that is what it now says.
> 
> The whole point of these two surfaces is that a save either lands or does not,
> and the user should know which BEFORE pressing S. A surface that says "no
> dialog" when there will certainly be a dialog is worse than no surface.

> sync: the CRDT engine moves to the kernel (#251)
> 
> PR-4 of the spaces collaboration work, and the point at which the engine stops
> being slides' and starts being the platform's.
> 
> It could move because it no longer knows what a slide is. A document shape is
> two property names injected at construction, so the algebra — composite node
> keys, fractional position keys, per-(node,key) registers, the token RGA over
> `html` — carries no app vocabulary at all. Moving it BEFORE that would have
> parked `doc.slides` and `sl.elements` inside kernel/src for a PR, against
> kernel/README.md's own rule that the kernel never sees an app's content shape.
> 
> kernel/src/sync/crdt.ts holds `SyncEngine`, `DocShape` and `shape()`. It
> declares the three types it needs structurally rather than importing an app
> model, because the dependency direction is app → kernel only. What the engine
> actually requires of a document is a container of parented nodes each with an
> `id`, under two keys the shape names — nothing more.
> 
> slides/src/sync/crdt.ts is now a FACADE, and stays one. Every consumer that
> imported the engine from that path still can: session.ts, online.ts,
> model.ts's type reach, three scripts, and server/guestbook-daemon, which
> bundles `SyncState` from there through wrangler. That last one does not fail
> loudly on a missing export — the guestbook just stops archiving — so the
> facade's completeness is verified at runtime (15 names) and by bundling the
> daemon exactly as wrangler does.
> 
> Docs follow the code: PLATFORM §9 and PARALLEL-WORK's kernel zone now name
> kernel/src/sync/crdt.ts, and say the rest of slides/src/sync/ (session,
> transport, blobs) is still slides-shaped and still serialized. kernel/README.md
> adds the engine to its inventory and to its frozen-contracts list, with the
> sentence that matters: every byte the engine mints is shipped-file
> compatibility surface.
> 
> DECISIONS.md carries the ruling — shape at construction, never serialized,
> never on the wire; no default on the argument; skipDoc derived; and the wire
> vocabulary frozen for every app, which must stay settled before spaces collab
> reaches a user, because after that spaces files carry it permanently.
> 
> Verified: equivalence rig LIVE and byte-identical at CI settings (a facade over
> the live engine compared against the frozen baseline is a genuine comparison —
> the case checked when the baseline was frozen); shape seam 14/14; test-sync.ts
> 46408 checks; test-crdt-delprop 22/22; release rig 40/40; slides and kernel
> typecheck standalone; both shells build and pass the splice gate; spaces
> unaffected at 97.5% of its ceiling; slides shell 677,668 B (+72 B, the facade).

> Hide a slide from the show, without taking it out of the deck (#267)
> 
> Backup numbers, an appendix, the detail slide you open only if somebody asks:
> material that belongs in the file and not in the walk. `hidden: true` drops a
> slide out of linear navigation, PDF export and the file thumbnail, while an
> element `link` still reaches it -- which is the whole point.
> 
> The machinery already existed. present.ts routes every navigation decision
> through one predicate, so hiding is mostly widening it: the feature is 44 bytes
> of compressed shell, and the numbering option below is 236 more.
> 
> TWO PREDICATES, DELIBERATELY NOT ONE. `inLinearFlow` answers "is this in the
> walk"; `paginates` answers "does this take a number". Navigation, print and the
> thumbnail ask the first; page fields, the presenter's counter and the sidebar
> ask the second. Collapsing them would let numberHidden walk an audience into a
> slide that was hidden on purpose.
> 
> NUMBERING IS CONTIGUOUS BY DEFAULT -- skipped means uncounted, the rule
> interactive states already follow. One rule for "slides the audience never
> sees" is smaller to hold than two, and contiguous numbering then falls out by
> construction rather than by setting. present.numberHidden restores what
> PowerPoint and Keynote do, where a hidden slide keeps its number so the visible
> ones do not renumber as you toggle slides during rehearsal. Measured before
> building it: the option costs 236 bytes, two-thirds of that the translated
> label -- so the case against it was never size, it was a second rule to explain
> and keep tested.
> 
> The sidebar shows what the AUDIENCE would count: struck through when the slide
> has a number, a dash when it has none. A slide you forgot you hid is a slide
> you rediscover mid-presentation.
> 
> validate() gains unreachable-hidden-slide -- hidden AND nothing links to it
> means it cannot be reached at all. Info rather than error, since it is a
> reasonable in-progress state, but invisible otherwise: a hidden slide is
> skipped silently whether or not anyone can still get to it.
> 
> Verified end to end: 1/3 2/3 3/3 with the hidden slide uncounted, 1/4 through
> 4/4 with the option on, the walk running s1 -> s2 -> s4, a link from s1 landing
> on the hidden s3, and PDF emitting 3 pages.

> sync: stop a live session crashing when two people create the same element (#249)
> 
> Third instance of one defect in this engine, and the first with a
> deterministic test.
> 
> assignNode built a dbg() template argument around
> `JSON.stringify(payload[k]).slice(0, 40)`. `k` iterates the UNION of the local
> node's keys and the incoming payload's, so `payload[k]` is undefined for every
> key the local node has and the payload does not — and JSON.stringify(undefined)
> is undefined, not "undefined". A template literal evaluates eagerly, so dbg()
> being a no-op unless __dbgEl matches did not save it.
> 
> REACHABLE, AND ORDINARY. Two replicas insert an element with the same id; one
> copy carries a property the other lacks. Sharing an element id across slides is
> the morph idiom — it is what id continuity exists for — so two people creating
> one concurrently is a normal event, not a collision to design out. The replica
> receiving the other's insert throws and the session stops. The file is intact;
> the tab just stops keeping up.
> 
> The two earlier instances (the `set` handler, then replayStash) are documented
> in scripts/test-crdt-delprop.ts, which also records that hand-built scenarios
> could not reach the second one, so its guard is the convergence generator. This
> site is not like that: it has a four-line trigger, verified to throw with the
> fix reverted and to pass with it, across all five property removals the rig
> already models. The rig is guarded so a regression REPORTS (16/22) instead of
> dying with a stack trace.
> 
> Found by the equivalence rig at 400 seeds x 120 steps x 5 actors. CI runs
> 200 x 60 x 4 and never reached it; test-sync.ts does not reach it at any depth,
> because its schedule differs.
> 
> THE FROZEN BASELINE IS RE-FROZEN, deliberately, and the reasoning matters more
> than the change. The baseline exists to pin the BYTES the field was written
> with. This fix mints exactly the same ops, the same SyncStateJSON and the same
> document — it only stops a throw — so applying the identical one-line guard
> there keeps the baseline faithful while letting the rig run past the crash. The
> entire delta is one line, shown in the PR. A change that altered a minted byte
> would not qualify: that is the case the frozen copy exists to catch, and
> re-freezing to hide one would be the failure rather than the fix. The file's
> header now says exactly this, so the next person has the test.
> 
> Verified: equivalence rig PASS at 400 x 120 x 5 (3x CI depth, and the depth
> that found the bug) and at CI settings; test-crdt-delprop 22/22, and 16/22 with
> the fix reverted; test-sync.ts 46408 checks; release rig 40/40; slides
> typechecks.

> bento/spaces 0.1.0 — the first release (#226)
> 
> * spaces M0: the format, the editor, and the thesis
> 
> bento/spaces was 414 lines of scaffold proving the kernel seam. This is the
> app: a tree of pages in one file, with links, backlinks and search across all
> of them.
> 
> THE FORMAT, and two decisions that depart from the design doc because
> measurement said so.
> 
> Block properties are FLAT, not nested under `props`. Under collaboration each
> (node,key) pair is one LWW register, so a nested props object is ONE register
> for a block's entire content: measured, one author ticking `done` while another
> sets a second field loses one of the two edits silently. Slides' elements are
> flat for exactly this reason. Free now, unrecoverable once files exist.
> 
> parseDoc returns a TAGGED result and never null. The scaffold returned null for
> anything invalid and the caller fell back to the starter, so opening a slides
> file -- or a document with one hand-edited typo -- showed an empty space over
> live data, and the first Cmd-S wrote it to disk. The only path to the starter
> is an absent or empty block; everything else refuses, names what it found, and
> offers the bytes back untouched.
> 
> Id repair is deterministic from the BYTES. Not Math.random (which diverges two
> readers of one file) and not docId (which template:true re-mints every open, so
> a docId-derived id gives two readers DIFFERENT ids -- the exact failure repair
> exists to prevent). Repairs are reported, never silent.
> 
> THE SANITIZER matches the href allowlist against getAttribute('href'), never
> the .href IDL property. The property returns the RESOLVED ABSOLUTE url, so a
> stored "#p/abc" reads back as "file:///…#p/abc" and fails an allowlist that
> passes on a static host -- invisible where an author develops, and fatal in the
> two environments this format exists for. The design doc specified `.href`; the
> stress pass caught it. Block-structure tags are UNWRAPPED rather than deleted,
> with a space at the boundary, so a pasted paragraph never loses its words.
> 
> THE EDITOR is per-block contentEditable hosts, never one editable container:
> that is what keeps Selection block-scoped so split and merge can never re-mint
> an id. Typing runs coalesce input into one undo entry per block per burst,
> which is also the later CRDT op unit. Markdown prefixes convert as typed,
> Tab/Shift-Tab re-parent, `[[` picks or creates a page, `/` opens the block
> menu, Cmd-K searches every page.
> 
> Verified in a real browser: markdown conversion, Enter/Tab/Shift-Tab/Backspace,
> undo, the sidebar tree, backlinks resolving both inline links and pagelink
> blocks, and the full file round-trip -- serialize, pull the block back out,
> re-parse, byte-identical, with unknown top-level fields, unknown per-node
> fields and unknown block TYPES all surviving and rendering a fallback.
> 
> Rig: scripts/test-spaces-model.ts, 38 checks, wired into CI. Each guarded
> property has a negative control that fires.
> 
> Shell is 26KB compressed.
> 
> * spaces: the About surface, encryption both ways, and markdown export
> 
> PLATFORM §10 wants a signed update path, an encryption story and an AI
> round-trip. All three go behind one button, because a self-contained document
> has nowhere else to put them.
> 
> THE ONE THAT MATTERED. Adding "set a password" to About without an unlock gate
> would have been the worst bug this app could ship: encrypt a space once and its
> author is locked out permanently, with no server to appeal to. The gate is
> implemented in the same change, and the password is held in memory so every
> later save stays encrypted. Verified end to end -- the block becomes a
> bento/enc envelope, no plaintext leaks into it, a wrong password is refused, a
> right one returns the document intact.
> 
> About also carries the honest limits rather than letting them be discovered: it
> says up front when the browser cannot write back to the file, and that language
> follows the reader and never enters the document.
> 
> Markdown export is the payoff for the renderer emitting semantic tags instead
> of divs-with-classes -- the mapping is direct. Every page, headings by tree
> depth, todos with their state, code fences, and links kept as [text](#p/id) so
> a reader outside the space can still see which page was meant.
> 
> docs/spaces-agents.md is the agent guide. It leads with the two things a
> generator gets wrong: both arrays are FLAT with nesting as a `parent` field,
> and ids must be unique document-wide first time -- a repaired id is a new id,
> so anything pointing at the old one now points at the wrong node. It also names
> the most-missed feature, which is that backlinks are free: link to a page and
> it lists the linker, with nothing to maintain.
> 
> Shell 31KB compressed.
> 
> * spaces: make it look and behave like the rest of the suite
> 
> The app worked and looked like a prototype beside bento/slides. This adopts
> slides' actual chrome rather than approximating it: its exact tokens (--ink,
> --chrome, --line, --accent, --blue, --radius), its button shape and hover
> states, its menu shadow and radius, and its LIGHT-ONLY ruling -- I had made
> spaces dark-mode-aware, which diverges for a documented reason: on a dark-mode
> phone the engine renders NATIVE controls dark while our ink stays dark, so
> dropdowns read blank.
> 
> Unicode glyphs became a real icon set, same lucide-style construction and
> stroke weight as slides/src/icons.ts. Not imported from slides -- PLATFORM §9
> keeps editor UX per-app, and sharing the set would drag one app's additions
> into the other's bundle.
> 
> What the interface was missing, rather than what it looked like:
> 
> - No affordances at all. Nothing on screen said a block could be moved or that
>   one could go here. Blocks now have a hover gutter -- add, and a grip that
>   drags to reorder (subtrees travel with their owner) or opens the block menu.
>   It sits outside the text column so it never reflows the prose.
> - The block menu was a centred modal, which loses the thing you were pointing
>   at. It now opens beside the caret, filters as you type, and is fully
>   keyboard-driven.
> - Every empty block advertised "Type / for blocks". A page of those reads as
>   clutter; the prompt now shows only on the block you are in.
> - Saving said nothing. It now reports Saved -- or "Saved a new copy", which is
>   doing real work on a browser without file-system access.
> - A page nested three deep gave no clue where it sat once the sidebar scrolled.
>   There is a breadcrumb trail now.
> - Search results and the page picker rendered differently from the block menu;
>   all three now share one row shape.
> 
> Two bugs found by measuring rather than looking: a toggle's body rendered
> BESIDE its title (it had become a flex item of the row), and the phone drawer
> could not be opened at all.
> 
> The drawer took three attempts. A logical inset and then a transform both
> measured as not moving, and I could not see why from here -- some of it was
> stale CSS confusing earlier readings, which is on me. It ships as display:none
> plus an explicit open rule: less pretty than a slide-in, and its behaviour is
> obvious from the rule. A transition can come back with a test that proves it.
> 
> Shell 35KB compressed.
> 
> * spaces: stylised page icons, a real topbar, and a print contract
> 
> Three gaps against bento/slides, all fair.
> 
> ICONS. Page icons were colour emoji, so a sidebar of twelve pages read as a row
> of stickers rather than one interface. `Page.icon` is now a NAME from a
> stylised set drawn at the same stroke weight as everything else, with a picker
> beside the page title. An emoji still renders if a file carries one -- older
> documents and anything an agent writes must keep working -- but the set is what
> the app offers.
> 
> TOPBAR. It had search, about and save. It now carries what slides carries: a
> Pages panel toggle at every width (a sidebar you cannot put away is one you
> resent on a laptop), an Insert menu so the block types are reachable without
> knowing "/" exists, New page, Undo/Redo that go disabled when there is nothing
> to undo rather than silently doing nothing, Search, Print, About, and Save as a
> split control with the less-common ways of writing this document elsewhere.
> 
> PRINT. Printing is the only export-to-PDF path, so it is a contract rather than
> a stylesheet. A sheet asks the whole space or this page, whether to include
> archived pages (off by default -- they were archived for a reason), and whether
> to emit a contents page. It renders a SEPARATE print tree rather than making
> the editor's DOM serve both, because the screen shows one page and print needs
> all of them; the tree is removed on afterprint so nothing is left changed.
> 
> Collapsed toggles print EXPANDED, always. Silently dropping a folded paragraph
> from a printed handbook is a data-loss-shaped bug -- the reader cannot know it
> happened. Verified with a collapsed toggle in the model: 5 pages, 5 contents
> entries, 0 of 1 toggle bodies hidden, 0 editable nodes in the print tree.
> 
> SHARING, as far as it can honestly go: Save a copy (forcePicker, so a later ⌘S
> does not start overwriting the copy), Export as Markdown, and print/PDF. There
> is no share-a-link because there is no server and no collaboration yet; saying
> so plainly beats a button that half works.
> 
> Shell 39KB compressed.
> 
> * spaces: images that do not make the file unmailable
> 
> Images are the only thing that makes a space large -- prose is essentially free
> -- so this is where the size story is won or lost. Two decisions do the work.
> 
> CONTENT-ADDRESSED STORAGE. The asset key is derived from the bytes
> (sha256 via crypto.subtle, with an FNV-1a fallback tagged 'f' in the key so two
> builds never mint one key from two hashes). Identical images are stored once,
> and dedupe is a hash lookup rather than slides' O(n) string compare. Because an
> FNV collision would not error but silently DEDUPE -- replacing image B with
> image A in a file the author then mails -- interning byte-compares on every key
> hit and mints a ~n variant on mismatch.
> 
> DOWNSCALING, VISIBLE AND REVERSIBLE. A phone photo is 4000px and several MB; in
> a 720px text column that detail is invisible and the megabytes travel forever.
> Images are re-encoded to 1600px WebP: measured, a 4.9MB PNG becomes 33KB. It
> never silently degrades a photograph -- the block records original:false, the
> image carries a "Resized" badge, and clicking it re-picks the untouched bytes.
> Small images and anything under 600KB are left alone, and an encode that came
> out BIGGER is discarded.
> 
> Insert from the Insert menu, by paste, or by dropping a file on the page.
> 
> ONE UNDO STEP, which took a second pass to actually deliver. The first version
> committed the empty block and then the image separately, so one undo removed
> the picture and left a stray empty block the author never made -- caught by
> testing undo rather than by testing insert. Everything async now happens BEFORE
> the commit: read, decode, re-encode, hash, byte-compare, then a single
> synchronous mutation that creates the block and fills it together. Verified: 2
> blocks, drop, 3 blocks, one undo, 2 blocks.
> 
> Also: a width control cycling 100/75/50/33% of the text column, an orphan-asset
> scan, and a weight readout.
> 
> * spaces: i18n plumbing — packed table, facade, and a gate that refuses half a language
> 
> English-string-as-key means the source sentence is the key in every locale, so
> N plain catalogs store the same English text N times, and deflate cannot dedupe
> it across catalogs spanning far more than its 32KB window. The packed table
> stores each key ONCE with translations by column and 0 for 'not translated',
> which falls back to the English key -- itself the source text, so a gap
> degrades to a readable string rather than a blank.
> 
> The key universe is swept from the SOURCE, not from the catalogs: a string
> added to the UI and forgotten in a catalog must show up as missing rather than
> silently shipping English. slides' own build script carries a warning that a
> regex once missed 54 of 650 entries, so this one anchors on the call and
> reports counts either way.
> 
> A core catalog ships inside every saved file and cannot be corrected without a
> release, so --check FAILS the build on an incomplete one rather than warning.
> Verified: it refuses right now, with all eight at 0/116.
> 
> * spaces: eight languages, complete
> 
> 116 UI strings in Japanese, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Spanish,
> French, German, Italian and Portuguese. Same locale set as slides, so a reader
> who has one app in their language has both.
> 
> Translated per-locale rather than string-by-string, each translator working
> from the product's own voice in starterdeck/starter.ts and from slides'
> existing catalog for the same language -- so shared concepts (Save, Undo,
> Search, Password, Language) match the sibling app and the two do not read as
> different products. Each locale committed to a term for space / page / block
> first and used it throughout; those choices are recorded in each catalog's
> header.
> 
> VALIDATED BEFORE WRITING ANYTHING, because the failure mode is silent: the
> English string is the lookup key, so a key differing by one character -- a
> straight quote for a curly one, a hyphen for an em dash -- falls back to
> English forever with nothing to notice. All 8 x 116 keys matched the swept
> source byte-for-byte, no unknown keys, no missing keys, and every {placeholder}
> survived in every string.
> 
> The packed table stores each English key ONCE with translations by column,
> because N plain catalogs would store the same English text N times and deflate
> cannot dedupe across catalogs far wider than its 32KB window.
> 
> Regional codes a browser actually reports are aliased onto a column: zh-TW,
> zh-HK and zh-MO to Traditional, zh-CN and zh-SG to Simplified, pt-BR to pt.
> Without those a zh-TW reader falls all the way back to English with the
> traditional catalog sitting right there. Caveat, the same one slides carries:
> pt is European, so a Brazilian reader gets "Guardar" rather than "Salvar"
> until pt-BR earns its own catalog.
> 
> Verified in the browser, not just in the table: the chrome renders Japanese
> while the DOCUMENT stays in the author's language -- the interface follows the
> reader, the document does not.
> 
> CI gate FAILS on an incomplete core catalog rather than warning, because a core
> catalog ships inside every saved file and cannot be corrected without a
> release. Negative control: deleting one German string trips it.
> 
> Shell 64KB compressed, up from 41KB. The corpus is what a second app costs to
> speak eight languages, and it is the same trade slides made.
> 
> * spaces: reading view, find and replace, and archive
> 
> READING VIEW is the same renderer with `editable` off, not a second one -- a
> separate read-only renderer would drift, and the drift would only appear in the
> view nobody develops in. It is a VIEW, never document state: nothing is written
> to the file, so a space cannot arrive locked because its author was reading
> when they saved. Esc returns to editing.
> 
> FIND is ours rather than the browser's, and that is the whole point. Native
> find cannot see a collapsed toggle's body, a page that is not currently
> rendered, or an archived page -- which is most of a space. This searches the
> model, jumps to each hit, and unfolds whatever was closed around it. Verified
> against text inside a collapsed toggle on a different page.
> 
> Replace-all is ONE commit for the whole sweep: a replace a user must undo forty
> times is not undoable in any sense they care about. Two things it gets right
> that a naive implementation does not:
> 
>   - It never touches markup. Searching for "a" and replacing it would otherwise
>     rewrite every <a href> on the page; substitution happens only outside angle
>     brackets. Measured: the naive version does break the hrefs.
>   - It is CASE-INSENSITIVE, matching the search that produced the count. It was
>     not, which meant reporting "14 found" and quietly changing nine of them.
> 
> ARCHIVE moves a page out of the sidebar into a collapsible section while it
> stays searchable and linkable -- someone about to share a file needs to see
> what is going with it. Deleting re-homes children to the deleted page's parent
> rather than taking a subtree the author was not looking at, and the
> confirmation counts the inbound links that will break, because that is the fact
> that decides it.
> 
> Also: afterPaint(). Anything whose CORRECTNESS depends on a frame now falls
> back to a timeout, because requestAnimationFrame does not fire at all in a
> hidden tab -- search a space, switch tabs before the frame lands, and the jump
> was silently never completed. I lost a while to this: the highlight looked
> broken when it was the measuring environment that could not run it, and I
> wrongly called the dev server stale after grepping a bundle for a comment that
> esbuild had stripped.
> 
> 28 new UI strings, translated into all eight locales and validated key-for-key
> before being written; 144 x 8, all complete. Shell 70KB.
> 
> * spaces: per-app release notes, agent guides, and tags
> 
> release.mjs read the root CHANGELOG unconditionally, so the first spaces
> release would have signed slides' release notes into the spaces manifest —
> which every shipped spaces file fetches at launch and renders inline in the
> About dialog. Not a build error: a correct-looking release that describes a
> different product. Unrecoverable in the ordinary way, since the notes are
> inside the signed envelope and the updater refuses to re-sign a version.
> 
> Every gate missed it because every gate was app-scoped and each check passed

> asserts the set of changelogs is the same size as the set of apps, and that

> 
> --print-notes prints what would be signed and exits before anything is built,
> wiped or signed.
> 
> Also: each app publishes its agent guide at bento.page/<app>/agents.md, the
> URL docs/agents.md already advertised but which was never written; slides keeps
> a copy at /agents.md, referenced by the harness SKILL.md that ships in a zip.
> Tags are prefixed for every app but slides, which has 23 bare vX.Y.Z tags and
> is at 1.0.15 — an unprefixed spaces 0.1.0 tag would sort into the middle of
> slides' history.
> 
> spaces: first-release version, its own changelog, and a README that describes
> the app that exists rather than the scaffold it grew from.
> 
> * spaces: parse untrusted html inert — a detached div still runs it
> 
> Measured in a browser on the built shell over file://:
> document.createElement('div').innerHTML = '<img src="404" onerror=…>' FIRES
> the handler. The div is detached, but its elements belong to the live document,
> so the resource loads. DOMParser, <template> and createHTMLDocument are inert.
> 
> That made the sanitizer its own vector: it must parse hostile markup before it
> can strip it, so the payload ran before the strip. sanitizeInline runs at render
> time, so the trigger was opening a space someone sent you — no click, no edit.
> 
> Four call sites: sanitizeInline, textOf, render.ts's code-block text
> extraction, and about.ts's markdown export, which ran what it was exporting.
> The fourth was found by the new guard rather than by reading.
> 
> Verified after the fix with the removed construction kept in the same page as a
> control: only the control fired. Nothing reached the DOM — no [onerror], no
> smuggled img, no svg[onload], no javascript: href — while the #p/ link
> survived, external links kept rel=noopener noreferrer, <p>a</p><p>b</p> still
> unwrapped to 'a b', and markdown export produced correct output.
> 
> The guard is a source assertion, like the .href-IDL one: the behaviour needs a
> DOM and a failing request, and the mistake is made in the source. Both negative
> controls fire.
> 
> * spaces: a space does not phone home when you open it
> 
> Measured: a space carrying <img src="https://…/pixel.png">, opened from
> file://, issued the request before any interaction — one PerformanceObserver
> resource entry. That is a tracking pixel: the recipient's IP and the moment
> they read your document, delivered to whoever wrote the file. In a format whose
> premise is that you can mail it, it is the wrong default, and it breaks
> PLATFORM §1 (no network required to open).
> 
> Remote images now render a placeholder naming the host, with the alt text and a
> button. Only asset: and data: load unasked. The predicate is an allowlist, not
> a blocklist of http: — a relative path is a real request on a static host, and
> so are //host/x, blob: and filesystem:.
> 
> It costs authors nothing: the editor never writes a remote src (picked images
> are downscaled, interned by content hash, stored as asset:), so the only
> documents affected are hand- or agent-authored ones, which is exactly where a
> reader should be asked.
> 
> Consent is viewer state like locale and reduced motion — a Set on the editor
> that dies with the session, never a document field. Verified: nothing is
> fetched before consent, exactly one request after, the document is unchanged by
> the click, undo removes the block rather than the consent, and the saved file
> carries no trace of it.
> 
> Guide and rig updated; the rig's negative control fires.
> 
> * spaces: an encrypted space is never written to disk in the clear
> 
> main.ts called putRecovery on a 2.5s debounce, unconditionally. The recovery
> snapshot is the document as plain JSON, so an encrypted space wrote its full
> plaintext into IndexedDB every few seconds — defeating the password entirely,
> for the one author who has demonstrably asked for secrecy.
> 
> putRecovery does not guard this: it is a kernel primitive and encryption state
> is app-side, so it is a caller contract. about.ts already cleared the version
> timeline when a password was set, which is what made the gap easy to miss —
> half was handled, and the half that ran continuously was not.
> 
> Measured on the built shell: typing into a plaintext space put the marker in
> the recovery store within three seconds (correct — it is the only backstop on
> iOS). Setting a password removes that row, later edits write nothing, and the
> saved file is still a bento/enc envelope with no plaintext in it.
> 
> Two source assertions, both negative-controlled.
> 
> * spaces: the number find shows is the number replace changes
> 
> Replace-all is destructive and lands in one commit, and it quoted three
> different numbers. The readout counted matching BLOCKS ('2 found'), the
> confirmation quoted that as '2 occurrence(s)', and the sweep then changed 4.
> 
> Counting from textOf() would be wrong the other way: a needle split across
> markup (wid<b>get</b>) reads as one word but cannot be replaced, so it would
> promise a change that never happens.

> PR-5 of the spaces collaboration work: the pages/blocks binding, its own
> fixtures, and a rig that asks two questions instead of one.
> 
> CONVERGENCE IS PERFECT. 400 seeds x 100 steps x 4 actors, 17,227 ops, the
> kernel engine bound to ('pages','blocks'): every replica agrees, every seed.
> The engine serves spaces as a CRDT with no change to its algebra. That is the
> question a CRDT rig normally asks, and it is the good news.
> 
> 52.4% OF MERGED DOCUMENTS ARE NOT LEGAL bento/spaces DOCUMENTS. 209 of 399
> seeds. Worst case in a single document: 5 page cycles, 5 dangling page parents,
> 3 dangling block parents, 3 pages out of pre-order, 1 block out of pre-order, 1
> duplicated block id.
> 
> `page.blocks` is flat and in pre-order — "a child always follows its parent, so
> one forward pass rebuilds the tree" — while the engine stores order as
> fractional position keys and `parent` as an ordinary LWW register. Two
> independent merge domains describing one visual tree. You indent a block, I
> move one; both edits are legal, both apply, every replica agrees, and no
> forward pass can rebuild the result. renderBlocks does not crash on it — it
> silently draws the block at root, un-nested.
> 
> THE CONTROL IS THE REASON TO BELIEVE THE NUMBER. Each seed also runs a LONE
> replica through the same edits, receiving nothing, and a seed whose solo
> document is already illegal is EXCLUDED rather than counted — so the statistic
> is over seeds where the generator is provably clean. It caught three generator
> bugs while this was being written: a cross-page move that orphaned children, a
> page re-parent that inserted before its new parent, and a subtree walk that
> missed grandchildren. Without it this commit would have claimed 88%.
> 
> WHAT IS ASSERTED, AND WHY IT IS ONLY CONVERGENCE. Everything in the format
> table is an open design question this rig exists to have discovered, not
> pre-judged — derive the tree at render time or repair after apply (and a repair
> that COMMITS mints ord ops and can ping-pong forever); a visited set in
> Store.tree(); and whether the engine's by-design node duplication on concurrent
> moves, which is the morph idiom in slides, is a defect in spaces, where block
> ids are unique document-wide and #p/<page>/<block> anchors assume it. Failing
> the build on any of them would assert an answer nobody has chosen. STRICT=1
> turns all six into assertions — verified to exit 1 today — so the day the
> decisions land, this rig becomes their enforcement.
> 
> FIXTURES ARE PER-SHAPE, NOT WIDENED. sync-fixtures.ts picks its mutation with
> `Math.floor(rnd() * 13)` and is shared by two slides rigs; adding a case there
> would re-roll the kind mapping for every seed in both and silently change what
> the slides coverage means, while the diff looked purely additive.
> 
> DECISIONS.md carries both rulings — the shape descriptor from the previous
> step, and this measurement with the three things that must be settled before a
> spaces file ever carries collaboration state. The previous step's entry is
> included here because its scripted append silently did not apply: it anchored
> on a heading that lives on an unmerged branch, and the script reported success
> without checking. It checks now.
> 
> Verified: spaces rig 2/2 assertions at CI depth and at 400x100x4; STRICT=1
> exits 1; equivalence rig byte-identical; shape seam 14/14; test-sync.ts 46408
> checks; delprop 22/22; slides and kernel typecheck.

- 89b4462bceef2992403a18469fb4b3c466807cf2 — https://github.com/nyblnet/bento/commit/89b4462bceef2992403a18469fb4b3c466807cf2
> Treat every document as untrusted input (#277)
> 
> A security audit of this repo found two ways a document could execute arbitrary
> JavaScript in the page holding it, and two exports that leaked material the
> author believed was protected. That page owns doc.collab.key, the owner and
> writer private keys, the IndexedDB autosave store (plaintext snapshots of
> recent documents) and the retained File System Access handle -- so this is the
> open deck AND the file on disk.
> 
> MEASURED EXECUTING in Chrome 141, through the real renderSlide path, before
> this change: `<svg onload>`, a rect `onclick`, `<img onerror>` inside
> `<foreignObject>`, `<form action="javascript:">` with a submit click, and
> `<button formaction="javascript:">`. MEASURED FETCHING: a stylesheet link, an
> `@import` in an svg `<style>`, an external paint server. MEASURED NAVIGATING:
> `<meta http-equiv=refresh>` took the reader off the document, and `<base href>`
> retargeted every relative URL in it. None of that needed a malicious file:
> clipboard payloads were inserted with no validation at all, so one paste was
> enough, and double-clicking a text box re-injected its raw html.
> 
> WHAT CHANGED
> 
> svg markup is sanitized at render through an ALLOWLIST of elements and
> attributes. The first attempt was a denylist and it shipped an open critical
> behind forty passing checks -- `action` and `formaction` were simply not on the
> list of things it knew to remove. An allowlist refuses what nobody thought of,
> which is the entire property worth having here. Sanitizing at RENDER rather
> than at parse covers clipboard and CRDT deliveries too, and keeps the format
> additive. ids survive (gradients and markers resolve through document-global
> url(#…)) and svg `<style>` survives, because removing either breaks real decks.
> 
> Table cells validate every value for the CSS context it lands in, rather than
> interpolating author strings into a style attribute where they could close it
> and mint an event handler.
> 
> startTextEdit sanitizes the html it re-injects. `{{page:2}}` and `$E=mc^2$` are
> plain text to the sanitizer, so the raw swap still does its job.
> 
> previewIsSafe gains a stylesheet check, so injected markup cannot ride into the
> saved shell OUTSIDE #bento-doc, where it is live DOM at parse time for every
> reader. Not the flat `<style` refusal first proposed: every app's preview
> legitimately carries one hoisted `<style>`, and refusing it would have silently
> deleted the thumbnail feature for every deck.
> 
> Clipboard payloads are rebuilt key by key from the generated model key tables,
> enum by enum, with required fields enforced -- a validator that emits an
> element the format cannot express just moves the crash.
> 
> "Copy document JSON" no longer copies the room's owner private key, which it
> did while the tooltip recommended pasting it into an AI chat. "Save as
> template…" no longer writes plaintext out of a password-protected deck. A third
> leak turned up in the same sweep: the invite copy kept writerPriv. The
> stripping is now one list in one place, and a rig scans for both shapes so a
> new export path cannot reintroduce either.
> 
> The iOS host reduces a page-supplied filename to its last component and asserts
> containment before writing. It opens ANY self-contained document and its own
> comments treat them as mutually untrusted, so a page-chosen path was an
> arbitrary write inside the container -- over another deck the user would later
> open and trust.
> 
> Blob fetches verify the content address they asked for. The at-rest KDF goes to
> 600k iterations for NEW envelopes; existing files carry their own count and keep
> opening, which is pinned by a fixture because a deck that stops opening is far
> worse than a weak KDF.
> 
> The dev-server entries bind loopback. They served working/ -- the guestbook
> admin bearer token and the room's owner private key -- on every interface, with
> directory listing on.
> 
> WHAT IS NOT HERE
> 
> The relay authorization work is held back deliberately (#270): a relay deploy
> cannot be undone by an update, the current branch has an unresolved regression
> in blob reads, and dash shares the same relay.
> 
> Rewriting git history is not done either. The audit's full object-database scan
> of both repos found no credential in any commit, ever, so the only thing a
> rewrite would buy is scrubbing emails -- and it would strand every open fork
> again, which this project has already paid for once.
> 
> RELEASING.md said the source repo was private. It is not, and the stale
> sentence was believed during this audit until an anonymous fetch returned 200.
> It now says so plainly: nothing in a commit is private, and the keys stay out
> by .gitignore and by never being committed, never by repository visibility.

> bento/dash: a spreadsheet you could use instead of Excel (#248)
> 
> * dash: the spreadsheet gestures — selection, keyboard, freeze, 3D
> 
> Seven modules, each with its own rig (790 checks), plus the grid and
> store changes that put them on screen.
> 
>   select.ts   ranges, the keyboard map, TSV clipboard, fill series
>   a1.ts       A1 references and the cell-formula grammar
>   rowcol.ts   insert/delete/move/resize/freeze/hide
>   filter.ts   predicates, multi-sort, top-N
>   condfmt.ts  colour scales, data bars, rules
>   gl.ts       a WebGL2 renderer in 3.7 KB deflated
>   viz3d.ts    surfaces, scatter and bars over a sheet
> 
> What changed in the feel, rather than the feature list:
> 
> TYPE TO EDIT. A printable key on a selected cell replaces its contents
> and seeds the editor with the character typed, and Enter/Tab commit and
> move (down/up/right/left). Before this every edit needed a double-click
> first, which is the single gesture that made the grid read as a viewer
> rather than a spreadsheet. It routes ahead of the key map, which returns
> null for bare printable keys precisely so typing can reach it.
> 
> A SELECTION OUTLINE AND A FILL HANDLE. A per-cell tint alone does not
> read as a selection; the eye wants the rectangle. The handle in its
> corner is how a spreadsheet user expects to fill — not a menu item.
> 
> FROZEN COLUMNS. Columns only: rows are positioned by index so a subset
> cannot simply stick, and the header is sticky already, so the gap a
> reader actually hits is losing the labels when scrolling right.
> 
> setSheetProps grew a `drop` list and lost its duplicate implementation.
> Deletes were spelled `props: {k: undefined}`, which `JSON.stringify`
> erases — over collab the delete would land locally and reach no other
> replica, and the same trap sat on the inverse, so undoing a newly-set
> key was a no-op everywhere else. Deletes are now a listed `drop`,
> undefined is refused rather than accepted as a second spelling, the
> structural-key guard is enforced on the path that actually writes, and
> the store delegates to rowcol.ts so the forward and the inverse cannot
> drift apart.
> 
> * dash: cell formulas, and a header you can read
> 
> =A1+B1 in a cell. Column formulas stay the better tool and the default —
> they name columns by identity, so they survive every structural edit —
> but a spreadsheet that cannot put a number in ONE cell is not a
> spreadsheet, and nobody is going to be argued out of typing =B4*1.2.
> 
> cellformula.ts owns no engine. a1.ts already decides what a reference is
> and where it points; formula.ts already parses, evaluates and owns the
> error values. The bridge is that formula.ts resolves a `ref` node by NAME
> against its context, so a reference needs no parser support: rewrite `B4`
> to a generated name bound to a one-element vector. A range binds the same
> way to a longer one, which is why SUM(A1:A5) works without `:` ever
> becoming an operator.
> 
> Order is the correctness problem, not evaluation, so it is Kahn over
> cells and anything left when the queue drains gets #CYCLE! — never a
> plausible number. The rig's first draft passed on ordering by LUCK: every
> fixture was written with dependencies to the left of their dependents, so
> a plain document-order walk got the right answer. Sabotaging the sort
> caught one check out of thirty-three. The fixtures now run backwards
> against the document, and it catches them.
> 
> A1 counts CANONICAL positions, never the visible grid. Sorting and
> filtering are view state, so a formula must not change meaning when a
> reader sorts: verified in the browser — SUM(D1:D6) reads 72,350 before a
> sort and 72,350 after one.
> 
> setOverrides had the same wire bug setSheetProps did: a delete was
> `v: [undefined]`, and JSON.stringify turns that into `[null]`, so over
> collab the delete arrived as a null override instead. null deletes too
> now. runEdit takes several patches as ONE undo step (writing a value and
> clearing the formula it replaced is two), with the inverses REVERSED —
> which the obvious test cannot show, because two patches on different
> structures commute and pass either way. The check that discriminates
> writes the same key twice.
> 
> THE HEADER. Every column read "A R", "B O", "C :" — the letter, name,
> type badge, filter caret and resize grip were sharing 130px and the name
> lost. Two lines now: letters on their own strip where Excel puts them,
> with the type badge riding along in the space going spare, and the name
> below with room to be a name. Moving the letter cost two `parentElement`
> reads that silently became NaN — column select and click-to-sort both
> died, and both are `closest` now.
> 
> Type is a popover rather than window.prompt. Import refuses to guess a
> type it cannot decide, and that refusal is only honest if fixing it is
> one click — not a native dialog asking for the NUMBER of the type you
> wanted.
> 
> * dash: references that follow their cells — and two bugs found doing it
> 
> Copy/paste and insert/delete now maintain A1 references. translateRef
> and shiftRefsForInsert were both written and tested and called by
> nothing; this wires them to the two events that need them.
> 
> They are DIFFERENT rules and conflating them is the classic spreadsheet
> bug, so the rig proves they differ on the same input:
> 
>   COPY   the formula moved, the cells did not. References follow it,
>          except the $-pinned ones. =$A$1+B2 copied two rows down is
>          =$A$1+B4.
>   INSERT the cells moved, the formula did not. EVERY reference moves,
>          $ included, because the cell it names physically moved. The
>          same input shifted by two rows is =$A$3+B4.
> 
> A reference into a deleted row becomes #REF!, never the row that slid up
> into the gap. A range spanning the hole shrinks instead.
> 
> TWO BUGS FOUND WHILE WIRING THIS, both silent, neither mine:
> 
> ⌘V NEVER REACHED THE GRID. The document paste listener routed every
> pasted block into the CSV importer, so pasting cells created a whole new
> sheet instead of filling the selection — and grid.pasteTsv, fully
> written, had no callers at all. ⌘V pastes into the cells now; importing
> a file is what the Import button is for.
> 
> DELETE ROW DELETED THE WRONG ROW. Every structural op in rowcol.ts takes
> a CANONICAL row index — it must, since a document edit cannot be
> expressed in one reader's view — but the context menu passed the VISIBLE
> one. Identical until somebody sorts. Measured on a Value-sorted grid:

> destroyed. The re-sorted view then rescrambled over the evidence. Both
> indices are converted through grid.canonicalRow now.
> 
> The order vector was stale after a structural edit too — it holds row
> indices and insert/delete renumber the rows underneath them, so the grid
> drew blanks and rows in an order matching nothing. It rebuilds on a
> structural invalidation.
> 
> Copy keeps an internal clip so a copied formula stays a formula, while
> the system clipboard still carries VALUES — paste into another app and
> £37,200 is what is wanted there, not =D1*3. The clip is only used when
> the pasted text still matches what we wrote, so copying something else
> in between can never paste a stale clip in place of it.
>

> 
> Copying makes a SECOND formula that should mean the same thing in its
> new place, so its references move. Cutting moves the ONE formula, and a
> formula that travels with its cells still means exactly what it did —
> so a cut clip pastes untranslated. Excel agrees, and reversing it
> silently re-points a moved formula at the wrong data.
> 
> Cut also did not clear what it cut: clearSelection wrote null VALUES
> through setCells and never dropped the `f` override, so the formula
> stayed and simply recomputed. Cutting a formula cell appeared to do
> nothing, and Delete on one was a no-op. It drops both now, in a single
> commit so one ⌘Z puts back the values and the formulas together.
> 
> Known limitation, documented at the call site: formulas ELSEWHERE that
> referenced the cut cells do not follow them to the new location — they
> keep pointing at the old, now-empty positions.

> 
> About reaches the same places slides' does: this file (version, counts,
> size against the budget, docId, write-in-place state), document

> take-it-elsewhere set (copy JSON, replace from JSON, duplicate as a new
> workbook, save a copy). Nothing was writing the version timeline before,
