> bento/spaces round 2: callouts, highlighting, import, the agent surface — and eleven defects (#237)
> 
> * spaces: on a phone, every control is reachable — including Save
> 
> Measured at 375px: the topbar wanted 678px, so seven of eleven controls were
> laid out past the right edge. Save was one of them. The file could not be saved
> on a phone, and nothing indicated it — the buttons were in the DOM, laid out,
> and simply painted off-screen.
> 
> The rule is slides' rule: drop text and fold, never scroll. A horizontally
> scrolling toolbar hides the same controls, just less honestly.
> 
> The failure to guard against is not the CSS, it is the SECOND LIST — a phone
> menu maintained by hand as a copy of the desktop row drifts the first time
> either one changes, and the drift is invisible to anyone not holding a phone.
> So the secondary actions are declared once and feed both the inline row and the
> ⋯ menu, and the rig asserts exactly that.
> 
> Right-end menus also opened outward, putting the ⋯ and Save menus half
> off-screen at 375px. They open inward now, and every menu is capped to the
> viewport.
> 
> Verified at both widths on the built shell: 375px — 7 controls, nothing
> clipped, all three menus open within the viewport, Save reachable. 1280px —
> all 11 inline, ⋯ hidden, wordmark and Save label back. Both negative controls
> fire. Six new strings, translated in all eight catalogs.
> 
> * spaces: one declaration per block type
> 
> Adding a block type meant five edits across four files — the renderer's tag map
> and list map, the / menu, the markdown-autoformat table, and the markdown
> exporter — with nothing connecting them. Four out of five looked finished and
> exported as a bare paragraph.
> 
> It is also the merge-conflict surface. Several people adding block types in
> parallel all edit the same four hot files; now each type is one independent
> entry in blocks.ts and every consumer derives from it.
> 
> The registry is pure data — no DOM, no import from render.ts or editor.ts — so
> the dependency arrow is one-way and a node test reads it directly.
> 
> Behaviour-preserving, and checked rather than assumed. The same 22-block
> document (every type, both toggle states, a remote image, a dead page link, and
> an unknown type from a newer build) renders to a byte-identical DOM before and
> after: 32,061 chars, SHA-256 ee4214d7… on both. Markdown export is byte
> identical too (502 chars, SHA c3bfacf4…), the / menu keeps its 13 entries in
> order, and all 11 autoformat triggers still fire — including the aliases '* '
> and '[ ] ', which a one-pattern-per-type registry would have dropped silently.
> 
> Two near-misses the rig now pins: filtering custom types out of the tag map
> lifts every to-do out of its <ul>, and collapsing the alias lists halves the
> markdown triggers. Both negative controls fire.
> 
> * spaces: an agent authoring a space can see what it wrote
> 
> An agent had two write verbs and no way to look at the result. Everything
> that goes wrong in a space goes wrong SILENTLY: a link to a page that was
> renamed away still looks like a link, a <p> inside a block's html is unwrapped
> at render with no complaint, an unknown block type falls back to its text, an
> asset nothing references is just megabytes. None of it throws and none of it
> is visible in the JSON that was just written.
> 
> So `window.bento` gains a report half and a patch half (spaces/src/agent.ts).
> 
> validate() reports what is wrong or suspect as structured findings —
> {code, severity, message, fix, page?, block?, path?} — covering duplicate and
> missing ids, a page inside its own subtree, parents naming nothing, dead #p/
> links and pagelink cards, unknown block types, block markup inside inline html
> (and markup dropped whole, which is content no reader will ever see), hrefs
> outside the allowlist, images with no alt, no size, a missing asset: or a
> remote src, a home naming nothing, pages with no blocks, and orphaned assets.
> outline() returns the whole tree with headings and outgoing links, so
> orienting is one call rather than one getPage per page. stats() says where the
> bytes are, biggest assets first, each with a use count.
> 
> The bar for the validator is silence, not few false positives: ZERO findings
> on the space every new file opens with, asserted in the rig, because that is
> the only baseline of "idiomatic" available and an agent that gets warnings for
> good documents learns to skip them. The corollary is what is NOT checked —
> unknown property names, which slides warns about, are how this format carries
> a future build's data and an agent's own metadata.
> 
> updateBlock / removeBlocks / moveBlock / updatePage / removePage join
> insertBlocks, each one undoable step. They PLAN, then apply: store.commit
> checkpoints undo before it mutates, so validating inside the commit would
> leave a refused patch with an undo entry that undoes nothing. Measured in the
> built shell: three refusals of three kinds, then one undo, reaches the state
> before the last real edit. The split also makes the write path testable in
> node — no store, no DOM — which is where the 16 new negative controls run.
> 
> Nothing is silently ignored: `id` in a patch, or `blocks` on a page, is
> refused. New verbs return {ok:false, err, detail}; insertBlocks and newPage
> keep the shapes they shipped with in 0.1.0.
> 
> An agent cannot write what the app could not have written. html goes through
> the editor's sanitizer on the way IN, not only on the way to the screen; a
> code block's html is escaped instead (the renderer shows its textContent, so
> sanitizing would delete the sample being shown) and only when it carries live
> tags, so replaying a patch cannot double-escape; a value JSON cannot carry is
> refused rather than vanishing at save time.
> 
> Two real defects fixed on the way. insertBlocks with an unknown afterId
> appended at the end and reported success — now an error. And bento.newPage()
> created a page with blocks: [], which MEASURED in the built shell renders 0
> editable hosts, 0 gutters and 0 block nodes: no caret, no gutter, no / menu,
> a page nobody can ever type in, and the editor cannot produce or repair one.
> newPage now mints a paragraph as model.newPage always did, removeBlocks
> refills a page it empties, and validate() calls a zero-block page an error.
> 
> Cost: +8,040 bytes on the shipped shell (73,787 → 81,827; compressed payload
> 72KB → 79KB), nearly all of it the finding messages. A code with no
> explanation is not actionable; shorten the prose before dropping a check.
> 
> Verified: tsc, build:single, shell-gate, i18n --check, 166/166 in
> scripts/test-spaces-model.ts, each new assertion proven by breaking the code
> and watching it fire. Exercised in a browser from file:// on a uniquely-named
> copy — the whole surface, undo granularity, and a genuinely frozen (version
> 99) file where every write returns err:'readonly' and the document is
> untouched.
> 
> * spaces: four things that were wrong in the file we shipped
> 
> A design review of the whole app turned up shipped defects that outrank any new
> feature. Each was verified in the code and then in a browser before being
> touched.
> 
> 1. 'Save a copy…' silently retargeted ⌘S. saveFile(doc, true) ASSIGNS the
>    picked handle to the kernel's in-place handle, so every later save wrote to
>    the copy while the original stayed frozen at the moment it was taken — you
>    go on typing into what you believe is your document. The call site even
>    carried a comment asserting the kernel kept the handle pointed at the
>    working file; it never did. writeUpdatedFileAs is the path that actually
>    holds that guarantee (keepHandle defaults false), and its own comment
>    records slides learning the same lesson. The confirmation was dead too:
>    saveFile returns 'saved-as' down that path, never 'saved'.
> 
> 2. doc.readonly was declared in the format and read by NOTHING. A space saved
>    as a reading copy opened fully editable — the one property the sender chose
>    was the one the file did not keep. Verified end to end on a spliced file:
>    it now opens with a banner, no editable host, and every write verb refusing.
> 
> 3. The agent API returned ids for blocks it never wrote. store.commit
>    early-returns on a read-only document; insertBlocks and newPage returned the
>    ids regardless, so an agent addressed blocks that do not exist and could not
>    tell that from an empty page. All three write verbs refuse out loud now.
> 
> 4. Block anchors were dead on arrival. sanitize.ts's allowlist ALREADY admits
>    #p/<page>/<block>, so such a link can appear in a file this build did not
>    write — and it resolved to nothing, not even the page, while the backlink
>    index keyed it on a page id that does not exist. Tolerance costs three lines
>    and cannot be retrofitted on the sender's behalf: sanitize.ts records why a
>    new fragment form is a one-way hazard, since a stricter later build strips
>    it on the next edit.
> 
> Also: the inert-parse guard iterated a HARDCODED list of the five files that
> existed when the hole was found, so findreplace.ts and blocks.ts were never
> checked and any new module could reintroduce it with the guard green. It globs
> every source file now — 22, not 5. A guard that only covers the code it was
> written against is a guard that expires.
> 
> And the find bar laid out 644px wide at a 575px viewport, starting at x=-87:
> the Find field itself was off the left edge. It wraps to two rows below 720px
> (measured: 359px inside 375px, everything reachable; desktop unchanged at one
> row).
> 
> * docs: settle the bento/spaces format decisions that block parallel work
> 
> Five design reviews proposed overlapping feature sets; most of it schedules in
> any order. These six do not — each is a place where two workstreams would
> invent conflicting PERMANENT shapes for the same thing, and there is no server
> and no migration to fix that afterwards.
> 
> Properties are blocks, not page keys, because an unknown block type still
> renders through render.ts's default branch while an unknown page key renders as
> nothing and is invisible to search, find-and-replace and undo. Containers are
> one declared mechanism so tables, callouts and columns do not each generalise
> the renderer's host stack. Render-time transforms may not decorate editable
> content — verified: input writes host.innerHTML into the model and the
> allowlist then deletes an unknown element together with its children, so a
> rendered <math> costs the equation AND its source text. And the effective-parent
> rule is written down as a format invariant, because it is what will make
> concurrent re-parenting converge without restricting what anyone can drag.
> 
> * spaces: the callout, and a tone vocabulary that cannot be taken back
> 
> The most-asked-for block spaces lacked. It is one registry entry plus the two
> things a registry cannot express: how a box looks, and what a box means.
> 
> THE TONES ARE GITHUB'S FIVE — note, tip, important, warning, caution — spelled
> the way GitHub spells them, so `tone` and `> [!TONE]` are the same word in both
> directions. Docusaurus's set and MkDocs' thirteen both need a mapping table in
> the exporter, and a mapping table is the kind of thing that can be got wrong
> once and then never corrected, because the wrong tone is already on someone's
> disk. Five and no `success`: the format is additive, so a sixth can be added
> later — this build renders an unknown tone neutrally, labels it with its own
> word and preserves the string, verified — while renaming one is impossible.
> When the decision is one-way, ship the smaller set.
> 
> THE ICON IS DERIVED, WITH AN OVERRIDE. Storing it always would freeze today's
> glyphs into every document written today, and would let the mark and the tone
> disagree — a "warning" wearing a party popper. The override is there because a
> celebration is a callout too, and it never changes what the tone means, in the
> styling or in the export.
> 
> MEANING IS NEVER IN THE HUE. Each tone's mark is a different silhouette —
> circle, bulb, square, triangle, octagon — and its name is rendered beside it as
> real text, translated, not a ::before and not aria-hidden. Amber, red and green
> are exactly the hues most colour-blind readers cannot separate, and browsers do
> not print backgrounds by default, so anything carried by fill alone is carried
> by nothing. Checked in greyscale under the print rules: box, heavier start
> rule, black label, distinct shape. Body text stays --ink rather than the tone
> colour — a box exists to make a sentence more readable.
> 
> NESTING IS A REGISTRY FACT NOW. `container` is 'fold' (toggle) or 'always'
> (callout), and render.ts opens a body element from that instead of testing for
> a type name; `mdQuoteChildren` drives the markers every descendant line needs.
> That last part is where markdown quietly goes wrong: a GitHub alert ends at the
> first line without `> `, and a blank line between two blocks of one alert closes
> the box, so half a callout exports as loose prose and nothing in the document,
> the renderer or the type system notices. mdLayout() works both out in one pass
> and is pure, so the rig can drive it — it is the part with the edge cases, so it
> is the part that had to be reachable from a test.
> 
> ⏎ inside a callout puts the next line INSIDE it and ⌫ on an empty line takes you
> out. That is what makes nesting discoverable without knowing Tab does it.
> Deliberately not extended to `toggle`: a fold can be shut, and a caret inside a
> shut fold is a lost line.
> 
> MEASURED. `> ` converts to a quote at the space, so `> [!NOTE] ` can never be
> typed as one trigger — the block is already a quote by the time the bracket
> arrives. The trigger is the tag alone, which fires just as well inside the quote
> it lands in, and that path is what people type. Export of a callout holding a
> paragraph, a bullet and a second paragraph comes out as a valid alert with the
> nested blocks intact. Shell 72KB → 76KB compressed.
> 
> Two holes found while nearby. The i18n sweep reads comments, so an example call
> written in one becomes a required key in all eight catalogs — it did, and CI
> would have failed on a comment. And `icon in ICONS` is true for 'toString': an
> icon name out of a mailed file resolved to a function and got stringified into
> the page. Both are pinned; the second was already in pageIcon and is fixed
> there too.
> 
> Eleven new assertions, each proven by breaking the code and watching it fire:
> tone sanitising, the per-line quote, the bare-`>` separator, the un-indented
> alert body, init not clobbering an existing tone, the ancestor hop cap (which
> hangs the export without it), the translated tone names, and the four
> consumers-must-derive checks. Nine strings, translated in all eight catalogs.
> 
> * spaces: code blocks are highlighted, and the colour never enters the file
> 
> A wiki full of unhighlighted code reads as unfinished, and every serious notes
> app colours it. The libraries do not fit: highlight.js is ~120KB and the useful
> subset of Prism ~30KB, against a 72KB shell whose whole premise is that you can
> mail the file. So this is our own lexer.
> 
> MEASURED, on the built shell: the lexer, the painter, the chip and the palette
> together cost 4.0KB compressed; all eight vocabularies together cost a further
> 1.4KB — about 180 bytes per language, because keyword lists are lowercase ascii
> and deflate eats them. Total 73,787 → 79,331 bytes, +5.4KB. The machinery is the
> cost and the languages are nearly free, which inverts the instinct to support
> fewer languages to save bytes. So the reason to stop at eight — JavaScript,
> TypeScript, Python, Shell, JSON, YAML, SQL, HTML/XML, CSS — is that those are
> the ones a working notebook accumulates and the ones this rig actually tests.
> Everything else renders plain, deliberately, and keeps its tag: a ```rust block
> round-trips, exports as ```rust, and lights up by itself the day the lexer
> learns it.
> 
> THE TOKENIZER RETURNS OFFSETS, NEVER STRINGS. A token is {kind, a, b} into the
> caller's text, and the tokens partition [0, len) exactly. That is the security
> property rather than tidiness — code in a space is text someone mailed you, and
> a highlighter that cannot produce a character cannot produce markup, whatever
> the input does. The painter walks the ranges and builds nodes with
> createTextNode, so there is no constructed markup string anywhere in the path
> and therefore no escaper to get wrong. The rig asserts the partition across
> every language over a corpus that includes </script>, <img onerror>,
> unterminated strings and lone backslashes, and pins the discipline in the source
> the way the inertBody guard above it does.
> 
> The document is untouched. b.html stays the html-escaped plain text it always
> was, so the same block is the same bytes whether or not the reading build knows
> the language, and reading view and print take their colour from the same
> renderBlock call the editor uses — verified: the print tree carries the spans
> and no chip. The editor's code host is therefore read as textContent (innerHTML
> now contains the colour spans) and written through sanitize.escText, which
> escapes & < > and NOT ", matching the html serializer exactly so an untouched
> block never serializes differently from the save before it.
> 
> HIGHLIGHTING A LIVE CONTENTEDITABLE: RECONCILE, DO NOT REPLACE. The painter
> diffs the token stream against the existing child nodes. The point is that on
> `input` the browser has ALREADY applied the keystroke, so re-tokenising usually
> yields byte-identical nodes. Measured in Chrome on the built shell: typing in
> the middle of a line produced one characterData mutation (the browser's own) and
> ZERO childList mutations, and the caret went 76 → 77 — untouched, not restored.
> Only a keystroke that moves a token boundary restructures anything; typing a
> quote produced childList records and the caret went 79 → 80, restored by
> character offset. The restore has to exist — assigning Text.data is specified to
> collapse a live range inside it to offset 0 — it just must not be the common
> path. IME composition is skipped until compositionend; the model keeps up
> regardless.
> 
> Language selection: a chip on hover, and the fence carries it, so ```py opens a
> Python block. Which needed the fence to be space-completed, where a bare ```
> converted on the third backtick and left no keystroke to type the tag into;
> every other trigger in that table is space-completed already.
> 
> Which is how the next one surfaced. EVERY MARKDOWN TRIGGER WAS DEAD. A space
> typed at the end of a contenteditable line is inserted as U+00A0 so it cannot
> collapse: after typing "## ", host.textContent is ['#','#',160], and /^## $/
> never matched it. So `# `, `- `, `1. `, `> `, `[] ` and `--- ` had not fired
> since 0.1.0, in the feature the starter space advertises on its Writing page.
> autoformat now normalises the NBSP before testing, never in the model.
> 
> Also, because a code block is text and not a paragraph: Enter adds a line
> instead of splitting the block, and Tab indents two spaces instead of
> re-parenting the block in the page tree. Enter is handled explicitly rather than
> left to the engine — what a browser inserts varies between a \n, a <br> and a
> wrapping <div>, and only the first survives being read back as textContent.
> 
> Rig: 27 new checks, and every one of the 18 new assertions was watched to fail
> against a deliberate mutation of the code it guards before being kept.
> 
> Known and left alone: a template literal, an f-string and a <script> body are
> one token each (nested grammars cost bytes to get right and nothing to get
> wrong); the chip is hover-only, so touch cannot reach it, exactly like the block
> gutter and the image tools it sits beside; and an edited multi-line block gains
> one trailing newline, which is Chrome's caret placeholder, is bounded at one
> (measured on a bare pre-wrap contenteditable with none of our code involved),
> and is the same byte the previous innerHTML read produced.
> 
> * sync: a rig that proves the bytes, not just the convergence
> 
> spaces is about to get live collaboration by PARAMETERIZING the shipped
> bento-sync engine over a document-shape descriptor (doc.slides[] ->
> slide.elements[] becomes doc.pages[] -> page.blocks[]) rather than forking it.
> Nothing about that plan is guarded today, and the exposure is not theoretical:
> every bento/slides file in the field carries persisted SyncStateJSON in
> doc.collab.sync and talks to the deployed relay. If parameterization changes any
> byte the engine mints -- an op, a frame, a snapshot, a fractional position key,
> a lamport stamp -- those files stop agreeing with their own copies, silently, in
> the field, and there is no way to push a fix to a file someone already saved.
> 
> WHAT WAS MISSING. scripts/test-sync.ts proves CONVERGENCE: replicas of the same
> engine agree at quiescence. That is strictly weaker than what we need. An engine
> that converges beautifully with ITSELF while minting different bytes than the
> shipped one sails straight through 300 seeds. The rig cannot see the failure
> because both sides of its comparison are the new engine.
> 
> WHAT I MEASURED. Four deliberately perturbed engines, each a legal and fully
> self-consistent CRDT: adopt() deriving different (order-preserving) fractional
> keys, one extra lamport tick per diff, ops serialized with their fields in a
> different order, SyncStateJSON.regs serialized in a different key order. All
> four CONVERGE. test-sync.ts passes every one of them. Every one of them would
> split shipped files. They now ship as this rig's self-test, and it catches all
> four -- op field order is caught ONLY by the op-bytes check, and regs key order
> ONLY by the state-bytes check, so neither comparator is redundant.
> 
> WHAT IT DOES. scripts/test-sync-equiv.ts runs a baseline engine and a candidate
> engine off ONE seeded PRNG stream and asserts the emitted bytes are identical,
> per step, per actor: the op batch (JSON.stringify, so field order counts), the
> resulting SyncStateJSON (so key order counts, and a key-order-only difference is
> labelled as such rather than hidden), and the materialized document. Plus eleven
> scripted scenarios for the paths a random walk never reaches -- adopt,
> mergeSnapshot, fromJSON, missingFor, the pre-v2 reject, the 300KB text RGA, the
> duplicate-id morph idiom. First divergence prints seed, step, actor, the first
> differing byte with context, and the diverging JSON paths (composite element
> keys shown with their U+001F escaped, because an invisible separator in a debug
> path is a trap). Exit is non-zero.
> 
> THE HONEST PART, AND WHY IT IS IN THE HEADER IN A BOX. There is one engine in
> the tree today, so the candidate import resolves to the same module -- they are
> === at runtime -- and the comparison is vacuous by construction. The rig says so
> at startup (NO-OP RUN) and will say LIVE RUN when the import is repointed. A rig
> that passes trivially and does not announce that it passes trivially is worse
> than no rig: it reads as coverage. The self-test is the part of a NO-OP run that
> carries signal.
> 
> TIMINGS, so CI can budget it: SEEDS=200 STEPS=60 ACTORS=4 is 1.46-1.51s wall
> clock, SEEDS=1000 STEPS=25 ACTORS=3 is 1.55-1.79s, both end to end including
> node startup, the scenarios and the self-test. The former is now a CI step
> beside the convergence rig.
> 
> Determinism is from the seed alone -- no Date.now, no unseeded Math.random. Each
> step's mutation is generated from a sub-seed derived from (seed, step) rather
> than drawn from the shared stream, so a difference in how much randomness one
> engine consumes can never cascade into a false divergence somewhere else.
> 
> Generator and fixtures moved to scripts/lib/sync-fixtures.ts, imported by both
> rigs. Two rigs with two generators would become two different opinions about
> what a document and an edit are, and the equivalence rig's whole value is being
> the convergence rig's stricter twin. test-sync.ts output is byte-identical
> before and after the extraction (45368 checks, and 46408 at SEEDS=300).
> 
> No product code was touched: git diff --stat slides/ kernel/ server/ is empty,
> and it is meant to stay empty for this step.
> 
> * spaces: markdown import, so a vault can arrive whole
> 
> Nobody adopts a notes app they cannot get their notes into. Drop a folder of
> .md files on the window, or pick them: each file becomes a page, the folder
> tree becomes the page tree, and [[wikilinks]] become #p/ links you can click.
> +14 KB compressed (72 -> 86 KB), roughly half of it the 28 new UI strings
> across eight catalogs.
> 
> MEASURED on a 20-note vault with three images, from the shipped shell in a
> browser rather than from reasoning: 25 pages, 82 blocks, 24 of 26 wikilinks
> resolved, 3 images embedded, the one deliberately absent image reported. 3.5 KB
> of markdown becomes 10.3 KB of document -- block ids and JSON structure are
> about 3x the prose. With the images the file is 343 KB, of which 246 KB is the
> two distinct pictures: prose is free, photographs are not.
> 
> THE PARSER IS ITS OWN MODULE AND HAS NO DOM. markdown.ts is pure, so 300 notes
> and their cross-links are asserted in node in 5 ms rather than clicked through.
> It also does NOT sanitize: raw inline html is reduced to an allowlisted
> skeleton there, and sanitizeInline -- the app's real policy, with a real parser
> -- runs over every block in the importer, once, before anything is committed.
> One security gate, in the place that already has the tests for it.
> 
> WIKILINKS RESOLVE AFTER EVERY PAGE EXISTS, by file name first (which is what
> Obsidian, Foam and Logseq link by), then page title, then vault-relative path.
> Between parse and resolution a link is an <a href="#w/target">, a scheme that
> can never reach a saved file: resolution rewrites all of them, and the
> sanitizer's allowlist is https/mailto/#p/ -- so the worst a bug here can do is
> lose a link, never write one that points somewhere unexpected. A target outside
> the import stays as the literal [[Name]] the author wrote rather than silently
> un-linking, and a target naming a page the space ALREADY has resolves to it, so
> adding one note to a year-old space is not dead text.
> 
> FRONTMATTER IS KEPT VERBATIM AND INTERPRETED NOWHERE: a code block marked
> frontmatter: true, lang yaml, inside a collapsed toggle. Spaces has no
> properties model, and a schema invented inside an importer -- from whichever
> keys one person's vault happens to use -- would settle that design by accident
> and be unrecoverable, because the format is permanent and there is no server to
> migrate anyone. The marker is what makes the eventual adoption a sweep instead
> of archaeology. Reasoning in full in docs/DECISIONS.md. The page title comes
> from a leading # Heading or else the FILE NAME, never from a title: key: a
> title that disagrees with the file name leaves [[Note]] pointing at a page
> nobody can name.
> 
> IMAGES, HONESTLY. A relative path in a .md file names a file on the author's
> disk and a browser cannot open it, so images resolve against the files actually
> selected -- exact relative path first, then base name, which is how ![[pic.png]]
> works -- and embed through the existing downscale. What cannot be found becomes
> visible text quoting the path, never an <img> that can only be broken. A remote
> URL stays a remote URL and still asks the reader before it loads. Past 12 MB of
> embedded images the import ASKS rather than stopping: the house rule for size
> is warn, never block.
> 
> TABLES ARE KEPT AS TEXT. This format has no table block yet, and turning one
> into paragraphs destroys it. Verbatim in a code block is aligned, searchable,
> exportable, and mechanically upgradable the day a table block ships.
> 
> ONE UNDOABLE STEP, and pages are ADDED -- an import that replaced someone's
> space is the one mistake that cannot be walked back. Everything slow (reading
> files, decoding images, hashing) happens before a single synchronous commit,
> the same shape as placeImage. The report says "removes the imported pages
> again", not "puts the space back exactly as it was": measured, undo restores
> `pages` byte-identically but the image bytes stay, because undo snapshots
> deliberately exclude assets and pruning them would break REDO, which re-inserts
> blocks pointing at those keys.
> 
> FOUND IN A BROWSER, not by reading: an index.md folder note titled a whole
> section "index"; a refused <a href="javascript:"> left its closing tag behind;
> and "1 of 1 wikilink(s) resolved. The rest name notes that were not in the
> selection." is a sentence about nothing.
> 
> The rig goes from 80 checks to 144. Every new one was proved by breaking the
> code under it and watching it fire -- 18 mutations, two of which caught
> assertions that were wrong as first written: deleting the sanitize pass PASSED
> an indexOf ordering check (-1 sorts before everything), and the folder-note
> check passed while two pages shared a title.
> 
> * spaces: markdown triggers never fired for anyone typing
> 
> A trailing space typed at the end of a contentEditable line is inserted by the
> browser as U+00A0, not U+0020 — otherwise it would collapse and the caret would
> appear not to move. So /^## $/ matched nothing a person typed, and every
> markdown trigger has been dead since 0.1.0: measured in the built shell with
> execCommand('insertText'), '# ', '## ', '- ', '1. ', '> ' and '[] ' all arrive
> as [.., 160] and converted nothing. The starter space advertises this feature
> on its Writing page.
> 
> It survived my own test, which reported all eleven triggers passing. That test
> assigned host.textContent directly, with a real space — which is not typing,
> and is a path no keystroke takes. Driving the same triggers through
> execCommand('insertText') converts zero of six before this change and ten of
> ten after.
> 
> Normalised for the TEST only. The model keeps whatever the browser put there:
> rewriting the author's text so a pattern matches would be a worse cure than the
> disease.
> 
> Found by an agent building code highlighting, which needed the same trailing
> space for its ```lang fence.
> 
> * spaces: an icon name from a mailed file must not resolve through the prototype
> 
> 'toString' in ICONS is true and resolves to a function, so a page whose icon is
> "toString" or "constructor" returned native source text and skipped the escape
> on the line below. It stringifies to text rather than markup, so this was not
> an injection — but it is author-supplied data reaching the page unescaped, and
> the next lookup table indexed with `in` might not be so lucky.
> 
> Found by an agent building callouts, which needed the same lookup for tone
> icons.
> 
> * spaces: the starter space must not teach a trigger that no longer fires
> 
> Every other hint in the starter shows its trailing space explicitly — '[] ',
> '> ' — because that space is part of the trigger. The two code-fence hints did
> not, and the fence is exactly where it now matters: the rule grew a language
> capture this round, so typing ``` alone stopped converting and only ``` plus a
> space does.
> 
> The starter space is the first thing anyone sees and the only documentation
> most people will read. An instruction in it that does not work is worse than no
> instruction.
> 
> * spaces: the duplicated lists four parallel agents each recreated
> 
> Four features merged in a day, built by agents who could not see each other's
> work, and each needed something the codebase already knew. Two copies got in:
> 
> model.ts gained KNOWN_BLOCK_TYPES beside the block registry, and agent.ts
> restated the sanitizer's unwrap policy as a lowercased literal. Both were
> correct on arrival, which is exactly what makes them dangerous — a copy is
> right until the original changes, and then it is wrong in a way nothing
> reports. validate() reporting a real block type as unknown would have an agent
> 'fix' a working document.
> 
> Both now derive: known types from SPECS, the unwrap set from the sanitizer's
> exported UNWRAP. Pinned by assertions whose negative controls fire.
> 
> Also: the sanitizer's UNWRAP is exported rather than duplicated, because
> validate() genuinely needs to tell an agent which block-level tags get
> unwrapped out of inline html.
> 
> * spaces: five defects an adversarial review reproduced, and four claims of mine that were not true
> 
> Every one of these shipped with all gates green. Each lived in a case the
> author's own spot-check did not reach, which is the argument for the review.
> 
> THE DEFECTS
> 
> 1. Markdown export broke the GitHub alert and the fence whenever a callout
>    child spanned more than one line. about.ts prefixed '> ' per returned
>    ELEMENT, but an element can hold newlines — a code block's body is one
>    multi-line string, and htmlToMd turns <br> into a newline. The 2nd line
>    carried no '>', which ends the blockquote, unterminates the fence and drops
>    the rest of the callout out of the box as broken prose. Quoted per line now,
>    with a bare '>' for blank lines because a truly blank line closes the quote.
> 
> 2. Markdown import double-escaped the visible text of every link, wikilink,
>    autolink and image alt: '[Q&A](…)' reached the file as 'Q&amp;amp;A' and the
>    reader saw the entity. Display text is not escaped at those four sites any
>    more — the single esc() at the end does it once, as it always did for
>    ordinary prose. Bold, italic and code were never affected because their text
>    sits outside a placeholder, which is exactly why a spot-check of "inline
>    formatting survived" passed.
> 
> 3. bento.updatePage(id, {parent}) hung the tab forever on a page cycle. parseDoc
>    preserves A.parent=B/B.parent=A (it only drops parents naming no page), so
>    the cycle arrives from any mailed file, and the ancestor walk had no visited
>    set. Measured: the call never returns, exit 124. The reachable sequence is
>    the RECOMMENDED one — validate() reports the cycle, an agent re-homes a page
>    to fix it, and that call kills the tab with every unsaved edit in it.
> 
> 4. Markdown import created pages with zero blocks — one per folder without a
>    folder note, one per empty file, plus the invented root — and then navigated
>    to one of them. A zero-block page has no editable host, no gutter and no /
>    menu, so the first thing a vault import showed you was a page you could not
>    put a caret in, permanently.
> 
> 5. A list item holding an image, followed by a continuation line, wrote the
>    literal string "undefined" into the document and hid the author's prose. An
>    image has no html and is not a container, so it is now neither a
>    continuation target nor a parent: the line becomes its own paragraph beside
>    the image rather than a child of it.
>

> assertions' negative controls fire, and the cycle guard is checked structurally
> as well as behaviourally so a regression FAILS rather than hanging CI.

> Then the review list:
> 
> - Reading view is read-only again: the callout tone chip had no guard, so a
>   click in reading view committed a tone change — undo entry, dirty flag and
>   all — while the renderer was deliberately emitting an inert span beside it.
> - Tab now NESTS. It always wrote `parent`; nothing rendered it, because only

>   Tab was a key that did nothing you could see. A list item hosts its own

>   described a runtime list that no longer exists.

> from toJSON() rather than listing six stable ones — the listed version would
> have been blind to any seventh field, including one added by the very
> parameterization the rig exists to check. Its mutants now survive a fromJSON
> round trip (crdt.ts's static fromJSON constructs `new SyncState` literally, so
> scenarios that restore state were testing the baseline against itself while
> reporting mutant coverage).

> 
> That site is NOT pinned by a hand-written case, and the comment in
> test-crdt-delprop.ts says so: two constructed scenarios failed to reach it and

> * spaces: a saved space shows its content to readers that run no script
> 
> Reported from the field: the file opened to the boot splash and stayed there.
> 
> The cause is not the splash. The runtime ships DEFLATED and is inflated by a
> loader at boot, so where scripting is off nothing inflates, nothing boots, and
> nothing ever removes the splash — the file shows a loading animation where its
> content should be. That is what macOS QuickLook, iOS Files, Bento Tray and any
> HTML preview pane see of every space saved so far. It only surfaced now because
> the splash became a full dark animation this week; the plain white one looked
> like a slow load rather than a hang.
> 
> Slides solved this in 0.9.x and spaces never called the mechanism: every save
> now writes a still render of the home page into the shell, followed IMMEDIATELY
> by a parser-blocking script that deletes both. A thumbnailer keeps it — it runs
> no script; a reader never sees it — the remover runs before the first paint.
> The shell gate already asserts that ordering for preview-carrying shells.
> 
> Verified on a real save: 3,513 bytes of preview (budget 64KB), the host
> followed directly by the remover and both ahead of #app, and the preview's
> z-index above the splash's so it covers it rather than hiding behind it.
> Rendered, it is the page — headings, prose, lists, links, and to-do state as ☐/☑
> glyphs, since an <input> is a control and a still has none.
> 
> Two rules it inherits and one it adds. Inherited: an encrypted space never
> carries a preview (plaintext beside ciphertext is the leak the password
> exists to prevent), and the preview REPLACES rather than appends. Added: the
> still may not FETCH — href and non-data src are stripped, so a remote image
> cannot phone home from a file manager, which is the remote-image consent rule
> applied where nobody could consent.
> 
> It has its own stylesheet rather than reusing the app's, because the app's
> ships deflated too and does not exist in this mode.
> 
> Shell ceiling 114 → 118 KiB, raised here with the reason, per the rule.

> dash M0: the app — it opens, edits, imports and saves (#233)
> 
> bento/dash is now a Bento file. 25 KB compressed shell, through the same
> splice conformance gate as slides and spaces.
> 
> WHAT IT DOES. Opens with a starter workbook that demonstrates every column type
> it knows, a totals row and a provenance step -- none of which is discoverable
> from an empty grid. Sort by clicking a header. Edit a cell by double-clicking.
> Import a CSV, by button or by pasting one. Export CSV. Undo. Save, to a real
> file, which re-opens with the data in it.
> 
> Verified end to end in a browser against the BUILT shell rather than the dev
> server: the starter renders, sorting leaves the document untouched and the file
> clean, an edit updates the totals row and undo restores both, a semicolon-and-
> German-decimals CSV imports with its dates REFUSED and explained, serialize
> round-trips to an identical document, and that serialized file boots as a fresh
> workbook with both sheets and correct totals.
> 
> THE BOOT DISPATCHER is the part worth reading. Only an absent or empty
> #bento-doc reaches the starter; everything else refuses, names what it found,
> and offers the bytes back untouched -- with no Store, no save handler and no
> autosave subscription constructed on that path, so nothing downstream CAN
> serialize over somebody's data. It also tells apart the case the kernel cannot:
> readEmbeddedDoc returns `text || null`, so a present-but-unreadable block
> arrives looking identical to an absent one, and only the boot site can still
> see the DOM to know the difference.
> 
> AUTOSAVE IS GUARDED by isEncryptionActive() -- the rule the kernel states in
> its own header, enforces nowhere, and which spaces' M0 therefore missed
> (raised on #226).
> 
> TWO LAYOUT BUGS, both found by looking rather than by types:
> 
> - The first two rows were hidden behind the header. `position: sticky` resolves
>   against the scroll container, so absolutely-positioned rows at top:0 landed
>   underneath it. Header and totals are now in normal flow with only the row
>   region absolute.
> - The findings banner kept a visible strip of its background when empty,
>   because `display: grid` beats the [hidden] attribute's own display:none.
> 
> Neither is expressible in a test that does not render.
> 
> The grid is WINDOWED -- 100k x 6 would be 600,000 nodes, and that, not the
> arithmetic, is what stops a browser. Sorting goes through store.view(): it
> sorts an order vector, never the data, so it takes no checkpoint and does not
> dirty the file. Registered in scripts/apps.mjs and built + gated in CI.
> 
> Deliberately not here: formulas, charts, collaboration, the vault binding.
> M1's acceptance sentence is the CSV round trip, and this is it.

#### 2. 0.12.3 / SAHI 0.12.3 - Apple Silicon GPU Support 🍎

item_id: obss/sahi::release::363534739
Data: 2026-08-01T13:41:04Z
URL: https://github.com/obss/sahi/releases/tag/0.12.3

Release notes (texto original):

> A patch release that puts Apple Silicon GPUs to work, adds a Turkish translation of the documentation, and clears CI maintenance gathered since `0.12.2`.
> 
> ### 🐛 Fixes
> 
> - **Apple MPS is now detected for device selection and postprocessing** ([#1408](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1408)). `select_device()` only looked for CUDA, so macOS users fell back to CPU even with a working Metal backend. Automatic selection is now CUDA -> MPS -> CPU, and the `torchvision` postprocessing backend is picked when either GPU is present. Detection goes through `torch.backends.mps.is_available()`, which exists on every supported torch version and reports `False` on non-Apple builds.
> - **`threading.currentThread()` replaced with `current_thread()`** ([#1392](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1392)), removing a `DeprecationWarning` on newer Python versions.
> 
> ### 📚 Documentation
> 
> - **Turkish translation** of the documentation, with a build step and `zensical` configuration to match ([#1401](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1401), [#1402](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1402), [#1404](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1404)).
> - Multilingual subpath links now resolve correctly ([#1403](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1403)).
> - Backend documentation lists MPS alongside CUDA ([#1410](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1410)).
> 
> ### 🧹 Maintenance & CI
> 
> - Device selection and postprocessing backend resolution are covered by tests ([#1409](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1409)).
> - Bumped `astral-sh/setup-uv` 8.3.2 → 9.0.0 ([#1399](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1399)), `actions/setup-python` 6.3.0 → 7.0.0 ([#1400](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1400)) and `actions/checkout` 7.0.0 -> 7.0.1 ([#1398](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1398)).
> - Relaxed the `twine` requirement to `>=5.1.1,<8.0.0` ([#1406](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1406)).
> 
> ### ⚡ Performance
> 
> NMS with the `IOU` metric, best of 5 runs, on an Apple M2 Pro:
> 
> | boxes | numpy | numba | torchvision (MPS) |
> | ----: | ----: | ----: | ----------------: |
> | 100 | 0.14 ms | 0.02 ms | 1.44 ms |
> | 500 | 1.53 ms | 0.36 ms | 1.42 ms |
> | 1000 | 5.46 ms | 1.40 ms | 1.45 ms |
> | 5000 | 81.37 ms | 34.16 ms | 4.05 ms |
> | 20000 | 1237.70 ms | 462.56 ms | 11.75 ms |
> 
> Below roughly 500 boxes `numba` stays ahead, but the difference there is about a milliseconds.
> 
> **Full Changelog**:
> <https://github.com/obss/sahi/compare/0.12.2...0.12.3>

> A patch release that fixes the `sahi` command line interface, which was broken on any installation that did not already have `matplotlib` present.
> 
> ### 🐛 Fixes
>

Because the import is eager, every `sahi` command failed on a clean install, including ones unrelated to plotting such as `sahi version`:

>       import matplotlib
>   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'matplotlib'
>   ```

#### 4. 0.12.7 / 0.12.7

item_id: obss/sahi::release::396252324
Data: 2026-09-25T02:55:26Z
URL: https://github.com/obss/sahi/releases/tag/0.12.7

Release notes (texto original):

> A patch release that adds an optional ultrafast-pycocotools backend to COCO evaluation, fixes four crashes and miscounts in COCO and video utilities, speeds up postprocessing and sliced prediction, and raises the torch floor to 2.13.0 on Python 3.10 and newer.
> 
> ## ✨ Features
> 
> - **`sahi coco evaluate` can run on ultrafast-pycocotools** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1452). Install it with `pip install "sahi[ultrafast]"` and pass `--backend ultrafast` on the CLI or `backend="ultrafast"` to `sahi.scripts.coco_evaluation.evaluate`. pycocotools stays the default, and the tests check that both backends return the same bbox and segm results (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1457).
> 
> ## 🐛 Fixes
> 
> - **COCO evaluation accepts a list of IoU thresholds** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1452). Passing `iou_thrs` as a list stopped in the summary step with a NumPy "nonzero on 0d arrays" error. Thresholds are now always stored as an array.
> - **Video prediction counts skipped frames correctly** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1449). The progress bar total only accounted for `frame_skip_interval` while a visual was shown, and the exported video used `fps / frame_skip_interval` instead of `fps / (frame_skip_interval + 1)`, so it played back faster than the source.
> - **`remove_invalid_coco_results` skips bboxes that do not have four values** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1455) instead of raising `IndexError`.
> - **`get_coco_segmentation_from_obb_points` returns an empty list for empty input** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1456) instead of raising `IndexError`.
> 
> ## ⚡ Performance
> 
> - **NMS and greedy NMM choose the stored-pair path again when boxes are spread out** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1443). Since `0.12.5` they always read rows from the STRtree on demand, which is slower than a stored pair list when boxes are spread out. They now pick the path by crowding the same way NMM does, and the output is unchanged.
> - **Streaming postprocessing drops boxes it has finished with** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1426). Settled boxes are removed from later STRtree queries, so crowded inputs query a tree that shrinks as the loop runs.
> - **Sliced prediction decodes the source image once** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1445). `get_sliced_prediction` used to decode the file four times. It now reuses the decode that slicing already holds.
> - **`slice_image` uses less peak memory** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1421). Local files decode straight to a NumPy array with OpenCV instead of going through Pillow, and `read_image_size` reads the size from the file header without decoding the image. 16-bit files and anything else OpenCV declines use the Pillow path as before.
> 
> ## 📦 Build
> 
> - **The torch floor is 2.13.0 on Python 3.10 and newer** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1440), 2.8.0 on Python 3.9 and 2.4.1 on Python 3.8, the newest release each of them still has wheels for.
> - **Development installs pick the torch build that matches the machine** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1446), CUDA or CPU, instead of always CPU.
> - **CI tests Python 3.13 and 3.14** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1433).
> 
> ## 📚 Documentation
> 
> - **Documented commands, defaults and examples match the code** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1427, https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1452). This includes the `coco evaluate` options, which now list `--type segm`, `--max_detections` and `--backend`.
> - **The quick start ends in a prediction, pages link to the next page, and API parameters are shown as tables** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1428, https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1429).
> - **The docs point at the site they are published on and serve their markdown** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1431), and demo links resolve outside GitHub (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1435).
> - **A new notebook measures batched sliced inference speed** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1447) on the machine it runs on and checks that batching does not change the detections.
> - **The README install example uses torch 2.13.0 on CUDA 13.0.**
> - **General cleanups** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1430, https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1436, https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1441, https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1442, https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1444): notebook outputs are stripped, autoref warnings and dead links are fixed, and punctuation is consistent.
> 
> **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/obss/sahi/compare/0.12.6...0.12.7

#### 5. 0.12.8 / 0.12.8

item_id: obss/sahi::release::398683837
Data: 2026-09-30T16:52:52Z
URL: https://github.com/obss/sahi/releases/tag/0.12.8

Release notes (texto original):

> 
> A patch release that adds LibreYOLO as a detection backend, fixes seven bugs in COCO category remapping, slicing, mask conversion and box merging, and builds boolean masks faster.
> 
> ### ✨ Features
> 
> - **LibreYOLO detection backend** ([#1425](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1425)). Install it with `pip install libreyolo` and load MIT-licensed LibreYOLO models with `model_type="libreyolo"`. It reuses the Ultralytics wrapper, and the models guide covers it in every language ([#1467](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1467)).
> 
> ### 🐛 Fixes
> 
> - **Sliced annotations that touch the slice border are kept** ([#1462](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1462)). When a polygon edge lay exactly on a slice border, the intersection came back as a mix of polygons and lines and the annotation was dropped with area 0. The polygon parts are now kept.
> - **NMM merges boxes whose overlap equals the match threshold** ([#1464](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1464)). These boxes were claimed by the keeper but never merged, so they disappeared from the output and the keeper box did not grow.
> - **`get_bool_mask_from_coco_segmentation` returns a boolean array** ([#1463](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1463)). It returned the float64 canvas, so `Mask.bool_mask` could not be used to index an image.
> - **Category remapping maps each id once** ([#1465](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1465)). With `remapping_dict={0: 1, 1: 2}` both categories ended up with id 2 and loading failed with `KeyError`.
> - **Subsampled, upsampled, area filtered and bbox clipped Coco objects keep their categories** ([#1466](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1466)). They applied `remapping_dict` a second time to ids that were already remapped, which also affected `clip_bboxes_to_img_dims=True`.
> - **Class-aware NMM and greedy NMM accept an image with no detections** ([#1470](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1470)) instead of raising `AttributeError`.
> - **`fix_shift_amount_list` and `fix_full_shape_list` accept empty lists** ([#1459](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1459)) instead of raising `IndexError`.
> 
> ### ⚡ Performance
> 
> - **Boolean masks from COCO polygons build about 8x faster** ([#1463](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1463)). The mask is drawn on a uint8 canvas instead of float64, which takes a 1080p mask from 1.03 ms to 0.13 ms on an Intel Core i7-13850HX and uses 8x less memory.
> 
> ### 📚 Documentation
> 
> - **The Chinese and Turkish docs match the English docs again** ([#1461](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1461)).
> - **The RT-DETR guide uses the Ultralytics weights the backend loads** ([#1467](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1467)), and the `coco slice` CLI docs no longer list a `--backend` option it does not have ([#1460](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1460)).

#### 1. v1.1.0 / v1.1.0

item_id: pionxzh/wakaru::release::323946981
Data: 2026-05-17T19:04:06Z

Release notes (texto original):

> ## wakaru v1.1.0
> 
> **Async/generator recovery, esbuild unpacking, better correctness.**
> 
> ### Highlights
> 
> - **Babel async & generators** — `regeneratorRuntime` and `_asyncToGenerator` are restored back to native `async/await` and `function*`
> - **esbuild unpacking** — scope-hoisted esbuild bundles are split into proper ES modules
> - **Babel 7.24+ classes** — `_callSuper` and single-arg `_createClass` recovered correctly
> - **Diagnostics** — opt-in structured warnings and TDZ violation reporting
> - **Sentry component names** — recovered from `data-sentry-component` attributes
> - **25 correctness fixes** — var/const scoping, duplicate imports, lexical `this`, unresolved marks, and more
> - **Fat LTO builds** — smaller and faster binaries
> - **Linux ARM64** — native release binaries
> 
> **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/compare/v1.0.0...v1.1.0
> 
> **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/compare/v1.0.0...v1.1.0

- 043997d0bc58758c4cc81f46bbff038056b58c2e — https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/043997d0bc58758c4cc81f46bbff038056b58c2e
> feat(core): synthesize import/export for esbuild scope-hoisted modules
> 
> The esbuild scope-hoisted module extractor correctly identified module
> boundaries via the `var NS = {}; __export(NS, {...})` pattern but
> emitted raw code without import/export statements.  Cross-module
> references (which the bundler resolved via direct bindings in the
> shared scope) were left as dangling free variables.
> 
> Restructure `extract_scope_hoisted_modules` into a two-pass approach:
> 
> Pass 1 — collect per-module metadata: declared bindings, referenced
> bindings, and exported atoms from the __export registration call.
> 
> Pass 2 — emit each module with synthesized ES imports for cross-module
> references and exports promoted from the __export binding map.
> 
> Additional fixes folded in:
> 
> - Case-insensitive filename dedup via a shared `dedup_filename` probe
>   loop (try `{base}.js`, `{base}_2.js`, …) matching the CLI's
>   `deduplicate_path` logic.  Factory filenames are deduped first, then
>   seeded into the same set so scope-hoisted names never collide.
> 
> - Consumed namespace decls and __export calls are restored into the
>   entry when the entry still references the namespace binding (e.g.
>   `export { math_exports as math }`), with imports for the individual
>   bindings so the __export getters resolve correctly.
> 
> - Effective export sets are expanded beyond T8-registered public API to
>   include any declared binding referenced from another module or the
>   entry, since the bundler's scope hoisting lets private helpers be
>   called across boundaries.
> 
> On the claude-code fixture: 340 scope-hoisted modules gain exports,
> 333 gain imports, and 0 import targets point at missing files.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
- 06785fd160052e87b2e6fb482f8b296d208f159c — https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/06785fd160052e87b2e6fb482f8b296d208f159c
> fix(core): bound synthetic name search
- 06fcbdd4276e280454f89734d1825d59713ab9e2 — https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/06fcbdd4276e280454f89734d1825d59713ab9e2
> fix(unpack): merge esbuild init factories into their target module
> 
> When a factory module (lazy init wrapped in `y(...)`) only assigns to
> bindings belonging to a single scope-hoisted module, merge its body
> into that module instead of emitting a separate file with invalid ESM
> (imports are read-only, so `import {x} ...; x = ...` would fail).
> 
> Also synthesizes imports for cross-module reads in merged bodies,
> detects UpdateExpr (count++) as writes, and skips bindings the target
> module already imports to avoid duplicate declarations.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
- 075e06e2545e1a976246a4a8ba24d77689237ae7 — https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/075e06e2545e1a976246a4a8ba24d77689237ae7
> fix(core): avoid invalid JSX attr renames
- 087f9b852dcb5ad2b4b2712d618d0973c3074d40 — https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/087f9b852dcb5ad2b4b2712d618d0973c3074d40
> feat: hoist embedded require() calls in un_esm pre-pass
> 
> Add a pre-pass to un_esm that hoists require() calls out of complex
> expressions (sequence expressions, inline conditional interops) into
> standalone statements that the existing classification logic can
> convert to ES imports.
> 
> Handles three patterns:
> - export default (i = require("./a"), require("./b"), expr)
>   → import i from "./a"; import "./b"; export default expr;
> - const a = (i = require("./x")) && i.__esModule ? i : {default: i}
>   → import i from "./x"; const a = i;
> - export default require("./f")(args)
>   → import _default from "./f"; export default _default(args);
> 
> Reduces remaining require() calls in real-world-1 from 38 to 4.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

- 26879c31ffaef764170d0bc00026759b0a028757 — https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/26879c31ffaef764170d0bc00026759b0a028757
> fix(core): synthesize imports in esbuild factory modules for scope-hoisted refs
> 
> Factory modules extracted by the esbuild unpacker had no import/export
> links for cross-module references. When a factory's body referenced a
> binding declared in a scope-hoisted module, that reference was invisible
> to the scope-hoisted extraction because factory bodies were already
> removed from the entry items. This caused scope-hoisted modules to not
> export private helpers that factories need, leaving dangling free
> variables that DCE would then incorrectly remove.
> 
> Restructure the esbuild unpack flow:
> - Phase 3 now defers factory emission and collects referenced bindings
>   from the resolved AST
> - Phase 5 accepts factory refs, expands scope-hoisted exports, and
>   returns a binding→filename map
> - New Phase 6 emits factories with synthesized import statements
> - Factory-referenced namespace bindings map to entry.js with synthesized
>   exports when the entry doesn't already export them
> - Relative import paths are computed correctly for subdirectory factories
> - Private helpers only referenced by factories are absorbed into the
>   last scope-hoisted module via expanded find_last_module_end
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

> refactor(core): extract shared decl_utils module to deduplicate pattern-walking
> 
> Five files had near-identical collect_decl_*/collect_pat_* functions for
> gathering binding names from declarations and patterns. Consolidate them
> into a single decl_utils module that delegates to SWC's find_pat_ids,
> which correctly handles all destructuring forms and skips expressions.
>

> feat(core): handle Babel 7.24+ _callSuper and 1-arg _createClass in un_es6_class
> 
> The IIFE class pattern with `return _createClass(Foo)` (1 arg, no methods)
> was not recognized because try_parse_create_class required >= 2 args.
> Additionally, `_callSuper(this, Foo, arguments)` (Babel 7.24+ super helper)
> had no rewriting support anywhere in the codebase.
> 
> Changes:
> - Allow 1-arg _createClass in return statements (seals prototype, no methods)
> - Add body-shape detection for _callSuper to babel_helper_utils (Inherits and
>   CallSuper variants in BabelHelperKind)
> - Detect by: 2-3 params, <=3 stmts, 3-arg Reflect.construct + param2.apply(param1)
> - Add CallSuperRewriter to transform safe call sites to super(...)
> - Bail class conversion entirely when third arg is unsafe (not `arguments`
>   or array literal) to avoid dangling inner-binding references
> - Remove orphaned _inherits and _callSuper fn declarations after conversion
> - Move is_inherits_fn to babel_helper_utils (drops unresolved_mark, uses
>   simple Object name check consistent with existing patterns)
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

> refactor(core): extract expr_utils, enforce unresolved_mark, adopt ExprFactory
> 
> Consolidates duplicate exprs_structurally_equal / is_undefined helpers
> into a shared expr_utils module. Threads unresolved_mark through
> UnArgumentSpread, UnNullishCoalescing, UnOptionalChaining, and RemoveVoid
> so that `undefined` identifiers are only matched when they refer to the
> true global. Also adopts ExprFactory::make_bin() in exponent,
> un_conditionals, un_template_literal, and un_nullish_coalescing.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

> refactor(core): disable DCE by default in decompile pipeline
> 
> DeadImports/DeadDecls no longer run in the default pipeline.
> A decompiler should preserve the original code faithfully — if a
> helper remains after transformation, that is a rule bug to fix,
> not something to silently clean up.
> 
> Callers that explicitly need DCE can still opt in via
> dead_code_elimination: true. The dead_decls and dead_imports test
> suites now do this.
> 
> Updated test expectations: helper leftovers that DCE was silently
> removing now appear in output. Tests assert rule-specific behavior
> rather than relying on downstream cleanup.
>

> fix(core): add ImportDedup to standard pipeline to merge duplicate imports
> 
> ImportDedup previously only ran in the sourcemap-enhanced path. Scope-hoisted
> bundles produce multiple import statements for the same specifier from the same
> module (e.g. `import { randomUUID as x } from "crypto"` repeated 3 times).
> Without dedup, UnImportRename generates unnecessary suffixed names (randomUUID_1,
> randomUUID_2). Also adds a merge pass that consolidates separate imports from the
> same source into a single statement.

> fix(core): prevent var→let/const conversion when var hoisting is relied upon
> 
> The var_decl_to_let_const rule was converting vars to let/const without
> checking if the code relied on var hoisting (reference before declaration).
> This caused TDZ violations in the output for patterns like:

> fix(core): prevent smart_rename→arguments/eval and un_prototype_class TDZ
> 
> Two fixes for remaining stderr warnings:
> 
> 1. smart_rename: add "arguments" and "eval" to the reserved keyword
>    blacklist. These cannot be used as binding names in strict mode
>    (ES modules are always strict), so renaming a variable to either
>    name produces a parse error.
> 
> 2. un_prototype_class: bail out when the function name is referenced
>    before its declaration. Function declarations are hoisted but class
>    declarations are not, so converting `function Foo(){}` to `class Foo{}`
>    when `module.exports = Foo` appears above creates a TDZ violation.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
- f938306d1fd711c66e66dae05925d0eeb5a36abc — https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/f938306d1fd711c66e66dae05925d0eeb5a36abc
> fix(core): fix var→const regression and resolve chained export renames
> 
> VarDeclToLetConst was treating `export { x }` specifiers as
> use-before-declaration references, forcing every exported var to stay
> as `var` when exports appeared before declarations (common in
> UnEsm-generated output). `export { x }` is a live binding that doesn't
> evaluate `x` at the statement position — skip it in the analysis.
> 
> UnExportRename was unable to rename `export { i as x }` when `x` was
> already a local binding, even if `x` itself was being exported away
> (`export { x as f }`). Pre-compute a "freed names" set by walking all
> rename chains from export specifiers; names along chains that terminate
> at a free slot are marked as freed and allowed as rename targets.
> 
> The freed-names computation mirrors planner eligibility: edges are
> rejected for shorter target names, already-exported bindings, shadowing
> conflicts, and contested targets (multiple edges claiming the same
> exported name). Cycles are detected and excluded.
> 
> Also fixes clippy lints (items_after_test_module, len_zero,
> too_many_arguments) and a typo in babel_helper_utils.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

> fix(core): preserve function expression statements in SimplifySequence
> 
> The rule incorrectly removed standalone function expressions (e.g.

>

- fea73a796d3b5466e9be998b982dec701bac9a55 — https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/fea73a796d3b5466e9be998b982dec701bac9a55
> fix(core): relocate pre-references after class in un_prototype_class
> 
> Instead of bailing out when a function is referenced before its
> declaration (which would lose the class transform entirely), relocate
> those referencing statements to just after the emitted class declaration.
> 
> Before: `module.exports = Foo; function Foo(){} Foo.prototype.m = ...`
> After:  `class Foo { ... } module.exports = Foo;`
> 
> This preserves readability (the class transform still applies) while
> avoiding TDZ violations (the reference now comes after the class decl).
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

#### 2. v1.7.0 / v1.7.0

item_id: pionxzh/wakaru::release::352786359
Data: 2026-07-12T15:50:42Z
URL: https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/releases/tag/v1.7.0

Release notes (texto original):

> The headline of this release is **experimental Vue 3 SFC recovery** — wakaru can now reconstruct `.vue`-style single-file components from compiled render modules. It's backed by a big wave of correctness fixes that make the everyday decompile path safer, plus new execution-equivalence testing that verifies recovered code actually *runs* the same as the original.
> 
> ## ✨ Experimental: Vue 3 SFC recovery (`--vue-sfc`)
> 
> ```bash
> wakaru bundle.js --unpack --vue-sfc -o out/
> ```
> 
> wakaru can now recover template-shaped SFC artifacts from compiled Vue 3 render code across **webpack, Vite, and SystemJS** outputs. It reconstructs templates, components and slots, directives (`v-model`, `v-for`, `v-html`, `v-memo`, event handlers with modifiers), conditional branches, and setup-block bindings — and there's a live Vue SFC preview in the playground now too.
> 
> This is experimental and there are still gaps, but it already handles a wide range of real-world compiler output.
> 
> ## 🚀 New recovery
> 
> - **Nullish assignment** (`??=`) recovery.
> - Expanded AMD and repro-edge recovery.
> 
> ## 🛡️ Correctness & semantics
> 
> A large set of fixes to guarantee decompiled output preserves the original program's behavior:
> 
> - **`const` vs `let`** — no longer emits `const` for bindings that are later reassigned (avoids runtime `TypeError`s): mutated IIFE args/loop targets, wrapped binding writes, and mutable destructuring are all preserved as mutable.
> - **Object rest & destructuring** — correct recovery of computed object-rest keys, computed parameter destructuring, and adjacent-pick requirements; preserves rest semantics.
> - **IIFE & eval** — preserves IIFE and method shapes around `eval` and duplicate parameters; tighter arrow eval scope guards.
> - **esbuild / TS helpers** — tightened mangled spread matching, gated object-alias detection, and cleanup of consumed TS helpers.
> - **DCE safety** — preserves TDZ reads, deferred lexical reads, observable no-op reads, and import-link checks during transform-only DCE.
> - **Misc** — signed numeric `switch` cases.
> 
> ## 🧪 Testing & CI
> 
> - **Execution-equivalence checks** added to the reproduction matrices (template, enum, and array matrices) — recovered code is now verified to run equivalently, not just look right.
> - Hardened Test262 correctness harness: baseline identity preflight, metadata semantics, candidate freshness, and decompile-timeout failures.
> 
> **Full changelog:** https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/compare/v1.6.0...v1.7.0

- 0278ce4feba74cc31aea9da2d1ebd4f35d757c94 — https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/0278ce4feba74cc31aea9da2d1ebd4f35d757c94

- 031e53661221d0346b10f85300e188b946f15e14 — https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/031e53661221d0346b10f85300e188b946f15e14
> refactor(vue): ctxt-gate cleaned-AST collectors, delete ScopeStack (Phase 2b, #196)
> 
> The last two scope-tracked collectors run on cleaned setup ASTs, so they could
> not be ctxt-gated until Phase 3 made the cleaners context-preserving. Now they are:
> 
> - Thread the resolver's unresolved context onto VueRecoveryContext
>   (unresolved_ctxt) and stamp it in ContextMemberCleaner's collapse of
>   _ctx.foo/$props.foo -> foo, so cleaned statements no longer carry
>   Default/empty contexts that would collide.
> - IdentRefCollector / ScriptImportRefCollector drop ScopeStack. A one-shot
>   DeclaredBindingIdents pre-pass collects the (name, ctxt) of every binding
>   *declared* in the walked subtree (var/param/arrow/catch/fn/class, excluding
>   assignment targets); a reference is free iff its (name, ctxt) is not declared.
>   Keying on the pair — not ctxt alone — is required because resolver() assigns
>   one context per scope, so sibling bindings share a context.
> - Delete context/scope.rs (ScopeStack + the visit_assign_expr_refs family). The
>   assignment-target-as-declaration fix is now free: a target and its declaration
>   share one binding identity.
> 
> Behavior-preserving: full core suite green (2686). Adds two discriminating
> white-box tests: sibling-scope free references are still reported (guards the
> per-scope-context trap), and shadowing locals are excluded.
> 
> Completes the ScopeStack removal (Phase 2). imports.rs StrongValueMemberCollector
> keeps its own shadow stack (not ScopeStack) and is a separate follow-up.

> fix(core): inline single-read let temp aliases
> 
> SmartInline pass 1 only accepted const declarations, but minifier
> output declares temps with let and VarDeclToLetConst never narrows an
> existing let, so a merged destructuring kept its source alias
> (let o = app_info; let { ... } = o). A let with one read and no writes
> inlines as safely as a const; writes (plain, compound, destructuring,
> update, for-in/of heads) now disqualify the candidate explicitly since
> a write target would otherwise count as the single use. Bindings named
> after stable builtins stay excluded so the builtin-alias passes keep
> their shapes.

> refactor(vue): ctxt-gate pristine-AST member collectors (Phase 2a, #196)
> 
> The member-base ref collectors run only on the pristine, resolver-processed
> render/setup AST, so shadow safety can come from SyntaxContext identity
> instead of a hand-rolled ScopeStack.
> 
> - ValueMemberIdentRefCollector, NonValueMemberRefCollector, and
>   RenderTemplateRefCollector drop ScopeStack and the fn/arrow/var/binding
>   scope bookkeeping. The member collectors emit (name, ctxt); the render
>   collector matches candidate sets by (name, ctxt) and keeps a name output
>   (its refs feed name-based matching downstream).
> - Candidate sets (tuple/object/unref) become (name, ctxt) via a new
>   collect_pat_binding_idents helper.
> - collect_setup_context consumers match against the setup declaration's
>   (binding.id.sym, binding.id.ctxt); should_emit_ref_script_setup_expr
>   takes &Ident. A nested local reusing a setup binding's minified name now
>   falls out via context mismatch rather than a shadow frame.
> 
> ScopeStack survives for now: IdentRefCollector / ScriptImportRefCollector
> run on cleaned ASTs (reset ctxt) and cannot be ctxt-gated until Phase 3.
> 
> Behavior-preserving: full core suite green (2684, +1). Adds an adversarial
> test where a nested arrow param reuses a setup ref's name.

> fix(vue): mark-gate helper recognition on import SyntaxContext (Phase 1, #196)
> 
> Record the resolved SyntaxContext of every top-level import binding
> (import_local_ctxts) and require helper/candidate references to match it.
> An inner-scope local that reuses a helper's (often minified) import name
> now resolves to a different context and is no longer misrecognized as a
> Vue call.
> 
> Gated: HelperInference candidate/known-helper lookups, helper_name_from_expr,
> namespace_helper_name, is_fragment_tag, and the standalone vue_helper_candidate
> callee checks used by ref/computed/slot classification. Fixed-vocabulary
> matches (.value, $event, Fragment fallback) and structurally-inferred helper
> aliases stay name-based.
> 
> Replaces Phase 0's stored-but-unused unresolved_mark field with the
> import_local_ctxts map that is actually consumed here.
> 
> Behavior-preserving: full core suite green; adds a control/shadow test pair
> proving the shadowed helper is no longer recovered.

> 
> The doc duplicated what pipeline.rs already encodes (order, stages,
> requires-edges, per-rule boilerplate rows) and had drifted: 67 entries
> vs ~97 registry descriptors, plus scaffolding framed around fact-system

> for every cell even when the honest answer was 'nothing notable', and
> those filler cells went stale invisibly.
> 
> Now the registry owns *what* (declared explicitly at the top) and the
> doc owns *why*: confirmed dependency chains with evidence, per-rule
> notes only where there is a non-obvious constraint or level-gating
> rationale, the distilled 2026-04 experiment log with its superseded
> conclusions marked, and open ideas. 1436 -> 325 lines.
> 
> Verified against the current registry: UnConditionals2 is still the
> final rule, SimplifySequence still first.

> syntax rejects as an early error.

> refactor(vue): replace import/decl alias renamers with BindingRenamer (Phase 3, #196)
> 
> Delete the hand-rolled ImportAliasRenamer and rename_top_level_decl_bindings
> (plus their pattern-rename helpers) in favor of rename_utils::BindingRenamer,
> per CLAUDE.md ("never rename by sym alone"). BindingRenamer is a functional
> superset -- it rewrites the declaration, every resolved reference, import/export
> specifiers, and expands object/pattern shorthand -- keyed on (sym, SyntaxContext)
> instead of hand-rolled scope frames.
> 
> Broadens Phase 1's import-context map to all top-level bindings
> (top_level_binding_ctxts: imports + var/fn/class decls) and adds binding_renames()
> to turn the name-keyed alias maps into SyntaxContext-keyed BindingRenames.
> 
> Confirms the cloned/cleaned setup statements retain resolver contexts (the
> renames still apply -- full core suite green), which de-risks the remaining
> setup-scope renamers.
> 
> The setup-scope renamers (SetupPropsRefRewriter, SetupAliasCleaner) rename
> setup-param/alias bindings and carry their own shadow_depths tracking; they need
> setup-scope context recording shared with the collector rewrite, so they move to
> the combined Phase 2+4 effort rather than here.

> fix(core): reject redeclared or mutated var builtin aliases
> 
> Candidate collection now drops any binding declared by more than one
> single-declarator var: the definition matcher and declarator removal both
> match by key alone, so a redeclaration (e.g. a polyfill assignment) was
> skipped during usage counting and deleted along with the alias, losing its
> side effects. The usage counter also counts update expressions and delete
> on an alias binding as blocked writes instead of replaceable reads; via
> the shared const-only path this also stops SmartInline from rewriting
> mutated const aliases.

> feat(core,cli): per-module provenance byte ranges from unpackers
> 
> Every UnpackedModule now records the byte ranges in the original input it
> was extracted from (source_ranges) and which input file those refer to
> (source_input, filled by the driver for multi-source unpacks):
> 
> - esbuild factories: the factory var declarator span
> - esbuild/Bun scope-hoisted modules: coalesced body item spans
> - webpack4/5: factory function / body statement spans
> - browserify: module array entry span
> - systemjs: System.register call span
> - cycle premerge: union of member ranges (same-input cycles only)
> - whole-input fallbacks: (0, len)
> 
> UnpackOutput gains a provenance field, and the CLI gains --provenance,
> which writes provenance.json ({module file -> {input, ranges}}) next to
> the unpacked modules, using final on-disk names after CLI-side dedup.
> 
> This lets source-map-based tooling map any unpacked module back to exact
> positions in the original bundle for any bundler format: package-origin
> ground truth, license/vuln auditing, bundle diffing, and jumping from a
> decompiled module to the minified original.

> refactor(vue): setup alias rewriting via BindingRenamer (Phase 3.1, #196)
> 
> SetupAliasCleaner was a bespoke name-matching + shadow_depths renamer, exactly
> what CLAUDE.md bans. Replace it with rename_utils::BindingRenamer keyed on each
> alias source's recorded (name, ctxt):
> 
> - Record each alias source's SyntaxContext in VueBindingTable.alias_ctxts, at
>   both insert sites (the const-alias in collect_setup_context and the
>   template-ref aliases from TemplateRefAliasCollector, which now captures the
>   ref binding's ctxt).
> - setup_alias_renames builds the (name, ctxt) -> new BindingRename list, falling
>   back to top-level binding contexts.
> - print_expr / clean_setup_stmt call rename_bindings instead of SetupAliasCleaner.
> - Delete SetupAliasCleaner + its shadow_depths machinery + VueBindingTable::sorted_aliases.
> 
> BindingRenamer preserves ctxt and expands Prop::Shorthand, so this is
> behavior-preserving (full core suite green, 2684) and moves alias rewriting onto
> ctxt identity — a step toward ctxt-consistent cleaned ASTs for Phase 2b. Adds a
> setup_alias_renames unit test; removes the SetupAliasCleaner test it replaces.
