> refactor(vue): setup props-ref rewriting via BindingRenamer (Phase 3.2, #196)
> 
> SetupPropsRefRewriter was the second bespoke sym-matching + shadow_depths renamer
> banned by CLAUDE.md. Replace it with rename_utils::BindingRenamer keyed on each
> props source's recorded (name, ctxt):
> 
> - Record the setup props parameter's ctxt (setup_props_context_ctxt, via new
>   setup_props_param_ctxt) and each props alias ctxt (setup_props_alias_ctxts).
> - setup_props_renames maps those sources -> the emitted props binding; the
>   render_local_declaration_with_aliases path calls rename_bindings instead of
>   rewrite_setup_props_refs.
> - Delete SetupPropsRefRewriter + its shadow_depths + pat_binds_atom/decl_binds_atom.
> 
> Behavior-preserving (full core suite green, 2684); the props refs it rewrites are
> bare idents left pristine by the cleaner chain, so ctxt matching is exact. Adds a
> setup_props_renames unit test; removes the SetupPropsRefRewriter test it replaces.
> 
> With Phase 3.1, both setup-scope renamer violations are cleared. The remaining
> cleaner, ContextMemberCleaner, is a member->ident collapse (not a rename); making
> its output ctxt-consistent is folded into Phase 2b, where unresolved_mark is
> threaded onto the context and the cleaned-AST collectors consume it.

> fix(core): tighten esbuild spread matching and scope alias cleanup
> 
> Two review findings against the mangled esbuild machinery:
> 
> Values-family aliases alone are not proof of esbuild output: a module can
> carry the alias preamble and still define a user descriptor-copy utility
> of the exact __spreadProps shape, which object spread would rewrite while
> dropping accessor semantics. spread_props_expr_matches — the single choke
> point for the decl and inline matching paths — now demands a matched
> __defNormalProp helper, an actual esbuild artifact that survives
> minification because the values helper body calls it.
> 
> The unused-alias sweeps in UnObjectSpread/UnObjectRest collected every
> unused Object alias in the module and ran whenever any spread/rest helper
> fired, so recovering an unrelated Babel helper deleted stray aliases that
> were never part of an esbuild preamble. Both sweeps are now gated on
> esbuild-specific evidence (matched mangled helpers, __defNormalProp, or
> inline esbuild spread calls).
> 
> The two guards interlock: the descriptor-copy regression test needs the
> cleanup gate too, so they land together.

#### 3. v1.9.0 / v1.9.0

item_id: pionxzh/wakaru::release::367357077
Data: 2026-08-09T02:17:39Z
URL: https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/releases/tag/v1.9.0

Release notes (texto original):

> This release has two headliners: **Bun single-file executable extraction** — point wakaru at a `bun build --compile` binary and it unpacks the JavaScript inside — and **Closure Compiler output recovery**. Previous releases only understood Closure's ModuleManager bundle format; wakaru now also recovers the code patterns Closure Compiler itself emits. Alongside them: webpack 5 detection handles bundles with no IIFE wrapper and array-form module tables, and the public Rust API on crates.io was redesigned.
> 
> ## 🧊 Bun single-file executables
> 
> ```bash
> wakaru ./compiled-app --unpack -o out/          # decompile the embedded JS
> wakaru bun extract ./compiled-app -o extracted/ # dump every embedded file
> ```
> 
> - `--unpack` accepts a Bun single-file executable (`bun build --compile` output — PE, Mach-O, or ELF): wakaru validates Bun's embedded module graph, selects the JS/JSX/TS/TSX entries, and sends them through the same unpack pipeline as ordinary bundles.
> - `wakaru bun extract` writes **every** embedded file record — JavaScript, assets, binaries — under `extracted/files/`, with a `manifest.json` mapping original Bun paths to safe output paths. Extraction only writes files; it never executes or trusts their contents.
> - Both the Bun 1.3.3–1.3.8 and the 1.3.9+ container record layouts are supported, and extraction memory usage was cut by reducing AST retention during factory extraction.
> 
> ## 📦 Webpack detection, expanded
> 
> - **Bundles without an IIFE wrapper** — modern webpack 5 output that inlines the runtime at top level is now detected and split, including extraction of the inline startup section as a proper entry module and entries with no `exports` anchor.
> - **Array-form module containers** (`webpack_modules` as an array) are now unpacked (#200), and minified entry loaders survive splitting.
> - HMR-style factory indirection, eager `import()` startups, Terser-merged statement sequences, and entry-owned runtime mutations are all handled; webpack 4 gains concat-offset and parenthesized-factory recovery.
> - New `--unpack=inspect` profile keeps finer module boundaries for static inspection of scope-hoisted output.
> - Multi-input unpacks now keep **stable public module paths**: sibling imports resolve to the right file instead of depending on argument order, and imports are rewritten after output-filename dedup.
> - A new emitted-module graph validator checks every unpack result for dangling imports and unparseable output as part of diagnostics.
> 
> ## 🚀 New recovery
> 
> - **Closure Compiler patterns** — wakaru now recovers `for...of` loops from Closure's `$jscomp.makeIterator` lowering and ES6 classes from its prototype-based class output, gated on the Closure runtime bootstrap so ordinary code is untouched. Recovery is verified by *executing* the recovered classes against the originals across multiple Closure Compiler versions.
> - Object literals are rebuilt from Babel's loose-mode computed-property assignments.
> - Optional chains rooted at parameters are recovered.
> - Inline export declarations from scope-hoisted bundles are adopted directly.
> 
> ## 🛡️ Correctness & semantics
> 
> - **Class recovery got a safety pass**: functions whose identity or construction behavior matters — `new.target` users, `Reflect.construct` newTargets, constructor-sensitive values flowing through aliases, prototypes with dynamic key order, reused `var` class bindings, default-exported constructors relying on hoisting, evaluated export initializers, duplicate sloppy-mode params — are now preserved instead of converted.
> - **JSX survives renaming**: export renames can no longer lowercase a component tag into a DOM element, capitalized aliases survive import renaming, and `createElement` calls in optional-call, paren-wrapped, callee, and member-object positions are guarded.
> - Reserved words in decomposed imports and export locals are aliased instead of emitted verbatim; regenerator decoding rolls back cleanly on unsupported shapes; sloppy-mode output is verified as script, not module.
> 
> ## 🦀 Public Rust API, redesigned
> 
> The `wakaru` crate now exposes a compiler-style service: `decompile(Source, DecompileOptions)` and `unpack(Vec<Source>, UnpackOptions)` (plus incremental `UnpackJob`), with structured diagnostics, provenance, and detection reports instead of warning strings — and `bun` / `debug` namespaces for standalone extraction and rule tracing. `wakaru-core` is published in lockstep as an implementation detail; the façade is the supported surface (`cargo doc -p wakaru` is the contract).
> 
> ## 📦 npm
> 
> `npx wakaru` now works — the bare `wakaru` package is an alias for `@wakaru/cli`, pinned to the same version.
> 
> ## ⚡ Performance
> 
> Scope-hoisted splitting indexes cross-cluster symbols instead of rescanning, and export-rename shadow analysis is batched.
>

> 
> The freed-name prepass modeled only specifier-vs-specifier competition.
> Pattern A (`export const X = z`) and Pattern C (exported getter
> namespace) plans also claim real bindings and target names; the planner
> honors those claims first and rejects the competing specifier edge, so
> the prepass over-predicted freed aliases and a later rename landed on a
> still-occupied name — a duplicate lexical declaration.

> resolved binding or target name competes with one. Order-dependent
> planner checks are not mirrored: over-approximating claims only shrinks

> fix(unpack): survive minifier sequences and wrapper-consumed anchors
> 
> Round-12 review findings:
> 
> - Terser merges consecutive expression statements, so the last runtime
>   definitions and the startup can share one comma sequence
>   (`r.d = ..., r.o = ..., loadEntry()`). The statement-granular boundary
>   marked the whole statement as runtime and silently dropped the
>   startup. The boundary statement's sequence is now split at the last
>   runtime assignment (by resolved require identity, on the probe) and
>   the tail joins the entry region. One tail shape is pure noise the
>   slicing previously hid: `require.r({})`, webpack's esModule marker
>   after the minifier inlined the unused exports anchor — the entry
>   normalizer now drops it as a semantic no-op.
> 
> - In a minified CommonJS/UMD library the export-helper anchor is also
>   the library value (`module.exports = t`, `return ..., t`). Renaming
>   it to a free `exports` and dropping its declaration produced entries
>   referencing an unbound `exports`. Helper evidence is now weighed
>   against the anchor's other uses (full depth — even a never-called
>   closure keeps the declaration alive): with wrapper plumbing present,
>   the region stays untouched and the pipeline recovers it faithfully
>   (`const t = {}; ... export default t`). The wrapper-return lowering
>   moved before this analysis so an inert `return t` does not count as
>   a wrapper use.
> 
> - Module ids are bounded to i32::MAX instead of u32::MAX: on wasm32
>   `usize` is 32 bits, so a u32-boundary `Array(n).concat` offset still
>   overflowed `id_offset + index` for the second element.

>   consumes for gated regions; object containers, accepted on shape

> fix(scope-hoist): keep bare top-level statements in the executable entry
> 
> A declarationless item (`state++;`, a top-level call) runs whenever the
> module holding it is first imported. The merge signals and the
> cross-item write union routinely pulled such statements into module
> clusters, so executable output ran them at import time — before entry
> statements that preceded them in source (silent value divergence for a
> bare writer; before 49a622e7 the same input failed loudly with a
> TypeError) — or never, when nothing imported the host chunk.
> 
> Move each bare statement into the entry, which emits items in original
> source order. A bare writer drags its whole write-group along (every
> writer must stay with the declaration it mutates — imported bindings
> are immutable), while pure readers stay behind and import the binding
> as a live view.
> 
> Returning bare statements to a singleton-contracted entry can close a
> false entry↔chunk cycle (the statements reference the chunks, the
> chunks reference the entry's singleton helpers), which the cyclic merge
> would collapse into an unsplit module. When that happens, retry with
> extract_executable_clusters, which assigns optional singletons to
> nearby module anchors instead of the entry. That relocation also means
> the esbuild dynamic-require helper can now be declared in any cluster,
> so its call-site restoration skips only the declaring item instead of
> the declaring cluster.
> 
> Two test fixtures encoded the old wrong shape and are reworked: the
> partial-var-export fixture consumed the b-group from a chunk nothing
> imported (its console.log never ran in the reference output), and the
> same held for the dynamic-require fixture's trailing statement. One
> private-suite reference output is regenerated for the same reason: its
> old entry never executed the app bootstrap.

> fix(core): make collapsed public-path claims yield to faithful ones
> 
> A derivation that discards leading path components — the `..` traversal
> strip, or an absolute input without a shared root falling back to its
> basename — produces a path another input may genuinely live at.
> Claiming was argument-order-first, so `wakaru --unpack ../x.js x.js
> consumer.js` let the collapsed `../x.js` take "x.js", displaced the
> faithful x.js to x_2.js, and consumer's "./x.js" silently linked to the
> parent directory's module.
> 
> public_path_for_input now reports whether the derivation collapsed, and
> plain inputs claim in two rounds: faithful paths first, collapsed ones
> after, regardless of argument order. Facade candidates are unaffected
> (collisions there are fatal in any order, and facades still claim
> before plain inputs).

> fix(scope-hoist): fold unreachable effectful clusters into the entry
> 
> Singleton repartitioning (and cluster extraction generally) assigns
> items by topological distance without requiring a reference
> relationship, so a cluster can end up that no module in the entry's
> import closure ever imports. Its code then never executes: a
> side-effectful initializer parked there — `const p = registerPolyfill()`
> — is silently dropped from the program. On the pathological-entry
> fixture, 127 of 193 emitted modules were unreachable from the entry.
> 
> After the bare-statement fold, compute cluster reachability from the
> entry over the reference graph and fold every unreachable cluster that
> carries startup effects into the entry, iterating to a fixpoint
> (folding a cluster makes its references reachable, which can spare
> other clusters). Pure unreachable clusters stay split: never running
> them is unobservable and they remain readable output. Effectfulness
> reuses the dead-module purity predicates, now shared from
> analysis::purity.
> 
> This also covers the older exclusive-consumer variant (9ef95b54) where
> a trailing effect statement was pulled into a chunk nothing imports —
> such chunks now either return to the entry (bare-statement fold) or are
> folded here.

> fix(unpack): address webpack5 detection review findings
> 
> Three issues from code review of the webpack5 array/entry work:
> 
> - Anchor misdetection (P1): the inline-startup extractor scanned forward
>   for any empty-object var decl and discarded the statements before it.
>   When a minifier drops the real `__webpack_exports__` anchor, an ordinary
>   entry local such as `const collector = {}` was picked instead, dropping
>   the preceding `const dep = require(1)` import and rewriting the local to
>   `exports`. The anchor is now only recognized as the first statement of
>   the startup region (where webpack always emits it); otherwise the whole
>   region is the entry with no exports binding.
> 
> - Lost ESM exports (P1): the no-IIFE top-level path dropped every
>   ModuleDecl, so an `experiments.outputModule` library lost its top-level
>   `export { ... }`. Recovering harmony exports faithfully is not yet
>   supported, so a bundle with any top-level import/export declaration is
>   now left untouched instead of extracted into an entry that silently
>   loses its public surface.
> 
> - Zero-parameter tables (P2): webpack omits unused factory parameters, so
>   a valid array table can be all zero-parameter factories (side-effect-only
>   deps). The factory-arity gate rejected these. Replace it with the
>   require-function/table relationship — the bootstrap invokes the table as
>   `modules[id](module, ...)` (or `.call(...)`) — which admits zero-param
>   factories and works regardless of how the require function is written.
>   Applied to array containers (objects inside the IIFE remain signal
>   enough) and as the blanket guard on the unwrapped top-level path.

> fix(core): preserve plain input public paths so sibling imports resolve
> 
> Plain passthrough inputs were flattened to their basename at module
> creation, so `sub/left.js` collided with a sibling `left.js`; dedup then
> suffixed whichever came second, and because filename rewrites are keyed
> by the renamed module's own input, a consumer from another input kept
> importing "./left.js" — argument-order-dependent linkage to the wrong
> module (or a dangling specifier), with no warning.
> 
> Plan public paths for every processed input, not just facade
> candidates: a plain input keeps its relative directory structure when
> the path is free, which removes the artificial collision and keeps
> cross-input sibling imports resolvable (including `../pkg/...`
> invocations, whose consumer now stays next to its facade). On a genuine
> collision — or an underivable path — the plain input falls back to the
> legacy basename flatten plus dedup suffix; duplicate filenames stay
> valid prepared-input API usage, and the hard "ambiguous public module
> path" error remains scoped to facade candidates, whose paths are an
> import contract for their namespaced children.
> 
> Boundary fallback and reservation logic keep operating on the facade
> set only (a CJS esbuild bundle must not grow a facade boundary), so
> plan_public_paths now returns the facade and per-input maps separately.

> fix(unpack): key detection facts by resolved binding identity
> 
> Fifth review round on the webpack5 detection heuristics — and the end of
> structural scope tracking, which has now failed one lexical construct at a
> time (nested functions, then blocks/catch/for heads, then named class
> expressions). Both analyses now clone the statements under inspection into a
> synthetic probe function, run the swc resolver over the clone
> (`resolve_probe`), and compare hygiene-resolved binding identities (`Id`)
> instead of identifier text. Every lexical scope is handled uniformly, and
> bindings declared outside the probed region resolve to a distinguishable
> unresolved context.
> 
> - Require-fn lifecycle (P1): facts were keyed by symbol, so an inner
>   block-local `const context = { exports: {} }` supplied the creation fact
>   while a same-named outer parameter supplied the invocation and
>   returned-exports facts, unpacking an ordinary dispatcher. All three facts
>   must now hold for one resolved binding, and the creation fact is only
>   granted to bindings declared inside the body — assigning a fresh module
>   object into a caller-supplied parameter no longer counts either. A cheap
>   symbol-level table-invocation prefilter avoids probing every factory the
>   bootstrap scan visits.
> 
> - Anchor evidence (P1): the structural shadow list missed named class
>   expressions, whose binding is visible in the class body and static blocks
>   (`class a { static { require.d(a, ...) } }` proved an unrelated outer
>   `const a = {}` was the exports anchor). The export-helper scan now compares
>   the anchor's resolved identity; the require callee must additionally
>   resolve to the unresolved context, since the require binding always lives
>   before the startup region.

> feat(unpack): extract webpack5 inline startup as entry module
> 
> When the entry module needs no IIFE wrapper and no require.s/require.O
> startup, webpack 5 inlines it at the end of the bootstrap after
> `var __webpack_exports__ = {};`. Only trailing-IIFE, ncc, and
> startup-call forms were recognized, so these bundles lost their entry
> code entirely.
> 
> Add a last-resort extractor: locate the require function (the FnDecl
> referencing the modules container binding), skip past the last runtime
> definition (assignments to require members like `require.d = ...`,
> which also rules out runtime state such as load-script's
> `var inProgress = {}`), and treat the empty-object var declaration that
> follows as the startup anchor. Everything after it becomes entry.js,
> with the detected require/exports bindings normalized — this works on
> mangled names and on minifier-merged declarators
> (`var o = {}, e = r(9);`).

>

> string require), imports of names the provider does not export,

> missing-name findings for its consumers instead of guessing. Writes are
> matched by resolved id, so shadowing needs no manual scope tracking.

> readability transforms" and carries no module-graph contract.

> machines; nonzero exit on findings) so benchmark harnesses can gate on

>

> fix(unpack): tie require-fn facts to one binding and full lexical scopes
> 
> Fourth review round on the webpack5 detection heuristics.
> 
> - Require-fn detection (P1): the scanner recorded a table invocation and any
>   returned `.exports` member as independent facts, so a mutating dispatcher
>   (`handlers[i](context); return context.exports;`) still matched and was
>   destructively unpacked. Detection now requires webpack's module lifecycle
>   tied to one binding `m` in one function scope: `m` is created locally as an
>   object literal carrying an `exports` property
>   (`var m = cache[id] = { exports: {} }`), `m` (or `m.exports`) is passed to
>   the table invocation, and a return yields `m.exports`. A dispatcher's
>   context is a caller-supplied parameter, never a locally-created module
>   object, so it fails the first fact.
> 
> - Anchor evidence scope (P1): skipping nested functions did not cover
>   JavaScript's other lexical scopes, so a nested block redeclaring the name
>   (`{ const a = {}; require.d(a, ...) }`) still falsely proved an unrelated
>   outer `const a = {}` was webpack's exports object. The export-helper scan
>   now skips any construct that shadows the binding: blocks and switches with
>   a lexical (`let`/`const`/`class`/`function`) redeclaration, catch clause
>   parameters, and `for`/`for-in`/`for-of` head declarations. `var` does not
>   shadow (it hoists to the same function scope).

> fix(unpack): recover eager-import startups and rewrite bound require ids
> 
> Round-10 review findings, both reproduced with generated webpack 5
> production output:
> 
> - An eager `import()` startup has no direct require call — webpack emits
>   `Promise.resolve().then(r.bind(r, 1))` — so the inline-startup gate
>   (which required a direct `r(...)` call) rejected the startup and the
>   entry was silently dropped while the modules still unpacked. The gate
>   now counts a member call on the require binding (`r.bind`, `r.e`,
>   `r.t`) as loader use.
> 
> - A mixed startup recovered its entry via the direct call but left the
>   eager loader as `require.bind(require, 1)` — invoking the host
>   require with a bare module id once the runtime is gone. The bound
>   form (`require.bind(require, id)` in webpack 5, `bind(null, id)` in
>   webpack 4) now gets the same filename rewrite as direct calls, in
>   both the numeric and string-id rewriters.

> fix(unpack): resolve the whole region and match the table by identity
> 
> Seventh review round on the webpack5 detection heuristics.
> 
> - Fn-expr self-binding (P1): the per-candidate probe carried parameters but

> locates the modules container's declaration in the resolved clone, and
> requires candidates to invoke that exact resolved binding
> (`table_invocation_base(call).to_id() == table_id`). Any shadow of the
> table's name at any depth — parameter, fn-expr self-binding, class
> expression name, enclosing function's parameter captured by a closure — is a
> different identity by construction. Per-candidate cloning is gone; the body
> scanner runs over the already-resolved AST with the candidate's
> caller-facing bindings (params + fn-expr self-name, via a pending-self
> handoff from visit_fn_expr to visit_function) excluded from the creation
> fact. A symbol-level prefilter still avoids resolving regions that never
> index the table.
> 
> Regression tests cover the reported repro plus the two adjacent shadow
> shapes the whole-region design closes with it: a class-expression name
> shadowing the table inside a static method, and a closure invoking an
> enclosing function's parameter spelled like the table (a latent hole in the

> fix(unpack): use structural require-fn and scoped anchor evidence
> 
> Third review round on the webpack5 detection heuristics.
> 
> - Table detection (P1): the `(module, module.exports)` argument pair still
>   matched an ordinary `handlers[i](module, module.exports)` dispatcher.
>   Replace it with webpack's runtime invariant: one function scope that both
>   invokes the table (`modules[id](...)` / `.call(...)`) and returns a
>   `.exports` member (the cached module's exports). A dispatcher returns its
>   call result directly, not a `.exports` access, so it no longer matches.
>   Nested function scopes are not descended into, so facts from unrelated
>   inner functions cannot combine to look like a require function.
> 
> - Anchor evidence scope (P1): the export-helper check matched by symbol and
>   descended into nested scopes, so a shadowing parameter in
>   `function helper(a) { require.d(a, ...) }` falsely proved an unrelated
>   outer `const a = {}` was webpack's exports object. Detection runs on

#### 4. v1.10.0 / v1.10.0

item_id: pionxzh/wakaru::release::376633014
Data: 2026-08-25T18:51:44Z
URL: https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/releases/tag/v1.10.0

Release notes (texto original):

> v1.10.0 is a correctness release: 95 fixes, no new bundler formats. Most of the work went into two areas — **SystemJS modules now decompile to real ESM exports** in many more shapes, and **CommonJS `.default` interop is recovered** behind cross-module proofs that fail closed. Also new: `wakaru debug validate` reports source locations and flags CommonJS residuals.
> 
> ## 🔗 SystemJS exports, reconstructed
> 
> - Exports written through `_export` in assignment, `var`-initializer, sequence, and expression forms are reconstructed into ESM export declarations instead of surviving as runtime calls.
> - Setter re-exports are recovered: live setter re-exports no longer synthesize fake locals, arbitrary and named-object setter re-export shapes are reconstructed, and re-export names are preserved exactly.
> - `System.register` modules whose `declare` takes no export parameter are reconstructed; unreadable `declare` parameters fail closed instead of guessing.
> - Every export emission path now proves the target name is free before binding an export directly; unrepresentable export names take the shared alias path, and function-callee IIFEs are parenthesized on every emit path.
> - Export sequence semantics, default-export expression context, chained exports (which now reuse live bindings), and IIFE exports preceding member assignments are all preserved.
> 
> ## 🎛️ CommonJS interop, proven then recovered
> 
> - Default-only providers, coupled lazy defaults, and exact ordered `Object.assign` copy shells are proven at the multi-module fact barrier and recovered — mixed surfaces, unresolved providers, extra runtime behavior, and cycles fail closed.
> - Proven CommonJS self reads, property imports, object imports, callable property imports, and named-only provider imports are repaired into direct ESM references.
> - CommonJS export-star loops are recovered, defaults are recovered from export getter maps, and default-compat postambles are matched in logical form and dropped when proven dead.
> - The proofs fail closed on direct `eval` reads, compound writes and optional chains, prototype-mutating members (`__proto__`, `__defineGetter__`, `__defineSetter__`), conditional callable exports, residual requires, and mid-body directives — `exports.__proto__ = value` stays an honest residual instead of becoming a fabricated named export.
> - Webpack inner-UMD wrappers: proven defaults are recovered, inner exports must be unconditional, and deferred rewrites are rejected.
> 
> ## 🚀 New recovery
> 
> - **Minified TypeScript CJS enums**: the collapsed `(exports.X || (exports.X = {}))` enum IIFE is proven literal-only and recovered as an exported enum object — with the reserved-name, deferred-read, `eval`, and binding-grammar holes closed and each rejected shape covered by tests.
> - Called module-export assignments are lowered through receiver chains, chained local default exports are split, and default exports are recovered from `var` initializers.
> 
> ## 🧭 Validation & diagnostics
> 
> - `wakaru debug validate` findings now carry source locations — `filename:line:column` in human output, one-based `line`/`column` fields in `--json`.
> - The validator reports CommonJS residuals: unresolved `module` / `exports` runtime uses left in files that contain ESM syntax (direct safe `typeof` probes excluded).
> - Import-backed local re-exports resolve to their origin, ambiguous star exports are detected, duplicate export declarations are pinpointed, reported import cycles carry a real cycle witness, and repeated parser recovery warnings are coalesced.
> - With `--unpack=inspect` and `--provenance`, fine modules split from one oversized write component carry optional `context_ranges` identifying the coarse evidence-pooling context in the original input.
> 
> ## 📦 Webpack
> 
> - CSS runtime modules: runtime metadata is recovered and emitted CSS adapter forms are handled.
> - Reused loader and runtime parameters are localized per factory, unsafe loader reuse is isolated, and reuse normalization is gated by alias lifetime.
> - String module IDs now emit JavaScript filenames: non-JS resource IDs append `.js` (`src/style.less` → `src/style.less.js`), loader queries and URL fragments are stripped from filesystem names, and collisions get stable suffixes.
> - Identity substitution requires a stable module surface, the guarded global fallback is hardened, generated global injection is recovered, empty-factory default exports are restored, and wrapper lifting respects class execution contexts.
> 
> ## 🛡️ Rename & binding safety
> 
> - A capture sweep across the rename rules: parameter defaults, named exports, alias recovery, value renames, and namespace aliases can no longer be captured by inner scopes or globals, and parameter-default binding order is preserved.
> - The shared rename shadow index now fails closed (and trips a debug assertion) when queried about a binding it never analyzed, and JSX intrinsic-tag checks use ASCII lowercase — matching the `/^[a-z]/` test JSX transforms actually apply.
> - Object-rest synthetic aliases are sanitized for string keys and made collision-free; mutable require locals stay mutable; `const` is recovered after declaration merges; externally used `for...of` loop bindings survive.
> 
> ## ⚙️ Async, accessors, generators
> 
> - Async flattening preserves callable names and renames colliding bindings instead of capturing them.
> - Class accessor recovery is verified before conversion, and legacy TypeScript accessor forms are preserved.
> - TypeScript async state machines and regenerator decoding preserve state-callback locals.
> 
> **Full changelog:** https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/compare/v1.9.0...v1.10.0

> fix(esm): stop treating prototype-mutating members as named exports
> 
> exports.__proto__ = value triggers the Object.prototype.__proto__ setter
> and creates no own property, so recovering it as export const __proto__
> both fabricates an export and erases the prototype change. The same
> assumption — that a static exports.name access is evidence about an
> ordinary named export — appeared in four more proofs. All now fail
> closed via a shared is_prototype_mutating_member_name helper:
> 
> - try_classify_cjs_export keeps exports.__proto__ = value as an honest
>   CommonJS residual (probe-confirmed: main previously printed
>   export const __proto__)
> - collect_stable_named_properties fails the whole read-recovery proof
>   when any exports use touches __proto__ / __defineGetter__ /
>   __defineSetter__, since those mutate proven properties without a
>   visible write of the affected name
> - webpack getter-map conversion (object map and 3-arg string forms)
>   fails closed rather than synthesizing exports.__proto__ = expr, which
>   would turn the original own accessor into a prototype write
> - facts: a plain __proto__: value literal entry and callable.__proto__
>   writes are excluded from declared/attached export properties (they
>   set the prototype, not an own property; shorthand/method/accessor
>   forms still count)
> 
> No corpus producer emits these shapes; this completes the fail-closed
> story started by the postamble dunder guard.

> fix(rules): recover minified TypeScript CJS enum IIFE exports
> 
> Handle the collapsed exports.X || (exports.X = {}) enum argument entirely

> for the late declaration-kind pass to promote safely.

> fix(core): recover default-only CommonJS adapters
> 
> Generated default-compatibility adapters publish one live identifier
> getter for exports.default and end with the postamble that marks the
> value __esModule, copies the exports namespace onto it, and republishes
> it as module.exports. When that is the complete surface — the getter and
> the final postamble, with no authored ESM and no other unresolved
> exports or module use — the adapter is rewritten onto the recovered
> binding: the observable __esModule definition and .default = self
> mirror remain, and native ESM replaces only the namespace copy and the
> final module.exports reassignment. Mixed or named default-bearing
> surfaces, computed access, whole-object escape, unresolved getter
> helpers, prototype-mutating member names, meaningful module use, and
> direct eval fail closed.

> fix(rules): close reserved-name, deferred-read, and eval holes in enum recovery
> 
> Follow-ups to the collapsed CJS enum hardening, all fail-closed:
> 
> - Reserved names: exports.class is a legal property, but the synthesized
>   binding export var class is a SyntaxError. Reject reserved binding
>   names before synthesizing.
> - Deferred reads: the public-export reference scan only looked at items
>   after the IIFE, so a function defined earlier could defer its
>   exports.X read until after the fold removed the only write. Scan
>   processed items too — for the collapsed path and the pre-existing
>   local-alias paths alike, which shared the same hole.
> - Direct eval: the AST name scan cannot see eval sources, so
>   eval("Mode") reading a global would be captured by the synthesized
>   module binding. Reject when any direct eval source is unknown or a
>   known source mentions the name (indirect eval runs in global scope
>   and cannot observe module bindings).

> fix(validate): resolve import-backed local re-exports to their origin
> 
> ESM resolves `import { x } from "./a.js"; export { x };` to the source
> module's binding, the same edge as `export { x } from "./a.js";`. The
> star-ambiguity resolver treated such exports as local bindings, so two
> modules forwarding the same origin through this shape read as distinct
> origins and produced a false ambiguity finding on a graph the runtime
> loads. Map import locals to their indirect resolution (named/default ->
> re-export, namespace -> namespace object; external or dangling specifiers
> stay unknown) and consult that map for source-less export specifiers.

>   stripping parentheses.

#### 5. v1.12.0 / v1.12.0

item_id: pionxzh/wakaru::release::387979395
Data: 2026-09-13T17:39:45Z
URL: https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/releases/tag/v1.12.0

Release notes (texto original):

> v1.12.0 is a performance release. **Wakaru is now 27–42% faster end-to-end on large bundles.** The rest of the release is correctness work on exports, loops, and esbuild splitting.
> 
> ## ⚡ Performance
> 
> Five changes make up the speedup: 27–29% less end-to-end time on medium bundles and 42% less on a large esbuild bundle, for a few dozen MiB more peak memory.
> 
> - The CLI binary uses mimalloc as its global allocator. The `wakaru` crate and the WASM build leave the allocator to their callers.
> - Both unpack phases start the largest modules first, so one big module no longer becomes the critical path.
> - Rules move statement and argument trees instead of deep-cloning them.
> - `UnEsm` checks whether a module has anything to convert before building its binding index.
> - Internal binding tables use a faster hasher.
> 
> ## 🔗 Exports and imports
> 
> - CommonJS named exports assigned under conditions become live ESM bindings, and the `exports.x = void 0` sentinels in front of them are dropped.
> - Named-export assignment chains are split into one binding per export when their values are stable.
> - Module-level copies of named imports are renamed after the import they copy.
> 
> ## 📦 esbuild splitting
> 
> Mutable state written from several esbuild modules is declared once by its owner and imported everywhere else. CommonJS-style factories go through the same path, so their bodies are always emitted.
> 
> ## 🛡️ Correctness
> 
> - For-of recovery keeps `let` when the loop body writes the binding, and leaves loops that write a `const` alone.
> - Export aliases stay separate when either side is reassigned.
> - Generator recovery matches the state parameter by scope, so a nested callback with the same minified name no longer blocks it.
> - `--diagnostics` and `debug validate` report `var` declarations that conflict with `let`, `const`, or `class` in the same scope.
> 
> ## 🧪 Debug CLI
> 
> - `wakaru debug enumerate-chunks` lists the chunk files a bundle would load at runtime, from a static read of one input: webpack lazy chunks and relative `import` / `import()` specifiers. Experimental, see the debug CLI reference.
> 
> ## 🔧 Dependencies
> 
> Bump `swc_core` to 78.0.2.
> 
> **Full changelog:** https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/compare/v1.11.0...v1.12.0

- 0457cd862abf6ba8676565b1c4b08247f92a1277 — https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/0457cd862abf6ba8676565b1c4b08247f92a1277
> fix(unpack): own factory-written state in one writer group
> 
> A standalone factory whose body assigns a top-level binding directly
> joined no ownership component. Every writing factory kept its own copy
> of the state declaration and entry.js kept another, so writes landed
> on separate variables. Add declaration write edges from factory bodies
> to the state owner, mark that group as a writer group, and seed entry
> relocation with the written state. The group now declares the binding
> once and entry reads it through an import.
> 
> Stripping the entry declaration requires every remaining entry writer
> to follow the state. A hoisted function declaration that writes the
> group's state joins the ownership unit when its binding is never
> reassigned and its other dependencies already have an emitted owner;
> entry calls it through an import. Any other unrelocatable writer cancels
> the split as before, and a CommonJS factory now demotes into entry as a
> synthesized cached callable instead of blocking demotion. When demotion
> is impossible, the writer's assignment to the imported state remains as
> the validator-visible residual it was before.
> 
> A demoted factory's synthesized cache or guard takes a name the entry
> does not already declare or import: reusing a `var` would report the
> factory as initialized and skip its body, and reusing a lexical binding
> is a duplicate declaration.
- 05d2da4f3a808a8e94f3fbb6436c521dbb55c7cf — https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/05d2da4f3a808a8e94f3fbb6436c521dbb55c7cf
> fix(unpack): route CommonJS factories through the shared ownership path
> 
> A CommonJS factory that assigned a top-level binding was excluded from
> the preassigned and importable factory maps, and merged emission skipped
> CommonJS bodies entirely. A scope module calling such a factory got no
> import edge, and when the module's region declared the written state the
> factory merged into that module and its body was never emitted anywhere.
> 
> Preassign every factory's binding and written state regardless of shape,
> merge only when a scope module claims the state, and emit merged and
> standalone factories through one emitter that produces the cached
> `require`-style callable for CommonJS and the guarded init function for
> lazy ESM. The emitter reserves its cache or guard name against the names
> already declared in the target module and against every identifier the
> factory body mentions: a body local or parameter with the chosen name
> would shadow the cache inside the callable and re-run the body on every
> call. The demotion path reserves the same way.

> fix(rules): match the generator state parameter by resolver identity
> 
> The regenerator and TypeScript `__generator` decoders kept the state
> callback's parameter as a bare `Atom` and matched every `state.next`,
> `state.catch(...)`, `state.sent()`, and `state.tN` reference by spelling.
> The slot lowering already compared `(sym, ctxt)`, but the detection and
> decode helpers around it did not.
> 
> A nested callback inside a case body whose own parameter shares the
> minified spelling (`function (e) { e.next = null }`, `.then(function (e) {
> return e.catch(noop) })`) therefore read as a state jump inside nested
> control flow, or as a `catch` call without a try-region table, and the
> generator was left un-recovered.
>

> `ctxt` in one `is_state_param_ref` helper, replacing the name-only
> matcher. Regression tests cover both regenerator shapes; the TypeScript
> decoder gets a regression for a block-local binding whose `.sent()` call
> must not consume the preceding yield.

> fix(repro): install npm tools through a staging directory
> 
> `ensureNodeTool` and `ensureLockedNodeTool` removed the tool directory,
> recreated it, and ran `npm install` in place, writing the marker last.
> Every matrix and test process shares `target/repro-tools`, and
> `node --test` runs test files in parallel workers, so a second process
> that checked the marker while the first install was still running
> deleted the first process's freshly written packages. The first process
> then wrote its marker and spawned Node in a directory whose package the
> second `npm install` had not yet restored.
> 
> Move the install into `lib/node-tool.mjs`: populate a private staging
> sibling, write the marker there, and rename it into place. A losing
> installer whose rename finds a directory with a matching marker discards
> its own copy; a stale directory is moved aside by rename before removal
> so a complete install is never deleted from under a process that already
> returned it. Both installers now share this path, with `npm install` and
> `npm ci` as the populate step.
> 
> Add tests for the single-process paths and a multi-process regression
> that staggers installers around a slow populate, and run them in the
> repro-stats workflow.

> types. Iteration order was never observable (the default hasher is seeded

> network requests. Stdin is accepted when piped, or explicitly with `-`.
> 
> The root carries `detected_format` (null when no structural format
> matches) and `enumeration` (null when neither the webpack runtime tables
> nor the relative-import collector produced a fact). `public_path` reports
> its status and, for `static` and `script_relative` only, the literal value
> a caller may prepend to `urls[].url`; asset URLs stay relative and never
> include the public path. `relative_imports[].specifier` is already a
> sibling URL relative to the entry and is resolved directly against it.
> `template` is a debug rendering with placeholders and is not a parseable
> contract.
> 
> Document the command and its JSON shape in the debug CLI reference under
> its compatibility policy, and list the enumeration module in the code map.

> perf(core): dispatch modules largest-first in both unpack phases
> 
> Phase 1 and Phase 2 mapped modules with par_iter, whose recursive range
> splitting can start the largest module after most workers have already
> gone idle, so that one module becomes the critical path of the phase.
> Route both phases through a shared helper that sorts items by source
> length, pulls them through par_bridge so each free worker takes the
> largest remaining module, and places results back in input order.
> 
> Output does not depend on scheduling: every module already runs under its
> own Globals, and results are re-sorted by original index before the facts
> barrier and before emit. Unit tests pin input-order results across worker
> counts and the descending dispatch order under a single worker.
- c6fcd3ebc5e66881dcb7269b6186a5efbabdb412 — https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/c6fcd3ebc5e66881dcb7269b6186a5efbabdb412
> perf: borrow rest statement history and move spread argument trees
> 
> UnObjectRest kept a second `recent_stmts` vector beside the rebuilt module
> body, deep-cloning every emitted statement so backward proofs could look
> behind the current statement. That history was always the tail of the
> output since the last module declaration. Track the start index of the
> current statement run and borrow `new_body[recent_start..]` instead; a
> private statement-view trait lets the proof helpers accept either statement
> lists or module-item lists. Module declarations still reset the boundary,
> and absorbed statements and replacement declarations keep their order.
> 
> UnObjectSpread cloned the first object's properties and every argument
> expression when flattening a helper call, so nested `_extends` recoveries
> copied already-recovered subtrees once per enclosing call. Consume the
> arguments after all rejection checks pass and move the property vectors and
> expression boxes.
> 
> Add an allocation-counting example for measuring rule and unpack allocation
> traffic, tests pinning the module-declaration boundary reset and the
> rebuilt-history lookbehind, and a pointer-identity test that fails when
> spread recovery clones argument trees.
- c75c6a9f74c0104c04d081f102923766910d66a3 — https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/c75c6a9f74c0104c04d081f102923766910d66a3
> feat(unpack): enumerate lazy-chunk references statically
> 
> Add a fail-closed analysis of one parsed input that lists the sibling files
> its runtime would request, without unpacking or executing anything.
> 
> Webpack 4/5 runtimes emit the chunk filename template as a function whose
> body concatenates string literals, the `chunkId` parameter, and object
> literal lookups keyed by chunk id (`__webpack_require__.u`, `.miniCssF`,
> webpack 4's `jsonpScriptSrc`). When the template and every id source are
> literal, expand the exact relative URLs; chunk ids come from the filename
> map or from binding-correlated literal ensure calls. A template with any
> non-literal part is reported as `dynamic_template` with no URLs, and a
> literal template without a static id source as `no_static_chunk_ids`.
> 
> `__webpack_require__.p` is classified by the same standard: a single
> string-literal assignment is `static`; webpack's automatic public path,
> an identifier traced from a script-URL source through the canonical
> `replace(/\/[^\/]+$/, "/")` normalization plus a literal `/`-terminated
> relative suffix, is `script_relative` carrying only the suffix; anything
> else is `runtime_computed`, where the filename is known but the complete
> URL is not. Runtime candidates are resolved by binding identity and require
> the function-valued runtime shape, so an unrelated object literal cannot
> be mistaken for the runtime table.
> 
> For native ESM code splitting the specifier itself is the chunk URL, so a
> format-independent collector records literal relative specifiers from
> `import`, `export ... from`, and `import()` as `relative_imports`, keyed
> by kind. Bare packages, absolute and protocol-relative URLs, and computed
> specifiers are skipped rather than guessed. The collector runs on the
> parsed input before detection, so no synthesized output can leak into it.
- cefc4c4bee6d7e2e8418b7d9762d1f5fed700c10 — https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/cefc4c4bee6d7e2e8418b7d9762d1f5fed700c10
> fix(rules): recover discarded numeric index holes in UnForOf
> 
> Babel loose + DCE leaves unused numeric indexes as `temp[i];`. UnForOf
> only accepted VarDecl slots, so the loop left stayed the whole entry.
> Treat unread consecutive indexes as ArrayPat holes without inventing names.

Release notes (texto original):

> This release contains a completely rewritten Wayland backend as a python C
> module, removing the complex-to-install dependency chain that was
> previously required. As a result, the dependencies to run wayland have
> completely changed. Of course this new wayland backend is still
> experimental, bug reports and patches welcome.
> 
> In this release we also add a new maintainer Richard Carnibella @richcarni,
> who has done a substantial amount of work to get the new wayland backend
> stable for merging and release.
> 
> As always, thanks to all the (other) contributors for this release:

- 2173cb6e4c07922842f4af37743e3c2d23a83433 — https://github.com/qtile/qtile/commit/2173cb6e4c07922842f4af37743e3c2d23a83433
> move to uv
> 
> This moves all of the non-docs infra to uv, deleting requirements.txt,
> requirements-dev.txt, setup.cfg, tox.ini, and dev.sh, each of which had a
> slightly different set of dependencies in them, and consolidates to
> pyproject.toml to manage all of this.
> 
> It also consolidates on using the makefile as the entry point for
> everything, and has CI call `make check check-packaging`. There are some
> new variables for supplying only a single backend or python version.
> 
> As a consequence of using `uv sync --all-extras` for CI, we now need to
> install the wayland deps in all environments even if we are only going to
> run the x11 backend tests, but that seems simpler than fragmenting these
> things again.
> 
> Finally, I organized the deps into four sections: dev, optional_core,
> widgets, and wayland. I wonder if optional_core is worth it, or if we
> should just start requiring all of those? But the other three seem
> reasonable to me.
> 
> It looks like the uv lock file is expected to be committed based on
> https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/9797 , but I generally find these
> kinds of lock files annoying, and we haven't needed one in the past. Given
> that we should encode any real constraints/bugs we know about (e.g. API
> incompatibilities, bugs, etc.) in pyproject.toml directly, I don't see a
> ton of value in uv.lock. I think it will also help downstreams to not feel
> like they have to package *exactly* the versions we happened to test with,
> but can just respect our pyproject.toml.
> 
> This commit drops scripts/ffibuild, because over a series of commits
> (9770e8c , 24435ad , and 5736f4f ) we removed the need to pre-build ffi
> stuff except for wayland, so the script ends up just being a wrapper around
> the single ffi build we still needed. There's no real need for it, we can
> just call that build script directly.
> 
> Signed-off-by: Tycho Andersen <tycho@tycho.pizza>
- 217df4ae144e99208cfc58f8fe7048cb1f9cec0a — https://github.com/qtile/qtile/commit/217df4ae144e99208cfc58f8fe7048cb1f9cec0a

> instead of 8, xorg-x11-font-utils is removed (needed for building
> XWayland). But it is still in the almalinux devel repo, so we get it
> from there.

- 4655d4a0542b94c5a59f8779ed7a0c2e2f33ad3d — https://github.com/qtile/qtile/commit/4655d4a0542b94c5a59f8779ed7a0c2e2f33ad3d
> don't reap processes spawned by asyncio
> 
> After the conversion of GenPollCommand to asyncio.create_subprocess_* I
> have a lot of:
> 
>     Unknown child process pid 1312154, will report returncode 255
> 
> from qtile's stderr in my xsession logs. It turns out that this is from
> asyncio [1] who is confused because our SIGCHILD handler wait()ed on its
> process. So let's do the same thing we do for tasks: keep a list of tasks,
> and not really wait on those (via WNOWAIT), so that we can leave them for
> asyncio so it doesn't get confused.
> 
> Much like create task, we need to be careful to use acall_process() vs.
> asyncio.create_subprocess_* whenever we want to await on one of these
> processes. (Well, not really: acall_process() doesn't return the task's
> exit code, so the only consequence of these is that it's slightly annoying
> logspam. But in the future if we decided we wanted the exit code from the
> acall_process() API, it might be confusing as to why we don't get it.)
> 
> [1]: https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/5bd4bf04c4ac1ad67760e0b7852a05e796741e6f/Lib/asyncio/unix_events.py#L937-L939
> 
> Signed-off-by: Tycho Andersen <tycho@tycho.pizza>
- 46a3c0589894e85b681ebe881333eb3ab9fe475f — https://github.com/qtile/qtile/commit/46a3c0589894e85b681ebe881333eb3ab9fe475f
> unify graceful_shutdown()
> 
> Wayland's implementation is better than x11's since it uses actual WM
> semantics, and also it's not generally very backend-specific, so let's
> adopt that approach for both backends. We can do this leveraging async so
> we don't need to block the rest of the event loop, potentially allowing for
> other shutdown code to happen.
> 
> There is one insidiously complex change hidden in here, which is the shift
> from:
> 
>     if not isinstance(win, base.Internal):
> 
> to:
> 
>     def normal_windows(self) -> list[base.WindowType]:
>         return list(
>             filter(lambda w: isinstance(w, base.Window), self.windows_map.copy().values())
>         )
> 
> it turns out our systray is not a base.Internal window, but also does not
> set NET_WM_PID, so we were previously not killing it in the x11 version via
> get_pid().
> 
> However, if you .kill() (i.e. WM_DELETE_WINDOW instead of the kill(2)
> syscall) the systray widget's window, the X server kills the connection
> that window was created from, which just so happens to be qtile's main
> connection, which kills the whole WM.
> 
> So instead, we switch to only trying to kill "normal" windows, since those
> are the clients with state we want to notify that we're shutting down.
> 
> (The systray widget is finalized [or not, modulo bugs :)] via the normal
> widget finalize() path.)
> 
> Signed-off-by: Tycho Andersen <tycho@tycho.pizza>

- 56955706709f1a4ec356de153e00c0d407e23685 — https://github.com/qtile/qtile/commit/56955706709f1a4ec356de153e00c0d407e23685
> Rework stretch widget length allocation
> 
> I've noticed that STRETCH widgets aren't centering text correctly. This code
> reworks `Bar._resize` to ensure that space is allocated correctly.
> 
> It addresses three scenarios:
> 1) When there is one group of STRETCH widgets. All available space is
>    distributed evenly amongst that group.
> 2) When there are two groups. Any widgets between the groups are
>    centered in the bar.
> 3) When there are three or more groups. Effectively the same as first
>    scenario, length is distributed evenly amongst each group.

> x11: drop string slinging for event handler resolution
> 
> While profiling Qtile, I see the number one source of allocations is:
> 
>     1   x11/core.py:387                          17.7 KiB
>         handler = f"handle_{event_type}"
> 
> which is unfortunate. Python doesn't intern these strings because they have
> a _ in them, so this slinging is a constant source of allocations.
> 
> However, it doesn't need to be. The set of functions we dispatch to is
> quite small, so let's just hardcode the list and use that for dynamic
> dispatch.

- 6c25810edc0e90d0994f7ea9802a1fc4e36229b0 — https://github.com/qtile/qtile/commit/6c25810edc0e90d0994f7ea9802a1fc4e36229b0
> Fix: Qtile freezes when launching programs that read from stdin
> 
> Launching programs that read from stdin (e.g. `/bin/cat`) through `lazy.spawncmd()`
> completely freezes Qtile, killing the spawned process from the TTY results
> in a zombie process, and Qtile remains frozen.
> 
> Steps to reproduce:
> 1. trigger `lazy.spawncmd()` through its assigned keybind
> 2. run `/bin/cat` using the spawn prompt
> 
> The issue is mostly triggered accidentally due to tab-completion, for example:
> - `pc` -> `pc1pc1toppm` instead of `pcmanfm`
> - `ma` -> `machinectl` instead of `materialgram`
> - `t` -> `tabs` instead of `telegram`
> 
> The `spawn` function is supposed to redirect standard file descriptors
> of the child process to `/dev/null` using dup2, but the order of arguments
> is incorrect which is causing it to silently fail.
> 
> Swapping `null.fileno()` and `0,1,2` fixes the issue, as the intended behavior
> is to duplicate `null.fileno()` to `stdio` and not the other way around.
> 
> Related documentation:
> * [os.POSIX_SPAWN_DUP2](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.POSIX_SPAWN_DUP2)
>   * (os.POSIX_SPAWN_DUP2, fd, new_fd)
>   * Performs os.dup2(fd, new_fd).
> * [os.dup2](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.dup2)
>   * os.dup2(fd, fd2)
>   * Duplicate file descriptor fd to fd2, closing the latter first if necessary.
> * [man dup2](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/dup.2.html)
>   * int dup2(int oldfd, int newfd);
>   * The file descriptor newfd is adjusted so that it now refers to the same open file description as oldfd.
> 
> Linked issue: [#5595](https://github.com/qtile/qtile/issues/5595)
- 6d9494cc09a03f2293b0aadeff3a71407c2e2543 — https://github.com/qtile/qtile/commit/6d9494cc09a03f2293b0aadeff3a71407c2e2543
> Server: Null check tree in view_at

> focused surface

> Release v0.34.0
> 
> This release contains a completely rewritten Wayland backend as a python C
> module, removing the complex-to-install dependency chain that was
> previously required. As a result, the dependencies to run wayland have
> completely changed. Of course this new wayland backend is still
> experimental, bug reports and patches welcome.
> 
> In this release we also add a new maintainer Richard Carnibella @richcarni,
> who has done a substantial amount of work to get the new wayland backend
> stable for merging and release.
>

> tests: exitcode tests should use our infra
> 
> There were a couple problems with this code:
> 
> 1. both exitcode tests used the same temporary socket file, so they
>    couldn't be run in parallel
> 2. that named socket file was never deleted
> 
> But also, we already have code that spawns qtile, creates processes, etc.
> that is complex and does all the multiprocessing stuff for us. Let's just
> use it.
> 
> In order to do that, we need to explicitly call the ._atexit() handler for
> Lifecycle, since it is not registered in our "little qtile" call. Perhaps
> we should just switch run_qtile() to write out the config and exec qtile,
> so that we get *exactly* the behavior we expect, vs. reimplementing a bunch
> of it. But for now, I'll just do this.
> 
> For some reason that I do not quite understand, this code *also* interfered
> with other qtiles in the test suite that ran after it with the
> graceful_shutdown() patch. But since this cleanup is a pretty big win, I
> didn't look very hard at root causing the problem.
> 
> Signed-off-by: Tycho Andersen <tycho@tycho.pizza>

> fix(_TextBox): length STATIC remove padding
> 
> Since padding is not added to widgets with static length, some problems
> arise when the padding is large, written fixes:
> 1. Padding is added to the left but not right, remove from left.
> 2. In vertical bars and rotate=False, padding*2 greater than the bar
> size will decenter text.
> 3. When scrolling, padding*2 greater than the bar size will write no
> text, use the entire _scroll_width.
> 4. When scrolling in vertical bars and rotate=False, padding*2 greater
> than the bar size will write no text, use the widget length to draw the
> scroll rectange.

- aee2b1d5c890f6fb20da965fbf53275dd6799532 — https://github.com/qtile/qtile/commit/aee2b1d5c890f6fb20da965fbf53275dd6799532
> improve udev rules
> 
> ...and drop `qtile udev`. It turns out that some distros (fedora, arch) run
> their udev daemon in the initramfs (which makes sense, of course, not sure
> why I didn't think of it earlier). That means that in order to run this
> code, we'd need to include it in the initramfs, which seems like a pain.
> 
> Instead, let's just rearrange the rules to chmod o+w things. This is
> simpler for users than having a special group, since groups that exists
> across distros are hard (sudo on ubuntu instead of  wheel on fedora, etc.).
> Distro packagers can use whatever rules make sense for their distro.
> 
> In the rules themselves, the backlight and battery there is just one file
> and it seems to exist sysfs symlink time for the device, so we can use a
> simple rule.
> 
> For the battery charge control, there is two files, so we need to run two
> commands (we could use shell globbing here to do one command, but the
> quoting is... annoying :).
> 
> I tried several different ways to match it at sysfs symlink creation time,
> but kept getting:
> 
>     BAT0: Process '/usr/bin/chmod o+w /sys/class/power_supply/BAT0/charge_control_start_threshold' failed with exit code 1
> 
> because the file is only created when the specific driver is loaded. So, we
> trigger on that, and hard code the battery path.
> 
> All this is to say: I believe this is simpler and easier to use, since it
> doesn't require anything in the initramfs or having a specific group hard
> coded, even if it is a bit uglier.
> 
> Fixes #5227
> 
> Signed-off-by: Tycho Andersen <tycho@tycho.pizza>

> My comparison of using setuptools compiler over a makefile:
> Advantages:
> - Simpler (i.e. for future maintainers)
> - Better compatability, for example never tested if makefile was BSD

> Disadvantages:

- b667f9efd37eab117943f739b01e4d15bad1e09f — https://github.com/qtile/qtile/commit/b667f9efd37eab117943f739b01e4d15bad1e09f
> drop DefaultEventLoopPolicy
> 
> python3.14 depreciates event loop policies entirely, in favor of just
> manually specifying the event loop as an argument to asyncio.run().
> 
> we were really using the event loop policy as a hack for not having a
> global variable, so let's switch to a global variable instead, and use it
> in the one place we need it.
> 
> we have to drop two verisons of python because they do not have the
> loop_factory= argument to asyncio:
> 
>     raise AssertionError(f"Error launching qtile, traceback:\n{error}")
>     AssertionError: Error launching qtile, traceback:
>     Traceback (most recent call last):
>       File "/home/runner/work/qtile/qtile/test/helpers.py", line 207, in run_qtile
>         ).loop()
>       File "/home/runner/work/qtile/qtile/libqtile/core/manager.py", line 216, in loop
>         asyncio.run(self.async_loop(), loop_factory=lambda: libqtile.event_loop)
>     TypeError: run() got an unexpected keyword argument 'loop_factory'
> 
> but maybe that's ok: 3.10 is outside of our last-three-versions policy, and
> 3.11 will be outside it in a few months when 3.14 is released.
> 
> There is another option here: since the motivation for this was really
> #2620, we could "just" switch the battery to running in-loop, which would
> mean that it is not run via run_in_executor() i.e. in a separate thread.
> That means that get_running_loop() would return the right loop, and we
> wouldn't need this hack at all.
> 
> (It also means that the battery could potentially block the UI while
> reading from e.g. procfs/sysfs files, but that seems unlikely. Perhaps it
> also suggests another widget type: something with an `async def poll()`,
> which could run in the main loop and avoid both of these problems.)
> 
> The only other widget which uses send_notification() is pomodoro, which
> doesn't read any files at all and just uses gettimeofday(), which is a VDSO
> i.e. memory access, that should also not block, so if we convert the
> battery widget, we should do this one as well.
> 
> Finally, we suggest use of send_notification() in the hooks documentation,
> but all hooks are fired from the main thread, so the get_running_loop()
> call should work fine there.
> 
> That does mean we'd have to be careful to always send_notification() from
> the main thread going forward, but it doesn't seem like that hard of a
> challenge.
> 
> Fixes #5346
> 
> Signed-off-by: Tycho Andersen <tycho@tycho.pizza>

- c1e85f942eca18424a7504ee1ac4b0ff52fbaa63 — https://github.com/qtile/qtile/commit/c1e85f942eca18424a7504ee1ac4b0ff52fbaa63
> docs(nixos): update flake usage to reflect removal of overlay
> 
> Qtile's flake no longer provides an overlay (#5420). Updated NixOS
> example to set `services.xserver.windowManager.qtile.package` directly
> from the flake input. Reworded intro, improved bullet list consistency,
> and
> added reST `.. note::` disclaimer.
> 
> Without these changes, flake users may encounter the following error:
> 
> ```bash
> error: attribute 'overlays' missing
>    at /nix/store/.../overlays.nix:3:6:
>     2|   nixpkgs.overlays = [
>     3|     (inputs.qtile-flake.overlays.default)
> ```
> 
> This can be confusing for those who haven’t seen the recent `flake.nix`
> update, especially newcomers to Nix.
> 
> **Why this refactor?**
> Previously, the flake returned an overlay, which required users to:
> 
> 1. Create an `overlays.nix` file.
> 2. Define Qtile’s overlay and import it locally.
> 3. Understand overlay mechanics — adding extra complexity for those
> unfamiliar with them.
> 
> By switching to direct package specification, we remove unnecessary
> steps and reduce complexity. The new approach is:
> 
> * Easier to read and maintain.
> * More explicit about which package is used.
> * Less work for the end user.
> 
> **TL;DR:** Returning an overlay was overkill. Directly defining the
> package is cleaner and simpler.

- c354cab3fd9c0eb116353ed20221587db518c6a9 — https://github.com/qtile/qtile/commit/c354cab3fd9c0eb116353ed20221587db518c6a9
> x11: don't focus twice in focus_by_click()
> 
> In focus_by_click(), we call:
> 
> group.focus() -> layout_all() -> current_window.focus()
> 
> but then we do an explicit window.focus() again in focus_by_click(),
> resulting in two focus events, two hooks called, etc.
> 
> Let's drop that second explicit focus_by_click(), so we only generate on
> event.
> 
> Signed-off-by: Tycho Andersen <tycho@tycho.pizza>

> LICENSE: change Copyright to "the Qtile contributors"
> 
> According to this:
> 
>     ~/packages/qtile master cat aldo_cortesi_blame.py
>     import os
>     import subprocess
> 
>     def run_git(args):
>         result = subprocess.run(
>             ['/usr/bin/git'] + args,
>             check=True,
>             stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
>             stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
>         )
>         return result.stdout.decode()
> 
>     def main():
>         files = run_git(['ls-files']).strip().split('\n')
> 
>         counts = {}
>         errors = []
> 
>         for path in files:
>             if not path:
>                 continue
>             env = os.environ.copy()
>             env['GIT_BLAME_IGNORE_REVS_FILE'] = '.git-blame-ignore-revs'
>             proc = subprocess.run(
>                 ['/usr/bin/git', 'blame', '--line-porcelain', 'HEAD', '--', path],
>                 stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
>                 stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
>                 env=env,
>             )
>             if proc.returncode != 0:
>                 errors.append((path, proc.stderr.decode(errors='replace').strip()))
>                 continue
> 
>             for raw_line in proc.stdout.splitlines():
>                 line = raw_line.decode(errors='replace')
>                 if line.startswith('author '):
>                     author = line[7:]
>                     counts[author] = counts.get(author, 0) + 1
> 
>         total_lines = sum(counts.values())
>         aldo_lines = counts.get('Aldo Cortesi', 0)
>         percentage = (aldo_lines / total_lines * 100) if total_lines else 0
> 
>         print(f"Aldo Cortesi lines: {aldo_lines}")
>         print(f"Total lines: {total_lines}")
>         print(f"Percentage: {percentage:.6f}%")
> 
>         if errors:
>             print('Encountered errors:')
>             for path, msg in errors:
>                 print(f"{path}: {msg}")
> 
>     if __name__ == '__main__':
>         main()
>     ~/packages/qtile master python3 aldo_cortesi_blame.py
>     Aldo Cortesi lines: 1038
>     Total lines: 94365
>     Percentage: 1.099984%
> 
> Aldo has ~1% of the lines in Qtile. Let's update all the copyright notices
> to reflect the actual copyright holders, which are the contributors

>

> https://github.com/qtile/qtile/issues/4502#issuecomment-1753121787
> 
> However, looking further,
> 
> `uv pip tree` gives us:
> 
>     pygobject v3.52.3
>     └── pycairo v1.28.0
> 
> Meaning that our PyGobject dependency is bring in + importing cairo, which
> was ultimately the thing causing the seg fault.
> 
> Without some hackery it does not seem possible to install pygobject
> without the pycairo dependency: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/pygobject/-/issues/395
> 
> We only use gobject (and thus pycairo) in some of our tests (git grep
> "import gi") to drive some test windows, so we can remove this as a runtime
> dependency but keep it as a test dependency (with the version with the
> bugfix hardcoded), hopefully making packaging a bit more obvious :)
> 
> Signed-off-by: Tycho Andersen <tycho@tycho.pizza>

> core: only cancel tasks once
> 
> While debugging something else in our exit path, I noticed we try to cancel
> asyncio tasks twice, once in libqtile/core/loop.py::_cancel_all_tasks(),
> and once in the finalizer.
> 
> The version in _cancel_all_tasks() is probably preferable, since it
> iterates over all asyncio tasks, so we will cancel stuff that's started by
> libraries or whatever. So, let's drop our own version.
> 
> Also, while I was here, I switched our task list to a set like the docs
> show, and removed some of the unnecessary callbacks by calling
> set.discard() directly.
> 
> Signed-off-by: Tycho Andersen <tycho@tycho.pizza>

- e7489719a5540fbe69b696aacba9c9fd28b84038 — https://github.com/qtile/qtile/commit/e7489719a5540fbe69b696aacba9c9fd28b84038
> [wayland] fix XCB connection
> 
> The wayland backend creates a connection to the x server to retrieve
> atoms in order to determine an xwayland window's _NET_WM_WINDOW_TYPE.
> 
> This caused an issue in CI as the connection was being made too soon and
> tried to connect to the previous test's server. This causes the
> `xcb_connect` request to hang because, although the socket existed,
> there was no data being provided. This blocked the code and caused the
> wayland backend to fail to launch.
> 
> The solution is to only create the x server connection once xwayland has
> fired the `ready` signal.

> x11: _geometry_getter() should only concat _ once
> 
> While profiling Qtile, one of the top ten allocations was:
> 
>     7   x11/window.py:103                        6.7 KiB
>         return getattr(self, "_" + attr)
> 
> ...which is a silly allocation. We can just move the math to find the
> underlying attribute outside of the closure, and then it will only be
> computed once when the getter is defined, instead of every time it is
> called.
> 
> Let's also do the same for setattr while we're here, although it didn't
> show up in my profile.
> 
> Signed-off-by: Tycho Andersen <tycho@tycho.pizza>

> [wayland] change foreign toplevel activation callback
> 
> Foreign toplevel activation requests just focused the window via the
> compositor but didn't change the group. This meant input was being
> directed to a window that may not have been visible.
> 
> This PR changes the way we handle activation requests. Instead, we treat
> them like we do in X11 i.e. an activation request from a third party
> client (such as `rofi`) will depend on how `focus_on_window_activation`
> is set in the user's config.

> Support building without wayland backend
>

> `backend=wayland` that can be used to disable building the Wayland
> backend entirely, rather than trying to build it anyway. This is
> important for redistributors who need to ensure reproducible build
> irrespective of whether Wayland dependencies are installed in the build
> environment or not. The automatic behavior is preserved if neither value
> is passed.

> as well -- it's not exactly helpful when you see a bunch of successful
> compilations followed by "Warning: Wayland backend not built. Backend
> will not run."

> bar: preserve bar and widget references during finalization
> 
> The core insight here is: finalization is for the resources allocated by a
> bar or widget, not deleting the bar or widgets themselves. If we do that,
> then when people turn their monitors back on, we will have mutilated their
> configs, deleting the bars.
> 
> Instead, we should finalize these python objects, since they know how to
> re-allocate the resources as necessary on _configure() again if someone
> re-attaches a screen. However, we do not do silly things like
> widgets.clear() (deleting all the widgets from a bar), or
> screen.top = None, removing the widget from the Screen.
> 
> This lets us revert 99c8a54b026d ("x11: don't ignore powered off
> monitors"), since we really do want to ignore powered off monitors, but we
> couldn't before because we were deleting widgets and bars from configs when
> the monitors were disconnected.
> 
> Fixes #5436
> 
> Signed-off-by: Tycho Andersen <tycho@tycho.pizza>

> Previously focus, regardless of origin, would ungrab click on windows

- 0c5e1285124eaef419c93519de7465e95cbe64a3 — https://github.com/qtile/qtile/commit/0c5e1285124eaef419c93519de7465e95cbe64a3
> *: drop some __future__ and TYPE_CHECKING imports
> 
> Move imports out of `if TYPE_CHECKING:` blocks to real module-level imports
> where it doesn't cause circular imports, and drop the accompanying
> `from __future__ import annotations` where possible. Forward references to
> still-needed TYPE_CHECKING-only imports are preserved, and the few files
> that still require them (e.g. for self-referential annotations or known
> circular dependencies between backend, config, manager, etc.) keep both
> the guard and the future import.
> 
> We can remove all of these __future__ and imports and TYPE_CHECKING guards
> once our lowest supported python version is 3.14, which imports PEP 649,
> deferred evaluation of annotations: https://peps.python.org/pep-0649/
> 
> This gets rid of ~300 lines of boilerplate that I often find inscrutable:
> "when should I put this in TYPE_CHECKING? when should I not? why the
> difference?".
> 
> Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

> [wayland] Fix segfault if window dies while Prompt open
> 
> When the prompt widget is open, it saves a reference to the current
> window. When the widget releases the keyboard, it tries to focus the
> previously focused window. If that window has been closed then the
> wayland backend tries to focus a view object that has already been freed
> in the backend, resulting in a segfault.
> 
> The fix is to check whether qtile is still managing the window before
> trying to focus it.
- 1f87c443c447cd3447e3b3f99373f5cddf76e25f — https://github.com/qtile/qtile/commit/1f87c443c447cd3447e3b3f99373f5cddf76e25f
> Fix Volume widget crash on reload
> 
> The Volume widget has a background task to check for volume changes.
> This task is not cleared when the config is reloaded and so tries to
> draw the bar with references to finalised `Drawer` and `TextLayout`
> objects.
> 
> This PR ensures the task is deleted when the widget is finalised.
> 
> Fixes #5886

> the hook exists but points to a non-existent window. This causes a
> segfault on wayland as we call `hide` on a destroyed window.

> prompt widget: options for block, invisible, and bar cursor
> 
> Added a new option `cursor_type` to the prompt widget. By default
> it is set to 'line', which is the regular appearance of the cursor.
> The other options are 'block', 'none', and 'bar'.
> 
>   - Block inverts the color of the character the cursor is on, instead
>     of drawing and underline.
>   - None does not show a cursor, but still applies the cursor color to
>     the selected character.
>   - Bar shows a Unicode character representing a bar. This looks nice at
>     the end of the text.

> Fix window lost focus when dragged between screens
> 
> Floating windows lose their focus border when dragged between screens. This is
> because the floating layout draws the border if client.has_focus is
> True. This is the case if the window is equal to qtile.current_window.
> qtile.current_window looks at the active group on the current screen.
> However, when dragging windows, we only change screen focus after the
> window has been added to the other group so qtile.current_window is
> looking at the old screen.
> 
> Fixes #5843

- ffaf391d8d3a722a431dc228da0036d4fc887ba5 — https://github.com/qtile/qtile/commit/ffaf391d8d3a722a431dc228da0036d4fc887ba5
> wayland: dispatch pointer enter/leave/motion to bar widgets
> 
> Like x11, bar widgets need mouse_enter / mouse_leave to drive things
> like tooltips. On x11 the EnterNotify / LeaveNotify / MotionNotify path
> already feeds Bar.process_pointer_* on each bar window. On wayland
> nothing was firing those, so hover callbacks (e.g. qtile-extras'
> TooltipMixin) never ran.
> 
> The qw_view returned by qw_server_view_at is already enough — when it
> points to an Internal view, fire pointer_internal_event_cb after the
> existing focus update. Track the previous wid in qw_cursor so each
> transition produces one ENTER / LEAVE / MOTION event. The python side
> just forwards into win.process_pointer_*, which is the same dispatch
> x11 uses.
> 
> No extra hit-testing on the hot path: the scene graph lookup was
> already running for ordinary pointer focus.

>

> fix(bar): stop drawing finalized widgets and bars
> 
> Qtile._finalize_configurables() finalizes widgets before bars, so a
> Bar._actual_draw() queued on the event loop before reload_config or
> restart could run against dead widgets (drawer.ctx and layout are
> None). Every restart then logged "error when calculating widget ...
> length" and "Widget failed to draw" tracebacks.
> 
> Guard the draw/length boundary with the existing finalized state:
> 
> - _Widget.length returns 0 once the widget is finalized
> - Bar._actual_draw() skips finalized widgets
