> Replace ; with && in sparse-checkout script to prevent commands running after clone failure
> 
> If git clone fails, subsequent commands (cd, sparse-checkout set, cp) would
> execute in the wrong directory, potentially mutating the sparse-checkout config
> of an unrelated repo. Using && ensures the script aborts on first failure.

#### 1. V0.6.0 / V0.6.0 Clarity ☀️

item_id: tw93/kaku::release::294389894
Data: 2026-03-08T12:18:16Z
URL: https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/releases/tag/V0.6.0

Release notes (texto original):

> <div align="center">
>   <img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tw93/Kaku/main/assets/logo.png" alt="Kaku Logo" width="120" height="120" />
>   <h1 style="margin: 12px 0 6px;">Kaku V0.6.0</h1>
>   <p><em>A fast, out-of-the-box terminal built for AI coding.</em></p>
> </div>
> 
> ### Changelog
> 
> 1. **Light Theme Improvements**: Kaku now brings a more polished light theme with dynamic font weight, improved ANSI colors, and Claude Code-specific color overrides, including better quote background rendering.
> 2. **AI Usage Visibility**: The AI settings panel now shows usage summaries and remaining quota more clearly, with added Kimi Code support, Kimi usage tracking, background loading, and more reliable Claude OAuth token refresh persistence. Custom request headers (`custom_headers`) can now also be set in the config file for private or proxied deployments.
> 3. **Interactive Settings TUI**: `kaku config` is now a richer interactive settings editor with save-on-exit behavior, theme-aware updates, and more reliable config syncing.
> 4. **Better Tab Workflow**: Tabs can now be reordered with drag and drop, renamed inline by double-clicking, reopened with `Cmd + Shift + T` after closing, or renamed programmatically via the `kaku set-tab-title` command.
> 5. **Path Hyperlinks**: Terminal output now supports opening file path hyperlinks directly, with better handling for relative paths and decoded file paths.
> 6. **Smarter Shell Integration**: Improved first-run shell setup without Homebrew, fixed zsh source line escaping, repaired Starship right prompt leakage after `Ctrl + C`, removed the forced `TERM=kaku` setting that broke the Delete key over SSH, and made AI shell hooks more reliable when `TERM` falls back to `xterm-256color`.
> 7. **Selection and UI Polish**: Preserved text selection during terminal output, fixed stale window padding overrides, improved fullscreen inset and padding alignment, and unified selection colors across displays.
> 8. **macOS Input and Window Fixes**: Fixed non-Latin IME blocking `Cmd + alnum` shortcuts, fixed `Cmd + Shift + Symbol` key bindings, improved dead key handling, fixed Turkish keyboard tilde input, and improved fullscreen, maximize, display refresh, and global hotkey restore behavior.
> 9. **Terminal, Memory, and Notification Improvements**: Added a Dock badge for unread bell notifications, improved scrollback memory with lazy allocation, capped background image and gradient render cache sizes for more stable long-session memory usage, and further improved update actions, menu command handling, and terminal interaction reliability.
> 10. **Release and Upgrade Hardening**: Hardened the automated release pipeline, centralized config migration metadata, and bumped the config migration version to `14` so existing users receive the required shell integration refresh and prompt helper fix.
> 
> ### 更新日志
> 
> 1. **浅色主题优化**：Kaku 这次重点打磨了浅色主题，支持动态字重，优化了 ANSI 配色，并补充了针对 Claude Code 的颜色覆盖，包括更自然的引用背景显示效果。
> 2. **AI 剩余用量显示**：AI 设置面板现在可以更直观地显示 usage 摘要和剩余额度，新增了 Kimi Code 支持、Kimi usage 统计、后台加载，并改进了 Claude OAuth token 刷新后的持久化逻辑。同时支持在配置文件中设置 `custom_headers`，方便私有化或代理部署场景使用。
> 3. **交互式设置 TUI**：`kaku config` 现在是更完整的交互式设置界面，支持退出即保存、主题感知更新，以及更稳定的配置同步体验。
> 4. **标签页工作流升级**：现在支持拖拽调整标签顺序、双击内联重命名、通过 `Cmd + Shift + T` 重新打开刚关闭的标签页，以及通过 `kaku set-tab-title` 命令从脚本或外部工具重命名标签页。
> 5. **路径超链接支持**：终端输出中的文件路径现在可以直接点击打开，同时改进了相对路径和解码后路径的处理。
> 6. **Shell 集成改进**：优化了无 Homebrew 场景下的首次 shell 初始化，修复 zsh source line 转义问题、Starship 在 `Ctrl + C` 后泄漏右提示符文本的问题，移除了强制 `TERM=kaku` 设置（该设置会导致 SSH 远端 Delete 键失效），并提升了 `TERM` 回退到 `xterm-256color` 时 AI shell hooks 的兼容性。
> 7. **选区与界面细节优化**：终端输出过程中不再破坏文本选区，修复陈旧 window padding 覆盖问题，优化全屏 inset 与 padding 对齐，并统一了不同显示器下的选区颜色表现。
> 8. **macOS 输入与窗口修复**：修复了非拉丁输入法阻塞 `Cmd + 字母/数字` 快捷键、`Cmd + Shift + Symbol` 组合键不响应、死键处理异常、土耳其键盘波浪号输入问题，并改进了全屏、最大化、显示器刷新和全局快捷键恢复等行为。
> 9. **终端、内存与通知体验优化**：新增未读 bell 的 Dock badge，Scrollback 改为懒加载并对背景图和渐变渲染缓存设置大小上限，长时间使用后内存占用更稳定，同时继续打磨更新菜单、命令执行和终端交互链路中的稳定性。
> 10. **发布与升级链路加固**：补强了自动发布校验，统一了配置迁移元数据，并将配置迁移版本提升到 `14`，确保老用户能正确收到这次 shell 集成刷新和 prompt helper 修复。
> 
> Special thanks to @frankekn, @ddnio, @GavinRiver, and @nguyenphutrong for their contributions to this release. If Kaku helps you, please consider giving it a star and recommending it to your friends.
> 
> > https://github.com/tw93/Kaku

- 3bad1e98ad9864d1b949139784e3b7ac61b9850e — https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/commit/3bad1e98ad9864d1b949139784e3b7ac61b9850e
> fix(shell): override TERM=xterm-256color for ssh sessions
> 
> When SSHing from a Kaku local shell, TERM=kaku is forwarded to the
> remote machine but TERMINFO_DIRS is not, so the remote has no kaku
> terminfo. This causes zsh plugins (autosuggestions, syntax-highlighting)
> to fall back to broken rendering paths, producing garbled display
> (e.g. "ls -lh" appearing as "lss s -lh").
> 
> Add an ssh wrapper to kaku.sh that applies the same TERM override
> already used by Kaku's built-in SSH domain (mux/src/ssh.rs:271).
> 
> 🤖 Built with SMT <smt@agora.build>

> fix(macos): update OpenGL context after system wake to prevent crash
> 
> When macOS wakes from long sleep/lock, the GPU may be reset and OpenGL
> surfaces can become invalid. This caused crashes when AppKit tried to
> flush the backing layer for fullscreen windows.
> 
> Fix by listening to NSWorkspaceScreensDidWakeNotification and updating
> all OpenGL contexts when the system wakes up.

- 659a9f940baa765412098d6673363f8a7ada710e — https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/commit/659a9f940baa765412098d6673363f8a7ada710e
> config: use SipHasher24 for stable bytecode cache hashing
> 
> Replace DefaultHasher with SipHasher24 in bytecode_cache_path and
> source_content_hash. DefaultHasher output is not guaranteed to be
> stable across Rust versions, which could silently invalidate all
> Lua bytecode caches after a toolchain upgrade. SipHasher24 provides
> deterministic, version-stable hashing.
> 
> siphasher was already a workspace dependency; added it as a direct
> dependency for the config crate.

> feat: add Cmd+Shift+T to reopen last closed tab
> 
> Implements ReopenLastClosedTab key assignment, mirroring Chrome's
> Cmd+Shift+T behavior. When a tab is closed without a confirmation
> prompt, the active pane's working directory is pushed onto a
> per-window history stack (max 10 entries). Pressing Cmd+Shift+T
> pops the most recent entry and spawns a new tab at that directory.
> 
> Changes:
> - config/keyassignment.rs: add ReopenLastClosedTab variant
> - kaku-gui/commands.rs: register CommandDef with Cmd+Shift+T default
>   keybinding and add to compute_default_actions
> - kaku-gui/termwindow/mod.rs:
>   - add closed_tabs: VecDeque<PathBuf> field to TermWindow
>   - refactor close_current_tab to record cwd only when the tab is
>     actually removed (not before a confirm dialog that may be cancelled)
>   - extract push_closed_tab_cwd helper
>   - handle ReopenLastClosedTab in perform_key_assignment

- aea19684c8b2c90633e96d01b02eaf115e063f38 — https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/commit/aea19684c8b2c90633e96d01b02eaf115e063f38
> fix(selection): preserve text selection during active terminal output
> 
> Programs with frequent output (status bar animations, streaming logs,
> spinners) produce dirty lines every render frame. The previous
> check_for_dirty_lines_and_invalidate_selection would auto-clear any
> selection that overlapped with these dirty lines, making it impossible
> to select and copy text while output is active — the selection would
> vanish the instant the mouse button was released.
> 
> Remove the dirty-line selection invalidation entirely. Let user actions
> (click elsewhere, new selection, ESC) manage selection lifetime instead.
> This is consistent with Alacritty, iTerm2, and Kitty behavior, and also
> eliminates the per-frame get_changed_since() allocation overhead.

> fix: fill transparent gap between tab bar and pane content
> 
> When window_background_opacity < 1.0, the background fill strips did
> not account for tab bar height on the bottom side:
> 
> - bottom_fill_height was missing tab_bar_height (visible when tab bar
>   is at bottom, which is the default)
> 
> This left an unfilled strip between the pane content and the bottom
> tab bar where the desktop showed through with blur but no background
> color.
> 
> Consolidate padding calculations into a shared DimensionContext and
> remove the now-redundant bottom_reserved_for_right_strip variable
> since bottom_fill_height now includes everything.

#### 2. V0.10.0 / V0.10.0 Chat 🪄

item_id: tw93/kaku::release::320038053
Data: 2026-05-10T01:27:16Z
URL: https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/releases/tag/V0.10.0

Release notes (texto original):

> <div align="center">
>   <img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tw93/Kaku/main/assets/logo.png" alt="Kaku Logo" width="120" height="120" />
>   <h1 style="margin: 12px 0 6px;">Kaku V0.10.0</h1>
>   <p><em>A fast, out-of-the-box terminal built for AI coding.</em></p>
> </div>
> 
> ### Changelog
> 1. **AI Chat**: One engine, two surfaces: `Cmd+L` opens the in-terminal panel inside Kaku, while `k` or `kaku chat` drops the same engine into an alternate-screen TUI that works in any terminal or over SSH, with streaming Markdown, syntax highlighting, shell context, project tools, web search, memory, theme detection, safer cancel and approval semantics, and inline `#` queries that land in shell history.
> 2. **AI Configuration and Safety**: Assistant settings now use Simple and Deep models per task with live model loading, proxy-aware requests, OAuth setup, and broader provider responses, while stricter shell approvals, sensitive-path guards covering search and project tools, tighter file write and patch limits, failed-command context, and clearer parse errors keep the engine inside safe lines.
> 3. **Smart Close Protection**: `Cmd+W` and `Cmd+Shift+W` now ask before killing a pane that runs claude, codex, cursor-agent, gemini, vim, cargo, npm, or any non-shell process, while bare shells still close silently.
> 4. **Window Snapshots**: Kaku auto-saves multi-tab and multi-pane layouts, restored via `Cmd+Option+Shift+T`, Shell → Restore Previous Window, or the Command Palette.
> 5. **AppleScript Dictionary**: Kaku ships a full AppleScript dictionary, so windows, tabs, and panes are scriptable from Shortcuts, Hammerspoon, or any automation tool that drives macOS apps.
> 6. **Animated Tab Drag**: Drag a tab and the neighbors slide into place instead of snapping, so reordering reads as one fluid gesture.
> 7. **Softer Dark Theme**: Kaku Dark now uses lower-saturation highlight colors and a slightly dimmed foreground, reducing glare on long sessions while keeping the overall Kaku look.
> 8. **Cold Start and Shell Speed**: Faster startup through Lua bytecode caching, deferred font and config initialization, and cached shell user vars.
> 9. **Background Updates**: Updates download in the background and fail closed on checksum mismatch, with more reliable proxy and MacPorts detection along the way.
> 10. **Bug Fixes**: Fullscreen crashes, display races, resize gaps, cursor reflow, links, selection, light-theme readability, and TUI copy are all addressed.
> 
> ### 更新日志
> 1. **AI 对话**：同一套引擎，两种入口：`Cmd+L` 在 Kaku 内打开对话面板，执行 `k` 或 `kaku chat` 把同一套引擎放进 alternate-screen TUI，任何终端或 SSH 远端都能用，流式 Markdown、语法高亮、shell 上下文、项目工具、网页搜索、本地记忆样样齐全，主题自动识别、取消和审批语义更稳，`#` 查询自动存入 shell 历史。
> 2. **AI 配置与安全**：Assistant 设置改为 Simple Model 与 Deep Model，支持在线模型加载、代理感知请求、OAuth 配置以及更多 provider 响应格式，shell 审批更严，敏感路径保护扩展到搜索类工具，文件写入与 patch 上限收紧，失败命令上下文和解析错误一并更稳。
> 3. **智能关闭保护**：`Cmd+W` 和 `Cmd+Shift+W` 在 pane 里跑着 claude、codex、cursor-agent、gemini、vim、cargo、npm 这类有状态进程时会先弹确认，bare shell 仍然直接关。
> 4. **窗口快照**：Kaku 自动保存多 tab、多 pane 布局，需要时按 `Cmd+Option+Shift+T`，或从 Shell → Restore Previous Window、命令面板恢复。
> 5. **AppleScript 字典**：Kaku 内置完整 AppleScript dictionary，窗口、tab、pane 都能被 Shortcuts、Hammerspoon 等自动化工具脚本化驱动。
> 6. **拖拽标签页动画**：拖动 tab 时相邻 tab 会平滑让位，不再生硬切换，重新排序变成一个连贯的动作。
> 7. **深色主题更柔和**：Kaku Dark 默认调色板降低了高亮色饱和度，前景文字微微调暗，长时间盯屏更不刺眼，整体还是 Kaku 的风格。
> 8. **冷启动与 Shell 速度**：通过 Lua 字节码缓存、字体与配置延迟初始化、shell 用户变量缓存，启动更轻。
> 9. **后台更新**：更新改为后台下载，checksum 不通过则失败关闭，代理与 MacPorts 检测一并更稳。
> 10. **问题修复**：修复全屏崩溃和卡住、显示器竞态、resize 缝隙、光标 reflow、链接、选择、浅色主题可读性和 TUI 复制。
> 
> Special thanks to @s010s, @SherlockSalvatore, @darion-yaphet, @ddotz, @beautifulrem, @yxspace, and @fanweixiao for their contributions to this release.
> 
> > https://github.com/tw93/Kaku

- 0286c8ecdf9d1118eca4bf79fcc8a10659f9b490 — https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/commit/0286c8ecdf9d1118eca4bf79fcc8a10659f9b490
> fix(macos): avoid main-thread hang on display reconfiguration after lock-screen return
> 
> On wake from lock screen, SkyLight fires a display reconfig notification.
> AppKit handles it synchronously: it enumerates all windows, calls
> _setFrameCommon on each, and synchronously posts NSWindowDidResizeNotification.
> Kaku's did_resize: observer was then dispatching WindowEvent::Resized in-place,
> kicking off the full termwindow resize+paint chain while still inside the
> CFNotificationCenter callout frame. If paint state could not converge (e.g.
> font metrics changing mid-paint due to DPI change), the unbounded 'pass retry
> loop spun CPU at 100%, causing the not-responding hang users reported.
> 
> Fix 1 (defensive): cap paint_impl retry loop at MAX_PAINT_RETRIES (8) to
> prevent any future unbounded spin on the main thread.
> 
> Fix 2 (root cause): defer WindowEvent::NeedRepaint and WindowEvent::Resized
> (screen_changed only) to the next main-thread run-loop turn via
> Connection::with_window_inner, so the heavy render work runs after AppKit's
> notification dispatch unwinds. Live resize (screen_changed=false) keeps its
> synchronous dispatch to avoid introducing latency in normal window dragging.
- 05b13b0a9db84a47e4643b18a1a13f8a39075d3a — https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/commit/05b13b0a9db84a47e4643b18a1a13f8a39075d3a
> feat(tab-bar): animated tab drag and swap
> 
> Add smooth motion when dragging a tab across the tab bar: the dragged
> tab follows the pointer in real time, and other tabs interpolate back
> to their new slot after a swap via tab_position_animations keyed by
> tab index.
> 
> - TabDragState: add drag_offset_x for the live cursor-follow offset.
> - TermWindow: new tab_position_animations map (tab_idx -> (start, ease))
>   and helpers compute_tab_render_offsets / cleanup_tab_animations /
>   is_tab_being_dragged.
> - mouseevent.rs: drive drag_offset_x on pointer motion and seed the
>   easing curve on drop/swap.
> - render/fancy_tab_bar.rs, render/tab_bar.rs: shift tab geometry by the
>   computed render offset each frame.

> fix(copy): join visually-wrapped TUI rows when copy_unwrap_tui_lines=true (closes #275)
> 
> The previous Layer B heuristic checked phys.len() against term_cols, which
> fails for Ratatui and Ink renderers: phys.len() is lazy cluster length (not
> term_cols), and word-wrapped CLI output breaks before the terminal edge.
> 
> New behavior: when copy_unwrap_tui_lines is on, always treat every row as
> wrapped-to-next. At each join seam, leading whitespace on the continuation
> row is stripped and a single space separator is inserted, so Ink-indented
> word-wrap ("  wrap to the next row") joins cleanly without double spaces or
> bare concatenation. DECAWM mid-word wraps (no leading spaces) are appended
> directly.
> 
> fix(crash): abort on close while in native macOS fullscreen (closes #278)
> 
> AppKit fires windowWillExitFullScreen: synchronously inside [NSWindow close],
> which we call while Connection::with_window_inner already holds
> inner.borrow_mut(). The direct borrow_mut() in will_exit_fullscreen panicked
> and aborted via FFI unwind.
> 
> Change will_exit_fullscreen, will_enter_fullscreen, and the second borrow
> block in did_enter_fullscreen to use try_borrow_mut, matching the pattern
> already used by window_will_close and did_exit_fullscreen.

> fix(font): honor FE0F as wide and stop ZWJ from polluting fallback
> 
> Two emoji rendering bugs from the same shaping path:
> 
> 1. ZWJ sequences like 👩‍🚒 (U+1F469 200D 1F692) split into 👩 + 🚒.
>    The async fallback resolver iterated codepoint-by-codepoint, so
>    U+200D was treated as a missing glyph and pulled an arbitrary
>    text-presentation font into the chain just to "cover" it. That
>    font then competed with Apple Color Emoji and broke the GSUB
>    merge of the ZWJ cluster. Filter ZWJ/ZWNJ alongside the
>    already-filtered VS16/VS15 — they are format controls, not
>    glyphs to look up.
> 
> 2. Text-default emoji with FE0F (⏱️ ⏲️ ⚠️) rendered tiny because
>    grapheme_column_width returned 1 for (Text, Some(Emoji)). The
>    previous fix (ec592da) chose wcwidth alignment over visual
>    parity. Restore width=2 when FE0F is explicit: the tradeoff is
>    reversed — paste-time cursor desync is rare, but a permanently
>    shrunken ⏱️ next to a normal-sized 🎉 is a daily eyesore
>    (closes #315).
> 
> Verified with cargo nextest run -p wezterm-cell (8 passed) and
> make test (850 passed).

- 2ca17c011df8e53be9842e5adf25e80437f03dbe — https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/commit/2ca17c011df8e53be9842e5adf25e80437f03dbe
> fix(env): set RUNEWIDTH_EASTASIAN to match Kaku's ambiguous width setting
> 
> go-runewidth (used by bubbletea/lipgloss Go TUI apps) auto-detects CJK
> locale and treats East Asian Ambiguous chars (e.g. │ U+2502) as width=2,
> while Kaku defaults to narrow (width=1). This mismatch causes text to be
> truncated and misaligned in Go TUI apps like opencode on Chinese macOS.
> 
> Setting RUNEWIDTH_EASTASIAN=0 (or 1 if treat_east_asian_ambiguous_width_as_wide
> is enabled) makes go-runewidth match Kaku's terminal cell model, so character
> positions are consistent.
> 
> Fixes missing text in opencode status bar (issue #274).

> fix(ai-chat): wrap input across multiple rows so long prompts stay visible
> 
> The chat input was rendered on a single fixed terminal row, so anything
> wider than `inner_w` cols was silently chopped by `truncate()` even
> though the bytes stayed in `app.input`. Wrap the prompt+input string
> grapheme-by-grapheme up to `MAX_INPUT_VISIBLE_ROWS` (5) and grow the
> input box vertically; the message area shrinks accordingly. When the
> wrapped input overflows the cap, scroll within the input so the caret
> stays on the bottom visible row.
> 
> A phantom empty row is appended when the cursor sits at the trailing
> edge of an exactly-full row (or mid-string at a wrap boundary) so the
> caret never collides with the right border. Mouse click-to-reveal
> during streaming now treats the input as a row range, not a single row.

> 
> When compute_double_click_range returns an empty range (end <= start),

> fix(config): watch parent directory for atomic-rename compatibility
> 
> Editors like vim, VS Code, and JetBrains write config files via tmp+rename,
> swapping the inode. Watching the file path directly binds to the old inode
> and stops firing after the first save.
> 
> Switch to watching the parent directory with per-file filtering so any
> rename into the watched directory is detected. A reference-count map
> (dir_watch_count) ensures the directory watcher is released when all
> target files in that directory are unwatched.
> 
> Also restore ReloadConfiguration (Cmd+Shift+R) as a real manual reload
> so users have an escape hatch when the watcher misses an event.

> 
> Treat opencli as an optional, externally-installed helper rather than a
> bundled tool. When a request clearly needs the user's browser login
> state (their own X timeline, a SaaS console, content behind a login
> wall) and public web_search / web_fetch is unlikely to work, the
> assistant runs `command -v opencli` once, mentions it if installed,
> and falls back gracefully if missing. Skipped for ordinary tasks so it
> does not add noise to the common path.

> fix(shell): skip Up/Down rebind if external history tool already owns the key
> 
> atuin, mcfly, and similar tools bind the Up key to their own widgets.
> If they load before kaku.sh, Kaku was silently overwriting their binding.
> 
> Now check the emacs binding for ^[[A before applying: if it is no longer

> fix(gui): skip native-line-editor shortcut path under alt-screen
> 
> maybe_handle_native_line_editor_shortcut was built for zsh + the
> setup_zsh.sh widgets it pairs with. It rewrites Shift/Cmd/Option
> arrow keys and Cmd+A into Kaku-private escape sequences
> (\x1b[990~, \x1b[991~, \x1b[992~, \x1b[995~) and feeds Ctrl-B/F/A/E
> to collapse its internal selection anchor. That is correct in a
> shell prompt. Under alt-screen it is wrong: TUIs (Claude Code,
> vim, less, htop) do not parse those private sequences, and once
> the anchor sticks, plain arrow keys stop emitting CSI and start
> emitting Ctrl-B / Ctrl-F / Ctrl-A / Ctrl-E instead, poisoning
> cursor movement in the TUI's own input widget.
> 
> Early return from the helper when pane.is_alt_screen_active() is
> true, after clearing any stale anchor so state doesn't leak back
> into a subsequent shell prompt session. Shell-prompt selection
> behavior stays unchanged. Precedent: SendStringIfNotAltScreen in
> d0a8938 uses the same gate.

- 8a7f25a58e2aba7d7bb1f77dd367d32d3e2d512c — https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/commit/8a7f25a58e2aba7d7bb1f77dd367d32d3e2d512c
> fix(macos): skip screen-parameter refresh when topology is unchanged
> 
> NSApplicationDidChangeScreenParametersNotification fires often on
> setups with menubar customizers (sketchybar, iStat Menus) and
> during AX-driven window moves (Raycast "move to next screen",
> yabai, AeroSpace). Every notification ran
> refresh_all_window_contexts_after_display_change, which arms a
> 150-300ms OpenGL present defer per window and sets screen_changed
> on the next Resized, forcing termwindow::resize through its full
> DPI and font-metric recompute path. On cross-screen hotkey moves
> the result was a beachball and a visible stall, even when the
> actual display topology had not changed at all.
> 
> Capture each NSScreen's (localizedName, frame, backingScaleFactor)
> into a static Mutex<Option<Vec<ScreenSig>>> snapshot. When the
> notification fires, rebuild the snapshot and compare. Matching
> snapshot = log trace and return immediately, no refresh, no paint
> defer. Real monitor attach/detach/resolution change still
> proceeds because the snapshot diverges.

>

>   so the model can request larger output for deep inspection.

>

> poked into the clipped arcs even after opting out. Thread the flag into
> both sites so the opt-out actually takes effect.

>   open/close so the new padding takes effect immediately, not on the
>   next external resize.

> - Shorten BlinkingBar / SteadyBar cursors to ~75% of cell height and
>   vertically center them on the x-height. Stops the cursor from
>   stretching the full cell-top to cell-bottom on tall line-height
>   configs.

> fix(macos): use user's intended scheme for initial window_frame
> 
> The bundled config builds config.window_frame from get_window_frame_colors
> keyed on config.color_scheme, which has already been resolved against the
> system appearance by line 3966. When a Dark-theme user runs on a Light
> system, config.color_scheme resolves to 'Kaku Light' before the user's
> kaku.lua override (`config.color_scheme = 'Kaku Dark'`) takes effect, so
> window_frame ends up with Light colors (border_top_height=1,
> border_top_color=#FFFCF0, active_titlebar_bg=#FFFCF0). The first frame on
> cold start renders that cream strip at the top until window-config-reloaded
> fires and build_managed_window_frame switches to the Dark colors.
> 
> Use is_user_light_theme() (already used to seed the font stack) to derive
> the user's intended scheme from a static read of their kaku.lua, then key
> window_frame off that. Dark-on-Light users now get Dark frame colors from
> the first frame; no extra work is added on the existing window-config-reloaded
> path.

> fix(ai-chat): eliminate cursor/border flicker during long-text scrolling
> 
> Root cause: the GPU render thread could read the terminal buffer mid-frame,
> seeing the cursor at (0,0) after ClearScreen but before the final cursor
> reposition, causing the visible jump to the top-left corner.
> 
> Fix: wrap every render frame with DEC synchronized output (mode 2026):
>   \033[?2026h ... all changes ... \033[?2026l
> 
> The mux layer already supports this (mux/src/lib.rs:382-406): it holds all
> terminal actions received inside the sync window and flushes them atomically
> when the window closes, so the GPU renderer only ever sees complete frames.
> Cursor hide/show is also added at frame boundaries as belt-and-suspenders.
> 
> Applied to both render_chat() and render_picker().
> 
> Refactor: extract push_picker_row() helper to eliminate the duplicated
> five-line bordered-row pattern in the slash/attach picker branches.

> fix(macos): skip did_resize dispatch when window is closing
> 
> did_enter_fullscreen and did_exit_fullscreen already bail early when
> is_closing is set, but did_resize did not. AppKit will fire
> windowDidResize: during teardown (and did_exit_fullscreen explicitly
> calls did_resize as part of its transition cleanup), which then
> dispatches Resized into an already-closing TermWindow, costs a round
> of layout work, and can surface as rendering oddities on the last
> frame. Add the same early-return guard used by the fullscreen
> callbacks so the close path goes quiet end-to-end.
- a591e6f2b4ccea972ae679aec6cba1248b272f6f — https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/commit/a591e6f2b4ccea972ae679aec6cba1248b272f6f
> fix(ai-shell): move # query spinner to a dedicated line below the buffer
> 
> The previous spinner relied on ESC[s/[u to mark the end of the `# query`
> buffer and then redraw on each tick. zsh's accept-line widget calls
> `zle reset-prompt`, which clobbers the saved cursor slot, so the
> restore on the next tick wiped out the user's query text and left the
> spinner orphaned in the middle of the line.
> 
> Drop save/restore. The spinner now occupies its own row below the
> prompt, with the cursor parked one row further down between frames.
> Each frame uses ESC[1A + \r + ESC[K to reach the spinner row, redraw,
> and return to the parking row. On clear, ESC[1A + \r + ESC[K erases
> the spinner row, leaving the cursor where zsh's `\x15` prompt redraw
> will land, so the injected command's cursor naturally sits at the end.

> fix(ai-chat): add 10-minute timeout on tool approval wait
> 
> The agent loop blocked indefinitely on reply_rx.recv() while waiting
> for the user's approve / reject decision. In normal operation the
> channel is drained promptly (user response, overlay Drop rejects via
> disconnect), but any path that leaves pending_approval alive without
> ever sending a reply would pin the agent thread and freeze the
> conversation. Switch to recv_timeout with a 10-minute cap: if the
> timeout fires, treat it as a rejection and surface a ToolFailed so
> the transcript shows what happened. Intentional approvals in seconds
> are unaffected; the cap is a safety net, not a UX constraint.

> fix(crash): skip displayIfNeeded when closing fullscreen window (closes #278)
> 
> The previous try_borrow_mut fix was incomplete. The unsafe block calling
> setNeedsDisplay: and displayIfNeeded ran unconditionally, even when
> try_borrow_mut returned Err (the close-while-fullscreen path). displayIfNeeded
> triggers AppKit draw callbacks that attempted borrow_mut() on the already-held
> RefCell, producing the same panic-abort chain (confirmed by user on nightly
> 259defe).
> 
> Move the unsafe display block inside the if-let-Ok branch so it is skipped
> entirely when the borrow fails. Release inner with drop() before calling into
> AppKit so draw callbacks can re-borrow without conflict during normal fullscreen
> exit.

> fix(macos): disable OS resize_increments to fix Raycast maximize gap (#131)
> 
> Window managers using the Accessibility API (Raycast, Rectangle, Magnet,
> AeroSpace) drive resize through setFrame, which AppKit rounds to multiples
> of setResizeIncrements. On external displays where visibleFrame is not a
> clean multiple of cell size, the rounded target landed on a smaller
> default_frame and left a 36pt gap at the bottom of the screen.
> 
> apply_dimensions already absorbs cell-quantization slack into top padding,
> so OS-level resize_increments is redundant. Disable it in the bundled
> config and drop the kaku_zoom override added in e46c6bf: runtime
> diagnostics confirmed it was never invoked, since the AX path bypasses
> [window zoom:] entirely.

> perf(macos): reduce power consumption with opacity and runloop fixes
> 
> Five changes targeting the high 12-hr power score reported in #271:
> 
> 1. NSView is_opaque returns YES when window_background_opacity >= 1.0,
>    letting the compositor skip alpha blending on every frame.
> 2. CAMetalLayer + sublayers also set opaque at init and on config change.
> 3. CFRunLoopObserver changed from kCFRunLoopAllActivities to
>    kCFRunLoopBeforeWaiting, firing once per idle cycle instead of on
>    every runloop state transition.
> 4. visibility_changed skips window.invalidate() when the window is
>    occluded — no paint needed for a window behind other windows.
> 5. mux_pane_output_event coalesces invalidations to at most once per 8ms,
>    avoiding runloop wakeups faster than the 60fps render interval.

> 
> The cwd-escape check only fired when both canonicalize(&path) and
> canonicalize(cwd) returned Ok. Either failing silently fell through to
> File::open, letting a relative path with ../.. components read outside
> the working directory whenever cwd itself could not be canonicalized

> symlink segment). Make the check mandatory: canonicalize both sides

> error.

> fix(macos): pin NSAppearance and defer show until GPU surface is attached
> 
> Two related cold-start chrome hardening changes:
> 
> 1. apply_window_appearance pins the NSWindow's NSAppearance to the resolved
>    theme so NSTitlebarContainerView's vibrancy material does not render the
>    system appearance for one frame before the GPU layer presents real
>    content. This is the secondary defense for users who set a custom
>    window_frame and therefore bypass the bundled is_user_light_theme()
>    path.

> 2. window.show() now runs after the GPU surface is attached. Showing earlier
>    exposes a window of time where AppKit composites titlebar chrome before
>    the Metal layer has anywhere to draw, leaking system-appearance vibrancy
>    on a dark theme.
> 
> 3. is_light_color is hoisted into the config crate so window-chrome
>    decisions (NSAppearance) and renderer decisions (text contrast, glyph
>    weight) cannot drift apart.

> fix(config): exclude trailing punctuation and wrappers from file link (#290)
> 
> The implicit file-path hyperlink rule used `[^\s\)\]\}>]+`, which
> swallowed the trailing character past the end of the actual path:
> sentence punctuation (`.md.`, `.md,`, `.md?`), CJK particles attached
> without whitespace (e.g. Korean `docs/foo.md에`, `docs/foo.md를`), and
> matched wrapper characters (backticks, straight quotes). The resulting
> `file://...md에` URI pointed at a non-existent path and the click was
> a silent no-op.
> 
> Tighten the rule so the last matched character must be ASCII word,
> slash, or dash, relying on regex backtracking to drop anything
> trailing. Admit backticks and straight quotes as leading/trailing
> boundary characters so wrapped paths are still detected. `file:line`
> and `file:line:col` suffixes continue to match because they end in a
> digit. The rule remains extension-neutral: `.rs`, `.py`, `.ts`, `.go`,
> extensionless files like `Makefile`, and dotfile-style `.env.local`
> all behave identically.
> 
> Cover the behavior with unit tests for trailing ASCII punctuation,
> Korean particles, wrapping delimiters, line:col preservation, an
> absolute-path regression, and the extension-neutrality invariant.
- f0bf88762ca4227e5c5a3874e4415a3abb4a83e2 — https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/commit/f0bf88762ca4227e5c5a3874e4415a3abb4a83e2
> fix(ai-auth): use chrono for Copilot token expiry parsing
> 
> The hand-rolled ISO 8601 parser found the first '+' or last 'Z' to
> strip the timezone, which silently mistreated negative offsets like
> -05:00 as UTC (off by 5 hours). GitHub currently emits UTC so this
> worked in practice; an upstream change would have expired tokens
> early or treated expired tokens as fresh. chrono is already a
> workspace dependency.

> fix(update): hold staging lock during cleanup
> 
> P1 fix. cleanup_staged_update() previously called remove_dir_all without
> the staging lock, so a concurrent installer could be mid-write. Acquires
> StagedUpdateLock first; bails silently if another process holds it. The

#### 3. V0.12.2 / V0.12.2 Steadier

item_id: tw93/kaku::release::338860905
Data: 2026-06-13T00:58:19Z
URL: https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/releases/tag/V0.12.2

Release notes (texto original):

> <div align="center">
>   <img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tw93/Kaku/main/assets/logo.png" alt="Kaku Logo" width="120" height="120" />
>   <h1 style="margin: 12px 0 6px;">Kaku V0.12.2</h1>
>   <p><em>A fast, out-of-the-box terminal built for AI coding.</em></p>
> </div>
> 
> ### Changelog
> 1. **Sleep Wake**: After the Mac sleeps or an external display is unplugged, Kaku no longer freezes on a stale frame; rendering recovers right away while your tasks keep running.
> 2. **External Displays**: Dragging a window on an external display no longer makes it jump at the first move, and Window Center plus `--position` land on the right spot when screens use different scales.
> 3. **Selection**: In mouse-enabled apps such as Claude Code, holding the left button while scrolling no longer paints a selection highlight that cannot be cleared, and a plain click clears any leftover one.
> 4. **Yazi**: Newer Yazi versions refused to start with config files written by earlier Kaku; those files are now repaired automatically.
> 5. **Windows**: A new window opened into a fullscreen Space fills the screen right away, and cold start no longer flashes a second empty window.
> 6. **Updates**: Clicking the update notification now asks for confirmation first, so running tasks are no longer interrupted by a stray click.
> 
> ### 更新日志
> 1. **休眠唤醒**：合盖休眠或拔掉外接显示器后，Kaku 不再停在旧画面上假死，渲染会立即恢复，正在跑的任务不受影响。
> 2. **外接屏**：在外接显示器上拖动窗口不再在起手时跳一下，屏幕缩放不同时 Window Center 和 `--position` 也会落在正确位置。
> 3. **选区**：在 Claude Code 这类启用鼠标的应用里，按住左键滚动不再误画出无法清除的选区高亮，普通单击会清掉残留的高亮。
> 4. **Yazi**：新版 Yazi 会拒绝旧版 Kaku 写入的配置导致无法启动，现在这些配置文件会被自动修复。
> 5. **窗口**：在全屏 Space 中新开窗口会立即铺满整屏，冷启动也不再闪现第二个空窗口。
> 6. **更新**：点击更新通知会先弹出确认，不会再因误点直接关闭所有窗口、打断正在运行的任务。
> 
> > https://github.com/tw93/Kaku

> docs(config): #453 clarify blur radius is integer 0-100 in template
> 
> macos_window_background_blur is a pixel blur radius passed straight to
> CGSSetWindowBackgroundBlurRadius, so it takes an integer. It sat directly
> under window_background_opacity (a 0 to 1 float) in the generated template
> with no range hint, so users wrote fractional values like 0.4 and hit a
> F64 to i64 conversion error. Annotate both lines with their value ranges.

> fix(window): #452 repaint after resize so fullscreen new window fills screen
> 
> A new window opened into an existing macOS fullscreen Space only rendered
> in the top-left corner: webgpu.resize reconfigures the surface, but the
> CAMetalLayer drawable is sized only when a frame is actually painted, so
> it stayed stuck at the initial size until an incidental later resize.
> Invalidate after a real dimension change to force that paint immediately.
- 3b93a765a4a9c4e18fbd4e140a82f19e7faa0b30 — https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/commit/3b93a765a4a9c4e18fbd4e140a82f19e7faa0b30
> fix(window): suppress phantom second window on cold start
> 
> On first launch macOS fires applicationOpenUntitledFile while the normal
> startup pipeline is still building the first window, so both paths spawned
> a window and two empty windows appeared. The existing app_event_handler_ready
> guard flipped true inside frontend try_new, before the pipeline registered
> its window, leaving a race the deferred conn.windows check could not close.
> 
> Add an explicit ownership flag set synchronously before any AppKit event can
> fire and cleared once the first window registers. While set, the untitled-file
> handler defers to the pipeline; after the first window exists a later dock-icon
> reopen still spawns normally.
- 61fc31a68666a0086b7d5f0801f24d9e135baa21 — https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/commit/61fc31a68666a0086b7d5f0801f24d9e135baa21
> fix(yazi): #457 emit #:schema comment and migrate $schema keys in user configs
> 
> yazi >= 26.5.6 rejects a $schema key in theme.toml/keymap.toml, and the
> bare-key form from the #433 fix is invalid TOML, so yazi failed to start
> and Kaku's --version probe reported it as not found. Existing files were
> never repaired because setup only wrote headers when the file was
> missing. Write the supported #:schema comment everywhere and self-heal
> old configs at kaku init, in the yazi wrapper, and on Cmd+Shift+Y. The
> kaku.lua helper is nested because the top-level chunk sits at Lua's
> 200-local limit.
- 6c0a6a40b474d8462b5a47529c7e64c8f45bfd93 — https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/commit/6c0a6a40b474d8462b5a47529c7e64c8f45bfd93
> docs(agents): track macOS platform rules and product-docs skill
> 
> Publish two reusable agent docs alongside the existing maintainer-sweep
> skill: the macOS AppKit menu/window platform rules and the product-docs
> skill for keeping the kaku.fun docs accurate. The release skill stays
> local because it documents signing credentials, keychain setup, and
> machine-specific paths that must not enter public docs.
- 8e72ed4b6601b4e3f8bec64247d004fca32136aa — https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/commit/8e72ed4b6601b4e3f8bec64247d004fca32136aa
> ci: split fast checks from release-shaped build validation
> 
> Every push paid ~20 minutes of wall clock, 15 of which were two release
> builds (arm64 + x86_64) that almost never break from routine Rust changes
> and produce no artifacts; rapid push bursts cancelled them anyway, so the
> protection was mostly theoretical while the maintainer flow (CI green
> before issue replies) ate the full cost. Checks keeps the ~5-minute
> correctness gates on every push; Build Validation runs the universal and
> bundle builds only when the build pipeline changes, daily, or on dispatch,
> and release.sh preflight now requires its latest run to be green.
- 90c01e66a5d1cbe81b5f7164beb8ebd473f227f6 — https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/commit/90c01e66a5d1cbe81b5f7164beb8ebd473f227f6
> fix(window): #456 stop mixing display scales in drag and centering
> 
> MouseEvent::coords is in the window's own backing scale while
> screen_coords is normalized to the primary display's scale, so deriving
> the window origin as screen_coords - coords teleported the window when
> a manual title-bar drag started on an external display with a different
> scale. Platforms now capture the true content origin on each event and
> the drag applies only screen-space deltas to it. Window > Center had
> the same scale mixing via ScreenInfo.rect plus an unflipped Y, so
> centering moved into the macOS layer on the window's own screen.
- a834dda7987fdc7464456a0eb42a268f80aab4a3 — https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/commit/a834dda7987fdc7464456a0eb42a268f80aab4a3

> chore(assets): remove unused high-res kaku.jpeg
> 
> kaku.jpeg (3974x2484, ~950KB) had zero references repo-wide. kaku.jpg

- c8f8470c08e810aa4476b8fa9e11c26bc8d856ff — https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/commit/c8f8470c08e810aa4476b8fa9e11c26bc8d856ff
> fix(gui): #458 reconfigure wgpu surface after wake invalidates drawable
> 
> macOS sleep/wake and display unplug tear down the Metal drawable without
> changing window dimensions. The Lost/Outdated recovery called resize(),
> which deliberately no-ops on identical dimensions, so the surface was
> never reconfigured and rendering froze on the last frame while the PTY
> kept accepting input. A nil nextDrawable (mapped to SurfaceError::Timeout)
> was skipped silently forever with the same result. All earlier sleep/wake
> hardening only covered the CGL backend, never the default WebGpu path.
> Force surface.configure on Lost/Outdated, reconfigure after consecutive
> timeouts, and keep capped recovery repaints flowing so idle windows heal.
- d9e8500ea181527a51f1ac992692516dfb9e44b3 — https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/commit/d9e8500ea181527a51f1ac992692516dfb9e44b3
> fix(update): confirm before applying staged update to protect running tasks
> 
> Clicking the update toast applied the staged update immediately, closing
> every window and stopping any running terminal task with no confirmation.
> Route the toast click through the same confirmation overlay used for
> closing panes and for Cmd+Q quit, so the user must confirm before the
> restart. Also document the background auto-update behavior and the
> check_for_updates switch in configuration.md.
- e76048aee31cc4af6b202794ef97514e37b8e6a1 — https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/commit/e76048aee31cc4af6b202794ef97514e37b8e6a1
> fix(mouse): #455 stuck selection highlight in mouse-reporting panes
> 
> Claude Code >= 2.1.150 keeps xterm mouse tracking enabled, which exposed
> two holes in selection lifetime handling.
> 
> The wheel-extend fast path ran before the mouse-reporting gate, so a left
> press forwarded to the application still armed scroll-and-extend, and a
> Magic Mouse / trackpad scroll during the press conjured a screens-wide
> selection out of thin air. Wheel extension now requires that the press
> actually resolved to a selection assignment.
> 
> With dirty-line invalidation gone, a plain click was the only remaining
> clear path, but SelectTextAtMouseCursor bindings are gated on
> mouse_reporting=false, so the highlight could never be cleared in such
> panes. A forwarded plain left press now clears the stale GUI selection
> before reaching the application, matching iTerm2.
- e8ed93d2e91d8742e294d9ca316d736eed71e0bd — https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/commit/e8ed93d2e91d8742e294d9ca316d736eed71e0bd
> fix(scripts): restore executable bit on release.sh
> 
> Lost in the previous commit, which staged the file with a hardcoded
> 100644 mode; the release flow invokes it directly and other scripts
> gate on -x checks.
- f40e2daf307187dcd7261e9d37f381497af19268 — https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/commit/f40e2daf307187dcd7261e9d37f381497af19268
> revert(menu): remove Kaku Help item
> 
> Reverts 1d30806. Back out the contributor-added Help menu docs entry;
> command_rank_for_menu returns to a function-local helper.
- f9100581c4b78d3d56d7d23100b0a68f5c099b0d — https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/commit/f9100581c4b78d3d56d7d23100b0a68f5c099b0d
> fix(window): align ScreenInfo.rect with canonical ScreenPoint space
> 
> --position on Retina landed at a quarter of the requested point: resolved
> x/y went through two scale divisions, one inherited from upstream in
> build_window and one in screen_point_to_cartesian. Screen rects also used
> per-screen backing pixels with unflipped Y, so named-screen origins and
> Lua screens() disagreed with set_window_position/window:set_position on
> multi-monitor setups. Express ScreenInfo.rect in the canonical space and
> drop the extra x/y division; verified at runtime on a 2x dual-screen
> arrangement.

#### 4. V0.13.0 / V0.13.0 Faster

Release notes (texto original):

> <div align="center">
>   <img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tw93/Kaku/main/assets/logo.png" alt="Kaku Logo" width="120" height="120" />
>   <h1 style="margin: 12px 0 6px;">Kaku V0.13.0</h1>
>   <p><em>A fast, out-of-the-box terminal built for AI coding.</em></p>
> </div>
> 
> ### Changelog
> 1. **Startup & Prompt**: Kaku now does less work before the first frame and keeps shell, config, and font caches warm, so new windows and prompts feel faster.
> 2. **Default Prompt**: The bundled prompt now shows Git status and Node version while keeping the same compact terminal feel.
> 3. **Tab Titles**: Tabs stay path-focused by default, with an optional Command Tab Titles setting for showing running tools such as `project·claude`; split panes also keep their titles readable.
> 4. **AI Chat**: Long streaming conversations no longer re-highlight the whole chat on every update, keeping the AI panel smoother during large sessions.
> 5. **Window & Terminal Stability**: Moving between displays, half-intensity text, resizing terminals smaller, and deferred config setup are handled more reliably.
> 
> ### 更新日志
> 1. **启动与提示符**：Kaku 现在会在首帧前少做一些工作，并缓存 shell、配置和字体相关结果，新窗口和提示符响应会更快。
> 2. **默认提示符**：内置提示符现在会显示 Git 状态和 Node 版本，同时保留原本紧凑的终端观感。
> 3. **标签标题**：标签默认继续以路径为主，需要时可以打开 Command Tab Titles 来显示 `project·claude` 这类正在运行的工具，分屏标题也会保持可读。
> 4. **AI 聊天**：长对话流式输出时不再每次都重新高亮整段聊天，AI 面板在大段会话里会更顺。
> 5. **窗口与终端稳定性**：跨显示器缩放、半亮文本、终端缩小时的滚动历史，以及延迟配置初始化都处理得更稳。
> 
> > https://github.com/tw93/Kaku

> perf(shell): cache starship init, byte-compile kaku.zsh, bound prompt commands
> 
> - The generated kaku.zsh caches the output of 'starship init zsh
>   --print-full-init' keyed on the starship binary path + mtime (recorded
>   on the cache's first line). Stock init forks starship twice per new
>   shell (the stub it prints re-runs --print-full-init); a warm cache now
>   forks zero times. The cache is written via a per-pid temp file + rename
>   so concurrent first shells cannot interleave a truncated cache, and a
>   starship upgrade or relocation refreshes it automatically.
> - setup_zsh.sh byte-compiles the generated kaku.zsh; zsh's source prefers
>   the .zwc while it is not older than the source, so each new shell skips
>   parsing the ~1600-line file and a failed zcompile is harmless.
> - starship command_timeout drops from 10s to 2s: the prompt blocks on
>   module commands, so a hung git/node froze every new prompt for up to
>   10s. git_status also sets ignore_submodules to keep the per-prompt
>   working-tree scan cheap in repos with submodules.

#### 5. V0.17.0 / V0.17.0 Linked

item_id: tw93/kaku::release::363699887

Release notes (texto original):

> <div align="center">
>   <img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tw93/Kaku/main/assets/logo.png" alt="Kaku Logo" width="120" height="120" />
>   <h1 style="margin: 12px 0 6px;">Kaku V0.17.0</h1>
>   <p><em>A fast, out-of-the-box terminal built for AI coding.</em></p>
> </div>
> 
> ### Changelog
> 1. **Responses API and Native Search**: Choose `api_mode = "responses"` for Responses-compatible endpoints, and turn on provider-hosted web search without a separate search key.
> 2. **Pick Your Managed Shell**: `kaku init` can install zsh or fish on purpose, and Kaku keeps that choice across XDG config paths instead of only trusting `$SHELL`.
> 3. **Richer Terminal Clicks**: Cmd+Click opens bare domains like `github.com`, file links can launch your editor via `config.file_link_editor`, and Option+Click moves the cursor inside the current input line.
> 4. **Safer AI Tools**: Tool paths, web requests, and code search are harder to abuse; incomplete streams no longer look like successful turns.
> 5. **Stability Fixes**: Launch no longer dies on oversized draw batches, windows stay below the menu bar, top tabs line up with traffic lights, font fallback is safer, and shell state plus drag-select scroll behave more predictably.
> 
> ### 更新日志
> 1. **Responses API 与原生搜索**：兼容端点可选 `api_mode = "responses"`，并开启服务商托管的 web search，不必再配单独搜索 Key。
> 2. **自选托管 Shell**：`kaku init` 可明确安装 zsh 或 fish，选择会写入状态并在 XDG 路径间保持一致，不再只听 `$SHELL`。
> 3. **更完整的点击交互**：Cmd+Click 可打开 `github.com` 这类裸域名；文件链接可用 `config.file_link_editor` 指定编辑器；Option+Click 可在当前输入行内移动光标。
> 4. **更安全的 AI 工具**：路径、网络请求与代码搜索边界更严；流式被截断时不会再被当成成功回合。
> 5. **稳定性修复**：超大绘制批次不再导致启动崩溃，窗口不会拖进菜单栏后方，顶栏标签与红绿灯对齐，字体回退更安全，Shell 状态与拖选滚动也更稳。
> 
> Special thanks to @ddotz and @F1Justin for their contributions to this release.
> 
> > https://github.com/tw93/Kaku

> now falls back to the pre-XDG location on first read, the CLI mirrors the
> managed-shell choice into an existing default-location file, and reset
> cleans both. The GUI writer no longer serializes absent fields as null,
> which the repair paths treated as corruption; shell-side repair now fixes
> the version key in place instead of rebuilding the object, preserving
> window_position and unknown fields. init refuses a shell whose executable
> is missing and records the selection before setup so retries converge;
> doctor states which integration it checks when $SHELL disagrees.

> fix(ai): harden tool security and stream robustness
>

> self-correct instead of losing the turn. Responses mode always requests

> replay under store:false. TUI saves keep assistant.toml comments via
> toml_edit instead of stripping them on every write.

> fix(gui): keep selection drag scroll pinned at scrollback top
> 
> Dragging a selection with the cursor held above the pane auto-scrolls
> the viewport up one row per mouse event. Once the drag reaches the top
> of scrollback (or streaming output prunes the position), the #448
> normalization maps positions below scrollback_top to None, snapping
> the view back to the bottom. The next drag event then starts climbing
> from the bottom again, so the content never stays scrolled — the
> "infinite return to the original position" loop.

> - mouseevent.rs: clamp scrollbar-track page-up like the wheel path
> - mod.rs: while a selection drag is active, pin a pruned viewport to
>   the oldest remaining row instead of snapping to the bottom (new
>   drag_normalize_viewport); #448 follow-live-output behavior is
>   unchanged outside active drags
> - copy.rs: clamp copy-mode cursor-follow scrolls to scrollback_top

> (425 tests).

> fix(render): clamp draw counts to quad buffer capacity
> 
> Kaku crashes with SIGABRT on startup whenever a paint pass fails to
> converge before `MAX_PAINT_RETRIES` is exhausted. Reproduced 100% on
> macOS 26.5.2 (M4 Pro) by restoring a session snapshot containing a
> horizontal split where both panes carry restored scrollback:
> 
>     WARN  paint_impl retry loop exceeded 200ms (604ms)
>     panic at kaku-gui/src/termwindow/render/draw.rs:258:65 -
>       called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value
> 
> `StagingLayer::allocate()` intentionally keeps incrementing `next_quad`
> past `capacity` so that `need_more_quads()` can report the shortfall,
> but only writes `capacity` quads worth of vertices, and the index buffer
> only ever contains `capacity` quads worth of indices.
> `vertex_index_count()` reported the unclamped count, so any frame drawn
> while still over capacity indexed out of bounds:
> 
>   - OpenGL: `slice()` returns `None`, `unwrap()` aborts the process.
>   - WebGpu: `wgpu error: Index 23118 extends beyond limit 192`
>     (192 = the 32-quad sub-buffers created by `RenderLayer::new`),
>     also fatal.
> 
> Since the app auto-restores the same snapshot on launch, this turns
> into a crash loop that requires deleting `last_session.json` by hand.
> 
>   - Clamp `vertex_index_count()` to `capacity`; an unconverged frame now
>     renders truncated instead of aborting.
>   - Replace the two `unwrap()`s in the glium draw path with errors so a
>     future mismatch is logged rather than fatal.
>   - Track when the retry loop exits while still growing the quad
>     buffers and invalidate the window, so the truncated frame is
>     immediately replaced by a complete one.
> 
> Verified against the offending snapshot: V0.16.0 aborts every launch;
> with the clamp reverted but the error path kept, the run logs
> `vertex buffer slice 0..15288 is out of range for layer 0` at the exact
> same point; with the full patch the session restores and renders
> cleanly. `make fmt-check`, `make check` and `make test`
> (1296 + 15 tests) pass.

> fix(render): align VS15 symbol width and style with shell expectations
> 
> Forcing VS15 sequences to width 1 desynced the cursor from libc
> wcwidth(), which ignores variation selectors and counts East Asian Wide
> bases like U+2615 as 2 cells; fall through to per-char summation so the
> model matches the shell's arithmetic. Neither bundled monospace font nor
> PingFang covers these symbols, so text-presentation requests fell to the
> square Apple Color Emoji bitmaps and overlapped in single cells; insert
> Apple Symbols ahead of the emoji font so text style resolves to
> monochrome glyphs that fit their cell.

- 0e208614197aa736c02f3efce995a23fca2c8537 — https://github.com/umputun/remark42/commit/0e208614197aa736c02f3efce995a23fca2c8537
> fix(security): reject non-image content-types in image proxy and /picture/ to prevent stored XSS (#2067)
> 
> * fix(security): reject non-image content-types in image proxy and /picture/ to prevent stored XSS
> 
> The /api/v1/img proxy and /api/v1/picture/{user}/{id} endpoints emitted
> http.DetectContentType on the served bytes as the response Content-Type. A
> controlled upstream serving Content-Type: image/png with an HTML body passed
> the upstream check (only the response header was inspected, not the body),
> and the body bytes then sniffed back to text/html — so the proxy served the
> attacker's HTML from the remark42 origin. Browsers honoured the declared
> text/html and executed the response as a document with access to cookies and
> CSRF tokens. Affected from v1.6.0 (April 2020) through v1.15.0; verified live
> via published docker images.
> 
> Layered defense applied to both handlers:
> 
> - rest.SafeImgContentType (in backend/app/rest/) validates sniffed content
>   against a strict allowlist: image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp,
>   image/bmp, image/x-icon. Anything else (HTML, XML, SVG, plain text,
>   octet-stream, or any future image type the stdlib sniffer may learn) is
>   rejected with no body echo. SVG is implicitly excluded — it sniffs as
>   text/xml or text/plain, never image/svg+xml, and SVG can execute scripts
>   when navigated to top-level. The previous octet-stream → image/* fallback
>   is gone.
> - Per-endpoint Content-Security-Policy override sets
>   "default-src 'none'; sandbox; frame-ancestors 'none'" on every response
>   (success, 304, or error). Sandbox neuters scripts even if Content-Type
>   ever regresses. The same policy is also applied to all /api/v1/* via
>   apiCSPMiddleware as defense-in-depth.
> - Content-Disposition: inline; filename="image" frames the response as a
>   file rather than a renderable document.
> - /picture/ rejection paths set Cache-Control: no-store so 4xx responses
>   are never cached.
> 
> The defense headers and the strict ETag matcher are extracted as
> rest.SetImageDefenseHeaders and rest.EtagMatches in the shared rest package
> (consumed by both proxy/image and api/rest_public — no package cycle).
> 
> The /api/v1/img path additionally bumps the ETag to a versioned `"v2:..."`
> so revalidating clients (top-level navigation, Ctrl+R, intermediaries) get
> a fresh 200 instead of a 304 against poisoned pre-fix cached HTML.
> 
> DELIBERATE TRADEOFF: Cache-Control on /api/v1/img success responses remains
> max-age=2592000 (30 days), unchanged from before. An aggressive "force
> revalidate on every reuse" policy was prototyped during review but reverted
> because the perf cost (a server round-trip on every image view, even with
> 304 saving the body bytes) outweighed the corner-case mitigation. The
> realistic exposure of cache carryover is narrow: cache carryover only
> affects users who navigated top-level to an attacker URL pre-fix and still
> have it in their local cache — the normal <img> embed path cached text/html
> but never executed it. Local browser caches that hold pre-fix bytes
> continue to serve them until their 30-day TTL expires or are evicted under
> memory pressure. The ETag bump reaches all clients that DO revalidate
> during the cached lifetime (Ctrl+R, intermediaries, post-expiry use); for
> the rest, exposure self-limits via cache expiry. Operators running a
> CDN/edge cache in front of remark42 should purge /api/v1/img after deploy.
> 
> The /api/v1/img handler short-circuits on a matching current-version
> If-None-Match before any store Load or upstream fetch, returning a bodyless
> 304 with the defense headers set. Safe because the 304 carries no body and
> the client's cached bytes came from a prior validated 200; an attacker
> fabricating an etag value can only short-circuit fetches for URLs they
> themselves crafted. This avoids upstream DoS amplification when clients
> revalidate on hot comment pages.
> 
> The /api/v1/img route was moved from the "open routes" group (which uses
> middleware.NoCache, stripping If-None-Match from incoming requests) to the
> "open routes, cached" group alongside /picture/ and /qr/telegram so the
> 304 revalidation path is no longer broken upstream of the handler.
> 
> The /picture/{user}/{id} endpoint does not need the v2 etag prefix. Upload
> validates input format via readAndValidateImage and the serve path
> re-validates the stored bytes via rest.SafeImgContentType. Bytes within
> the resize dimension limits are preserved verbatim, so the browser defense
> relies on the response headers (validated Content-Type + nosniff + strict
> CSP + Content-Disposition: inline), not on byte normalization.
> 
> Global CSP: font-src data: → font-src 'none'. Audit confirmed no @font-face,
> no base64 fonts, no icon-font library in the bundle. Drops an unnecessary
> attack surface; no behavioural change.
> 
> Tests: TestImage_ContentTypeHandling table-tests a real PNG and attack
> shapes (HTML claimed as image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/svg+xml,
> image/webp; svg with onload; html fragment; polyglot PNG+HTML), proving
> the defense holds across arbitrary upstream Content-Type variation.
> Polyglot case is intentionally served as image/png — the browser cannot
> execute the trailing HTML when the response type is image/png with nosniff.
> TestImage_ContentTypeHandling_CacheHit exercises the cache-hit branch with
> attacker bytes preloaded into the store. TestImage_PerRequestRevalidation
> alternates upstream PNG/HTML across four proxy calls to prove no trust
> accumulates between requests. TestImage_RoutesUsingCachedImage asserts
> cache-poisoning is caught at serve time. TestImage_EtagVersioned asserts
> the v2 prefix invalidates pre-fix etags AND that the revalidation 304
> triggers no store Load. TestImage_RevalidationSkipsIO proves the
> short-circuit works even with no upstream reachable. TestSafeImgContentType
> covers the allowlist directly. TestRest_LoadPictureDefenseHeaders and
> TestRest_LoadPictureRejectsNonImage exercise the /picture/ endpoint.
> TestRest_apiCSP covers the strict CSP middleware on JSON API + RSS routes;
> TestRest_securityHeaders confirms /web/ HTML pages keep the global CSP.
> 
> Verified end-to-end against the dev docker image: the original demo URL
> (arbitrary HTML claimed as image/png) now returns 415 application/json with
> CSP/nosniff/Content-Disposition set, no XSS in the browser.
> 
> * fix(security): set Cache-Control: no-store on image-proxy error paths, sync stale route comment
> 
> Addresses two review comments on #2067:
> 
> 1. Cache-Control: max-age=2592000 and Etag were set before the
>    load/download/validation block, so 404/400/415 error responses inherited
>    the 30-day cache TTL and the versioned etag — a transient failure (or an
>    intentionally triggered 415) would be pinned in browser/intermediary
>    caches for that TTL, keeping users locked out even after the underlying
>    cause was resolved. Now: etag is computed but not set as a header until
>    after validation succeeds; error paths route through sendImageProxyError
>    which sets Cache-Control: no-store and never sets Etag. The 304
>    short-circuit still sets both because that path serves the same validated
>    content the client already has cached.
> 
> 2. The comment at rest.go:282 still described the prototyped
>    no-cache/must-revalidate Cache-Control policy that was reverted before
>    the PR landed. Updated to match the actual 30-day max-age behavior.
> 
> Tests: TestImage_ContentTypeHandling now asserts reject paths carry
> Cache-Control: no-store and have no Etag header, and accept paths carry
> the max-age=2592000 + v2: etag.

> fix(api): reject path traversal and sanitise error in /picture/{user}/{id}
> 
> The unauthenticated GET /api/v1/picture/{user}/{id} handler concatenated the
> two URL params verbatim into a filesystem path via path.Join, so a request
> like /api/v1/picture/../remark.db resolved to <base>/../remark.db, escaping
> the image directory. With Partitions=0 (a documented option) this is a
> direct arbitrary-file read; with the default Partitions=100 the constructed
> path lands in a CRC-derived subdirectory but the server still leaks the
> internal filesystem path back to the unauthenticated caller via the JSON
> error body — confirmed against demo.remark42.com (master-80c12a3) which
> returned `stat /var/folders/.../staging/.../remark.db` for `..` requests.
> 
> Validate both URL segments via safePictureSegment (no traversal markers,
> no path separators, no NULs) at the handler entry, and replace the raw
> storage error with a generic "image not found" response. The original
> error is logged for operators.
> 
> Reproduction test asserts that ../remark.db, foo/..%2Fremark.db and
> %2E%2E/remark.db all return 400 with no internal path leaked.

- 78d6de6bce1e961f023969da3ec8a00dd80c9ae8 — https://github.com/umputun/remark42/commit/78d6de6bce1e961f023969da3ec8a00dd80c9ae8
> Add X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy security headers
> 
> Add two missing security headers to the existing securityHeadersMiddleware:
> 
> - X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff — prevents browsers from MIME-sniffing
>   responses away from the declared Content-Type, stopping e.g. a
>   user-uploaded image from being reinterpreted as executable HTML/JS
> 
> - Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin — limits URL information
>   leaked in the Referer header on cross-origin requests to just the origin
>   (no path), and sends nothing at all on HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrades

- 8224626ed46d10e98d8fee29c9e9e1083a82b12c — https://github.com/umputun/remark42/commit/8224626ed46d10e98d8fee29c9e9e1083a82b12c
> fix(image): reject decompression-bomb dimensions before raster decode
> 
> readAndValidateImage caps the byte size of incoming images but the resize()
> helper that follows still called image.Decode unconditionally, allocating
> pixel memory proportional to the *declared* image dimensions. A ~100 KB
> compressed PNG or GIF that declares 65535x65535 px forces image.Decode to
> allocate ~17 GB of raster, OOMing the service on a single comment upload
> (or on the proxy's CacheExternal path when caching a malicious upstream).
> 
> Hardening:
> 
> - maxImagePixels = 16 MP constant. Covers any realistic image (~4096x4096)
>   while bounding peak allocation.
> - resize() now runs image.DecodeConfig first (cheap, no pixel allocation)
>   to read declared width/height before any full decode.
> - Multiplication of width × height uses int64 to defeat 32-bit overflow
>   (GOARCH=386, 32-bit arm): on those targets, int(cfg.Width)*int(cfg.Height)
>   could wrap below maxImagePixels and bypass the cap. GIF's 16-bit logical
>   screen and JPEG's 16-bit SOF dimensions both reach this if int-multiplied.
> - Bytes exceeding the cap, or non-image input that fails DecodeConfig,
>   return nil. prepareImage propagates the rejection as a clear error
>   instead of storing the malformed/oversized data verbatim.
> - The no-resize-needed path returns the validated original bytes verbatim
>   so animated GIFs round-trip without being flattened to a single frame.
> 
> The DecodeConfig precheck applies even when MaxWidth/MaxHeight are 0
> (resize disabled) — the dimension cap is unconditional defense-in-depth.
> 
> Two adjacent fixes surfaced by the new resize contract:
> 
> 1. readAndValidateImage previously did `data[:512]` without a bounds check,
>    panicking on any body shorter than 512 bytes. Now bounded with min().
> 2. image/webp was listed as an allowed format but no WebP decoder was
>    registered, so DecodeConfig would refuse legitimate WebP uploads. Added
>    `_ "golang.org/x/image/webp"` (already in go.mod via x/image/draw) so
>    the registered decoders match the allowlist.
> 
> Tests:
> 
> - TestService_resizeRejectsDecompressionBomb builds a 14-byte GIF87a header
>   declaring 65535x65535 and asserts resize() refuses it both at the unit
>   level and through SaveWithID end-to-end (no store write).
> - TestService_SaveWithIDShortPayload regression-tests the short-body panic.
> - TestService_SaveWithIDWebP regression-tests WebP round-trip through
>   prepareImage with the new DecodeConfig requirement.
> - TestService_resize subtests updated to assert non-image bytes are now
>   refused (previously the helper fell back to returning the raw bytes
>   verbatim, letting malformed content reach the store).

- a4c5e17bbb0188d45911d8ece7468a730f7c8499 — https://github.com/umputun/remark42/commit/a4c5e17bbb0188d45911d8ece7468a730f7c8499
> Probe /auth/status from frontend to avoid 401 on /user (closes #1188) (#1763)
> 
> * Probe /auth/status from frontend to avoid 401 console noise on /user
> 
> GET /api/v1/user requires auth and returns 401 for anonymous visitors,
> which the browser logs to console even when JS catches it. Probe
> /auth/status first (always 200), then fetch /user only when logged in.
> Stale auth cookies are cleared when status reports "not logged in" to
> preserve the cleanup-on-probe behaviour previously triggered by /user 401.
> 
> Closes #1188.
> 
> * Don't clear auth cookies when /auth/status probe itself fails
> 
> A transient network/5xx on the /auth/status probe used to fall through
> into the cookie-clear branch and silently log the user out on the next
> page load. Distinguish "probe failed" (null) from explicit "not logged
> in"; only the latter clears JWT/XSRF cookies. Lock the distinction with
> a negative assertion in the probe-failure test.
> 
> Also align packages/api prettier config with apps/remark42 (trailingComma: 'es5')
> so future edits don't sweep unrelated trailing commas into the diff.

> - strings.SplitSeq replacing strings.Split in range (avoids allocation)
> - strings.CutPrefix replacing HasPrefix+TrimPrefix
> - min() replacing manual if/else

> existing serialisation behaviour.

- c26f45e55ee2f239c3f303eb30296825c0df6f1e — https://github.com/umputun/remark42/commit/c26f45e55ee2f239c3f303eb30296825c0df6f1e
> Clean up deprecated CSS and fix silent CSS bugs in frontend (#2012)
> 
> * frontend: remove deprecated iframe attrs and non-standard CSS
> 
> Three separate cleanups:
> 
> 1. remove deprecated HTML attributes from iframe creation (create-iframe.ts)
>    - frameborder="0": deprecated since HTML5; border is already set to none via CSS
>    - allowtransparency="true": non-standard Microsoft attribute never in any spec;
>      transparency is handled by body { background: transparent } in CSS instead
>    - scrolling="no": deprecated since HTML5; overflow is already hidden via CSS
>    - horizontalscrolling/verticalscrolling: non-standard IE-era attributes with
>      no effect in modern browsers; remove without replacement
> 
> 2. replace allowtransparency with explicit CSS (global.css)
>    - add background: transparent to body; this is the spec-correct way to make
>      an iframe document transparent, as documented by MDN
> 
> 3. drop -moz-touch-enabled media query prefix (5 comment CSS files)
>    - -moz-touch-enabled was a Firefox-only non-standard media feature removed
>      in Firefox 58 (2018); pointer: coarse is the standard equivalent and was
>      already present as the second condition in every query, so removing the
>      dead -moz prefix reduces the media query to just (pointer: coarse)
> 
> note: colorScheme: 'none' in create-iframe.ts is intentionally left unchanged;
> it is tracked by #1430 and requires a broader color-scheme implementation
> 
> * frontend: fix CSS bugs and replace deprecated properties
> 
> Bugs fixed:
> 
> - comment-votes.module.css: add missing comma between transition values;
>   without it the shorthand was invalid and colour transitions on vote
>   buttons were silently ignored
> 
> - icon-button.module.css: fix "transfrom" typo (should be "transform");
>   the misspelling made the transition declaration a no-op, so the hover
>   scale animation jumped instantly instead of easing
> 
> - auth.module.css: remove doubly-nested rgb(rgb(var(…))) call; the outer
>   rgb() rejected the inner rgb() result, so the .title element's colour
>   fell back to inherited instead of the intended --secondary-text-color
> 
> Deprecated properties replaced:
> 
> - comment-form__markdown-toolbar.css: replace deprecated clip: rect()
>   with clip-path: inset(50%); clip was deprecated in CSS Masking Level 1
> 
> - raw-content.css: replace word-wrap with overflow-wrap; word-wrap was
>   renamed in CSS Text Level 3, all current browsers support overflow-wrap
>

> fix(auth): close OAuth open-redirect by wiring AllowedRedirectHosts (#2049)
> 
> * fix(auth): close OAuth open-redirect by wiring AllowedRedirectHosts
> 
> Bump go-pkgz/auth/v2 to master (v2.1.2-0.20260421203319-686683f19cf7)
> which carries the `from` redirect validator from go-pkgz/auth#275.
> 
> The library default with a nil AllowedRedirectHosts is permissive
> (preserves legacy behavior for existing consumers on a dep bump), so
> just bumping the dep leaves remark42 vulnerable — a crafted
> /auth/<provider>/login?from=https://evil.example.com/... still issues
> the 307 to the attacker host after the user completes legitimate
> OAuth. Verified end-to-end against a local dev-auth instance before
> and after this commit.
> 
> Wire Opts.AllowedRedirectHosts in getAuthenticator to the operator's
> existing --allowed-hosts config, stripping the CSP "self" sentinel
> which is not a real hostname. RemarkURL's own host is always implicit
> per the library contract, so a default single-site deployment gains
> the protection with no config change. Multi-host embeds work as soon
> as their embedding hosts are added to AllowedHosts (they already need
> to be there for CSP frame-ancestors).
> 
> Refreshed vendor tree to match the new module version.
> 
> * chore(lint): suppress G703 false positives on image Save
> 
> CI's newer gosec flags os.MkdirAll/os.WriteFile in FileSystem.Save with
> G703 because id flows in from the caller. id is validated at the HTTP
> layer (safePictureSegment in rest_public.go) and dst is derived via
> f.location — not a real traversal. Targeted //nolint with reason.
> 
> * fix(auth): normalise AllowedRedirectHosts entries + add unit test
> 
> Address Copilot review on PR #2049. The previous closure passed raw
> s.AllowedHosts entries straight to the auth library, but --allowed-hosts
> holds CSP frame-ancestors source expressions: scheme-prefixed values
> (https://blog.example.com), entries with ports, and wildcards
> (*.cdn.example.com) are all valid there but the auth library compares
> against u.Hostname() and would silently drop them — breaking legitimate
> redirects on multi-host deployments.
> 
> Extract getAllowedRedirectHosts that:
> * trims whitespace, drops empty / 'self' / "self" / wildcard entries
> * prepends https:// if scheme missing then url.Parse to extract Hostname
> * logs a warning on parse failure rather than poisoning the allowlist
> 
> Wire the closure in getAuthenticator to call the helper.
> 
> Test_getAllowedRedirectHosts covers all the edge cases Copilot flagged
> (scheme stripping, port handling, self spellings, wildcards, empty,
> mixed real-world).
> 
> * fix(auth): preserve explicit port in AllowedRedirectHosts + clarify fs_store nolint
> 
> Address Copilot follow-up on PR #2049:
> 
> * getAllowedRedirectHosts stripped explicit ports via u.Hostname(), which
>   broadened the allowlist. The auth validator checks both Hostname() and
>   Host, so an entry like admin.example.com:8443 can and should be kept
>   host:port — allowing only that port, not any. Emit u.Host when
>   u.Port() != "", u.Hostname() otherwise. Updated tests.
> 
> * fs_store Save nolint rationale said "id validated at HTTP layer", but
>   Save is reached via image.Service.Save and SaveWithID (cache), neither
>   of which is HTTP validation. id is actually a server-generated hash in
>   both paths. Updated the comment.

> test: use testing/synctest to eliminate wall-clock sleeps (#2048)
> 
> Go 1.25's testing/synctest package (GA) provides a fake clock bubble
> for deterministic goroutine and timer testing. Convert tests that
> waited on real-time durations to use synctest, removing most wall-clock
> time.Sleep workarounds.
> 
> Converted (11 tests, 9 files):
> - notify/notify_test.go — all tests, replaced 17 time.Sleep(110ms) with synctest.Wait()
> - store/service/service_test.go — VoteSameIPWithDuration, UserReplies, submitImages,
>   ResubmitStagingImages, deleteImagesOnCommentDelete
> - store/image/{image,bolt_store}_test.go — Cleanup, Submit, SubmitDelay
> - store/engine/bolt_test.go — FlagListBlocked
> - providers/telegram_test.go — DispatchTelegramUpdates
> - migrator/backup_test.go — TestBackup_Do
> - _example/memory_store/accessor/data_test.go — FlagListBlocked
> 
> Simplifications along the way:
> - notify/notify_mock.go: dropped the 10ms time.After delay and
>   ctx.Done select in MockDest — the artificial I/O simulation is
>   pointless and blocked synctest.Wait from draining the queue
> - Removed three dead-code time.Sleep(1s) calls in EditCommentDurationFailed,
>   EditCommentAdmin, and Info tests: prepopulated comments from 2017
>   already exceed any EditDuration/ReadOnlyAge under real clock, making
>   the sleeps meaningless
> - UserReplies: replaced the Eventually+Sleep+mutex polling with a
>   direct time.Sleep under fake clock
> 
> Skipped (incompatible with synctest):
> - fs_store_test.go: relies on OS file mtime (real wall clock)
> - rss_test.go: needs real wall-clock second boundary for pubDate
> - admin/rest_private/rest_public tests: httptest network I/O
> - cmd/server_test.go: real HTTP server startup polling
> 
> Notes on quirks encountered:
> - synctest.Wait() does NOT advance fake time, contrary to what one
>   might expect. It only returns once all other bubble goroutines are
>   durably blocked. To advance the fake clock, the test goroutine must
>   itself call time.Sleep
> - BoltDB keys the "last" bucket by comment.Timestamp nanosecond string.
>   Rapid b.Create calls under frozen fake time produce identical keys
>   and overwrite each other. TestService_UserReplies adds
>   time.Sleep(time.Nanosecond) between Creates to advance the clock
> - Bolt image Cleanup uses strict age > ttl. Under fake time the
>   age-ttl delta is exactly zero at the boundary, so subtract 1ms from
>   the passed ttl to stay strictly under
>
