> ci: pin pnpm/pnpm clone to v11.11.0 in vp install E2E test (#2133)
> 
> pnpm/pnpm main now pins packageManager to pnpm v12 alphas
> (pnpm/pnpm#12811).
> The @pnpm/exe v12 alpha ships a placeholder bin that pnpm's version
> self-switch executes before the install script replaces it with the real
> binary, failing with a shell syntax error and breaking this job on every
> main run.
> 
> Pin the clone to the latest stable tag (packageManager pnpm@11.9.0, the
> same version the last green run used) and support an optional ref field
> in the repos list so future pins are one-line changes.

- de65091b6a520373c69e10bc06d60f99610168c7 — https://github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/commit/de65091b6a520373c69e10bc06d60f99610168c7
> feat(env): add `vp env clean` command (#2003)
> 
> Close #1983
> 
> This pull request add a `vp env clean` command that is used to clean all
> unused Node.js runtime and package managers downloaded by Vite+ and
> corepack.
> 
> The clean order:
> 1. `corepack cache clean`
> 2. Clean `$VP_HOME/js_runtime` (Except the current use one and the
> default one)
> 3. Clean `$VP_HOME/package_manager`
> 
> The reason why `corepack cache clean` is done first is Node.js runtime
> cleaning may delete the runtime corepack needed, which slows down the
> cleaning process.
> 
> This PR also adds a small note in `vp env list` and `vp env list-remote`
> command to suggest users use `vp env clean` command. Personally, I think
> adding tips in all `vp env` sub commands can be noisy and conflict with
> #1799's philosophy.
> 
> 🤖 Generated with Codex

> test: skip upstream-flaky snap/runtime cases (#2099)
> 
> Skips three CI cases that fail on transient upstream conditions, not on
> code in this repo.
> 
> ## Node `latest` alias on musl
> unofficial-builds.nodejs.org lists a Node release in index.json as soon
> as its directory is created, before every architecture's binary is
> built. Resolving the `latest` alias can pick a version whose
> linux-*-musl tarball is not published yet, so the download fails with
> HashNotFound (seen with node-v26.5.0-linux-x64-musl.tar.gz). Official
> nodejs.org releases are atomic, so glibc, darwin, and windows keep full
> coverage.
> 
> - runtime unit test
> `test_download_runtime_for_project_with_latest_alias_in_node_version`:
> skipped on musl
> - snap-tests-global `command-env-install-version-alias`: skipped on musl
> 
> ## astro create shim
> `vp create astro --template basics` scaffolds an astro dependency pinned
> to the create-astro template's current reference, which between releases
> is the next unpublished version (astro@^7.0.7 while 7.0.6 is latest).
> The following `vp install` then fails with ERR_PNPM_NO_MATCHING_VERSION
> on every platform.
> 
> - snap-tests-global `create-framework-shim-astro`: skipped (the vp
> migrate astro shim cases still cover the shim itself)
- fd4144bd5ca3a277155a7372902f0ab553306b37 — https://github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/commit/fd4144bd5ca3a277155a7372902f0ab553306b37
> test(snapshots): bound the PTY spawn with the per-step timeout (#2102)
> 
> The per-step timeout only wrapped the interaction phase
> (`rx.recv_timeout`): `TestTerminal::spawn` (openpty + fork/exec the
> child into the PTY) ran synchronously before it. On runners where that
> spawn can block (the Linux analog of the ConPTY blocking that keeps the
> Windows snapshot job on a GitHub-hosted runner), a wedged spawn was
> unbounded, and because the parallel execution gate holds the case's
> lease, it stalled the whole suite (6h job default, no step log).
> 
> Run the spawn on a helper thread bounded by the same per-step timeout: a
> wedged spawn now fails that one case, like any other step timeout, and
> the suite proceeds. The success path is unchanged (verified against the
> interactive picker cases). The abandoned helper thread is fine for a
> dev-only test binary that exits when the run ends.
> 
> ## What a wedged spawn looks like now
> 
> Forcing the spawn to block (the failure this fixes), the case now fails
> at its per-step timeout instead of hanging the run:
> 
> ```
> ---- app_root_listing::picker_select::global ----
> step `vp build` timed out after 2s; partial output:
> (PTY spawn did not complete)
> 
> failures:
>     app_root_listing::picker_select::global
> 
> test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 84 filtered out; finished in 2.02s
> ```
> 
> (`2s` is a shortened demo timeout; the real per-step default is 50s. The
> other cases keep running and the step log is preserved, versus the old
> behavior where this same block hung the whole step until the 6h job
> default with no log.)

Release notes (texto original):

> 
> ### 🐛 Bug Fixes
> 
> - Preserve add paths across special filenames (#506)

Compare (se coletado): https://github.com/wfxr/forgit/compare/d4bece432b8c4d2be631abf1e2e76b49f5c87f26...17110bfc611209f00a3faeeb318aef67d636a0e3

Status factual do intervalo: complete
Quantidade de commits no intervalo: 1
Erro do intervalo: nenhum registrado

Commits coletados:

- 17110bfc611209f00a3faeeb318aef67d636a0e3 — https://github.com/wfxr/forgit/commit/17110bfc611209f00a3faeeb318aef67d636a0e3
> fix: preserve add paths across special filenames (#506)
> 
> Keep `forgit add` on the porcelain `git status --porcelain -zs` path so
> filenames containing backslashes continue to work, while restoring the
> behaviors that regressed when we moved away from Git's cwd-relative output.
> 
> This change makes the status picker emit a display label and a hidden
> absolute-path payload separately. That lets the UI keep showing intuitive
> cwd-relative paths, while preview, edit, and add actions operate on the real
> path instead of reparsing the rendered status line. As a result, untracked
> files, subdirectory workflows, and special filenames now share one consistent
> path flow.
> 
> It also restores the old-Git fallback for plain `?? path` output before status
> filtering, raises the required fzf version for `--accept-nth`, and adds
> regression coverage for backslashes, spaces, tabs, subdirectory entries,
> sibling directories, and logical symlink paths.
> 
> We explored a few alternatives before landing here. Keeping a single
> human-readable line and reparsing it downstream remained too fragile for
> quoted paths and backslashes. Shell-only display-path rewriting worked for
> some cases but stayed brittle across logical vs physical paths and still
> failed in macOS CI. A per-path `realpath` approach would have been easier to
> read, but GNU-style relative-path support is not portable across the
> platforms we test and would add one external process per file in a hot path.
> 
> The final tradeoff keeps the pipeline batch-oriented and portable by doing
> the path normalization once in a single helper step, even though that is less
> lightweight than the earlier shell-only versions. That complexity is
> justified here because it fixes the old-Git untracked regression, preserves
> correct preview/add behavior from subdirectories, and avoids reintroducing
> long-standing filename parsing bugs.

> perf: avoid listing modified files twice in checkout-file (#546)
> 
> _forgit_checkout_file called _forgit_list_modified_files once to check for
> an empty result and again to feed fzf, running git diff twice on every
> invocation. Cache the result and reuse it for both checks.
- 9fa93b08610d50cd4108df15699e1ee4bb36e200 — https://github.com/wfxr/forgit/commit/9fa93b08610d50cd4108df15699e1ee4bb36e200
> perf(fish): migrate FORGIT_ vars without spawning subprocesses (#543)
> 
> The backwards-compatibility block that exports unexported FORGIT_ config
> variables ran `set | awk | grep` plus a `set -x | grep` for every variable,
> forking multiple external processes on every interactive fish startup.
> 
> Replace the pipeline with fish's built-in `set -n`/`set -xn` and
> `string match`, which run in-process. Behavior is unchanged: unexported
> FORGIT_ variables are still detected, warned about, and exported; nothing
> is emitted when all variables are already exported.
> 
> Co-authored-by: AllanZyne <AllanZyne@users.noreply.github.com>
> Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

> perf: speed up modified file lookup in large repositories (#544)
> 
> Use a modified-file-only path for `git-forgit restore` (`grs`) and
> `git-forgit checkout_file` (`gcf`) so these interactive selectors do not scan
> large sets of untracked files. This keeps both commands responsive in
> repositories with many untracked files.

#### 2. v6.0.0 / v6.0.0

item_id: wkentaro/gdown::release::307966905
Data: 2026-04-12T06:38:15Z
URL: https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/releases/tag/v6.0.0

Release notes (texto original):

> A lot has changed since v5.2.1 back in January. 33 pull requests (109 commits) went into this release, touching nearly every part of the codebase.
> 
> ### Highlights
> 
> - `gdown --folder` / `download_folder()` now supports folders with more than 50 files
> - `download()` raises `DownloadError` on failure instead of returning `None`
> - New `progress` parameter in `download()`
> - Path traversal vulnerability fixed in `extractall()` ([GHSA-76hw-p97h-883f](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/security/advisories/GHSA-76hw-p97h-883f))
> - All deprecated APIs from v5 have been (finally) removed
> - Python 3.10+ required (3.8 and 3.9 dropped)
> 
> Most users should be able to upgrade without issues. The one change that will likely need code updates is the switch from returning `None` to raising `DownloadError` on failure.
> 
> ### Breaking changes
> 
> - **`download()` and `download_folder()` now raise `DownloadError` instead of returning `None`** ([#451](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/451))
> 
>   Previously, `download()` and `download_folder()` returned `None` when a download failed. Now, they raise `DownloadError` (or its subclass `FileURLRetrievalError`).
> 
>   If your code looks like this:
> 
>   ```python
>   output = gdown.download(url, output="file.txt")
>   if output is None:
>       print("Download failed")
>   ```
> 
>   Change it to:
> 
>   ```python
>   try:
>       output = gdown.download(url, output="file.txt")
>   except gdown.DownloadError as e:
>       print(f"Download failed: {e}")
>   ```
> 
> - **`fuzzy` parameter and `--fuzzy` CLI flag removed** ([#455](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/455))
> 
>   Previously, you needed `fuzzy=True` (or `--fuzzy`) to download from Google Drive share links like `https://drive.google.com/file/d/FILE_ID/view`. gdown now always extracts the file ID from any Google Drive URL format. Just pass the URL directly.
> 
> - **`--remaining-ok` flag and `FolderContentsMaximumLimitError` removed** ([#453](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/453))
> 
>   Folder downloads used to be limited to 50 files due to a Google Drive API constraint, and `--remaining-ok` let you proceed with a partial download. gdown now uses the `embeddedfolderview` endpoint, which has no file count limit. The flag and exception class are no longer needed.
> 
> - **`md5` parameter removed from `cached_download()`** ([#450](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/450))
> 
>   The `md5` parameter was deprecated in v5. Use the `hash` parameter instead:
> 
>   ```python
>   # Before
>   gdown.cached_download(url, md5="abc123")
> 
>   # After
>   gdown.cached_download(url, hash="md5:abc123")
>   ```
> 
> - **`--id` CLI flag, `md5sum()`, and `assert_md5sum()` removed** ([#448](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/448), [#449](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/449))
> 
>   These were deprecated in v5. Use `gdown.parse_url()` for URL parsing and `hashlib` for checksum verification.
> 
> - **Python 3.8 and 3.9 are no longer supported** ([#423](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/423))
> 
>   gdown now requires Python 3.10 or later. Python 3.10 through 3.14 are tested in CI.
> 
> ### Security fixes
> 
> - **Arbitrary file write via path traversal in `extractall()`** ([GHSA-76hw-p97h-883f](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/security/advisories/GHSA-76hw-p97h-883f))
> 
>   `gdown.extractall()` now validates that archive members stay within the target directory, preventing zip or tar archives from writing files outside the extraction path via `../` traversal, absolute paths, or symlinks. On Python 3.12+, extraction uses the `data` filter. ([#445](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/445), [#446](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/446), [#447](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/447))
> 
> ### Features
> 
> - New `progress` parameter in `download()` for hooking into download progress ([#427](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/427))
> - Folder downloads now support more than 50 files via the `embeddedfolderview` endpoint ([#453](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/453))
> 
> ### Bug fixes
> 
> - Detect Google Docs/Sheets/Slides via URL patterns instead of page title, fixing downloads on non-English Google accounts ([#438](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/438))
> - Sanitize path separators in filenames on all platforms ([#437](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/437))
> - Handle corrupted cookies file instead of crashing ([#441](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/441))
> - Fix output directory detection and filename handling on Windows ([#440](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/440))
> - Append correct extension for Google exports in folder downloads ([#443](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/443))
> - Return `None` instead of `False` from `parse_url()` for non-Google-Drive URLs ([#434](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/434))
> - Remove redundant resume check in `download_folder()` ([#444](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/444))
> 
> ### Enhancements
> 
> - Type annotations on all public API functions ([#430](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/430))
> - `py.typed` marker for PEP 561 support ([#436](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/436))
> - Build toolchain now uses `uv`, `ruff`, `ty`, and `hatchling` with VCS versioning ([#423](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/423), [#424](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/424), [#425](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/425))
> - CI tests on Python 3.10 through 3.14 across Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows ([#454](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/454))

#### 3. v6.3.0 / v6.3.0

item_id: wkentaro/gdown::release::389814986
Data: 2026-09-16T10:10:17Z
URL: https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/releases/tag/v6.3.0

Release notes (texto original):

> 
> ### Added
> 
> - Add a `secretstorage` installation extra for importing Chromium cookies from GNOME Keyring with `pip install 'gdown[secretstorage]'` or `uvx --from 'gdown[secretstorage]' gdown`. ([#505](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/505))
> - `download()`, `download_folder()`, and `cached_download()` accept a requests-style `timeout`, exposed on the command line as `--timeout SECONDS`, so a stalled server no longer blocks forever. ([#510](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/510))
> - Add opt-in `--retries N` and Python `retries=N` for automatic recovery of interrupted file and folder downloads, with bounded backoff and validated byte-range resume; `--continue` still controls reuse of earlier downloads. ([#517](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/517))
> 
> ### Changed
> 
> - `cached_download()` verifies `hash` while streaming instead of reading the finished file back from disk. ([#512](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/512))
> - The command line reports a hit `--timeout` as a timeout instead of asking to file an issue. ([#513](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/513))
> 
> ### Fixed
> 
> - Propagate progress callback exceptions unchanged instead of misreporting chunked-encoding errors as incomplete downloads. ([#519](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/519))
> 

Compare (se coletado): https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/compare/dacdd945e83d76fcd45fce85deeb887c9df65156...8cef19a9401ce4bc9a35bb108fd66cbbe83683d1
Commits (consulta): https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/commits/8cef19a9401ce4bc9a35bb108fd66cbbe83683d1

- 00e4506b6bd432e492962f82c4030bf5c0c36c55 — https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/commit/00e4506b6bd432e492962f82c4030bf5c0c36c55
> chore: add retry changelog fragment
> 
> Record the automatic download retry feature for PR #517.
- 0738f442c7d5b66f826e20278b5033a375d1b406 — https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/commit/0738f442c7d5b66f826e20278b5033a375d1b406
> feat: accept a timeout for folder downloads
> 
> download_folder() has its own request for the folder listing and drives
> one download per file, so without a timeout of its own a stalled server
> hung a folder download even after the single-file path could recover.
- 07b35a3dd440580adef2eafba17b8cf2f9a505cd — https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/commit/07b35a3dd440580adef2eafba17b8cf2f9a505cd
> perf: hash a cached download while it streams
> 
> Verifying a cached file re-read it from disk right after writing it,
> doubling the I/O for a multi-gigabyte download. Feed the bytes to the
> hash as they arrive and drop the second read.
> 
> When resuming, the bytes already on disk are fed to the hasher before
> the range request, and no caller in the repository reaches that path,
> so a test covers it directly.
- 0b7c318345f8203e67a566165584797577e38adf — https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/commit/0b7c318345f8203e67a566165584797577e38adf
> refactor: represent retry state as a dataclass
- 0ba9cd735b75a91269c598860ae513d5ae789428 — https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/commit/0ba9cd735b75a91269c598860ae513d5ae789428
> feat: add a timeout for stalled downloads
> 
> The streaming request waited forever for the next byte, so a server that
> accepted the connection and then went quiet hung the caller with no way
> out. Accept a requests-style timeout, defaulting to the previous
> unbounded wait.
- 209a160929ccb3e7c892e240b45323cd43c744d8 — https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/commit/209a160929ccb3e7c892e240b45323cd43c744d8
> fix: reject incomplete resumed byte ranges

> docs: record rejected progress callback cancellation

> refactor: build the hasher apart from the file read
> 
> Parsing the algorithm out of the expected hash, hashing a file, and
> comparing the two lived in one function, so nothing could verify a
> hash it had computed another way. Split them, and validate the
> algorithm once where the hasher is built rather than again where the
> file is read.

> feat: retry interrupted downloads with bounded backoff

> and hashes, and validate ranged responses before appending bytes.

> feat: report a hit --timeout as a timeout in the CLI
> 
> A stall used to surface through the catch-all handler, which prints the
> raw requests error and asks the user to file an issue. Someone who set
> --timeout and then hit it was being told to report a bug.
> 
> Recognise both shapes a timeout takes: a requests Timeout when the
> server never answers the request, and a ConnectionError wrapping
> urllib3's read timeout when it stalls mid-stream. Print one line naming
> the configured timeout instead.

Release notes (texto original):

> 
> ### Added
> 
> - Optional cancellation events for `download()` and `cached_download()` interrupt stalled response reads and download waits without shortening network timeouts, raising `DownloadCancelled` while preserving partial-file cleanup. ([#525](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/525))
> 
> ### Changed
> 
> - An invalid `--speed` value now reports the accepted units instead of an internal function name. ([#527](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/527))
> 
> ### Removed
> 
> - `importlib` is no longer exported from the `gdown` package; it was listed in `__all__` by accident. ([#526](https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/pull/526))
>

> feat: allow cancelling stalled downloads
> 
> Accept a caller-owned event to stop response reads and download waits
> without shortening network timeouts. Preserve partial-file cleanup and
> raise DownloadCancelled separately from download failures.
> 
> Use cancellable buffered reads across HTTP, HTTPS, and proxy connections.
> Cover timeout preservation, publication boundaries, and cancellation
> cleanup with local-server tests, and record the API decision.
- 57bfb4993e635ac444bf6c6fdcdaa625c736d2c6 — https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/commit/57bfb4993e635ac444bf6c6fdcdaa625c736d2c6
> refactor: make the speed size parser non-public
> 
> It was never exported and only the command line calls it. The argument
> parser prints the type function's name when a value is rejected, so the
> rename would have surfaced an underscored name to users; report the
> accepted units instead. Nothing passes None any more, so that branch and
> its test go, and the rejection is tested through the command line.
- 72b6267240ccb1c282968db19dd7e9df0b23b481 — https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/commit/72b6267240ccb1c282968db19dd7e9df0b23b481

> fix: stop exporting importlib from the package
> 
> The standard-library module was bound in the package namespace to read
> the version, so the export manifest had to list it and star imports
> handed it to callers. Bind only the version lookup under a non-public
> name.
- 7b67d7d92104e0e8324cbcee05219d6eda67671a — https://github.com/wkentaro/gdown/commit/7b67d7d92104e0e8324cbcee05219d6eda67671a

#### 1. 0.92.0 / 0.92.0

item_id: zenml-io/zenml::release::266615008
Data: 2025-12-02T06:42:19Z
URL: https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/releases/tag/0.92.0

Release notes (texto original):

> ## ⚠️ Breaking Changes
> 
> * `StepRunResponse.regular_inputs` and `StepContext.inputs` are now of type `Dict[str, List[ArtifactVersionResponse]]` instead of `Dict[str, ArtifactVersionResponse]`.
> 
> ## New Features
> 
> * The local image builder can now use the Docker CLI instead of the Python SDK, enabling BuildKit options that the Python SDK does not support.
> * The Evidently integration has been updated and now supports NumPy 2.0.
> * The active project can now be specified during login using the `--project` flag (for example, `zenml login ... --project ...`).
> * The GCP Image Builder now supports configuring the region in which the build should happen.
> 
> ## Bugfixes
> * Run metadata can now store sets and tuples.
> * An error that occurred when connecting to a ZenML server without the `local` extra installed has been fixed.
> * Weave import side effects when `enable_weave=False` is configured for the Weights & Biases experiment tracker have been fixed.
> 
> ## What's Changed
> * Add version 0.91.1 to legacy docs by @github-actions[bot] in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4213
> * Add 0.91.2 to the migration tests by @github-actions[bot] in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4215
> * Fix `mlflow` test by @bcdurak in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4208
> * Increase disk space on CI runners by @schustmi in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4217
> * Fix Azure ML compute cluster validation typo by @htahir1 in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4226
> * Pin sagemaker to avoid pulling in the huge 3.0 dependencies by @stefannica in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4235
> * Fix AzureMLOrchestratorSettings AttributeError with optional parameters by @htahir1 in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4228
> * Fix CLI login error message with deprecated flag  by @htahir1 in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4229
> * Replace `@` command invocation with `/` invocation by @strickvl in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4244
> * Add DeepSeek Packt book thumbnail + link to `README` by @strickvl in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4245
> * Feature:4151 Heartbeat activation logic by @Json-Andriopoulos in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4216
> * AWS/Sagemaker dynamic pipelines by @stefannica in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4232
> * Add display_name field to flavors for better UI presentation by @htahir1 in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4233
> * Add pipeline deployment to onboarding by @htahir1 in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4231
> * Map/Reduce implementation for dynamic pipelines by @schustmi in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4159
> * Fix alembic order by @schustmi in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4250
> * [WIP] Fix set serialization in metadata system by @htahir1 in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4249
> * Update evidently integration to support NumPy 2.0 by @htahir1 in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4243
> * Added the option for setting project when logging in by @adam6878 in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4224
> * Enable running dynamic snapshots by @schustmi in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4253
> * Fix CLI profiling CI by @schustmi in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4255
> * Use correct backoff limit for isolated steps on Kubernetes by @schustmi in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4256
> * Fix security check for jinja2 autoescape in k8s by @safoinme in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4211
> * Add option to build docker images using subprocess calls by @schustmi in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4205
> * Disable heartbeat for deployments by @schustmi in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4254
> * Add nested `AGENTS.md` files for AI agent codebase guidance by @strickvl in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4259
> * Store Kubernetes step job names in run metadata by @schustmi in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4180
> * Fix ImportError when using zenml login without SQL dependencies by @strickvl in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4252
> * Better typing for docker build options by @schustmi in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4262
> * Add support for dynamic pipelines to the Vertex orchestrator by @schustmi in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4246
> * Fix Claude workflow triggers to use `@claude` instead of `/claude` by @strickvl in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4264
> * Misc dynamic pipeline improvements by @schustmi in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4261
> * Fix weave import side-effects when `enable_weave=False` by @strickvl in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4265
> * Add regional location support to GCP Image Builder by @strickvl in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4268
> 
> ## New Contributors
> * @adam6878 made their first contribution in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4224
> 
> **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/compare/0.91.2...0.92.0

> Fix typo in Azure ML compute type validation (#4226)
> 
> The compute type validation for Azure ML compute clusters had a typo
> that prevented proper identification of AML compute resources. The code
> was checking for "amIcompute" (with capital I) instead of the correct
> "amlcompute" (with lowercase l), causing runtime failures when users
> attempted to use compute cluster mode.
> 
> This fix corrects the string comparison to match the actual compute
> type identifier returned by the Azure ML SDK, allowing compute cluster
> mode to work as intended.
> 
> Fixes #4222

> Fix set serialization in metadata system (#4249)
> 
> Sets were documented as a supported MetadataType but failed during
> serialization because json.dumps() cannot serialize Python sets. This
> change uses the standard pydantic_encoder to convert sets (and tuples)
> to lists before JSON serialization, making them compatible with JSON
> while preserving type information via MetadataTypeEnum.
> 
> The fix uses pydantic_encoder directly (via json.dumps(value,
> default=pydantic_encoder)) at all serialization points, following the
> same pattern used throughout the ZenML codebase. This ensures
> consistency and proper handling of all supported types including nested
> sets/tuples, UUIDs, datetimes, etc.
> 
> Changes:
> - Update validate_metadata() in metadata_types.py to use pydantic_encoder
> - Update Client.create_run_metadata() to use pydantic_encoder
> - Update SQLZenStore.create_run_metadata() to use pydantic_encoder
> - Add unit tests for set/tuple validation
> - Document supported metadata types in user guide
> 
> Fixes #4248
> 
> Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

> Add display_name field to flavors for better UI presentation (#4233)
> 
> * Add display_name field to flavors
> 
> Flavor names with underscores (e.g., vm_kubernetes) can now have a
> separate display_name that is shown in the UI. This allows flavors to
> have user-friendly display names while keeping technical names unchanged.
> 
> Changes:
> - Add display_name column to flavor database table
> - Add display_name field to FlavorRequest and FlavorUpdate models
> - Add display_name to FlavorResponseBody (required field in responses)
> - Add display_name property to FlavorResponse
> - Update FlavorSchema.to_model() to use display_name or fall back to name
> - Create Alembic migration to add the database column
> 
> The display_name field is optional and defaults to None. When not set,
> the API will return the flavor name as the display_name for backward
> compatibility.
> 
> Addresses https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml-dashboard/issues/908
> 
> * Add automatic display_name generation for all flavors
> 
> All flavors now automatically generate a human-readable display_name from
> their technical name by default. For example, "vm_kubernetes" becomes
> "VM Kubernetes". Flavors can override this property to provide custom
> display names if needed.
> 
> Changes:
> - Add display_name property to base Flavor class with smart default
> - Update Flavor.to_model() to include display_name in FlavorRequest
> 
> This ensures all integration flavors and custom flavors automatically
> have proper display names without requiring manual updates to each
> flavor class.
> 
> Related to https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml-dashboard/issues/908
> 
> * Fix migration parent revision to depend on 0.91.2
> 
> The migration was incorrectly depending on ff538a321a92 (from version 0.81.0).
> Updated to depend on 0.91.2, which is the current latest release on develop.
> 
> * Use flavor display_name in components and add manual overrides for VM flavors
> 
> - Update ComponentResponseBody to use flavor's display_name instead of technical name
> - Add display_name overrides to VM flavors:
>   - vm_gcp -> "VM GCP"
>   - vm_aws -> "VM AWS"
>   - vm_azure -> "VM Azure"
> - Fixes issue with automatic title-casing not handling acronyms properly
> 
> * Add display_name overrides for flavors with acronyms
> 
> - AWS flavors: aws -> "AWS"
> - SageMaker flavors: sagemaker -> "SageMaker"
> - GCP flavors: gcp -> "GCP"
> - Vertex AI flavors: vertex -> "Vertex AI"
> - S3 flavor: s3 -> "S3"
> - AzureML flavors: azureml -> "AzureML"
> - MLflow flavors: mlflow -> "MLflow"
> - VM flavors: vm_kubernetes -> "VM Kubernetes", vm_lambda -> "VM Lambda"
> 
> This fixes automatic title-casing that doesn't handle acronyms properly,
> ensuring consistent display names across the dashboard.
> 
> * Update src/zenml/zen_stores/schemas/component_schemas.py
> 
> * Apply title-case transformation in display_name fallbacks
> 
> Ensures consistency between new flavors (with display_name set) and
> existing flavors (with NULL display_name) by applying the same
> transformation in the fallback logic.
> 
> * Simplify component flavor_name fallback logic
> 
> * Add display_name to FlavorFilter and update Skypilot flavor names
> 
> - Add display_name field to FlavorFilter model for filtering by display name
> - Add display_name parameter to Client.list_flavors method
> - Update all Skypilot flavor display names to include "Skypilot" prefix:
>   - "VM AWS" → "Skypilot AWS"
>   - "VM Azure" → "Skypilot Azure"
>   - "VM GCP" → "Skypilot GCP"
>   - "VM Kubernetes" → "Skypilot Kubernetes"
>   - "VM Lambda" → "Skypilot Lambda"

> Fix AttributeError in AzureML settings validation (#4228)
> 
> When using AzureMLOrchestratorSettings with an existing compute cluster,
> users should be able to omit optional parameters. However, line 47 in
> azureml_utils.py used getattr without a default value, causing an
> AttributeError when optional fields were not set.
> 
> This fix adds None as the default value for getattr when accessing
> settings parameters. The existing None check on line 49 ensures that
> unset fields are gracefully skipped during validation.
>

> - check_settings_and_compute_configuration handles missing optional fields

- 73356a60e902d2e70a4dffbc5a9c054c5972012c — https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/commit/73356a60e902d2e70a4dffbc5a9c054c5972012c
> Add regional location support to GCP Image Builder (#4268)
> 
> * Add regional location support to GCP Image Builder
> 
> Users can now specify a `location` parameter to run Cloud Build in a
> specific GCP region instead of the global endpoint. This enables:
> - Data residency compliance (GDPR, etc.)
> - Lower latency when building near GCS buckets/Artifact Registry
> - Required for Cloud Build private pools
> 
> The Service Connector region does not control Cloud Build region, so
> this must be set explicitly on the Image Builder component.
> 
> * Add validator to normalize empty location strings
> 
> Adds a Pydantic field_validator that strips whitespace and converts
> empty strings to None at parse time. This prevents edge cases where
> location="" would produce an invalid endpoint like
> "-cloudbuild.googleapis.com".

> Add pipeline deployment to onboarding (#4231)

> * Add snapshot creation and deployment tracking to onboarding
> 
> This adds backend support for tracking two new onboarding steps related
> to pipeline snapshots: snapshot creation and deployment. These steps help
> guide users through the workflow of creating and deploying pipeline snapshots.
> 
> Changes:
> - Add SNAPSHOT_CREATED and SNAPSHOT_DEPLOYED enum values to OnboardingStep
> - Track SNAPSHOT_CREATED in create_snapshot method when users create a snapshot
> - Track SNAPSHOT_DEPLOYED in create_deployment method when users deploy a snapshot
> 
> This implements backend support for zenml-io/zenml-dashboard#913
> 
> * Only track SNAPSHOT_CREATED for user-created named snapshots
> 
> Modified the SNAPSHOT_CREATED onboarding tracking to only fire for
> user-created snapshots with names, not for internal system-generated
> snapshots created during pipeline runs. This prevents false positives
> in the onboarding flow.
> 
> When run_snapshot is called internally, it creates unnamed snapshots
> that shouldn't count toward user onboarding progress.
> 
> * Update src/zenml/zen_stores/sql_zen_store.py
> 
> * Remove SNAPSHOT_CREATED tracking from onboarding
> 
> Based on product feedback, removed SNAPSHOT_CREATED enum and tracking
> since snapshot creation and deployment happen in the same onboarding
> step (collapsible section). Only SNAPSHOT_DEPLOYED tracking remains
> to mark when users deploy their pipeline.
> 
> This aligns with the simplified onboarding flow where users will
> directly deploy pipelines via `zenml pipeline deploy` command.
> 
> * Clean up merge conflict markers - remove SNAPSHOT_CREATED tracking
> 
> * Rename to PIPELINE_DEPLOYED and gate onboarding completion
> 
> Changes:
> - Renamed SNAPSHOT_DEPLOYED to PIPELINE_DEPLOYED to align with new terminology
> - Moved OSS_ONBOARDING_COMPLETED and PRO_ONBOARDING_COMPLETED to trigger
>   only when PIPELINE_DEPLOYED event fires (when user deploys a pipeline)
> - Removed automatic onboarding completion from pipeline run logic
> 
> This ensures users must complete the full onboarding flow including
> deployment before onboarding is marked as complete.

> the evidently.legacy.* compatibility layer, we maintain full backward
> compatibility with existing ZenML code while gaining NumPy 2.0 support.

#### 2. 0.94.0 / 0.94.0

item_id: zenml-io/zenml::release::293110242
Data: 2026-03-04T18:22:00Z
URL: https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/releases/tag/0.94.0

Release notes (texto original):

> <!-- ZENML_GITBOOK_RELEASE_NOTES_START tag=0.94.0 -->
> ### Breaking Changes
> 
> * Old endpoints and client methods for legacy triggers, actions and event sources have been removed. **This shouldn't affect you unless you explicitly used those endpoints or methods in your code.**
> * Custom step operator flavors must implement new `submit_step` and `get_step_status` methods to work with dynamic pipelines. The legacy `launch` method will only work in static pipelines as a fallback. The Spark step operator is not yet compatible with dynamic pipelines. [PR #4515](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4515)
> * Running pipelines with a client `<=0.92.0` and step logs enabled is not working due to a client/server incompatibility.
> 
> #### 🚀 New Integrations
> 
> - **Run:AI Step Operator**: ZenML now supports running individual pipeline steps on Run:AI clusters with fractional GPU allocation, enabling more efficient resource utilization for ML workloads. [PR #4439](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4439)
> 
> #### ✨ New Features
> 
> - **Step and Pipeline Replays**: You can now replay existing step or pipeline runs with the same inputs and configuration. When replaying a pipeline run, you can specify which steps to skip and reuse from the original run. A debug mode is also available to run replays on your active stack with a local orchestrator. [PR #4456](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4456)
> 
> - **Triggers and Native Schedules (PRO)**: Introduced the `Trigger` concept for automated pipeline execution. The first supported trigger type is Schedules, which offers lifecycle management, automatic synchronization with orchestrators, and centralized management across stacks. [PR #4482](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4482)
> 
> - **Step Run Filtering by Version**: Added the ability to filter step runs by version, making it easier to track and manage specific versions of your pipeline steps. [PR #4518](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4518)
> 
> #### 🔧 Improvements
> 
> - **Enhanced Dynamic Pipeline Monitoring**: Improved the execution and monitoring of isolated steps in dynamic pipelines. Step submission is now separated from monitoring, preventing thread blocking during step execution. [PR #4369](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4369)
> 
> - **SkyPilot Integration Update**: Updated the SkyPilot integration to support version 0.11.x, including migration to the new async API and support for new resource settings. [PR #4462](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4462)
> 
> - **Kubernetes Retry Configuration**: Added configurable timeout options for Kubernetes orchestrator and step operator API calls, ensuring proper retry behavior and preventing unnecessary hanging. [PR #4525](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4525)
> 
> - **Git Submodule Support**: Code archives now include files from git submodules when uploading to the artifact store, ensuring complete code tracking for repositories with submodules. [PR #4496](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4496)
> 
> <details>
> <summary>Fixed</summary>
> 
> - Fixed handling of variadic keyword arguments in pipeline functions, ensuring they are properly flattened before being passed to the pipeline. [PR #4528](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4528)
> 
> - Fixed Azure integration dependencies by limiting the `azure-mgmt-resource` version to avoid compatibility issues with the 25.0.0 package split. [PR #4516](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4516)
> 
> - Fixed handling of external artifacts with `None` values and reduced chunk size when fetching many step runs to avoid URI too large errors. [PR #4551](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4551)
> 
> </details>
> <!-- ZENML_GITBOOK_RELEASE_NOTES_END tag=0.94.0 -->

Release notes (texto original):

> <!-- ZENML_GITBOOK_RELEASE_NOTES_START tag=0.94.1 -->
> #### 🎯 Pipeline Execution Control
> 
> - **Pause and Resume Pipeline Runs**: Introduced `zenml.wait(...)` to pause dynamic pipelines while waiting for external inputs, automatically freeing resources until the input is provided. Runs can be resumed automatically (when using remote orchestrators with snapshot support) or manually via `zenml pipeline runs resume <ID>`. [PR #4588](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4588)
> - **Override Step Inputs on Replay**: You can now override step inputs when replaying a pipeline run, giving you more flexibility to rerun pipelines with different data. [PR #4590](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4590)
> 
> #### 🔧 Materializers and Data Handling
> 
> - **Dataclass Materializer**: Added a built-in materializer for JSON-serializable dataclasses, making it easier to pass structured data between steps. [PR #4600](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4600)
> - **LakeFS Data Versioning Example**: New example demonstrating the "pass references, not data" pattern for terabyte-scale datasets. ZenML steps exchange lightweight LakeFS pointers while actual data stays in LakeFS, accessed via its S3-compatible gateway. [PR #4559](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4559)
> 
> #### ☁️ Infrastructure and Deployment
> 
> - **Helm Environment Variable Overrides**: Environment variables specified in `zenml.environment`, `zenml.secretEnvironment`, and worker deployment configurations can now override computed settings from the Helm chart. [PR #4595](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4595)
> - **Secret Environment Variables in Helm**: Added support for injecting secret environment variables into the ZenML server deployment via Helm without committing secrets to values.yaml, enabling better GitOps workflows. [PR #4606](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4606)
> - **Docker Build Arguments**: Build arguments defined in `DockerSettings` are now properly declared with `ARG` instructions in auto-generated Dockerfiles. [PR #4612](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4612)
> 
> #### 🔐 Authentication and Credentials
> 
> - **Improved GCP Credentials Refresh**: Implemented native GCP credentials refresh using service connector logic, replacing periodic expiration checks for more reliable OAuth2 credential handling. [PR #4527](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4527)
> 
> #### 📊 Pipeline Configuration
> 
> - **Step Parameter Schema Storage**: Step parameter specifications are now stored for better schema validation when triggering pipeline snapshots. [PR #4591](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4591)
> 
> <details><summary>Fixed</summary>
> 
> - **Exception Handling for Isolated Steps**: Isolated steps in dynamic pipelines now raise the correct exception types instead of always wrapping them in `RuntimeError`, making error handling more intuitive and consistent. [PR #4589](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4589)
> - **Kubernetes API Request Timeout**: Fixed typing issue in the Kubernetes orchestrator and step operator to ensure `api_request_timeout` is properly applied as an integer value. [PR #4605](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4605)
> - **Client-Server Compatibility**: Resolved compatibility issue with clients `<=0.92.0` by not passing both pipeline run ID and step run ID to logs requests. [PR #4614](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4614)
> - **Dynamic Pipeline Monitoring**: Fixed dictionary size change error that occurred when the main thread modified the `_steps_to_monitor` dictionary while the monitoring thread was iterating over it. [PR #4619](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4619)
> - **Step Config Template Parameters**: Step parameters defined in config templates now correctly take precedence over function default values in dynamic pipelines. [PR #4624](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4624)
> 
> </details>
> 
> #### 📦 Dependencies
> 
> - Updated Pydantic to version 2.12.5. [PR #4552](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4552)
> <!-- ZENML_GITBOOK_RELEASE_NOTES_END tag=0.94.1 -->
>

> Fix S3 double-close AssertionError on cleanup (#4593)
> 
> * Harden S3 write close temp-file handling
> 
> * Defer S3 existence check to error path
> 
> Move the _remote_path_exists() call from __init__ to the error handler,
> eliminating an S3 HEAD request on every write-mode open. Also fix double
> _extract_missing_path call, replace getattr with direct attribute access,
> consolidate s3:// prefix stripping, and add debug logging to bare except
> blocks.
> 
> * Add missing *args docstring to __exit__ method
> 
> darglint requires all parameters (including *args) to be documented.
> 
> * Suppress Bandit B108 false positive in S3 test
> 
> The /tmp path is a string literal inside a FileNotFoundError
> constructor, not actual filesystem usage.
> 
> * Remove _SafeS3WriteFile wrapper class
> 
> The wrapper addressed a secondary concern (temp file race on close)
> that added ~180 lines of production code relying on s3fs internals.
> The core fix for the double-close issue (#4586) remains intact.
> 
> * Fix S3 double-close AssertionError on cleanup (#4586)
> 
> Route both cleanup paths (_close and close_session) through a shared
> _safe_aexit_s3_creator wrapper that catches the specific
> AssertionError("Session was never entered") raised by aiobotocore
> when __aexit__ is called on an already-closed session.
> 
> * Add missing Raises section to _safe_aexit_s3_creator docstring
> 
> Fixes darglint DAR401 error for the re-raised AssertionError.

> Handle activation exceptions for individual integrations (#4490)
> 
> * Handle activation exceptions for individual integrations
> 
> When activating integrations at startup, a single integration failing
> (e.g., OSError from Windows DLL loads, ImportError from missing optional
> deps) would crash the entire activation loop, preventing all subsequent
> integrations from activating.
> 
> Wrap each integration.activate() call with a try/except for ImportError
> and OSError, log the failure with full traceback, and continue activating
> the remaining integrations.
> 
> * Improve activation error handling and add tests
> 
> - Upgrade log level from WARNING to ERROR (logger.exception) to match
>   the severity pattern used in _initialize() and surface failures
>   clearly in CI/ops logs
> - Add inline comments explaining why ImportError/OSError are caught
> - Update docstring to document best-effort activation semantics
> - Add unit tests covering OSError, ImportError, and continuation message
> 
> * Address review feedback on activation error wording
> 
> Schustmi pointed out two inaccuracies:
> 
> 1. The comment "missing optional dependencies" was wrong — if deps
>    were simply absent, check_installation() would already return False.
>    The real cause is broken/incomplete installs or undeclared transitive
>    dependencies despite metadata looking correct.
> 
> 2. The log message "its features will be unavailable" was misleading —
>    activation failure only skips eager registration (materializers,
>    service connectors). Later on-demand imports (loading stored
>    artifacts, stack components) may still attempt the same imports
>    and could fail independently.
> 
> Updated docstring, inline comments, log message, and test assertion
> to reflect the actual semantics.

#### 4. 0.95.1 / 0.95.1

item_id: zenml-io/zenml::release::341384007
Data: 2026-06-18T12:24:26Z
URL: https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/releases/tag/0.95.1

Release notes (texto original):

> <!-- ZENML_GITBOOK_RELEASE_NOTES_START tag=0.95.1 -->
> #### Dynamic pipelines with step operators
> 
> Dynamic pipeline execution is more reliable when steps use step operators.
> 
> <details><summary>Fixed</summary>
> 
> - Fixed an issue where running a step with a step operator in a dynamic pipeline could fail unless that step was explicitly listed in `pipeline.depends_on`.
> - ZenML now falls back to the orchestrator image in this case, matching the behavior already used for isolated steps without step operators. [PR #4960](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4960)
> 
> </details>
> 
> #### Faster pipeline and step run queries
> 
> Common pipeline run and step run views should now load more efficiently, especially on larger deployments.
> 
> - Improved database query performance by adjusting how related data is loaded for common pipeline run and step run queries.
> - This helps avoid expensive query plans in MySQL for paginated run listings, making these queries more scalable. [PR #4965](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4965)
> 
> #### Logging stability
> 
> Logging shutdown is now safer when using artifact-backed log stores.
> 
> <details><summary>Fixed</summary>
> 
> - Fixed a deadlock that could happen during logging context shutdown when using `fsspec`-based artifact log stores with debug logs enabled.
> - ZenML now avoids writing back into the log store during shutdown, improving reliability for pipeline and step log collection. [PR #4964](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4964)
> 
> </details>
> <!-- ZENML_GITBOOK_RELEASE_NOTES_END tag=0.95.1 -->
> 
> ## What's Changed
> * Add version 0.94.6 to legacy docs by @github-actions[bot] in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4957
> * Add 0.95.0 to the migration tests by @github-actions[bot] in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4959
> * Exclude `zenml` from its own dependency audit by @strickvl in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4961
> * Fallback to orchestrator image by @schustmi in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4960
> * Fix logging shutdown deadlock by @schustmi in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4964
> * Improve DB query plans by using selectinload by @schustmi in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4965
> * Prepare release 0.95.1 by @github-actions[bot] in https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4966
> 
>

- f2536ab4648a3718cac82631b64b1f5348c22a47 — https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/commit/f2536ab4648a3718cac82631b64b1f5348c22a47
> Exclude zenml from its own dependency audit (#4961)
> 
> pip-audit looks up installed package versions in advisory databases. It
> cannot meaningfully audit ZenML's own package, and during release prep
> the local version is intentionally bumped ahead of PyPI (e.g. 0.95.0
> before it is published). With --strict, pip-audit treats the unresolvable
> zenml version as a fatal error, aborts before writing any JSON, and the
> severity gate then fails on an empty/unusable report.
> 
> Uninstall zenml from the isolated audit venv before running pip-audit.
> This removes only its own dist-info and leaves every dependency in place,
> so the audit still covers the full dependency set while no longer choking
> on the project's own unreleased version.

#### 5. 0.96.0 / 0.96.0

item_id: zenml-io/zenml::release::348039896
Data: 2026-07-02T12:52:05Z
URL: https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/releases/tag/0.96.0

Release notes (texto original):

> <!-- ZENML_GITBOOK_RELEASE_NOTES_START tag=0.96.0 -->
> 
> ### Known Issues
> If the Docker credential helper contains invalid credentials for a registry that ZenML is trying to use, those will have precendence over the credentials set by the service connector and will cause the following error: `RuntimeError: Docker error: denied: Your authorization token has expired. Reauthenticate and try again..`. This will be fixed in the next release, in the meantime `docker logout <REGISTRY>` should fix it.
> 
> ### Breaking Changes
> 
> * The minimum supported `transformers` version has been raised. If you use ZenML with Hugging Face/`transformers`, update your environment and dependency pins to a newer compatible `transformers` release before upgrading ZenML. [PR #4976](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4976)
> * The Azure integration now requires newer Azure dependency versions, and support for the deprecated `azureml-core` library has been fully removed. If you use ZenML on Azure, update your Azure-related dependency pins and migrate any remaining `azureml-core` usage to the currently supported Azure SDK packages before upgrading. [PR #4987](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4987)
> * In open-source ZenML server deployments without RBAC enabled, service account and API key management is now restricted to admins only. Non-admin users will no longer be able to manage service accounts or API keys they previously created, so move any required credentials and automation to admin-managed accounts as part of your upgrade. [PR #5007](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/5007)
> 
> #### New integrations and execution backends
> 
> - **Trackio experiment tracking**: ZenML now includes a Trackio experiment tracker integration, allowing pipelines to log experiment data through Trackio’s public API. This makes it easier to manage trial results and connect ZenML runs with Hugging Face-backed Trackio workflows such as datasets, spaces, and buckets. [PR #4841](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4841)
> - **Backblaze B2 artifact store**: You can now configure Backblaze B2 as a ZenML artifact store. This adds another S3-compatible storage option for teams that want to store pipeline artifacts in Backblaze infrastructure. [PR #4791](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4791)
> - **Baseten step operator**: ZenML now supports a `baseten` step operator flavor for running GPU workloads as Baseten Training jobs. It supports regular single-node steps with ZenML artifacts and logs, as well as multi-node distributed training through command steps that can consume Baseten’s distributed training environment variables. [PR #4973](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4973)
> - **Generic OAuth2 service connector**: A new OAuth2 service connector lets you authenticate external services using a static token, client credentials, or a client ID with refresh token. This provides a reusable connector option for services that expose OAuth2-based authentication. [PR #4992](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4992)
> 
> #### Workflow controls and platform operations
> 
> - **Replay input overrides by step name**: When replaying a run, you can now use `step_default_input_overrides` to override a step input for every invocation of a step with the same name. Per-invocation `step_input_overrides` still take precedence, giving you both broad and targeted control during replay. [PR #4978](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4978)
> - **Trigger cycle protection**: ZenML now detects execution loops in Platform Event Trigger chains at the pipeline level. Cyclic trigger dispatches are skipped with the new `SKIPPED_TRIGGER_CYCLE` status, while unrelated downstream dispatches can continue normally and the affected cycle can be inspected through the SDK. [PR #4971](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4971)
> - **Optional sandbox cleanup on exit**: Sandbox sessions can now be configured to destroy the sandbox automatically when the session exits. The option defaults to `False`, preserving the behavior from previous releases unless you opt in. [PR #4986](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4986)
> - **Configurable Kubernetes API retries**: Kubernetes-based deployments can now configure retry behavior for Kubernetes API calls. This gives operators more control over resilience in clusters where transient API failures or throttling can occur. [PR #5004](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/5004)
> - **Dashboard filtering and connector selection improvements**: The dashboard Timeline View now has additional filtering options, including more status filters. Component creation also gets a more efficient connector selector, making setup flows smoother in larger workspaces. [PR #1084](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml-dashboard/pull/1084)
> 
> #### Performance and scalability
> 
> - **Faster pipeline sorting by latest run**: Listing pipelines sorted by latest run is now more efficient on large deployments. ZenML changed the query shape and supporting database indexing so the server no longer has to scan all runs for all pipelines just to compute the latest run timestamp. [PR #4969](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4969)
> - **More efficient run and artifact queries**: Several common server queries now load only the data they need and fetch related metadata more efficiently. This improves performance for DAG, pipeline run, step run, artifact version, and model version views, especially in workspaces with many entities. [PR #4994](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4994)
> - **Catch-up cleanup for expired API transactions**: Expired API transaction cleanup now works through bounded catch-up passes instead of a single fixed delete per interval. This helps servers recover from cleanup backlogs while keeping each database operation bounded, and also allows completed expired idempotency transactions to be safely reclaimed. [PR #4943](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4943)
> 
> <details><summary>Fixed</summary>
> 
> - **Artifact store caching prevents server OOMs**: The ZenML server now caches artifact store instances used for operations such as reading logs and visualizations. This avoids repeatedly rebuilding heavy storage clients and helps prevent memory growth that could previously lead to OOM kills on busy servers. [PR #4974](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/4974)
> - **Docker credentials for image builds and pushes**: ZenML now configures Docker credentials correctly when building and pushing container images. This fixes cases where username/password credentials were not applied to the expected registry URI, which could cause authentication failures in build and push workflows. [PR #5005](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/5005)
> - **Secret backup and restore authorization**: Secret backup and restore endpoints now enforce an explicit admin check when RBAC is disabled. This closes an authorization gap where an authenticated non-admin user could access admin-only secret operations in the default non-RBAC setup. [PR #5009](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/5009)
> - **Safer custom flavor loading**: Custom flavor sources are now validated before server-side hydration. ZenML ensures the configured source resolves to a `Flavor` subclass before instantiation, preventing arbitrary zero-argument callables from being invoked during flavor loading. [PR #5008](https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/5008)
> 
> </details>
> <!-- ZENML_GITBOOK_RELEASE_NOTES_END tag=0.96.0 -->
> 
> ## What's Changed

>   per-exec timeout in its public API.

> * Add LocalSandbox flavor (subprocess-based; built-in)
> 
> A no-isolation, no-deps Sandbox flavor that runs commands as
> subprocess.Popen on the same machine. Built-in (registered in
> FlavorRegistry.builtin_flavors), so `zenml sandbox register foo
> --flavor=local` works out of the box.
> 
> Intended for:
> - Examples / quickstarts that should work without a Modal account
> - Unit tests of code that consumes the Sandbox interface
> - Local development against the abstraction
> 
> NOT intended for untrusted LLM-generated code — a loud warning is
> emitted on every create_session() call so the no-isolation property is
> impossible to miss. Real isolation comes from the container/microVM
> flavors (Modal today; Agent Substrate / E2B / Daytona on the roadmap).
>

> * Add SandboxProcess.collect() + SandboxOutput dataclass
> 
> Codifies the agent-tool idiom of "drain stdout, drain stderr, wait,
> return everything" into one base-level helper, so flavor consumers
> (and example code) don't have to repeat the three-line dance.
> 
> - New @dataclass SandboxOutput(stdout, stderr, exit_code,
>   stdout_truncated, stderr_truncated). Returned by collect().
> - New SandboxProcess.collect(*, max_bytes=1_048_576) -> SandboxOutput.
>   Drains BOTH streams to completion (so the underlying provider's
>   wait() doesn't block on un-emptied buffers), caps the returned
>   strings, flags per-stream truncation explicitly.
> - Module-level _drain_capped helper used by collect() (so flavors can
>   reuse it if they want).
> - 3 new tests covering: full drain happy path, per-stream truncation
>   flags, full consumption even when truncated (iterator goes to
>   StopIteration so provider wait() is safe).
> - plan.md updates: note the Modal-credentials-not-in-config limitation
>   surfaced by the live smoke test (workaround: stack secret with
>   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET as env vars; proper fix: SecretField on
>   ModalSandboxConfig — tracked as a follow-up).

> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
> 
> * Sandbox logs: direct-emit instead of LoggingContext stack push
> 
> The old design pushed a LoggingContext source="sandbox:<id>" onto the
> step's logging stack on __enter__. That captured *everything* the step
> process logged while the with-block was open -- not just sandbox
> output. The 'sandbox:<id>' label was misleading.
> 
> New model: each SandboxSession lazily creates one LogsResponse +
> BaseLogStoreOrigin on first exec, and emits records DIRECTLY to that
> origin via log_store.emit(...). The step's own LoggingContext stack is
> never touched.
> 
> What the 'sandbox:<id>' source now contains, and only this:
> 
>   $ python -u -c 'import math; print(math.pi)'  (level INFO, from _log_command)
>   3.141592653589793                              (level INFO, from sandbox stdout)
>   ...
> 
> What it no longer wrongly captures:
> 
>   - step process's logger.info(...) calls
>   - zenml internal logging that happens during the with-block
>   - retries / setup chatter from pydantic-ai or whatever
> 
> Implementation notes:
> 
> - SandboxSession owns _log_store / _log_origin / _log_response on the
>   base. Lazily registered on first _emit_sandbox; deregistered on
>   _close_log_origin (called from close()).
> - Origin setup failure latches _log_forwarding_disabled so the
>   per-line emit path doesn't retry on every call.
> - LocalSandboxSession.exec calls _log_command before launching Popen.
>   LocalSandboxProcess takes session=, routes stdout/stderr through
>   session._wrap_stream so each line emits to the origin.
> - BaseSandbox.forward_session_logs and BaseSandbox.forward_lines are
>   deleted -- they're superseded by the session-level helpers.
> 
> Updated test suite to assert direct emission (no more
> LoggingContext mocking).
>

> 
> * Reuse LoggingContext for sandbox-log routing (no more duplicated origin plumbing)
> 
> The previous direct-emit path duplicated ~50 LOC of LoggingContext's
> internals in SandboxSession — manually calling generate_logs_request,
> zen_store.create_logs, log_store.register_origin / deregister_origin,
> and constructing LogRecord objects to pass into log_store.emit. That
> was correct-but-wrong: the architectural primitive (LoggingContext)
> already does all of this; we just didn't want its stack-push semantics
> because pushing it onto the thread's active-context stack would
> false-attribute every step-side logger call.
> 
> Fix: split the stack-push from the origin lifecycle in LoggingContext
> itself. New methods:
> 
> - LoggingContext.begin() — register_origin without joining the
>   active-context stack. Idempotent.
> - LoggingContext.end() — deregister + flush. Idempotent.
> - LoggingContext.emit_to(record) — emit to *this* context's
>   origin, bypassing the active-context lookup that .emit() does.
> 
> __enter__ / __exit__ now compose these as expected (push +
> begin / end + pop) — behavior identical for all existing callers
> (step_runner, step_launcher, dynamic runner, deployer service,
> kubernetes orchestrator, pipeline definition, etc.).
> 
> SandboxSession switches to:
> - setup_logging_context(source, step_run, pipeline_run) for the
>   LogsResponse + LoggingContext (the canonical helper).
> - ctx.begin() to register without stack push.
> - ctx.emit_to(record) for command + stdout/stderr lines.
> - ctx.end() on close.
> 
> Drops _log_store / _log_origin / _log_response state
> fields. _ensure_log_origin / _close_log_origin renamed to
> _ensure_log_ctx / _close_log_ctx. Latch-on-failure
> preserved (_log_forwarding_disabled).
> 
> Net: -55 LOC in session.py for the helpers; LoggingContext gains
> ~45 LOC of public surface that's actually reusable by anyone who
> needs a side-channel log source.

> * Address schustmi PR #4866 review: deadlock fix, architectural refactor, style sweep
> 
> Block items:
> 
> - B2 collect() deadlock: SandboxProcess.collect() drained stdout
>   serially before stderr. A child writing >~64KB to stderr alone
>   filled the pipe buffer, blocked on write(), never closed stdout,
>   and collect() hung forever waiting for stdout EOF. Now drains
>   both streams concurrently in daemon threads, joining before
>   wait(). Added a regression test that spawns a real subprocess
>   writing 200KB to stderr only with a 25s timeout.
> 
>   Also: process.py:165 — _drain_capped no longer skips intermediate
>   lines after the cap; once truncated, no further lines are
>   appended (no mid-stream gaps the user can't see). And:
>   process.py:133 — collect() called more than once on the same
>   process no longer double-logs the exec-result marker (latched
>   via _collected).
> 
> - B1 version-skew: documentation-only per repo precedent. New
>   StackComponentType values have shipped without client-side gates
>   (DEPLOYER, LOG_STORE, etc.); same pattern applies here.
> 
> Architectural fixes:
> 
> - BaseSandboxConfig now inherits from BaseSandboxSettings (the
>   pattern every other sandbox flavor already uses and that the
>   partial-dict override path expects). Same for LocalSandboxConfig
>   inheriting LocalSandboxSettings. Previously the two-class shape
>   caused settings-overlay semantics to silently misbehave when the
>   flavor relied on config-level defaults.
> 
> - STEP_IMAGE sentinel + base_image + timeout_seconds removed from
>   the base. They were either ignored by the only shipped flavor
>   (LocalSandbox ignores all three) or a hacky sentinel for an
>   orchestrator concept that doesn't belong in BaseSandboxSettings.
>   Each flavor (Modal, k8s_agent_sandbox) declares its own image
>   + timeout fields. resolve_step_image() removed alongside —
>   unexercised here, and the cross-layer reach into
>   ContainerizedOrchestrator was a smell.
> 
> - BaseSandboxSnapshot.provider renamed to sandbox_flavor;
>   component_id added as an optional UUID so flavors with
>   non-portable refs (cross-cluster, cross-connector) can gate
>   restore to the producing component. _validate_snapshot_provider
>   now checks both.
> 
> - Env+secrets schizophrenia cleaned up: secret resolution moved to
>   the shared `resolve_secrets_to_env(secret_ids)` helper in
>   env_utils, called from both `BaseSandbox._resolve_session_environment`
>   and `get_runtime_secret_environment`. Sandbox path now also
>   skips empty secret_values with a permissions warning and coerces
>   values via str(), matching the canonical path.
> 
> Refactors (W2, W3, W5):
> 
> - W2: StackComponent gets a `_merge_settings(overlay_dict)` helper
>   that wraps the config(exclude_unset) + overlay + model_validate
>   pattern. Both StackComponent.get_settings and
>   BaseSandbox.resolve_settings now call it. No more divergent
>   inline merges.
> 
> - W3: as above — `resolve_secrets_to_env` extracted.
> 
> - W5: SandboxSession.__exit__ now wraps close() in try/finally
>   and always calls _close_log_ctx(). The base owns the log-source
>   cleanup contract instead of relying on subclasses to remember
>   the call. LocalSandboxSession.close() dropped its redundant
>   _close_log_ctx() call.
> 
> schustmi line-comment fixes:
> 
> - logging_utils.py:335 — self.end() now wrapped in try/finally
>   so the remaining cleanup (super().__exit__, step_names_token
>   reset) runs even if end() raises.
> - session.py:227 — walrus operator: `if url := self._dashboard_url():`
> - session.py:382 — sandbox stderr now emits at INFO (was WARNING).
>   Sandbox stderr is diagnostic output, not an application-level
>   warning. Kept the WARNING level on _log_exec_result for non-zero
>   exit codes, where it's a real failure signal.
> - local_sandbox.py:107 — LocalSandboxProcess accepts started_at
>   via __init__ instead of post-construction mutation.
> - local_sandbox.py:266 — _workdir double-concat bug: when cwd was
>   None and self._workdir was relative, the resolution
>   os.path.join(self._workdir, effective_cwd) produced
>   self._workdir + self._workdir. Now distinguishes cwd=None

> * Adversarial-review fixes: thread-safety, exception capture, snapshot migration
> 
> The adversarial workflow's four parallel skeptics surfaced 4 real
> bugs in the recent review-fix commit (da2cb03a88). All addressed.
> 
> Bug 1: LoggingContext.emit_to _disabled flag race
> =================================================
> 
> The `_disabled` reentrancy guard was a plain bool. With B2's new
> concurrent stdout+stderr drain threads both routing through
> ctx.emit_to, one thread's in-flight `True` caused the other to
> return early silently — sandbox log lines lost for every dual-output
> command. Switched to threading.local() so the guard is per-thread:
> concurrent emits serialize through the log store, not against each
> other.
> 
> Bug 2: SandboxProcess.collect() drain-thread exception swallowing
> =================================================================
> 
> Drain threads previously caught nothing. If stdout() / stderr()
> raised mid-iteration (realistic for cloud-provider SDK streams, and
> possible for log-store-backed wrappers today), the thread died,
> results[idx] stayed None, the SandboxOutput fell back to empty
> captured strings, AND subprocess.wait() could re-deadlock on an
> undrained pipe — re-introducing the exact failure mode B2 was
> supposed to fix.
> 
> Now: drain threads capture exceptions, collect() kills the process
> + best-effort waits + re-raises after join(). The caller sees the
> real failure instead of silently-empty output.
> 
> Bug 3: Snapshot field rename has no migration path
> ==================================================
> 
> `BaseSandboxSnapshot.provider` → `sandbox_flavor` (per schustmi
> review) broke deserialization of any snapshot persisted before the
> rename. Added a `@model_validator(mode="before")` that accepts
> legacy `provider` and aliases it to `sandbox_flavor` when only the
> old field is present. New field takes precedence on collision.
>

>   _collected latch wasn't covered with a session attached; verifies
>   exactly one OK/FAIL marker fires across two collect() calls.
> - test_drain_exception_kills_process_and_reraises: a stream
>   iterator that raises mid-iteration must cause collect() to kill
>   the process and re-raise, not silently swallow.
> - test_concurrent_drain_on_both_streams_at_volume: 1000 lines on
>   each stream — verifies the threaded drain handles both streams
>   without interleaving or drop.
> - test_exit_flushes_log_ctx_when_close_raises: confirms the W5
>   base-owns-cleanup contract works even when subclass close()
>   raises.
> - test_legacy_provider_alias_accepted +

>   backward compat.
> - TestResolveSecretsToEnv with 6 cases covering empty input,

>   try/except, empty secret_values warning, override on collision.

- 7abf789599e61e78edbe9dd1ce701154e964616e — https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/commit/7abf789599e61e78edbe9dd1ce701154e964616e
> Fix misleading multi-node example in Baseten step operator error
> 
> The RuntimeError raised when a regular step requests node_count>1 told
> users to switch to `CommandStep(command=["torchrun", "train.py"])`. That
> is wrong on two counts: bare torchrun is single-node (it coordinates
> ranks but does not launch across nodes), and because the operator passes
> the command through shell_join, an unwrapped `$BT_*` reference is quoted
> and never expands.
> 
> Point users at the correct, shell-wrapped form instead, wiring Baseten's
> real per-node rendezvous variables (BT_GROUP_SIZE, BT_NODE_RANK,
> BT_LEADER_ADDR, BT_NUM_GPUS) into torchrun, matching the example already
> documented in the Baseten step-operator docs.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

> Simplify _docker_auth: require explicit registry_auth_secret
> 
> Auto-upsert from active stack registry credentials was wrong:
> the step operator can be used in multiple stacks with different
> registries, so the named secret would be overwritten by whichever
> stack ran last. Short-lived credentials are also not handled well.
> 
> Now _docker_auth returns a DockerAuth only when registry_auth_secret
> is explicitly configured. Removes upsert_secret from BasetenApiClient
> and the related tests that covered the auto-create path.

- 8afa9321480dd3cf53b924666b3b095abc46e86f — https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/commit/8afa9321480dd3cf53b924666b3b095abc46e86f
> Add Baseten step operator integration
> 
> Adds a 'baseten' step operator that runs steps as Baseten training jobs.
> Regular steps run single-node with full ZenML features; multi-node
> distributed training is expressed via a CommandStep (node_count > 1),
> which Baseten fans across nodes and which owns its own distributed launch
> (e.g. torchrun reading the injected BT_* rendezvous vars). A runtime gate
> in submit() rejects multi-node regular steps, since running ZenML's step
> machinery on every node would duplicate artifacts, outputs and logs.
> 
> Status and cancellation use the Baseten Training REST API (project-scoped),
> storing both the job id and training project id as step metadata. Sensitive
> env vars (e.g. the ZenML store token) must be routed through Baseten secrets
> via the 'secrets' setting rather than inlined. The job image is the source
> of truth: push() runs from an empty source dir with enable_baseten_workdir
> disabled so the local working directory is not uploaded.
> 
> Includes unit tests (mocked truss SDK) covering the gate, env/secret
> splitting, status mapping, cancel, metadata recording, docker auth and the
> validator, plus docs.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- 908f3b04f77a3e0c924d3758d30c8e28a5fbcc74 — https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/commit/908f3b04f77a3e0c924d3758d30c8e28a5fbcc74
> Auto-sync ZenML store token into a Baseten secret for regular steps
> 
> Regular (non-command) steps run on Baseten need the ephemeral ZENML_STORE_API_TOKEN
> to call back to the ZenML server. Rather than refusing the token (which blocked
> single-node regular steps) or inlining it into the job config, the operator now
> upserts it into a managed Baseten secret (zenml-store-api-token-<operator-id>)
> on each submit and references it. The token never lands in the inlined config,
> and an explicit secrets mapping still takes precedence. Command steps continue to
> drop the token since they never talk to the server.

- ae7953948d96b036a2ce68ab1dbb5364580ba3a0 — https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/commit/ae7953948d96b036a2ce68ab1dbb5364580ba3a0
> Expose HF-mount and cache-affinity cache settings; doc nits
> 
> Surface two more of Baseten's CacheConfig knobs as step operator settings,
> mirroring the GR00T training recipe Baseten shared:
> - cache_enable_legacy_hf_mount (default False): also mount the legacy Hugging
>   Face cache path so HF downloads are reused across jobs.
> - cache_require_affinity (default True, matching truss): set False to let a
>   project run across different GPU types at the cost of cache warmth.
> Both only apply when enable_cache is True.
> 
> Also address review nits: note Baseten offers more GPU types than H100/H200.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

> Add Baseten robot policy training example
> 
> A demo pipeline (behavior-cloning policy for a 2D reaching task) that runs the
> GPU-heavy training step as a single-node Baseten H100 job while the rest of the
> pipeline runs under the local/remote orchestrator. Steps are fully connected via
> artifacts, track under a ZenML Model, log metadata, and conditionally promote.
> 
> Runs locally with --local (NumPy fallback, no GPU) or on Baseten with
> --step-operator. Includes the temporary dev-image docker helper so the branch's
> zenml is baked into the Baseten training image.

- c9b195b5b499a1c6a4a57440ef03bfe47fcd0283 — https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/commit/c9b195b5b499a1c6a4a57440ef03bfe47fcd0283
> Fix databricks test leaking the global custom source root (#4979)
> 
> * Fix databricks test leaking the global custom source root
> 
> test_configure_databricks_wheel_environment_sets_source_root calls
> configure_databricks_wheel_environment, which sets the process-global custom
> source root via set_custom_source_root. The test only monkeypatched sys.path
> and env vars, so the global leaked into later tests in the same randomly-ordered
> integration-tests-fast shard — surfacing as spurious 'outside the source root'
> failures in unrelated tests (e.g. test_pipeline_parallel), which run pipeline
> subprocesses that resolve modules against that global.
> 
> Add an autouse fixture that snapshots and restores source_utils._CUSTOM_SOURCE_ROOT
> so it cannot bleed across tests.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
> 
> * Use explicit save/restore fixture for custom source root
> 
> Replace the monkeypatch.setattr(x, attr, <same value>) idiom with a plain
> save/yield/restore generator fixture. Behavior is identical, but the intent
> (snapshot before, restore after) is obvious instead of reading like a no-op.
- cc65b3fcb65994cda0da38cb07cedcf70dfb6d63 — https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/commit/cc65b3fcb65994cda0da38cb07cedcf70dfb6d63
