- cf370c470c6dcb0731c378d2f9ab6176fcd51def — https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/commit/cf370c470c6dcb0731c378d2f9ab6176fcd51def
> Document multi-node distributed training via CommandStep (#4980)
> 
> * Document multi-node distributed training via CommandStep
> 
> Adds a generalized "bring your own launcher" pattern to the GPU/distributed
> training tutorial: wrap any external distributed launcher (TorchX, Ray,
> SkyPilot, torchrun) in a CommandStep that runs on a step operator. ZenML owns
> the run and the launcher lifecycle; the launcher owns the worker gang.
> 
> Includes a launcher comparison table, a full TorchX + Volcano on Kubernetes
> worked example (vanilla torch.distributed train.py, pipeline, worker
> Dockerfile), Ray/SkyPilot variants, and notes on image contents, logging,
> dynamic pipelines/resource pools, and gang scheduling. Cross-links the command
> steps how-to page.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
> 
> * Drop SkyPilot, add single-node multi-GPU CommandStep example
> 
> Removes SkyPilot from the distributed-training launcher options and adds a
> single-node multi-GPU section using torchrun --standalone in a CommandStep, so
> the page covers both single-node multi-GPU and multi-node from one pattern.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
> 
> * Use relative links for internal docs pages
> 
> The absolute docs.zenml.io URLs for the distributed-training tutorial and
> resource-pools page 404 on the live site (their published paths differ from the
> repo tree). Switch internal cross-references to relative markdown links, which
> CI validates against the actual files.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
> 
> * Apply review feedback to multi-node distributed training docs
> 
> - Use @pipeline(dynamic=True, depends_on=[train]) for command-step examples
>   (per Michael) and explain why a dynamic pipeline needs depends_on.
> - Present single-node multi-GPU as three equal patterns: a native step that
>   spawns processes itself (no Accelerate needed), the Accelerate integration,
>   and a CommandStep running torchrun. Previously over-anchored on Accelerate.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
> 
> * Refine single-node dynamic example: isolated runtime, accurate depends_on
> 
> - Native single-node training step now uses @pipeline(dynamic=True) with
>   @step(runtime="isolated") so the GPU step runs in its own container rather
>   than inline in the orchestrator process.
> - Correct the depends_on explanation: it builds a dedicated image for
>   step-operator steps in dynamic pipelines (regular steps use the pipeline
>   image and don't need it), per zenml/config/step_run_info.py.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
> 
> * Hoist torch imports to module top in native step example
> 
> The ZenML environment running the pipeline has the libraries installed, so the
> in-function torch imports aren't needed — import at the top like normal.
> 
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
> 
> ---------
> 
> Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

> Add catch-up cleanup for expired API transactions (#4943)
> 
> * Add DB indexes and request timeout fix
> 
> * Add catch-up cleanup for expired API transactions
> 
> * Avoid caching read-only request transactions
> 
> Read-only orchestration polling already has idempotent semantics. Keeping those requests out of the SQL-backed API transaction cache avoids adding write pressure and cleanup contention to high-frequency control-plane checks.
> 
> * Address API transaction cleanup review
> 
> Keep GET requests cacheable, simplify get-or-create race handling, move cleanup validation into server configuration, and cover the interval/time-budget invariant with unit tests.
> 
> * Document API transaction retry race
> 
> ---------
> 
> Co-authored-by: Stefan Nica <stefan@zenml.io>
